| `separator`, vertical   | rest     | `border-inline-start` | `border.width.025` in `color.border.subtle`            |
| `separator`, vertical   | rest     | `margin-block`        | `space.100`                                            |
| `separator`, horizontal | rest     | `border-block-start`  | `border.width.025` in `color.border.subtle`            |
| `separator`, horizontal | rest     | `margin-inline`       | `space.100`                                            |

`ToolbarButton`, every colour:

| Part                   | State | Property                    | Token                                                                         |
| ---------------------- | ----- | --------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `button`               | rest  | `height`, `min-width`       | `size.control`                                                                |
| `button`               | rest  | `padding-inline`            | `space.300`; 0 when `data-icon-only`                                          |
| `button`               | rest  | `gap`                       | `space.150`                                                                   |
| `button`               | rest  | `border-radius`             | `radius.md`                                                                   |
| `button`               | rest  | `border-width`              | `border.width.025`                                                            |
| `label`                | rest  | `font`, `letter-spacing`    | `typography.label`, with its tracking twin                                    |
| `startIcon`, `endIcon` | rest  | `--perron-icon-size`        | `icon.size.400`                                                               |
| `button` (`focusRing`) | focus | `outline`, `outline-offset` | `focus.width` in `color.border.focus`, `focus.offset` (drawn by `perron.css`) |

`ToolbarButton`, `neutral`:

| Part     | State    | Property           | Token                    |
| -------- | -------- | ------------------ | ------------------------ |
| `button` | rest     | `background-color` | `transparent`            |
| `button` | rest     | `border-color`     | `transparent`            |
| `button` | rest     | `color`            | `color.text.primary`     |
| `button` | hover    | `background-color` | `color.surface.hover`    |
| `button` | pressed  | `background-color` | `color.surface.selected` |
| `button` | disabled | `background-color` | `transparent`            |
| `button` | disabled | `color`            | `color.text.tertiary`    |

`ToolbarButton`, `brand`:

| Part     | State    | Property           | Token                         |
| -------- | -------- | ------------------ | ----------------------------- |
| `button` | rest     | `background-color` | `color.surface.brand`         |
| `button` | rest     | `border-color`     | `color.border.brand`          |
| `button` | rest     | `color`            | `color.text.on-color.dark`    |
| `button` | hover    | `background-color` | `color.surface.brand-hover`   |
| `button` | pressed  | `background-color` | `color.surface.brand-pressed` |
| `button` | disabled | `background-color` | `color.surface.inset`         |
| `button` | disabled | `border-color`     | `transparent`                 |
| `button` | disabled | `color`            | `color.text.tertiary`         |

A disabled brand button looks like a disabled neutral one on a fill, `color.surface.inset` with `color.text.tertiary` and no edge: disabled is a colour, and a yellow that can't be pressed shouldn't still mark the main action.

Highlighted, open, selected and invalid don't apply: a toolbar item takes focus rather than `data-highlighted`, a popup trigger rendered through `render` keeps the button's look when its popup is open, and a toolbar holds no choice or value.

## Keyboard and ARIA

From the Base UI reference for `Toolbar` and the installed `ToolbarRoot`, `ToolbarButton`, `ToolbarGroup`, `ToolbarSeparator` and the composite root they build on. "From" says who does it.

| Key                    | Does                                                                                                                                                                                                  | From                                           |
| ---------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `Tab`, `Shift+Tab`     | Moves focus into the toolbar, to the item that last had it (the first enabled item at first), and out of it again: the toolbar is one tab stop                                                        | Base UI                                        |
| `ArrowRight`           | In a horizontal toolbar, moves focus to the next item, wrapping from the last to the first while `loopFocus` is on; the previous item under an `rtl` `DirectionProvider`, which Perron doesn't set up | Base UI                                        |
| `ArrowLeft`            | In a horizontal toolbar, moves focus to the previous item, wrapping from the first to the last while `loopFocus` is on; the next item under an `rtl` `DirectionProvider`, which Perron doesn't set up | Base UI                                        |
| `ArrowDown`, `ArrowUp` | In a vertical toolbar, move focus to the next and the previous item, wrapping while `loopFocus` is on                                                                                                 | Base UI                                        |
| `Enter`, `Space`       | Activate the focused button: fire `onClick`, or open the popup of a trigger given through `render`                                                                                                    | The browser; Base UI for a non-button `render` |

`Home` and `End` do nothing: Base UI's toolbar doesn't turn them on (`enableHomeAndEndKeys` is off in the installed `ToolbarRoot`), and the component adds no keys of its own.

| Element                | Role                                                               | Accessible name from                                                                         | States announced                                                                    |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `root`                 | `toolbar`, from Base UI                                            | The caller's `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`                                               | `aria-orientation`                                                                  |
| `button`               | `button`, native; `role="button"` when `render` gives a non-button | Its text content, the label's `children`; for an icon-only button, the caller's `aria-label` | Disabled: `aria-disabled` while focusable when disabled, else the native `disabled` |
| `startIcon`, `endIcon` | none: `aria-hidden="true"`                                         | none                                                                                         | none                                                                                |
| `group`                | `group`, from Base UI                                              | The caller's `aria-label`, when the group needs one                                          | none                                                                                |
| `separator`            | `separator`, from Base UI                                          | none                                                                                         | `aria-orientation`, across the toolbar's                                            |

What axe won't catch, from the contract, each with how this component meets it:

- [ ] Everything the eye is told, the ear is told, for every shape each prop accepts: a button's label is the text it is named by, and an icon-only button's `aria-label` says what its icon shows; the icons are `aria-hidden`; `color` carries emphasis, not meaning; disabled is announced by `aria-disabled` or `disabled`; the separator is announced as one.
- [ ] Every landmark and named region has an accessible name: the toolbar is named by the caller's `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`, which every story sets, so two toolbars on a screen tell themselves apart.
- [ ] Every default label can be overridden: none here; the toolbar owns no strings.
- [ ] Every shape the type accepts renders, in every variant: a button's `children`, `startIcon` and `endIcon` render a string, an element and a list alike, in both colours and both orientations.
- [ ] A hidden copy kept for animation is `aria-hidden`, and a collapsed region is `inert`: none here; the toolbar keeps no hidden copy and collapses nothing.
- [ ] Native semantics first: native `<button>`s from `Toolbar.Button`, and Base UI's `toolbar`, `group` and `separator` roles, with ARIA only for the toolbar's and an icon-only button's names.
- [ ] Focus moves in reading order and returns on close: the arrow keys move through the items in document order, swapped only under an `rtl` `DirectionProvider`, which Perron doesn't set up, and the toolbar opens nothing of its own; a popup opened through `render` returns focus to its trigger, by Base UI.
- [ ] Every target is at least `size.target-min` square: the smallest target is an icon-only button, `size.control` (34 px) square.
- [ ] Loops stop when the system asks for less motion: none here; the toolbar has no loop and no transition.

## Owned strings

No owned strings: every word comes from the caller, as a button's `children`, an icon-only button's `aria-label`, or the toolbar's `aria-label`.

## Component rules

Rules for this component alone, numbered so the build and the review can cite them.

- **CR-1.** Base UI's toolbar already gives the one tab stop, the roving `tabIndex`, the arrow keys, the wrap and the disabled cascade from root and group to button, so the components rebuild none of it and add no key handlers.
- **CR-2.** `ToolbarButton`, `ToolbarGroup` and `ToolbarSeparator` only render inside a `Toolbar`: Base UI's parts read its context. Every story renders them in one.
- **CR-3.** Each of the four takes `{...rest}` before its own attributes and its own props out of `rest` first (`orientation`, `disabled`, `color`, `startIcon`, `endIcon`; an inherited Base UI prop such as `loopFocus` stays in `rest`, keeping Base UI's default), and merges `className` after its own `pn-` class; `ref` reaches its one element.
- **CR-4.** `ToolbarButton`'s root always carries `data-color`, default included, and `data-icon-only` when it has a `startIcon` and no `children`; the CSS selects on them, one class then attributes: `.pn-ToolbarButton[data-color='brand']`. The toolbar's layout reads Base UI's `data-orientation`: `.pn-Toolbar[data-orientation='vertical']` is a column.
- **CR-5.** The states keep the button's geometry: hover, pressed, focus and disabled change colours only, never the height, padding, gap, border width or radius. Every button draws a `border.width.025` border, `transparent` on a neutral button and a disabled brand one, so both colours share one size and Windows' forced colours draw an edge round each.
- **CR-6.** Hover is read inside `@media (hover: hover)`; pressed (`:active`) takes the pressed tokens, a step past hover, in a rule after it and outside it, so a touch press shows. Neither applies to a disabled button: both rules exclude `[data-disabled]`, since a button focusable when disabled has no native `disabled` and still matches `:hover` and `:active`.
- **CR-7.** Focus uses the ring `perron.css` draws on `:focus-visible`; the component draws no ring of its own and never removes the outline. The root's `space.100` padding and gap leave the ring, `focus.offset` plus `focus.width` out, inside the bar.
- **CR-8.** The colour is set on the button's `color`; the label and the icons take it through `currentColor`. No rule sets a colour on an icon. The icon spans are `aria-hidden="true"`, rendered only when their prop is given, and set `--perron-icon-size` to `icon.size.400`.
- **CR-9.** A button's label stays on one line (`white-space: nowrap`), the button growing with it, rather than wrapping inside the fixed `size.control` height.
- **CR-10.** A `brand` button keeps its `color.border.brand` edge at rest, on hover and pressed: the light-theme yellow fill reaches only 2.1:1 on the surfaces, and the edge carries the 3:1 ([Semantic colours](../foundations/semantic-colours.md#brand)).
- **CR-11.** The separator is drawn as a border on a box of no size (`border-inline-start` across a horizontal toolbar, `border-block-start` across a vertical one), stretched across the bar with `align-self: stretch`, never as a background, which forced colours remove.
- **CR-12.** Changes of state are immediate: no `duration.*` token fits a button's state change, so the CSS has no transition.
- **CR-13.** The toolbar sizes to its content (`display: inline-flex`); placing it on the map, its `z-index` and its distance from the edge belong to the pattern that uses it, such as MapControls.

## Stories

The deferred design's page draws two components: the toolbar, with one variant property, `orientation` (`horizontal`, `vertical`), and its button, with `color` (`neutral`, `brand`) and `State` (`default`, `hover`, `focus`, `disabled`). Each story is named by its variant name (`penpot/README.md`, "Conventions").

The button's stories, and a later drawing's exports, are prefixed `Button`, as `ButtonNeutralDefault`, beside the toolbar's `Horizontal` and `Vertical`, since the Penpot conventions name a variant by its property values alone.

The toolbar stories render a toolbar named "Map controls" (zoom in, zoom out, a separator, then a group with "Show whole line" and a brand "Show departures"), with `packages/perron/icons/`'s `plus`, `minus` and `locate`. The button stories render one labelled button, "Show whole line", in a toolbar named "Actions", and set `disabled` for a `Disabled` story. The hover and focus stories render at rest: the visual check drives the state, and their `play` tests check it.

| Story                   | Shows                                                                                           | `play` test                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ----------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Horizontal`            | horizontal toolbar: two icon-only buttons, a separator, a group of two labelled buttons         | Tab focuses the first button; ArrowRight moves through each button, skipping the separator, and wraps to the first; ArrowLeft goes back; Enter fires `onClick` once; Shift+Tab leaves, and Tab returns to the last focused button |
| `Vertical`              | vertical toolbar: zoom in, zoom out, a separator, locate, all icon-only                         | ArrowDown and ArrowUp move between the buttons and ArrowRight doesn't; the separator's `aria-orientation` is `horizontal`                                                                                                         |
| `ButtonNeutralDefault`  | neutral button, at rest                                                                         | none                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `ButtonNeutralHover`    | neutral button, hover                                                                           | Hovering lays `color.surface.hover` over the transparent fill                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `ButtonNeutralFocus`    | neutral button, focus                                                                           | Tab gives the button `:focus-visible` and the ring                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `ButtonNeutralDisabled` | neutral button, disabled                                                                        | The button has `aria-disabled` and `data-disabled`, Tab still reaches it, and a click fires no `onClick`                                                                                                                          |
| `ButtonBrandDefault`    | brand button, at rest                                                                           | none                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `ButtonBrandHover`      | brand button, hover                                                                             | Hovering sets the `color.surface.brand-hover` fill and keeps the `color.border.brand` edge                                                                                                                                        |
| `ButtonBrandFocus`      | brand button, focus                                                                             | none                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `ButtonBrandDisabled`   | brand button, disabled                                                                          | none                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `IconOnly`              | horizontal toolbar of three icon-only neutral buttons, two given `false` and `''` as `children` | Each button is named by its `aria-label`, has `data-icon-only` and no label span, its icon span is `aria-hidden`, and it is `size.control` square                                                                                 |
| `Disabled`              | horizontal toolbar with `disabled`                                                              | Every button carries `data-disabled`, the arrow keys still move between them, and a click fires no `onClick`                                                                                                                      |

## Do and don't

For a caller using the component, with the reason.

| Do                                                                                                                                                       | Don't                                                                                                                                |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Name every toolbar with `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`, such as "Map controls", so a screen reader tells it from the next one                         | Leave a toolbar unnamed: two on a screen are both announced as "toolbar"                                                             |
| Put each action in a `ToolbarButton`, so the arrow keys reach it                                                                                         | Put a Button, an IconButton or a plain `<button>` straight into the toolbar: it falls out of the arrow-key order and adds a tab stop |
| Give an icon-only button an `aria-label` that names the action: "Zoom in"                                                                                | Leave an icon-only button without one: its icon is `aria-hidden`, so the button has no name                                          |
| Open a menu, popover or dialog through `render`, `<ToolbarButton render={<Menu.Trigger />}>`, and set `disabled` on the `ToolbarButton`, not the trigger | Disable the trigger itself: Base UI says the button then leaves the toolbar's arrow-key order                                        |
| Wrap a button in a [Tooltip](tooltip.md) with `<Tooltip trigger={<ToolbarButton … />}>…</Tooltip>`, the tooltip around the button                        | Pass the tooltip's trigger to `ToolbarButton`'s `render`, as for popups                                                              |
| Give one button per screen `color="brand"`, for its main action                                                                                          | Mark several toolbar buttons `brand`, or use it for emphasis: a second yellow action leaves neither the main one                     |
| Keep a disabled button focusable, the default, so it can explain itself through a tooltip                                                                | Restyle a disabled button with `opacity`: disabled is `color.text.tertiary`, a colour                                                |
| Use a SegmentedControl or FilterChips for a choice or an on-and-off filter                                                                               | Build a toggle out of a `ToolbarButton`: it draws no selected state                                                                  |
| Place the toolbar over the map in a pattern, which sets its position and stacking                                                                        | Set a `z-index` or a margin from the screen edge on the toolbar itself: the component sizes to its content                           |

# Brand

The Mylder mark beside the wordmark "mylder", drawn in both themes from the tokens, for the brand slot of a top bar or a kiosk bar.

## Anatomy

Penpot page `Components/Brand`, not drawn yet: the design is deferred (`docs/adr/0010-unattended-runs-with-design-deferred.md`), so this spec decides the drawing from [Logos](../foundations/logos.md), [Typography](../foundations/typography.md), [Layout](../foundations/layout.md) and the tokens. Family: none. Shared parts: `VisuallyHidden`, which holds the brand name when the mark stands alone.

The mark is drawn inline as an `<svg>` whose three shapes take their colours from the tokens in CSS, not from `packages/perron/logos/mylder-mark.svg` as an image. A file can't follow the theme ([Logos](../foundations/logos.md#the-mark)), and the contract keeps `[data-theme]` selectors and `prefers-color-scheme` queries out of component CSS ([CSS](README.md#css)), so an inline mark reading `color.transit.mode.bus`, `color.transit.line.a` and `color.text.primary` is the one way the component shows the right mark on either ground. Its geometry is the file's (CR-3).

| Part (Penpot layer) | What it is                                                                                                                            | Base UI part                                   | Class                               | `slotProps` key |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- | --------------- |
| `root`              | The lockup: an inline row holding the mark and then the wordmark                                                                      | none: a `<span>` rendered by `useRender`       | `pn-Brand`                          | none            |
| `mark`              | The Mylder mark, an inline `<svg>` of the logo file's 27 × 19 viewBox, hidden from screen readers                                     | none: a plain `<svg>`, no behaviour to borrow  | `pn-Brand-mark`                     | none            |
| `bus`               | The mark's bus dot: the left circle, filled                                                                                           | none: a `<circle>` inside `mark`               | `pn-Brand-bus`                      | none            |
| `sTog`              | The mark's S-tog dot: the upper circle, filled                                                                                        | none: a `<circle>` inside `mark`               | `pn-Brand-sTog`                     | none            |
| `ring`              | The mark's estimated ring: the right circle, stroked and unfilled                                                                     | none: a `<circle>` inside `mark`               | `pn-Brand-ring`                     | none            |
| `wordmark`          | The brand name, "Mylder", set lowercase in `typography.heading-md` bold. Only with `variant='full'`                                   | none: a plain `<span>`, no behaviour to borrow | `pn-Brand-wordmark`                 | none            |
| `label`             | With `variant='mark'`, the brand name for screen readers only, in place of the wordmark. Never seen, so a drawing has no layer for it | none: the `VisuallyHidden` shared part         | `pn-VisuallyHidden`, the part's own | none            |

Brand has one variant property, `variant`, with `full` (the mark and the wordmark, the default) and `mark` (the mark alone, the brand name read to screen readers through `VisuallyHidden`). Hiding it under `breakpoint.compact-phone` is left to the screen or pattern that places it, since a component reads no `breakpoint.*` token and sizes to its container: [Logos](../foundations/logos.md#usage) keeps the mark alone for where space is tight, and [Layout](../foundations/layout.md#breakpoints)'s "the brand mark goes" is the screen's rule, applied by its caller.

## Base UI parts

Brand imports no Base UI component: the registry gives it no `baseUiParts`, and Base UI has nothing that draws a logo. It uses two Base UI utilities, at the version pinned in `package.json`: `useRender` (`@base-ui/react/use-render`) for the root, which gives it the contract's `render` prop, and `mergeProps` (`@base-ui/react/merge-props`) to merge the caller's props with its own.

| Base UI part                     | Renders  | Perron sets                                                                                                                           | Passed through                                                            |
| -------------------------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `useRender` (a hook, not a part) | `<span>` | `defaultTagName: 'span'`; `className` (`pn-Brand` first, then the caller's); `data-variant` from `variant`; the children (CR-1, CR-2) | `render`, `ref`, `className`, `style` and the `<span>`'s other attributes |

The root is a `<span>`, so the lockup is phrasing content and fits inside a link, a heading or a button the caller renders it as.

Base UI already does: swapping the root element for the one `render` gives, keeping the class, data attribute and children; merging the caller's `ref` with the element's; and merging event handlers, `className` and `style` through `mergeProps`; a `render` element's own props are merged last (CR-1).

## Props

In MUI's layout. Every prop here gets this description as its JSDoc. Brand takes no `children`: it draws its own mark and words, so the props type leaves `children` out. It has no `slotProps`, because the contract keys `slotProps` by inner Base UI part and Brand has none; a caller restyles it through `className` on the root.

| Name             | Type                   | Default      | Base UI prop | Description                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ---------------- | ---------------------- | ------------ | ------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `variant`        | `'full' \| 'mark'`     | `'full'`     | none         | `full` sets the mark beside the wordmark, as the brand appears by default; `mark` shows the mark alone, for where space is tight, with the brand name read to screen readers.             |
| `render`         | Base UI's `render`     |              | inherited    | Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render. |
| `brandNameLabel` | `string`               | The locale's | none         | Overrides "Mylder", the brand name seen in the wordmark, shown lowercase, with `variant='full'`, and heard alone with `variant='mark'`.                                                   |
| `className`      | `string`               |              | none         | Merged after `pn-Brand` on the root                                                                                                                                                       |
| `style`          | `CSSProperties`        |              | none         | Reaches the root                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `ref`            | `Ref<HTMLSpanElement>` |              | none         | Reaches the root                                                                                                                                                                          |

Brand comes in one size, with no `size` prop: the mark at its drawn size, 27 × 19 px, from the inline `<svg>`'s own `width` and `height` attributes as the logo file sets them, and the wordmark in `typography.heading-md`. [Logos](../foundations/logos.md#usage) sets the drawn size as the smallest the mark may be and gives the wordmark one role, no token holds a larger mark or wordmark, and a larger brand for the kiosk bar can join as a `size` value through the `design-tokens` skill when that pattern needs it.

## Tokens

One row per part, variant and property. Brand is not interactive, so its only design state is rest; rendered as a link through `render`, its focus ring is the one `perron.css` already draws on `:focus-visible`.

| Part                      | State | Property                    | Token                                                            |
| ------------------------- | ----- | --------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `root`                    | rest  | `display`                   | none: `inline-flex`, `align-items: center`                       |
| `root`                    | rest  | `gap`                       | `space.200`                                                      |
| `root`                    | rest  | `min-block-size`            | `size.target-min`                                                |
| `root`                    | rest  | `vertical-align`            | none: `middle`, so the lockup sits centred on a line of text     |
| `root`                    | rest  | `text-decoration`           | none: `none`, so a link through `render` keeps the lockup's look |
| `mark`                    | rest  | `display`                   | none: `block`                                                    |
| `mark`                    | rest  | `flex`                      | none: `none`, so it never shrinks in the row (CR-5)              |
| `mark`                    | rest  | `inline-size`, `block-size` | none: the `<svg>`'s own `width="27"` and `height="19"` (CR-3)    |
| `bus`                     | rest  | `fill`                      | `color.transit.mode.bus`                                         |
| `sTog`                    | rest  | `fill`                      | `color.transit.line.a`                                           |
| `ring`                    | rest  | `fill`                      | none: `none`                                                     |
| `ring`                    | rest  | `stroke`                    | `color.text.primary`                                             |
| `wordmark`                | rest  | `font`                      | `typography.heading-md`                                          |
| `wordmark`                | rest  | `font-weight`               | `font.weight.bold`                                               |
| `wordmark`                | rest  | `letter-spacing`            | `typography.heading-md-tracking`                                 |
| `wordmark`                | rest  | `color`                     | `color.text.primary`                                             |
| `wordmark`                | rest  | `text-transform`            | none: `lowercase`                                                |
| `wordmark`                | rest  | `white-space`               | none: `nowrap`, so a longer `brandNameLabel` stays on one line   |
| `label`, `variant='mark'` | rest  | none                        | none: the `VisuallyHidden` part's own styles, never seen         |

The gap between the mark and the wordmark is `space.200`, and the wordmark's colour is `color.text.primary`, the ring's ink. [Logos](../foundations/logos.md) names neither; `space.200` (8 px) is close to the ring's width (8.9 px), the clear space the mark keeps from everything else, and the mark's one neutral colour is `color.text.primary`.

The root keeps a `min-block-size` of `size.target-min`, so the lockup is at least 24 px tall when a caller renders it as a link to the start screen: the wordmark's line is 23 px (20 px at 1.15) and the mark 19 px, a pixel short of the contract's smallest target, and the extra pixel changes nothing in a 46 px top bar.

The mark's colours are the logo file's, held by the tokens [Logos](../foundations/logos.md#the-mark) names: bus `#D99A00` light and `#F2B630` dark, S-tog A `#00A1DE` in both, the ring `#12181B` light and `#EBEEEB` dark.

## Keyboard and ARIA

No Base UI part, so nothing from Base UI here. Brand takes no focus of its own; a caller that renders it as a link makes it one stop in the tab order.

| Key   | Does                                                                                                       | From                                         |
| ----- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| None  | The lockup takes no focus and no keys; Tab passes it by                                                    | Perron                                       |
| Enter | Rendered as a link (`render={<a href="/" />}`), follows it; Tab focuses it and `perron.css` draws the ring | The browser, through the caller's `<a href>` |

| Element    | Role                                                           | Accessible name from                                                                                         | States announced |
| ---------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------- |
| `root`     | None: a `<span>`; `link` when the caller renders an `<a href>` | Its text: the `wordmark`, or with `variant='mark'` the `label`, both the `brandName` owned string ("Mylder") | None             |
| `mark`     | None: `aria-hidden="true"`, hidden                             | None: the brand name beside it, seen or hidden, says it                                                      | None             |
| `wordmark` | None: text                                                     | Its text, "Mylder", shown lowercase                                                                          | None             |
| `label`    | None: text, visually hidden                                    | Its text, "Mylder"                                                                                           | None             |

What axe won't catch, from the contract, each with how this component meets it:

- [ ] Everything the eye is told, the ear is told, for every shape each prop accepts: the eye reads the brand from the mark and the wordmark; the ear hears the brand name, from the wordmark with `variant='full'` and from the `VisuallyHidden` label with `variant='mark'`, so neither variant is silent
- [ ] Every landmark and named region has an accessible name: none here, the lockup is not a region; the top bar or kiosk bar that holds it names its own
- [ ] Every default label can be overridden: `brandNameLabel` overrides "Mylder", in the wordmark and in the hidden label alike
- [ ] Every shape the type accepts renders, in every variant: both `variant` values, each with and without `brandNameLabel`, and each as a `<span>` and as a link through `render`: the `Full` and `Mark` stories as a `<span>`, `Link` and `MarkLink` as a link, and `BrandNameLabel` with `brandNameLabel` in both, its link named by the override
- [ ] A hidden copy kept for animation is `aria-hidden`, and a collapsed region is `inert`: none here, nothing animates or collapses; the `aria-hidden` mark is a picture, not a copy
- [ ] Native semantics first: a plain `<span>` with no role; the caller's `<a href>` through `render` for a link, never `role="link"` or `role="img"`
- [ ] Focus moves in reading order and returns on close: nothing takes focus but a caller's link, which sits in the tab order where it sits in the page
- [ ] Every target is at least `size.target-min` square: rendered as a link, the lockup is at least `size.target-min` tall and wider than tall in both variants (the mark alone, 27 px)
- [ ] Loops stop when the system asks for less motion: none here, nothing moves

## Owned strings

The brand name is a word the component shows and announces that the caller doesn't give, so it is an owned string: `expectOwnedStrings` fails a text run that is neither in the dictionary nor the caller's.

| Key         | English  | Override         | Seen or heard where                                                                                                             |
| ----------- | -------- | ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `brandName` | `Mylder` | `brandNameLabel` | The `wordmark`, shown lowercase as "mylder" with `variant='full'`; the `VisuallyHidden` label, read only, with `variant='mark'` |

The brand name is a new owned-string key, `brandName`, with "Mylder" in all four locales (a name, not translated), shown lowercase through `text-transform: lowercase` on the wordmark rather than written lowercase in the dictionary. The logo file's title and the docs write the name "Mylder", so screen readers meet a capitalised name, the wordmark still reads "mylder" as [Logos](../foundations/logos.md#usage) asks, and a `brandNameLabel` override is lowercased the same way.

## Component rules

- **CR-1.** The root renders through `useRender` with `defaultTagName: 'span'`, so `render`, `className`, `style` and `ref` behave as the contract's [Root](README.md#root) and [Customising](README.md#customising) say, with no Base UI component underneath. The rest props are merged first, so `pn-Brand` and `data-variant` win over them; a `render` element's own props are merged last, as Base UI does.
- **CR-2.** The root always carries `data-variant`, `'full'` included, so a caller's CSS can select on it; Brand's own CSS needs no variant selector, since the wordmark renders only with `full`, and selects it by its one class, `.pn-Brand-wordmark`. Its children are the `mark`, then, with `full`, the `wordmark`, or, with `mark`, the `VisuallyHidden` `label`, both holding the `brandName` string with `brandNameLabel` laid over it through `useOwnedStrings({ brandName: brandNameLabel })`.
- **CR-3.** The mark's geometry is `packages/perron/logos/mylder-mark.svg`'s, exactly: `viewBox="0 0 27 19"`, `width="27"`, `height="19"`; the bus dot at (5.5, 12.5), r 4.3; the S-tog dot at (13.5, 5.5), r 4.3; the ring at (21.5, 12.5), r 3.6, stroke width 1.7. Its colours are not in the markup: each shape's `fill` or `stroke` is set in `Brand.css` from the tokens in [Tokens](#tokens), so the mark follows the theme. A test holds the inline circles to the file's, so the two never drift apart.
- **CR-4.** The mark is `aria-hidden="true"` and `focusable="false"`, with no `<title>`: the brand name in the wordmark or the label is the one thing a screen reader hears, once.
- **CR-5.** Keep the mark as drawn ([Logos](../foundations/logos.md#usage)): no prop or class recolours, outlines or rearranges its three shapes, and the mark never shrinks below its drawn size in a flex row (`flex: none`).
- **CR-6.** In `(forced-colors: active)`, the bus and S-tog dots fill and the ring strokes in `CanvasText`, and the wordmark takes `CanvasText`, so the mark stays visible when the system replaces colours ([Accessibility](../foundations/accessibility.md#what-a-person-checks)): the ring's `color.text.primary` can vanish on a forced dark `Canvas`, the three shapes still tell the mark apart by their place, fill and ring, and StationIcon does the same.
- **CR-7.** Brand reads no `breakpoint.*` token and no media query beyond the contract's three: the screen or pattern that places it hides it, or picks `variant='mark'`, at its own breakpoints, such as [Layout](../foundations/layout.md#breakpoints)'s `breakpoint.compact-phone`.

## Stories

No Penpot design yet, so the stories are named by the variant names the design will have: `variant`, each value in PascalCase (the Conventions of `penpot/README.md`); `Link`, `MarkLink` and `BrandNameLabel` show how a caller uses it, not a variant of the drawing. Each renders on a `color.surface.raised` ground, as in a top bar's glass group; the build's light and dark Storybook themes show both marks.

| Story            | Shows                                                                                                                                                      | `play` test                                                                                                                                       |
| ---------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Default`        | The default props, `variant='full'`, as the docs page and the contract story show Brand; the contract story renders it, and its args pass every rule alone | The root has `data-variant="full"`, the text "Mylder" and a `ref` on the root `<span>`                                                            |
| `Full`           | `variant='full'`: the mark beside the wordmark "mylder"                                                                                                    | The root has `data-variant="full"` and the text "Mylder"; the mark is `aria-hidden`; Tab passes the lockup by                                     |
| `Mark`           | `variant='mark'`: the mark alone                                                                                                                           | No wordmark is shown; the `VisuallyHidden` label holds "Mylder", so the root's text is still the brand name                                       |
| `Link`           | `variant='full'` rendered as a link to the start screen, `render={<a href="/" />}`                                                                         | The page has a link named "Mylder" (case-insensitive); Tab focuses it, its box is at least `size.target-min` tall, and Shift+Tab moves focus back |
| `MarkLink`       | `variant='mark'` rendered as a link to the start screen, `render={<a href="/" />}`: a link named only by the `VisuallyHidden` label                        | The page has a link named "Mylder"; Tab focuses it, its box is at least `size.target-min` tall and wide, and Shift+Tab moves focus back           |
| `BrandNameLabel` | `brandNameLabel='Perron'` in both variants, each rendered as a link: the wordmark "perron" beside its mark, and the mark alone                             | The wordmark holds "Perron", shown lowercase; the page has two links named "Perron" and none named "Mylder"                                       |

## Do and don't

For a caller using the component, with the reason.

| Do                                                                                                                             | Don't                                                                                                                                        |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Use Brand wherever the Mylder brand appears in an interface, so the mark follows the theme                                     | Put `mylder-mark.svg` in an `<img>` on a themed ground: a file can't follow the theme, so the ring disappears in dark                        |
| Keep `variant='full'`, and switch to `variant='mark'` only where space is tight                                                | Show the wordmark alone, or set "mylder" in text beside an icon: the lockup is the mark and the wordmark together                            |
| Hide the whole Brand, or pick `variant='mark'`, at the screen's own breakpoint, such as `breakpoint.compact-phone`             | Hide parts of it with `className`, which can leave a mark that no screen reader hears or a wordmark without its mark                         |
| Render it as a link to the start screen with `render={<a href="/" />}`, so the name and the link are one stop in the tab order | Wrap it in a `<button>` with its own `aria-label`, or give the link a second name: the brand name is already its accessible name             |
| Keep at least the ring's width of clear space around it, as [Logos](../foundations/logos.md#usage) asks                        | Resize, recolour or restyle the mark with `className`, which breaks its drawn size and turns its colours, which are data states, into others |

title: Count
markdown:
# Count

A small pill holding how many there are, such as the "3" after "Delays" in a filter chip or the "12" after "Lines" on a tab, set in tabular figures on an inset or tinted surface.

<!-- run notes -->

The design is deferred (ADR 0010, `docs/adr/0010-unattended-runs-with-design-deferred.md`): this spec decides what the drawing would, from the [contract](README.md), the [foundations](../foundations/README.md), [content design](../content-design.md), the tokens and the specs of its Display siblings, [Stat](stat.md)'s, [Text](text.md)'s and [LineBadge](line-badge.md)'s. Count has no Base UI component and nothing in `dependsOn`, and the extracted prototype is not reachable from this branch, so nothing here rests on it. The foundations already name its look: [Typography](../foundations/typography.md#roles) gives `typography.data-sm` to "counts in chips and tabs", [Elevation](../foundations/elevation.md) puts counts on `color.surface.inset`, [Semantic spacing](../foundations/semantic-spacing.md#radius) rounds them with `radius.full`, and [Semantic colours](../foundations/semantic-colours.md) gives `color.surface.warning` to "a warning message or count".

## Anatomy

Penpot page `Components/Count`. Family: none, since it is a static mark that joins no family's treatment: it is not pressed, takes no hover and is not one of the Rows, Fields, Popups, Panels or Tooltips. Shared parts: VisuallyHidden, through the `UnknownValue` helper, which says an unknown count in words (CR-5).

The drawing will have a `root` board holding one text layer, `text`, and one variant property, `color`, with the values `neutral`, `success`, `warning`, `danger` and `info`, in that order. There is no `State` property: Count is not interactive and has only its rest state; the unknown count is rest with `data-unknown`.

| Part (Penpot layer) | What it is                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | Base UI part                                  | Class      | `slotProps` key |
| ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | ---------- | --------------- |
| `root`              | The pill: an inline `<span>` on the intent's surface, its text centred, at least as wide as it is tall, so a single digit sits in a circle                                                                                    | none: a `<span>` rendered through `useRender` | `pn-Count` | none            |
| `text`              | The count, such as "3" or "1 204", from the caller's `children`; the root's own text, with no element, class or `slotProps` key of its own. With no count it is "—", hidden from screen readers, and "Unknown" for them alone | none: the root's text                         | none       | none            |

No part has a Base UI component, because a count has no behaviour for Base UI to give: no focus, keys, state or popup. The root renders through Base UI's `useRender` hook instead, which gives it the `render` prop, as LineBadge's does. With the root holding the text directly there is no inner part, so Count takes no `slotProps`.

The root is a `<span>`: a count sits inside a chip's or a tab's `<button>`, a heading or a sentence, where only phrasing content is allowed.

## Base UI parts

No Base UI component: `baseUiParts` stays empty in `packages/perron/components.json`. The root renders through the `useRender` hook from `@base-ui/react/use-render` and merges its props with `mergeProps` from `@base-ui/react/merge-props`, at the version pinned in `packages/perron/package.json` (1.9.0). `get_reference` has no page for `useRender`; its types are in `node_modules/@base-ui/react/use-render/useRender.d.ts`.

| Base UI part | Renders  | Perron sets                                                                                                                                                                         | Passed through                                                           |
| ------------ | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `useRender`  | `<span>` | `defaultTagName: 'span'`; `ref`; `props`: `mergeProps(rest, own)`, where `own` is `className: 'pn-Count'`, `data-color`, `data-unknown` when the count is unknown, and the children | `render`, `ref`, `className`, `style` and every other `<span>` attribute |

Base UI already does: swapping the root element for the `render` element or function while keeping Perron's class, data attributes and `ref`; joining `className` strings, merging `style` objects and chaining event handlers in `mergeProps`. Count adds no behaviour of its own.

## Props

In MUI's layout. Every prop here gets this description as its JSDoc. No slots: Count has no part but its root.

| Name           | Type                                                        | Default      | Base UI prop | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| -------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | ------------ | ------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `color`        | `'neutral' \| 'success' \| 'warning' \| 'danger' \| 'info'` | `'neutral'`  | none         | The intent: what the count means. `neutral` is a plain tally, such as lines on a tab; the status intents tint the pill for a count of good or bad news, such as `danger` for lines with delays. Always beside words that say what is counted, such as "Delays": colour is never the only sign. |
| `children`     | `ReactNode`                                                 |              | none         | The count, written as the screen shows it: `3`, `'1 204'`, `'99+'`. Leave it out when no data gives the count, and Count shows "—" and says "Unknown". `0` is a count, and shows.                                                                                                              |
| `render`       | Base UI's `render`                                          |              | inherited    | Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render.                                                                                                      |
| `unknownLabel` | `string`                                                    | The locale's | none         | Overrides "Unknown", heard in place of "—" when there is no count                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `className`    | `string`                                                    |              | none         | Joined after `pn-Count` on the root                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `style`        | `CSSProperties`                                             |              | none         | Reaches the root                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `ref`          | `Ref<HTMLSpanElement>`                                      |              | none         | Reaches the root element                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |

`render`, `className`, `style`, `ref` and the other `<span>` attributes reach the root, as the contract's [Root](README.md#root) says; `render` is inherited from `useRender` as it is, with Base UI's JSDoc, and `CountProps` does not declare it again. `CountProps` declares `className`, `style` and `ref` itself, with these descriptions as their JSDoc, as FactList's and Delay's props do.

Count offers `color` with `neutral` and the four status intents, `success`, `warning`, `danger` and `info`, and not `brand`. Each of the five has a text token and a tinted surface in the contract's [Intents](README.md#intents) table, and [Accessibility](../foundations/accessibility.md) measures each status text at 4.5:1 on its own tint, so every pill's figure reads; the foundations already give status tints to counts. `brand` is left out because the contract keeps it for the main action, and a count is never an action. The status intents take their tinted surface, not `color.status.*` as a solid fill, since the contract gives them no solid fill: no text colour is measured on `color.status.*`.

Count ships with one size and one look, with no `size` and no `variant` prop. `typography.data-sm` is the role made for "counts in chips and tabs", the only places a count goes so far, and both props can join later as optional props without a break. With neither, the root carries `data-color` alone of the contract's three attributes.

Count takes the count as `children`, written by the caller, and neither formats it nor caps it, with no `max` prop. As Stat's spec reasons, the caller already writes numbers in the screen's locale ("1 204" in English, "1.204" in Danish) and content design's way, a `value` prop belongs to controls with `defaultValue` and `onChange`, and `<Count>3</Count>` reads as the screen shows it; a caller who caps writes `'99+'` itself. A bare number still renders as given (CR-2), and a `max` can join later without a break.

## Tokens

One row per part, state and property. Count has one design state, rest: it is never interactive (CR-8). The unknown count is rest with `data-unknown` on the root. The text layer has no element, so every row is the root's.

| Part   | State                           | Property               | Token                                                                                                               |
| ------ | ------------------------------- | ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `root` | rest, `color` neutral           | `background`           | `color.surface.inset`                                                                                               |
| `root` | rest, `color` neutral           | `color`                | `color.text.primary`                                                                                                |
| `root` | rest, `color` success           | `background`           | `color.surface.success`                                                                                             |
| `root` | rest, `color` success           | `color`                | `color.text.success`                                                                                                |
| `root` | rest, `color` warning           | `background`           | `color.surface.warning`                                                                                             |
| `root` | rest, `color` warning           | `color`                | `color.text.warning`                                                                                                |
| `root` | rest, `color` danger            | `background`           | `color.surface.danger`                                                                                              |
| `root` | rest, `color` danger            | `color`                | `color.text.danger`                                                                                                 |
| `root` | rest, `color` info              | `background`           | `color.surface.info`                                                                                                |
| `root` | rest, `color` info              | `color`                | `color.text.info`                                                                                                   |
| `root` | rest, `data-unknown`            | `background`           | `color.surface.inset`, whatever its `color` (CR-6)                                                                  |
| `root` | rest, `data-unknown`            | `color`                | `color.text.tertiary`, whatever its `color` (CR-6)                                                                  |
| `root` | rest                            | `font`                 | `typography.data-sm`                                                                                                |
| `root` | rest                            | `letter-spacing`       | `typography.data-sm`, its tracking                                                                                  |
| `root` | rest                            | `border-radius`        | `radius.full`                                                                                                       |
| `root` | rest                            | `padding-block`        | `space.050`                                                                                                         |
| `root` | rest                            | `padding-inline`       | `space.150`                                                                                                         |
| `root` | rest                            | `min-width`            | `space.050`, as `calc(1lh + 2 * var(--perron-space-050))`: one line of the count plus its block padding, its height |
| `root` | rest                            | `font-variant-numeric` | none: the keyword `tabular-nums`, so a changing count keeps its width                                               |
| `root` | rest                            | `white-space`          | none: the keyword `nowrap`, so "1 204" never breaks                                                                 |
| `root` | rest, `(forced-colors: active)` | `outline`              | `border.width.025`, `solid` in the system colour `CanvasText` (CR-7)                                                |

The root is `display: inline-block` with `box-sizing: border-box`, `text-align: center` and `vertical-align: baseline`, keywords all, so its figure sits on the baseline of the words beside it. Its height is one line of `typography.data-sm` (11 px at 1.3, 14.3 px) and `space.050` above and below, about 18 px; `min-width` is the same, so "3" sits in a circle and "12" or "1 204" stretches into a pill.

The pill is padded `space.050` (2 px) above and below and `space.150` (6 px) either side, at least `calc(1lh + 2 * var(--perron-space-050))` wide, with a `border.width.025` outline in `CanvasText` in forced colours. No `size.*` token holds a count's height, and none is needed: the line height and the block padding give it, about 18 px, small enough to sit inside a 34 px `size.control` chip beside its `typography.label` words; 6 px either side matches LineBadge's medium padding, and the `min-width` makes one digit a circle rather than a squeezed oval, using the `1lh` the contract allows. Forced colours drop the background, so without the outline the pill would vanish into the words beside it; an outline takes no space, so the geometry holds in both modes.

## Keyboard and ARIA

Count has no keys of its own and is never focusable. A caller who makes it a link or button through `render` brings that element's own keys, and its target size with them.

| Key  | Does                               | From   |
| ---- | ---------------------------------- | ------ |
| None | Count is not focusable or operable | Perron |

| Element                           | Role                         | Accessible name from                                                        | States announced |
| --------------------------------- | ---------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------- |
| `root`                            | None (generic `<span>`)      | Not named; its text is read in place, after the words beside it: "Delays 3" | None             |
| The "—" in `root`, when unknown   | Hidden: `aria-hidden="true"` | Not read                                                                    | None             |
| The words in `root`, when unknown | Text, in VisuallyHidden      | The owned string "Unknown", or `unknownLabel`                               | None             |

What axe won't catch, from the contract, each with how this component meets it:

- [ ] Everything the eye is told, the ear is told, for every shape each prop accepts: the count is read as shown, as part of the text around it; "—" is `aria-hidden` and the ear hears "Unknown" in its place (CR-5). A status `color` tells the eye nothing the caller's words beside it don't say ("Delays 3"), and the review holds the stories to it (CR-9).
- [ ] Every landmark and named region has an accessible name: none here; the root is not a landmark or region.
- [ ] Every default label can be overridden: `unknownLabel`.
- [ ] Every shape the type accepts renders, in every variant: `children` is a `ReactNode`; a number, a string, an element and a list each render, `0` and `'0'` are counts and not unknown (CR-4), and `Count.test.tsx` renders each shape. The colour stories give a number or a string.
- [ ] A hidden copy kept for animation is `aria-hidden`, and a collapsed region is `inert`: none here; nothing animates or collapses. The "—" is `aria-hidden` because the words speak for it, not for animation.
- [ ] Native semantics first: a plain `<span>`, with no role and no ARIA beyond `aria-hidden` on the "—"; the caller's own element through `render`.
- [ ] Focus moves in reading order and returns on close: Count takes no focus and opens nothing.
- [ ] Every target is at least `size.target-min` square: no target; Count is not pressed. The chip or tab it sits in is the target, and meets the size itself.
- [ ] Loops stop when the system asks for less motion: none here; Count has no motion.

## Owned strings

Every word Count shows comes from the caller, as `children`, but for the one it announces when there is no count.

| Key       | English   | Override       | Seen or heard where                                                           |
| --------- | --------- | -------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `unknown` | "Unknown" | `unknownLabel` | `root`, heard in place of the `aria-hidden` "—" when there is no count (CR-5) |

`unknown` is the key `packages/perron/src/locale/en.ts` already has for Stat and FactList, with its Danish, Swedish and Norwegian; the build adds Count to its JSDoc line and adds no key.

With no count, Count shows "—" in `color.text.tertiary` on `color.surface.inset`, whatever its `color`, `aria-hidden`, followed by the owned string "Unknown" in VisuallyHidden, as Stat and FactList do. Content design writes "—" for unknown and the brand never shows a guess, so Count shows neither `0` nor nothing when the data is missing; a screen reader skips or spells a bare "—", so the ear gets "Delays Unknown". An unknown count says nothing good or bad, so it drops its status tint; `color.text.tertiary` is allowed for the "—" of an unknown figure, always next to stronger text, as [Accessibility](../foundations/accessibility.md) lists it. A caller who wants no pill at all renders no Count.

## Component rules

Rules for this component alone, numbered so the build and the review can cite them.

- **CR-1.** Count renders one `<span>` through `useRender`, `defaultTagName: 'span'`. `render` swaps it, and the swapped element keeps `pn-Count`, the data attributes and the `ref`. Props merge as `mergeProps(rest, own)`, the caller's first, so Count's own class and data attributes win and `className` reads `pn-Count` and then the caller's. `color`, `children`, `unknownLabel` and `render` are taken out of `rest` before the merge, so none reaches the DOM as an attribute.
- **CR-2.** Count doesn't format or cap the count: `children` renders as given, a number as React writes it, as [Props](#props) decides for `children`.
- **CR-3.** The root always carries `data-color` with the prop's value, the default included, and no `data-variant` or `data-size`: Count has neither prop, as [Props](#props) decides.
- **CR-4.** The count is unknown when `children` renders nothing (`null`, `undefined`, a boolean, `''`, or an array of only such values) or is a number that is not finite (`NaN`, `Infinity`), as Stat decides it. `0` and `'0'` are counts. When unknown, the root carries the bare attribute `data-unknown`.
- **CR-5.** An unknown count shows "—", the character U+2014 in its own `aria-hidden="true"` `<span>`, followed by the owned string "Unknown" (or `unknownLabel`) in the VisuallyHidden shared part, its own text run so `expectOwnedStrings` reads it as a dictionary value. Count renders both through the `UnknownValue` shared helper from `packages/perron/src/internal/UnknownValue.tsx`, which wraps VisuallyHidden, and never draws its own dash or hiding styles.
- **CR-6.** `.pn-Count[data-unknown]` sets `background` to `color.surface.inset` and `color` to `color.text.tertiary`, and comes after the `[data-color]` rules, so it wins over every intent at the same specificity: an unknown count has no status to tint, as [Owned strings](#owned-strings) decides.
- **CR-7.** Inside `@media (forced-colors: active)`, the root draws an `outline` of `border.width.025` in `CanvasText`, since forced colours drop its background and the pill would vanish into the words beside it. An outline takes no space, so the pill keeps its geometry, as [Tokens](#tokens) sets it.
- **CR-8.** Count is not interactive: no `tabIndex`, no handler of its own, no hover. The caller's handlers and attributes reach the root unchanged.
- **CR-9.** A status `color` comes with words that say what is counted: "Delays 3", not a red "3" alone. Count can't hold this for the caller, so its JSDoc for `color` says it and the review holds the stories to it.
- **CR-10.** Count is not a live region and never moves focus. A screen whose counts update announces changes of state in its own polite live region, as [Accessibility](../foundations/accessibility.md) asks.
- **CR-11.** Count sizes to its content: no width of its own beyond its `min-width`, and it never wraps or truncates (see [Tokens](#tokens)).

## Stories

One per variant the deferred design will draw, named by the Penpot convention: the `color` value in PascalCase. `Unknown` is the neutral variant with no count, and proves CR-4 to CR-6. With no `Default` story, the [subject story](README.md#root) is the alphabetically first export, `Danger`. Each story's args are Count's alone, so the subject story's args render it alone; each status story's `render` sets the caller's words before the pill, such as "Delays" before `Danger`'s "3", so the tint is never the only sign (CR-9). `Unknown`'s `render` sets "Delays" before its "—" too, since the foundations allow its `color.text.tertiary` only next to stronger text, and the ear then hears "Delays Unknown". `Neutral` renders Count alone, since a plain tally carries no tint. Each status story's words are the [content design](../content-design.md) word for what the [foundations](../foundations/semantic-colours.md#status) give that intent: "Delays" for `danger`, which the foundations give delay disruptions; "Diversions" for `info`, which they give early and diversions; "Ageing" for `warning`, which they give a partial live picture, vehicles whose reports are 1 to 5 minutes old; and "Delays" at `0` for `success`, a line running normally. Planned works take `color.text.secondary`, not a status colour, so no story counts them.

| Story     | Shows                                                                                                                                    | `play` test                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| --------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Danger`  | `color='danger'`, the count `3`, after "Delays"; the subject story, which the contract story renders, and its args pass every rule alone | The root carries `data-color='danger'`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `Info`    | `color='info'`, the count `2`, after "Diversions"                                                                                        | none                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `Neutral` | `color='neutral'`, the default, the count `'12'`, with an `onClick`                                                                      | The root is a `<span>` with class `pn-Count` and `data-color='neutral'`, without `data-unknown`, and the `ref` reaches it; its computed `font-variant-numeric` is `tabular-nums` and `white-space` is `nowrap`; a click on it calls the caller's `onClick` once (CR-8); nothing in it takes focus |
| `Success` | `color='success'`, the count `0`, after "Delays", which shows as a count, zero delays being the good news of a line running normally     | The text is "0" and the root has no `data-unknown`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `Warning` | `color='warning'`, the count `5`, after "Ageing", a single digit                                                                         | Its rendered width and height differ by less than 1 px, so one digit sits in a circle                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `Unknown` | `color='neutral'` with no `children`: "—", after "Delays"                                                                                | The root carries `data-unknown`; "—" is `aria-hidden`; the accessible text is "Unknown"                                                                                                                                                                                                           |

## Do and don't

For a caller using the component, with the reason.

| Do                                                                                                                      | Don't                                                                                                                    |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Put a Count after the words that say what it counts, with a space between them in the markup: `Delays <Count>3</Count>` | Leave the space out: the accessible name may run the words together, "Delays3"                                           |
| Leave out `children` when no data gives the count, so Count shows "—" and says "Unknown"                                | Pass `0` or a guess when the count is unknown: the brand never claims more than the data knows                           |
| Render no Count when there is nothing to count and the screen hides empty tallies                                       | Rely on Count to hide itself at `0`, as MUI's Badge does: `0` is a count, and Count shows it                             |
| Write the count in the screen's locale, and cap it yourself if the space is short: `'1 204'`, `'99+'`                   | Squeeze a long count into a narrow chip and let it overflow: Count never wraps or truncates                              |
| Use a status `color` for a count of good or bad news beside the words that name it, such as `danger` after "Delays"     | Let the tint be the only sign, or colour a plain tally such as the number of lines on a tab                              |
| Use Stat for a key figure and Text with a `data` role for a number in a row or a sentence                               | Use Count as a key figure or inside running text as a number: it is a small pill for tallies in chips, tabs and headings |
| Use LineBadge to name a line                                                                                            | Put a line's name in a Count: it takes the operator's colour, not an intent                                              |
| Announce a changed count in the screen's own polite live region, when it changes state                                  | Make a Count a live region: a tally that updates every few seconds floods the screen reader                              |

title: FactList
markdown:
# FactList

A short list of facts about one thing, each a name and what it is, such as "Operator: Movia" and "Last report: 08:14" about a vehicle, set as a description list in a detail panel or a report.

<!-- run notes -->

The design is deferred (ADR 0010, `docs/adr/0010-unattended-runs-with-design-deferred.md`): this spec decides what the drawing would, from the [contract](README.md), the [foundations](../foundations/README.md), [content design](../content-design.md), the tokens and the specs of its Display siblings, [Stat](stat.md)'s and [Text](text.md)'s.
