FactList has no Base UI component and nothing in `dependsOn`, and the extracted prototype is not reachable from this branch, so nothing here rests on it.

## Anatomy

Penpot page `Components/FactList`. Family: none, since it is static content that sits on its container's surface: it is not one of the Rows family's options, menu items or list rows, which are pressed and take a hover, and it draws no surface of its own. Shared parts: VisuallyHidden, which says an unknown value in words (CR-5).

The drawing will have a `root` board holding one `item` board per fact, each holding two layers, `label` and `value`, and no variant property, so its one variant is `Default` ([Props](#props) and CR-1). There is no `State` property: FactList is not interactive and has only its rest state.

| Part (Penpot layer) | What it is                                                                                                                                                          | Base UI part                          | Class               | `slotProps` key |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- | ------------------- | --------------- |
| `root`              | A `dl` laying the facts out in a grid of two columns, names in the first and values in the second                                                                   | None: `useRender`, a `dl` by default  | `pn-FactList`       | none            |
| `item`              | A `div` holding one fact's name and value, one per entry of `items`, laid on the root's two columns                                                                 | None: `useRender`, a `div` by default | `pn-FactList-item`  | `item`          |
| `label`             | A `dt` holding the fact's name, the item's `label`: "Operator"                                                                                                      | None: `useRender`, a `dt` by default  | `pn-FactList-label` | `label`         |
| `value`             | A `dd` holding what the fact is, the item's `value`: "Movia". With no value it holds "—", hidden from screen readers, and the words "Unknown" for them alone (CR-5) | None: `useRender`, a `dd` by default  | `pn-FactList-value` | `value`         |

No part has a Base UI component, because none has behaviour for Base UI to give: no focus, keys, state or popup. Each part renders through Base UI's `useRender` hook instead, so the root takes `render` and each inner part takes one through its `slotProps` key, as EmptyState's and Stat's parts do.

A `dl` with a `div` around each `dt` and `dd` is HTML's own element for name and value groups, which the contract's "native semantics first" asks for: most screen readers say it is a list and how many facts it holds, and reads each name as a term and each value as its definition. The `div` is the one wrapper HTML allows inside a `dl`, and it is what lets each fact be styled, keyed and given props as one row.

The name comes first in the DOM and on screen, at the start of its row, so the ear hears "Operator, Movia" in the order the eye reads it.

## Base UI parts

No Base UI component: `baseUiParts` stays empty in `packages/perron/components.json`. Each part renders through the `useRender` hook from `@base-ui/react/use-render` and merges its props with `mergeProps` from `@base-ui/react/merge-props`, at the version pinned in `packages/perron/package.json` (1.9.0).

| Base UI part          | Renders | Perron sets                                                                                                                                                                                       | Passed through                                                       |
| --------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `useRender` for root  | `dl`    | `defaultTagName: 'dl'`, `ref`, the class `pn-FactList`, and one item part per entry of `items` as children                                                                                        | `render`, `className`, `style`, `ref` and the rest of the `dl` props |
| `useRender` for item  | `div`   | `defaultTagName: 'div'`, the class `pn-FactList-item`, `data-unknown` when the fact's value is unknown (CR-4), the React `key` from the entry's `key` or its index, and the label and value parts | `slotProps.item`, on every item                                      |
| `useRender` for label | `dt`    | `defaultTagName: 'dt'`, the class `pn-FactList-label`, the entry's `label` as children                                                                                                            | `slotProps.label`, on every label                                    |
| `useRender` for value | `dd`    | `defaultTagName: 'dd'`, the class `pn-FactList-value`, `data-unknown` when unknown (CR-4), the entry's `value` as children, or the "—" and its words when unknown (CR-5)                          | `slotProps.value`, on every value                                    |

Base UI already does: swapping each part's element through `render` while keeping its class and props, joining `className` strings and `style` objects and chaining event handlers in `mergeProps`, and setting `ref` on the rendered element.

## Props

In MUI's layout. Every prop here gets this description as its JSDoc. Slots come last.

| Name              | Type                              | Default      | Base UI prop          | Description                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ----------------- | --------------------------------- | ------------ | --------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `items`           | `ReadonlyArray<FactListItem>`     |              | none                  | The facts, in reading order, each `{ label, value, key }`: `label` names the fact, `value` says what it is, and `key` is its React key when the facts change order. Required              |
| `render`          | Base UI's `render`                |              | inherited             | Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render. |
| `unknownLabel`    | `string`                          | The locale's | none                  | Overrides "Unknown", heard in place of "—" for a fact with no value                                                                                                                       |
| `className`       | `string`                          |              | none                  | Joined after `pn-FactList` on the root                                                                                                                                                    |
| `style`           | `CSSProperties`                   |              | none                  | Reaches the root                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `ref`             | `Ref<HTMLDListElement>`           |              | none                  | Reaches the root element                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `slotProps.item`  | `useRender.ComponentProps<'div'>` |              | `useRender` for item  | Props for every `item` part                                                                                                                                                               |
| `slotProps.label` | `useRender.ComponentProps<'dt'>`  |              | `useRender` for label | Props for every `label` part                                                                                                                                                              |
| `slotProps.value` | `useRender.ComponentProps<'dd'>`  |              | `useRender` for value | Props for every `value` part                                                                                                                                                              |

`FactListItem`, exported from `FactList.tsx` beside `FactListProps`, is `{ label: ReactNode; value?: ReactNode; key?: Key }`, each member with its JSDoc: `label` the fact's name, required; `value` what it is, left out when no data says it; `key` the React key for its row, the entry's index when left out.

`render`, `className`, `style`, `ref` and the other `dl` props, such as `aria-label`, reach the root, as the contract's Root section says; `render` is inherited from `useRender` as it is, with Base UI's JSDoc, and `FactListProps` does not declare it again. `FactListProps` leaves out the `dl`'s `children`: the facts come from `items` alone.

FactList takes its facts as one `items` prop, an array of `{ label, value, key }`, not as children written with a FactListItem component. The contract makes a child the caller writes many times a component of its own folder and registry entry, and `packages/perron/components.json` has one entry, FactList; an array keeps every row's `dt`, `dd` and unknown value FactList's own, so a caller can't put a stray element in the `dl` that breaks its grouping. The item's fields are `label` and `value`, as Chakra's DataList names them, since they are fields of an entry and not props of FactList, so the contract's `value`, a control's state with `defaultValue` and `onChange`, never reaches them; `label` is the name Stat gives its own name. Every name here is one the contract's Names from other libraries table leaves free.

FactList ships one look, with no `variant`, `color` or `size`. Every fact list on Mylder's screens is a short block of names and values in a detail panel or report, so one look keeps them alike; a status colour on a value would say good or bad by colour alone, which [Accessibility](../foundations/accessibility.md) rules out; and a stacked layout, a name over its value, can join later as an optional `variant` without a break.

FactList leaves formatting to the caller, as Stat does: each `value` renders as given, so the caller writes it as content design writes numbers, "32 km/h", "08:14", "≈ 30", in the screen's locale.

## Tokens

One row per part, state and property. FactList has no interactive state, so every row is rest; an unknown value is rest with `data-unknown` on the value.

| Part    | State                | Property               | Token                                                                      |
| ------- | -------------------- | ---------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `root`  | rest                 | `column-gap`           | `space.300`                                                                |
| `root`  | rest                 | `row-gap`              | `space.200`                                                                |
| `item`  | rest                 | `border`               | none: no divider between rows                                              |
| `label` | rest                 | `font`                 | `typography.label-sm`                                                      |
| `label` | rest                 | `letter-spacing`       | `typography.label-sm`, its tracking                                        |
| `label` | rest                 | `color`                | `color.text.secondary`                                                     |
| `value` | rest                 | `font`                 | `typography.label`                                                         |
| `value` | rest                 | `letter-spacing`       | `typography.label`, its tracking                                           |
| `value` | rest                 | `color`                | `color.text.primary`                                                       |
| `value` | rest                 | `font-variant-numeric` | none: the keyword `tabular-nums`, so a figure that updates keeps its width |
| `value` | rest, `data-unknown` | `color`                | `color.text.tertiary`                                                      |

The layout is two aligned columns, every name at the start of its row and every value start-aligned in a second column, with `space.300` between the columns and `space.200` between the rows. The root is a grid with `grid-template-columns: minmax(0, max-content) minmax(0, 1fr)`, keywords and not tokens, and each item spans both columns with `grid-template-columns: subgrid` and `align-items: baseline`, so the names size to the longest, the values line up down one edge whatever their length, and the 12 px name sits on the 13 px value's baseline. A value that wraps then reads as running text, where an end-aligned one would be ragged on its left. 12 px is the measure [Semantic spacing](../foundations/semantic-spacing.md#space) gives a detail panel's parts, set apart here as name and value, and 8 px keeps the rows of one block closer than the panel's parts. Both columns wrap (`overflow-wrap: anywhere`), so a long Danish name or a long value still fits 320 px; the root and every part reset the margins their element brings, the `dd`'s inline indent among them.

The rows are undivided, with no hairline between them. The brand asks for calm, and a few facts spaced `space.200` apart read as rows without lines; the panel around them already has its edge, and a divider is the Rows family's mark for pressable rows. A caller who wants one adds it through `slotProps.item.className`, in `border.width.025` and `color.border.subtle` as the Rows family draws it.

The name is in `typography.label-sm` and `color.text.secondary`, and the value in `typography.label` and `color.text.primary` with tabular figures. `typography.label-sm` is the role for "field and stat labels" and the one Stat names its figure with, so the Display family names things alike; `typography.label` is the role for "names in lists", a value one step stronger than its name, so the eye reads the value first; tabular figures keep a time or speed that updates from shifting, as [Typography](../foundations/typography.md#roles) asks for anything compared.

## Keyboard and ARIA

FactList has no keys of its own and is never focusable. A value the caller makes a link or button brings that element's own keys, in reading order.

| Key  | Does                                  | From   |
| ---- | ------------------------------------- | ------ |
| None | FactList is not focusable or operable | Perron |

| Element                            | Role                                                 | Accessible name from                                         | States announced                                      |
| ---------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `root`                             | None in ARIA: the browser exposes a description list | Not named, or the caller's `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` | None; most screen readers say how many facts it holds |
| `item`                             | None (generic `div`)                                 | Not named; its name and value are read in place, name first  | None                                                  |
| `label`                            | `term`, from the `dt`                                | Its text, from the item's `label`                            | None                                                  |
| `value`                            | `definition`, from the `dd`                          | Its text, from the item's `value`                            | None                                                  |
| The "—" in `value`, when unknown   | Hidden: `aria-hidden="true"`                         | Not read                                                     | None                                                  |
| The words in `value`, when unknown | Text, in VisuallyHidden                              | The owned string "Unknown", or `unknownLabel`                | None                                                  |

What axe won't catch, from the contract, each with how this component meets it:

- [ ] Everything the eye is told, the ear is told, for every shape each prop accepts: each name and value is read as shown, name first; "—" is `aria-hidden` and the ear hears "Unknown" in its place (CR-5). No colour carries meaning: values are `color.text.primary`, and tertiary only for the "—" the words speak for.
- [ ] Every landmark and named region has an accessible name: none here; the `dl` is a list, not a landmark or region, and a caller who names it gives `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` on the root.
- [ ] Every default label can be overridden: `unknownLabel`.
- [ ] Every shape the type accepts renders, in every variant: `label` and `value` are `ReactNode`s; a string, a number, an element and a list each render, `0` is a value and not unknown (CR-4), an empty `items` renders an empty `dl` (CR-8), and `FactList.test.tsx` renders each shape. The `Default` story gives string names and values.
- [ ] A hidden copy kept for animation is `aria-hidden`, and a collapsed region is `inert`: none here; nothing animates or collapses. The "—" is `aria-hidden` because the words speak for it, not for animation.
- [ ] Native semantics first: `dl`, `div`, `dt` and `dd`, HTML's description list, with no role and no ARIA beyond `aria-hidden` on the "—".
- [ ] Focus moves in reading order and returns on close: FactList takes no focus and opens nothing; focusable values, such as links, come in the order of `items`.
- [ ] Every target is at least `size.target-min` square: no target of its own; a link a caller puts in a value is the caller's to size.
- [ ] Loops stop when the system asks for less motion: none here; FactList has no motion.

## Owned strings

Every word FactList shows comes from the caller, through each item's `label` and `value`, but for the one it announces for a fact with no value.

| Key       | English   | Override       | Seen or heard where                                                               |
| --------- | --------- | -------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `unknown` | "Unknown" | `unknownLabel` | `value`, heard in place of the `aria-hidden` "—" when an item has no value (CR-5) |

A fact with no value shows "—" and says "Unknown", reusing Stat's `unknown` key. Content design writes "—" for unknown and the brand never shows a guess, while a screen reader skips or spells a bare "—", so the ear would hear a name with nothing after it; Stat and Delay do the same, and one word across the Display family keeps every screen agreeing. `unknown`, "Unknown", is the key Stat added to `packages/perron/src/locale/en.ts`, with Danish "Ukendt", Swedish "Okänd" and Norwegian Bokmål "Ukjent"; its JSDoc, which names Stat alone, widens to name any figure or value no data gives.

## Component rules

Rules for this component alone, numbered so the build and the review can cite them.

- **CR-1.** FactList has one look: no `variant`, `color` or `size` prop and no `data-variant`, `data-color` or `data-size` attribute, as [Props](#props) sets out.
- **CR-2.** FactList renders one item part per entry of `items`, in the array's order, each holding its label part then its value part, and nothing else inside the `dl`, so the description list stays valid.
- **CR-3.** FactList doesn't format a value: each `value` renders as given, a number as React writes it.
- **CR-4.** A value is unknown when it renders nothing (`null`, `undefined`, a boolean, `''`, or an array of only such values) or is a number that is not finite (`NaN`, `Infinity`). `0` and `'0'` are values. When unknown, the item and the value part both carry the bare attribute `data-unknown`: the CSS reads the "—" colour from the value's, as `.pn-FactList-value[data-unknown]`, one class then an attribute, so a caller restyles it through `slotProps.value.className`, selected with `[data-unknown]` as FactList's is; the item's lets a caller style the whole row.
- **CR-5.** FactList shows an unknown value itself, as "—" in `color.text.tertiary` with `aria-hidden="true"`, followed by the owned string "Unknown" in the VisuallyHidden shared part, as Stat does. The "—" is the character U+2014 in its own `span`, and the words are their own text run, so `expectOwnedStrings` reads them as a dictionary value. Tertiary is allowed because the "—" always sits beside its name.
- **CR-6.** FactList composes the VisuallyHidden shared part from `packages/perron/src/parts/VisuallyHidden/` and never draws its own hiding styles.
- **CR-7.** Each inner part's props are its `slotProps` value merged with `mergeProps`, the component's own props last, so its class, `data-unknown` and children stay while the caller's `className` joins and its `render` swaps the element. One `slotProps` value reaches every item, label or value alike; a caller's `id` there would repeat, so FactList's docs say to give none.
- **CR-8.** An empty `items` renders an empty `dl`. Every shape the type accepts renders, the `ref` and `className` still land, and a list with no facts is the caller's to replace with EmptyState, as [Do and don't](#do-and-dont) says; returning nothing would leave a `ref` that is sometimes `null`.
- **CR-9.** `items`, `unknownLabel`, `slotProps` and `render` are taken out of the rest props before they reach the root, so none reaches the DOM as an attribute.
- **CR-10.** FactList is not a live region and never moves focus. A screen that updates its facts announces changes of state in its own polite live region, as [Accessibility](../foundations/accessibility.md) asks.
- **CR-11.** FactList fills its container's width, as a block, and its columns size as [Tokens](#tokens) sets out, with logical properties only, so the name stays at the start of its row in right-to-left text.

## Stories

One per variant the deferred design will draw. It has no variant property, so its one variant is `Default`; `Unknown` is the same variant with one fact that has no value, and proves CR-4 and CR-5. The contract story renders `Default`.

| Story     | Shows                                                                                                                                                                     | `play` test                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Default` | Four facts about a bus: "Operator" "Movia", "Vehicle" "8412", "Speed" "32 km/h", "Last report" "08:14"; the contract story renders it, and its args pass every rule alone | The root is a `dl` with four `div` items, each a `dt` then a `dd`; each name comes before its value in the accessible text; no item has `data-unknown`; a value's computed `font-variant-numeric` is `tabular-nums`; nothing takes focus; an empty FactList beside it takes its `ref` and `className` on an empty `dl` (CR-8) |
| `Unknown` | "Operator" "Movia", "Speed" with no value, "Last report" "08:14": "—" beside "Speed"                                                                                      | The "Speed" item and its value carry `data-unknown` and the others don't; "—" is `aria-hidden`; the accessible text of that item is "Speed" then "Unknown"; nothing takes focus; in `en`, `da`, `sv` and `nb` every word it shows is the caller's or an owned string                                                          |

## Do and don't

For a caller using the component, with the reason.

| Do                                                                                                                | Don't                                                                                                                        |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Leave out an item's `value` when no data gives it, so FactList shows "—" and says "Unknown"                       | Write "0", "n/a" or a guess for a value nobody knows: the brand never claims more than the data knows                        |
| Name each fact in a word or two, "Operator", "Last report", and write its value as content design does, "32 km/h" | Put the name inside the value, such as "Speed 32 km/h": the name and value then read as one term with no definition          |
| Use FactList for several facts about one thing, such as a vehicle in its detail panel                             | Use it for one key figure, which is a Stat, or for rows people compare across many things, which is a table                  |
| Name the list with `aria-labelledby` pointing at the panel's heading when the panel holds more than one list      | Give the list a heading inside `items`: every entry is a fact, a name and its value                                          |
| Say a status in words in the value, or show it with a SeverityLabel or a Delay                                    | Colour a value through `className` to say it is good or bad: colour alone tells no screen reader and no colour-blind person  |
| Show EmptyState in place of FactList when there are no facts to show                                              | Render FactList with an empty `items` and nothing beside it: an empty list tells the person nothing                          |
| Keep `render` on the root to another `dl`, or a component that renders one                                        | Swap the root for a `ul` or `div` through `render`: its `dt` and `dd` would sit outside a `dl`, which HTML and axe both fail |
| Announce a changed fact in the screen's own polite live region, when it changes state                             | Make FactList a live region: a speed or report time that updates every few seconds floods the screen reader                  |

title: Kbd
markdown:
# Kbd

Kbd shows one key of the keyboard, such as "Esc", "+" or "↑", inside help text, so a sentence like "Keys: + and − zoom, arrows pan, Esc closes panels." shows each key as a key.

## Anatomy

Penpot page `Components/Kbd`. Family: none. Shared parts: none.

The design is deferred (ADR 0010, `docs/adr/0010-unattended-runs-with-design-deferred.md`), so this spec sets what the drawing will have: one board, `root`, holding the key's text; no variant property, so the design has one variant, `Default`; and no `State` property, since a key in help text is never interactive (CR-2) and has only its rest state.

| Part (Penpot layer) | What it is                                                                                                                                                                                                       | Base UI part                                 | Class    | `slotProps` key |
| ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | -------- | --------------- |
| `root`              | The key: a small bordered box on the line of the text around it, holding the key's name or glyph from the caller's `children`. The text is the root's own, with no element, class or `slotProps` key of its own. | none: a `<kbd>` rendered through `useRender` | `pn-Kbd` | none            |

## Base UI parts

No Base UI component: `baseUiParts` is empty in `packages/perron/components.json`, and a key in help text has no behaviour to borrow. The root renders through Base UI's `useRender` hook, from `@base-ui/react/use-render` at the version pinned in `packages/perron/package.json`, so the contract's `render` prop works, and the component's props are merged with `mergeProps` from `@base-ui/react/merge-props`, as LineBadge and Text do.

| Base UI part | Renders | Perron sets                                                                                                             | Passed through                                                                      |
| ------------ | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `useRender`  | `<kbd>` | `defaultTagName: 'kbd'`; `ref`; `props`: `mergeProps(rest, own)`, where `own` is `className: 'pn-Kbd'` and nothing else | `render`, `ref`, `children`, `className`, `style` and every other `<kbd>` attribute |

Base UI already does: swapping the root element for the `render` element or function while keeping Perron's class and `ref`, merging the caller's `ref` with the element's under React 19, and joining `className` strings, merging `style` objects and chaining event handlers in `mergeProps`. Kbd adds no behaviour of its own.

## Props

In MUI's layout. Every prop here gets this description as its JSDoc. No slots: the key has no inner part.

| Name        | Type               | Default | Base UI prop | Description                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ----------- | ------------------ | ------- | ------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `children`  | `ReactNode`        | none    | none         | One key, as the keyboard prints it or the platform names it: "Esc", "Enter", "+", "−", "↑". Required: a key with no name says nothing. A combination is one Kbd per key (CR-5).           |
| `render`    | Base UI's `render` |         | inherited    | Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render. |
| `className` | `string`           |         | none         | Joined after `pn-Kbd` on the root                                                                                                                                                         |
| `style`     | `CSSProperties`    |         | none         | Reaches the root                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `ref`       | `Ref<HTMLElement>` |         | none         | Reaches the root element                                                                                                                                                                  |

`KbdProps` extends `useRender.ComponentProps<'kbd'>` without its `children`, which it declares again as required, as LineBadge's props do; `render` is inherited from `useRender` as it is, with Base UI's JSDoc, and `KbdProps` does not declare it. `className`, `style`, `ref` and the other `<kbd>` attributes reach the root, as the contract's [Root](README.md#root) says. No `*Label` props: Kbd owns no strings.

Kbd ships one look, with no `variant`, `color` or `size`: every key in Mylder's help sits in a sentence of `typography.body` or `typography.caption`, and one look sized to fit both keeps every hint alike; a key carries no meaning a colour could add, and the props API only grows, so a `size` can join when a screen needs one.

`children` is required, with no default: an empty key draws a box that names nothing, and the contract's "everything the eye is told, the ear is told" needs a name in every key; LineBadge requires its `children` for the same reason.

## Tokens

One row per part, state and property. Kbd has one part, `root`, and one design state, rest: it is never interactive (CR-2). Every colour is one of the tokens [Semantic colours](../foundations/semantic-colours.md) gives for both themes, so the key needs no rule for the dark theme.

| Part   | State                | Property         | Token                                                                                                                                |
| ------ | -------------------- | ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `root` | rest                 | `background`     | `color.surface.raised`                                                                                                               |
| `root` | rest                 | `border`         | `border.width.025` solid in `color.border.strong`                                                                                    |
| `root` | rest                 | `border-radius`  | `radius.xs`                                                                                                                          |
| `root` | rest                 | `color`          | `color.text.primary`                                                                                                                 |
| `root` | rest                 | `font`           | `typography.data-sm`                                                                                                                 |
| `root` | rest                 | `line-height`    | `font.line-height.tight`, in place of the role's own, so the key is short enough to leave room between the keys of two wrapped lines |
| `root` | rest                 | `letter-spacing` | `typography.data-sm-tracking`, the role's twin                                                                                       |
| `root` | rest                 | `padding-inline` | `space.100`                                                                                                                          |
| `root` | rest                 | `padding-block`  | none: `0`, so the key is one line of its text and its border tall                                                                    |
| `root` | rest                 | `margin-block`   | `calc(-1 * border.width.025)`, so the border paints outside the line's layout and only the key's 1lh counts toward the line          |
| `root` | rest, forced colours | `border`         | none: the same border, which Windows' contrast themes paint in the text colour, so the key keeps its edge when the fill is dropped   |

The key is a `color.surface.raised` box with a `border.width.025` solid edge in `color.border.strong`, `radius.xs` corners and `color.text.primary` text. The raised fill and solid edge read as a key on every surface the help sits on, panel, glass or card, and set it apart from its Display neighbours: a count is an inset pill and a tag a dashed one. `color.border.strong` is the token for lines that decorate rather than show a control, which a key in text is, so its edge needs no 3:1 and doesn't look pressable the way `color.border.control` would; `radius.xs` is the radius for small marks, a step under a line badge's `radius.sm`; `color.text.primary` reaches 17.92:1 on `color.surface.raised` in light and 13.45:1 in dark ([Accessibility](../foundations/accessibility.md#text-on-surfaces)).

The key's text is in `typography.data-sm`, JetBrains Mono at 11 px and 500, set at `font.line-height.tight`, 1.15, in place of the role's 1.3: a monospace face is how keys are printed in help, and Perron's one monospace face is `font.family.data`, reached only through a `data` role. At 11 px the key sits a step under `typography.caption` (12 px) and three under `typography.body` (14 px), the two roles help text takes, so a key reads as a mark in the sentence and not as a word of it; the tight line height suits a key, which is one line with nothing under it to clear, and still holds the caps and the descenders inside the border.

The face Perron ships, the latin subset of JetBrains Mono that `packages/perron/styles/fonts.css` loads, carries "+", "−", "↑" and "↓", but not "←" or "→" (U+2190 and U+2192): in a Kbd those two fall back to the system's monospace, smaller, heavier and lower than the other keys. So help text names the arrows in words, "arrows pan", as [content design](../content-design.md) writes it, and a Kbd holds "↑" or "↓" but never "←" or "→".

The key takes `space.100` either side of its text and no padding above or below. Every character of a monospace face is as wide, so a one-character key such as "+" is a little wider than it is tall from that padding alone, and needs no minimum width. With no padding above or below, the key is 1lh of its text, 12.65 px, and its border, 14.65 px in all. A margin of minus the border's width above and below takes the border out of the line's layout, so the line counts only the key's 12.65 px: inside the 18 px line of `typography.caption` and the 21 px line of `typography.body` wherever the baseline places it, so a key never pushes its line apart (CR-3). The border still paints, in the line's half-leading. When a caption wraps and puts one key under another, the two boxes stand more than 3 px apart, so their edges read as two keys and not as one doubled line. `space.100`, 4 px, is the step that keeps "Esc" compact.

## Keyboard and ARIA

No keys: Kbd is not focusable and does nothing when pressed (CR-2). It names a key; the key's action is the screen's, and the control the key works is the caller's to mark with `aria-keyshortcuts`, as [Accessibility](../foundations/accessibility.md#rules) gives the keys.

| Key  | Does                             | From   |
| ---- | -------------------------------- | ------ |
| None | Kbd is not focusable or operable | Perron |

| Element | Role                                                            | Accessible name from              | States announced |
| ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------- | ---------------- |
| `root`  | none: a `<kbd>`, which has no ARIA role and is read as its text | Its text, the caller's `children` | none             |

A screen reader reads the key's text in the sentence around it, as written: "Esc", "plus", "minus", "up arrow" for "Esc", "+", "−", "↑". Kbd adds no `aria-label` and no owned word for the key: the caller's text is already the key's name, and a `<kbd>` without a role can't carry `aria-label` reliably.

What axe won't catch, from the contract, each with how this component meets it:

- [ ] Everything the eye is told, the ear is told, for every shape each prop accepts: the box only says "this is a key"; the key itself is the text inside it, which a screen reader reads in place, and `children` is required.
- [ ] Every landmark and named region has an accessible name: none here; the key is inline text.
- [ ] Every default label can be overridden: no owned strings, so no `*Label` props.
- [ ] Every shape the type accepts renders, in every variant: `children` renders as a string, an element and a list alike, on one line inside the box; `Kbd.test.tsx` checks all three, each inside the one `<kbd>` with `pn-Kbd` first.
- [ ] A hidden copy kept for animation is `aria-hidden`, and a collapsed region is `inert`: none here; the key has no motion.
- [ ] Native semantics first: the native `<kbd>`, with no ARIA.
- [ ] Focus moves in reading order and returns on close: never focused; it has no tab stop.
- [ ] Every target is at least `size.target-min` square: no target; Kbd is never pressed. A pressable key hint is the caller's button with the Kbd inside it, which meets the minimum itself.
- [ ] Loops stop when the system asks for less motion: none here; the key has no motion.

## Owned strings

No owned strings: the key's name is the caller's `children`, and Kbd announces nothing else.

## Component rules

- **CR-1.** The root is the native `<kbd>`, rendered through `useRender` with `defaultTagName: 'kbd'`, with `pn-Kbd` first in its `className` and the caller's after. It sets no role and no ARIA attribute, and no data attribute, since it has no `variant`, `color` or `size` prop.
- **CR-2.** The key is never interactive: no hover, focus, pressed or selected look, no tab stop, no role. A key hint the rider can press is a Perron button with the Kbd inside it.
- **CR-3.** The key sits on the line of the text around it and never breaks it: `display: inline-block`, `vertical-align: baseline`, so its text shares the sentence's baseline; `white-space: nowrap`, so it never wraps or truncates; `text-align: center`, so its text centres in its box. `margin-block: calc(-1 * border.width.025)`, so the border paints outside the line's layout and only the key's 1lh of `typography.data-sm` at `font.line-height.tight` counts toward the line. In `typography.body` and `typography.caption` text it is shorter than the line, by enough that the keys of two wrapped lines stand apart, so the lines around it keep their spacing and two keys never touch.
- **CR-4.** The CSS reads only the component layer's [token families](README.md#token-families), with no `opacity`, no `text-transform` and no `[data-theme]` selector: the key shows its text as the caller wrote it, "Esc" and not "ESC", in both themes through the semantic tokens.
- **CR-5.** One Kbd holds one key: a combination is written as one Kbd per key with the "+" between them in the caller's text, with no `keys` prop, no separator and no nested `<kbd>`. Mylder's keys are single, "+", "−", the arrows and Esc, as [Accessibility](../foundations/accessibility.md#rules) lists them; a separator Kbd drew itself would be an owned string with nothing to say in four languages; and the caller writing `<Kbd>Ctrl</Kbd> + <Kbd>K</Kbd>` reads to a screen reader as the sentence says it.

## Stories

One per variant the deferred design will draw. Kbd has no variant property, so its one variant is `Default`; `SingleCharacter` and `InHelpText` are the same variant with other text, and prove CR-3. Each `play` test reads the DOM and the accessibility tree, not the pixels.

| Story             | Shows                                                                                                                                                                | `play` test                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Default`         | The key "Esc"; the contract story renders it as the subject, and its args pass every rule alone                                                                      | The root is a `<kbd>` with `pn-Kbd`, no role, no ARIA attribute and no `data-*`; its accessible text is "Esc"; it has no `tabindex`, and nothing in it takes focus                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `SingleCharacter` | The key "+"                                                                                                                                                          | The root is at least as wide as it is tall, and its text is "+"                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `InHelpText`      | A Text in `variant='caption'` reading "Keys: + and − zoom, arrows pan, Esc closes panels.", with "+", "−" and "Esc" each a Kbd, in a column narrow enough to wrap it | The paragraph's accessible text is the whole sentence, in order; each Kbd's height is no more than the paragraph's computed line height; a Kbd on a wrapped line stands apart from a Kbd on the line above by more than both their borders; the paragraph is no taller than a copy of it in the same column with each Kbd swapped for an inline-block stand-in of the same text and width, so both wrap at the same words; each Kbd's text stays on one line; no Kbd overflows the column |

## Do and don't

For a caller using the component, with the reason.

| Do                                                                                                                         | Don't                                                                                                                                            |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Name keys in help text, one Kbd per key, as content design writes it: "Keys: + and − zoom, arrows pan, Esc closes panels." | Write a key as a quoted word, "press 'Esc'", where a Kbd says it is a key                                                                        |
| Write the key as the keyboard prints it or the platform names it, in its own case: "Esc", "Enter", "−", "↑"                | Write it in capitals ("ESC"), as an emoji, or as an icon; the key's text is what a screen reader hears                                           |
| Name the left and right arrows in words, or all four as "arrows", as content design writes it: "arrows pan"                | Put "←" or "→" in a Kbd; the font Perron ships has no glyph for them, so they fall back to the system's monospace and look unlike the other keys |
| Give a combination one Kbd per key, with "+" between them in the text: `<Kbd>Ctrl</Kbd> + <Kbd>K</Kbd>`                    | Put a whole combination or a sentence in one Kbd; the box is sized for one key                                                                   |
| Mark the control a key works with `aria-keyshortcuts`, and keep the action reachable by pressing the control too           | Make the Kbd the only way to learn or do the action, or add `onClick` or `tabIndex` to it                                                        |
| Show key hints where people have a keyboard, such as the help on a desktop screen                                          | Show keys on a phone's screen, which has no keyboard to press them on                                                                            |

title: Meter
markdown:
# Meter

A bar that shows where one measured value sits within a known range, with the words that name it and the figure it reaches, such as "Reporting live" at "82%", for the share of a network's vehicles that report their position.

<!-- run notes -->

The design is deferred (ADR 0010, `docs/adr/0010-unattended-runs-with-design-deferred.md`): there is no read-back, code map or export, and this spec decides what the drawing would, from the [contract](README.md), the [foundations](../foundations/README.md), [content design](../content-design.md), the tokens and the Base UI reference for `@base-ui/react` 1.9.0. Meter has nothing in `dependsOn`, and the extracted prototype is not reachable from this branch, so nothing here rests on it. The [Semantic colours](../foundations/semantic-colours.md#status) page gives the one meter Mylder already names, the live share, its thresholds, and [Motion](../foundations/motion.md) gives meters their fill change.

## Anatomy

Penpot page `Components/Meter`. Family: none, since it is a static display that sits on its container's surface and joins no family's treatment: it is not pressed, takes no hover and is not one of the Rows, Fields, Popups, Panels or Tooltips. Shared parts: none; the words for an unknown value reach the ear through `aria-valuetext`, not through VisuallyHidden (CR-5).

The drawing will have a `root` board holding three layers, `label`, `value` and `track`, with `indicator` inside `track`, and one variant property, `color`, whose values name its variants `Neutral`, `Success`, `Warning`, `Danger` and `Info` (`penpot/README.md`, "Conventions"). There is no `State` property: Meter is not interactive and has only its rest state.

| Part (Penpot layer) | What it is                                                                                                                                                                               | Base UI part      | Class                | `slotProps` key |
| ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------- | -------------------- | --------------- |
| `root`              | A `div` with `role="meter"`, a two-column grid: the label and the figure on the first row, the track across both columns on the second                                                   | `Meter.Root`      | `pn-Meter`           | none            |
| `label`             | A `span` holding the caller's `label`, what the meter measures, such as "Reporting live"; the meter's accessible name                                                                    | `Meter.Label`     | `pn-Meter-label`     | `label`         |
| `value`             | A `span` at the inline end of the first row holding the figure Base UI formats, "82%", or "—" when the value is unknown (CR-5); `aria-hidden`, since the root's `aria-valuetext` says it | `Meter.Value`     | `pn-Meter-value`     | `value`         |
| `track`             | A `div` across the second row: the whole range, from `min` to `max`, in an inset pill                                                                                                    | `Meter.Track`     | `pn-Meter-track`     | `track`         |
| `indicator`         | A `div` inside `track`, from its inline start: the share of the range the value reaches, its width set by Base UI as a percentage, in the colour of the meter's `color`                  | `Meter.Indicator` | `pn-Meter-indicator` | `indicator`     |

Every part has its Base UI part, so each one's props come through its `slotProps` key and the root takes the component's own. Base UI's root also appends a `span` with `role="presentation"`, its own `visuallyHidden` style (`position: fixed`, `clip-path: inset(50%)`) and the text "x" after its children. It is no part of Perron's: it has no class, no layer and no `slotProps` key, and its fixed position takes it out of the grid (CR-9).

The label comes first in the DOM and on screen, then the figure, then the track: the eye reads the name before the number, as Stat does, and the screen reader hears the root's name and `aria-valuetext` whatever the order, since Base UI hides the figure from it. Chromium still exposes Base UI's visually hidden "x" `span` as text inside the meter (Playwright reads `meter "Reporting live": Reporting live x`); Meter keeps Base UI's root as it is (CR-1) until the maintainer decides, and no screen reader has yet confirmed whether the "x" is heard.

## Base UI parts

Imported from `@base-ui/react/meter`, at the version pinned in `packages/perron/package.json` (1.9.0 installed).

| Base UI part      | Renders                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | Perron sets                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | Passed through                                                                                                                        |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Meter.Root`      | `<div role="meter">` with `aria-valuenow` (the value clamped to `min` and `max`), `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax`, `aria-valuetext` (the formatted value, or what `getAriaValueText` returns) and `aria-labelledby` the label's `id`; its children, then the hidden "x" `span` | `className` (`pn-Meter`, then the caller's), `ref`, `data-color`, `data-unknown` when the value is unknown, `value` (`min` when unknown), `locale` (the PerronProvider's when the caller gives none), `aria-valuetext` (the owned "Unknown" when unknown), and the four parts below | `min`, `max`, `format`, `getAriaValueText`, `aria-valuetext` (while the value is known), `render`, `style` and every other `div` prop |
| `Meter.Label`     | `<span role="presentation">` with an `id` (the caller's, or one Base UI generates) that it registers as the root's `aria-labelledby`                                                                                                                                            | `className` (`pn-Meter-label`, then the caller's), `label` as children                                                                                                                                                                                                              | `slotProps.label`, merged with `mergeProps`, the component's own props last                                                           |
| `Meter.Value`     | `<span aria-hidden="true">` holding the formatted value, or what a function `children` returns from `(formattedValue, value)`                                                                                                                                                   | `className` (`pn-Meter-value`, then the caller's), `data-unknown` when unknown, and "—" when unknown, from a function `children` (CR-5)                                                                                                                                             | `slotProps.value`, merged the same way; its function `children` formats the figure while the value is known                           |
| `Meter.Track`     | `<div>`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | `className` (`pn-Meter-track`, then the caller's), and the indicator as children                                                                                                                                                                                                    | `slotProps.track`, merged the same way                                                                                                |
| `Meter.Indicator` | `<div>` with an inline `style` of `inset-inline-start: 0`, `height: inherit` and `width` the value's percentage of the range, clamped to 0 to 100%                                                                                                                              | `className` (`pn-Meter-indicator`, then the caller's)                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | `slotProps.indicator`, merged the same way                                                                                            |

Base UI already does: the `meter` role and its four `aria-value*` attributes; clamping the value to `min` and `max` for `aria-valuenow`, the figure and the fill, with `NaN` taken as `min` and `Infinity` as `max`; formatting the figure with `Intl.NumberFormat`, by default as the percentage of the range the value reaches (`value` 1046 of `max` 1204 reads "87%"), or with the caller's `format` options applied to the clamped value; keeping the shown figure and `aria-valuetext` the same text, unless `getAriaValueText` or `aria-valuetext` gives the ear a fuller one; naming the root by the label through a generated `id`; hiding the figure from screen readers, since `aria-valuetext` says it; and sizing the indicator as a percentage of the track.

## Props

In MUI's layout. Every prop Meter declares gets this description as its JSDoc; the inherited ones keep Base UI's. Slots come last, and `slotProps` itself says "Props for each inner part, merged with the part's own, which win", as Stat's does.

| Name                  | Type                                                        | Default                     | Base UI prop                        | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| --------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------- | ----------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `label`               | `ReactNode`                                                 |                             | none: the children of `Meter.Label` | What the meter measures, in a few words, such as "Reporting live": shown above the track, and the meter's accessible name. Required                                                                                                                     |
| `value`               | `number \| null`                                            |                             | `value`                             | Required. The measured value, between `min` and `max`; one outside them is shown at the nearest end. `null`, or a number that is not finite, when no data gives it: Meter then shows "—" over an empty track and says "Unknown" (CR-5)                  |
| `min`                 | `number`                                                    | `0`                         | inherited                           | The minimum value                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `max`                 | `number`                                                    | `100`                       | inherited                           | The maximum value                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `color`               | `'neutral' \| 'success' \| 'warning' \| 'danger' \| 'info'` | `'neutral'`                 | none                                | The intent: what the fill means. `neutral` is a plain measure in ink; the status intents tint the fill for a value that is good or bad news, such as the live share's. Always beside words that say what the value means: colour is never the only sign |
| `format`              | `Intl.NumberFormatOptions`                                  |                             | inherited                           | Options to format the value.                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `locale`              | `Intl.LocalesArgument`                                      | The PerronProvider's locale | `locale`                            | The locale `Intl.NumberFormat` formats the figure in: "82%" in English, "82 %" in Danish, Swedish and Norwegian. Left out, the nearest PerronProvider's                                                                                                 |
| `getAriaValueText`    | `(formattedValue: string, value: number) => string`         |                             | inherited                           | A function that returns a string value that provides a human-readable text alternative for `aria-valuenow`, the current value of the meter.                                                                                                             |
| `aria-valuetext`      | `string`                                                    |                             | inherited                           | A string value that provides a user-friendly name for `aria-valuenow`, the current value of the meter.                                                                                                                                                  |
| `render`              | Base UI's `render`                                          |                             | inherited                           | Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render.                                                               |
| `unknownLabel`        | `string`                                                    | The locale's                | none                                | Overrides "Unknown", heard in place of the figure when the value is unknown                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `className`           | `string`                                                    |                             | none                                | Joined after `pn-Meter` on the root                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `style`               | `CSSProperties`                                             |                             | none                                | Reaches the root                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `ref`                 | `Ref<HTMLDivElement>`                                       |                             | none                                | Reaches the root element                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `slotProps.label`     | `Meter.Label.Props`                                         |                             | `Meter.Label`                       | Props for the `label` part                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `slotProps.value`     | `Meter.Value.Props`                                         |                             | `Meter.Value`                       | Props for the `value` part. Its function `children` writes the figure from `(formattedValue, value)` while the value is known                                                                                                                           |
| `slotProps.track`     | `Meter.Track.Props`                                         |                             | `Meter.Track`                       | Props for the `track` part                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `slotProps.indicator` | `Meter.Indicator.Props`                                     |                             | `Meter.Indicator`                   | Props for the `indicator` part                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |

`MeterProps` extends `Meter.Root.Props` without `children` and the members it declares again, and declares `label`, `value`, `color`, `locale`, `unknownLabel`, React's `className`, `style` and `ref`, and `slotProps`; `min`, `max`, `format`, `getAriaValueText`, `aria-valuetext` and `render` are inherited as they are, with Base UI's JSDoc and `@default`. Meter takes no `children`: its content is its four parts, and a caller's children would land after the track inside the `meter` role, where a screen reader never reads them.

`label` is required: it is the meter's accessible name, a `meter` with no name fails axe's `aria-meter-name`, and Stat's `label` is required for the same reason.

`value` is the measured value of a display, not a control's: Meter has no `defaultValue` and no `onChange`, since nothing the person does changes it. It keeps Base UI's name, as MUI's `LinearProgress` does, rather than Stat's `children`, because it is a number Meter draws and formats, not text the caller writes.

`value` can be unknown: it is `number | null`, and `null` or a number that is not finite is unknown: Meter passes `min` to Base UI, so the fill is empty, shows "—" in place of the figure and sets `aria-valuetext` to the owned "Unknown" (CR-5). Base UI takes `NaN` as `min` and `Infinity` as `max` and would show "0%" or "100%", a figure no data gave, where the brand says no more than the data knows; Stat, Count and FactList show an unknown the same way.

Meter takes a `color` prop, with the intents the contract gives meters a mark for, and leaves the choice to the caller: `'neutral' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'danger' | 'info'`, default `'neutral'`, as Count offers, and no thresholds of its own: the live share's 70% and 40% are one measure's, which the screen that shows the live share maps to `success`, `warning` and `danger`, while another meter's good and bad lie elsewhere or nowhere. `brand` has no mark, so Meter doesn't offer it.

Meter formats the figure in the PerronProvider's locale when the caller gives no `locale`, through a `useLocale()` hook added beside `useOwnedStrings` in `packages/perron/src/PerronProvider.tsx` and left out of the barrel: Base UI's own default, the runtime locale, shows "82%" on a Danish screen in an English browser and can differ between the server's render and the browser's, while Perron's locales `en`, `da`, `sv` and `nb` are each a tag `Intl.NumberFormat` takes. A caller's `locale` still wins.

Meter has no `size` and no `variant`: one track height and one layout serve a report, a panel and the kiosk, and either can join later as an optional prop without a break. The figure is always shown; a caller that wants other words in it, such as "1 046 of 1 204", writes them through `slotProps.value.children` and says the same to the ear through `getAriaValueText`.

## Tokens

One row per part, state and property. Meter has one design state, rest: it is never interactive. The unknown value is rest with `data-unknown` on the root and the value.

| Part        | State                           | Property           | Token                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| ----------- | ------------------------------- | ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `root`      | rest                            | `column-gap`       | `space.200`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `root`      | rest                            | `row-gap`          | `space.100`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `label`     | rest                            | `font`             | `typography.label-sm`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `label`     | rest                            | `letter-spacing`   | `typography.label-sm`, its tracking                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `label`     | rest                            | `color`            | `color.text.secondary`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `label`     | rest                            | `overflow-wrap`    | none: the keyword `anywhere`, so a long Danish word breaks inside its column (CR-7)                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `value`     | rest                            | `font`             | `typography.data`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `value`     | rest                            | `letter-spacing`   | `typography.data`, its tracking                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `value`     | rest                            | `color`            | `color.text.primary`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `value`     | rest                            | `white-space`      | none: the keyword `nowrap`, so "82 %" never breaks from its sign                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `value`     | rest, `data-unknown`            | `color`            | `color.text.tertiary`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `track`     | rest                            | `background-color` | `color.surface.inset`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `track`     | rest                            | `block-size`       | `size.meter-track`, a new base token of `6px`, "Height of a meter's track", added through the `design-tokens` skill and listed in the size marker on [Layout](../foundations/layout.md); 6 px reads as a bar under 12 px text without outweighing it, and no `size.*` token holds a bar's height. |
| `track`     | rest                            | `border-radius`    | `radius.full`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `track`     | rest                            | `overflow`         | none: the keyword `hidden`, so the fill keeps inside the pill's ends                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `track`     | rest, `(forced-colors: active)` | `outline`          | `border.width.025`, `solid` in the system colour `CanvasText` (CR-8)                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `indicator` | rest, `color` neutral           | `background-color` | `color.text.primary`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `indicator` | rest, `color` success           | `background-color` | `color.status.success`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `indicator` | rest, `color` warning           | `background-color` | `color.status.warning`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `indicator` | rest, `color` danger            | `background-color` | `color.status.danger`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `indicator` | rest, `color` info              | `background-color` | `color.status.info`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
