## Component rules

Rules for this component alone, numbered so the build and the review can cite them.

- **CR-1.** The root always carries `data-color` with the `color` value, default included, written in Alert's own props after the caller's so it cannot be overwritten, and the CSS reads every colour from it: `.pn-Alert[data-color='danger']`. The text colour is set once, on the root; the icon part sets its own `color` and the icon takes it through `currentColor`, as [Icons](../foundations/icons.md#style) asks.
- **CR-2.** A status `color` comes with words that say it, such as "Could not load departures" on `danger`. Alert can't hold this for the caller, so the JSDoc of `color` says it and the review holds the stories to it.
- **CR-3.** The optional parts render only when given: no `title` part without `title`, no `description` part without `children`, no `action` part without `action`, no `close` part without `onClose`. The `icon` part renders the caller's `icon` when it is given, the intent's icon when `icon` is left out (`undefined`), and nothing when `icon` renders nothing (`null`, `false`, `''`, or an array of only such values) or when `color` is `neutral` and `icon` is left out, so no empty wrapper takes up a gap.
- **CR-4.** The intent's icon is drawn by the `IntentIcon` shared part, never in Alert's own folder, and is the icon file's own drawing, inlined as JSX: the file's `viewBox`, `fill`, `stroke`, `stroke-width`, `stroke-linecap` and `stroke-linejoin` and its child elements, unchanged, with no `width` or `height`, the class `perron-icon`, `aria-hidden="true"` and `focusable="false"`, as SeverityLabel's CR-3 does. The build adds `info-circle` and `exclamation-circle` to `packages/perron/icons/` following [Icons](../foundations/icons.md), joins them to `icons.json`, and runs `npm run tokens` to rebuild the set's table. `IntentIcon` joins the contract's Shared parts table, composed in Alert and Toast, with `pn-IntentIcon` and the two icons drawn for it, `info-circle` and `exclamation-circle`, as what only its folder holds: SeverityLabel and NormalService draw `warning` and `check-circle` too, so those two stay the set's; and Alert joins `CloseButton`'s row there.
- **CR-5.** The `icon` part always carries `aria-hidden="true"`, after the caller's `slotProps.icon` props, so those props cannot make the icon speak; the words say what it shows. A `render` element's own props are the caller's: `useRender` merges them last, as Base UI does, so a caller that swaps the icon's element leaves `aria-hidden` off it.
- **CR-6.** The close button is the `CloseButton` shared part, in `packages/perron/src/parts/CloseButton/`, never a button drawn again: Alert composes it with `label` from `useOwnedStrings({ close: closeLabel })` (`packages/perron/src/PerronProvider.tsx`) and the class `pn-Alert-close`, and its CSS sets only the two margins. It is never disabled: `slotProps.close` is typed `Omit<ComponentPropsWithRef<'button'>, 'children' | 'disabled'>`, as Dialog's and Popover's close slots leave `disabled` out, and Alert passes no `disabled` of its own, so the `CloseButton` part needs no disabled look; a message that must stay leaves `onClose` out. Its props are `mergeProps(slotProps.close, { onClick, className: 'pn-Alert-close' })`, the component's own last: Base UI's `mergeProps` runs the rightmost handler first, so Alert calls `onClose(event.nativeEvent, 'close-press', { reason: 'close-press', event: event.nativeEvent })` first and the caller's `onClick` runs after it, and the class comes first in the string. The caller cannot stop `onClose` from its `onClick`, and does not need to: Alert never hides itself, and the caller removes it in `onClose`.
- **CR-7.** Alert never hides or unmounts itself and never moves focus: pressing close only calls `onClose`. The caller removes the alert there and moves focus to the element before it, or to the heading of the panel it sat in, so focus is not dropped to `<body>`; the stories' `play` tests do so to show the pattern.
- **CR-8.** The root's role is `status` unless the caller gives one, `rest.role ?? 'status'` among the own props merged after the caller's, so the caller's `role` wins: `role="alert"` for a danger message that stops the task in hand, such as a failed save. A message that must be heard as it appears is added inside a live region already on the page, or kept mounted with its words changed, since a `status` inserted with its words already in it is not reliably announced; a message present when the page loads needs nothing.
- **CR-9.** Alert sizes to its container, with no width or max-width of its own, and long words wrap (`overflow-wrap: anywhere` on the root and on the title and the sentences, `min-inline-size: 0` on the content), so a long Danish stop name fits a 320 px screen and the close button stays at the row's end.
- **CR-10.** The root keeps a `border.width.025` edge, `transparent`, so Windows' forced colours draw an edge round the alert when they drop the tint, as Tag's CR-4 does. No `(forced-colors: active)` rule is needed.
- **CR-11.** `color`, `title`, `icon`, `action`, `onClose`, `closeLabel`, `children`, `slotProps` and `render` are taken out of the rest props before they reach the root, so the HTML `title` attribute never reaches the element. Each inner part's props are its `slotProps` value merged with `mergeProps`, the component's own props last, so its class, `aria-hidden`, children and the close button's `onClick` stay while the caller's `className` and `onClick` join and its `render` swaps the element (CR-6).
- **CR-12.** Alert is drawn so Toast can take it whole: the parts are named as Base UI's Toast names them (`content`, `title`, `description`, `action`, `close`), the intents and their surfaces, icons and colours are the same `color` values and rows, and the icon is the `IntentIcon` shared part. Toast's spec reuses the [Tokens](#tokens) rows for its own parts and adds what a floating message needs; Alert itself takes no Toast behaviour, such as a timeout or swiping.

## Stories

One per variant the deferred design will draw, named as the `color` values in PascalCase. With no `Default`, `Danger` is alphabetically first and the contract story's subject, so its args render the alert alone. Each `play` test reads the accessibility tree and the DOM, not the pixels, and ends with focus where it started.

| Story     | Shows                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | `play` test                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| --------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Danger`  | Every part: `color='danger'`, the `exclamation-circle` icon, `title` "Could not load departures", the sentence "The real-time feed stopped answering at 08:02. Departures show the timetable only.", an action, a `small` `outline` `neutral` Button "Try again", and `onClose`. The subject story | The root has `role="status"` and `data-color='danger'`; the icon part is `aria-hidden` and draws in `color.status.danger`; what is heard is the title, the sentence, "Try again" and "Close"; Tab reaches "Try again", then "Close", and Shift+Tab leaves them; pressing "Close" calls `onClose` once with `'close-press'` and a `details.reason` of `'close-press'`; the close button's pressed fill renders apart from its hover one and its rule comes after the hover rule (`stateFill`, `pressedAfterHover`); `icon={null}` mounted beside it renders no `pn-Alert-icon`; `role="alert"` mounted beside it wins over `status`; focus ends where it started |
| `Info`    | `color='info'`, the `info-circle` icon and the sentence "Departures after 01:00 follow the night timetable.", with no title, action or close                                                                                                                                                       | `data-color` is `info`; only the root, the icon, the content and the description render: no `pn-Alert-title`, `pn-Alert-action` or `pn-Alert-close` element; nothing in it takes focus                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `Neutral` | `color='neutral'`, the default: the sentence "Departures update every 30 seconds.", with no icon                                                                                                                                                                                                   | `data-color` is `neutral`; no `pn-Alert-icon` renders; with an `icon` given, mounted beside it, the icon part renders, `aria-hidden`, holding it                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `Success` | `color='success'`, the `check-circle` icon, `title` "Report sent" and `onClose`                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | `data-color` is `success`; the close button is named "Close", and with `closeLabel="Dismiss"`, mounted beside it, "Dismiss"; pressing it calls `onClose`, and the alert stays in the document (CR-7); with a caller's `slotProps.close.onClick`, mounted beside it, pressing it calls `onClose`, then that `onClick`, each once (CR-6); a caller mounted beside it that removes the alert in `onClose` and focuses the button before it leaves focus on that button                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `Warning` | `color='warning'`, the `warning` icon, `title` "Signal fault at Danshøj" and the sentences "Trains between Flintholm and Ny Ellebjerg run slower than planned. We don't know yet when the fault will be fixed."                                                                                    | `data-color` is `warning`; no close button renders without `onClose`; in a 320 px container with a title of one long Danish compound and an `onClose`, the title wraps onto more than one line, stays inside the alert, the close button stays at the row's end beside the title's first line, and the alert stays inside the container (CR-9)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |

## Do and don't

For a caller using the component, with the reason.

| Do                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | Don't                                                                                                                                     |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Say what is happening, then how sure we are, in plain sentences: a title such as "Signal fault at Danshøj" above a sentence such as "Trains between Flintholm and Ny Ellebjerg run slower than planned. We don't know yet when the fault will be fixed." | Write "Error!" or "Something went wrong": content design has no exclamation marks, and the title should say what failed                   |
| Pick the `color` the words say: `success` for something that went well, `warning` for something to take care with, `danger` for something that failed                                                                                                    | Let the colour or the icon be the only sign: every message says its meaning in words too                                                  |
| Use SeverityLabel or a DisruptionCard for a disruption on a line, and NormalService for a line running normally                                                                                                                                          | Use an Alert for each disruption: a disruption has its own words, icons and colours, and a list of tinted boxes is not calm               |
| Use DataStatePanel or EmptyState when a data view is loading, empty or could not load                                                                                                                                                                    | Put an Alert in place of the data view's content: it sits beside content, it doesn't stand in for it                                      |
| Give one action at most, a `small` `outline` `neutral` Button or a LinkButton                                                                                                                                                                            | Add a `brand` action: a screen has one brand action at most, and the message is not it                                                    |
| Remove the alert in `onClose` and move focus to the element before it                                                                                                                                                                                    | Leave focus on a close button that is gone: it drops to the top of the page                                                               |
| Add a message that must be heard as it appears inside a live region already on the page, or pass `role="alert"` for a failure that stops the task                                                                                                        | Pass `role="alert"` on every danger message, or add a live region of your own around an Alert shown on load: it interrupts, or adds noise |
| Show a message that comes and goes on its own, such as "Link copied", as a Toast                                                                                                                                                                         | Make an Alert disappear on a timer: an inline message stays until the person or the data says otherwise                                   |

title: EmptyState
markdown:
# EmptyState

Stands in for a list or panel that has nothing to show, and says in plain words what is empty, why, and what to try next.

<!-- run notes -->

The design is deferred (ADR 0010, `docs/adr/0010-unattended-runs-with-design-deferred.md`): this spec decides what the drawing would, from the [contract](README.md), the [foundations](../foundations/README.md), [content design](../content-design.md) and the tokens. EmptyState has no Base UI component and nothing in `dependsOn`.

## Anatomy

Penpot page `Components/EmptyState`. Family: none, since it is static content that sits on its container's surface and joins no family's treatment. Shared parts: none.

| Part (Penpot layer) | What it is                                                                                             | Base UI part                          | Class                       | `slotProps` key |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------- | --------------------------- | --------------- |
| `root`              | A `div` stacking the parts below in a centred column                                                   | None: `useRender`, a `div` by default | `pn-EmptyState`             | none            |
| `icon`              | A `div` holding the caller's `icon`, hidden from screen readers; rendered only when given              | None: `useRender`, a `div` by default | `pn-EmptyState-icon`        | `icon`          |
| `title`             | A `p` holding the caller's `title`: what is empty                                                      | None: `useRender`, a `p` by default   | `pn-EmptyState-title`       | `title`         |
| `description`       | A `div` holding the caller's `children`: why, and what to try; rendered only when given                | None: `useRender`, a `div` by default | `pn-EmptyState-description` | `description`   |
| `action`            | A `div` holding the caller's `action`, such as a button that clears a filter; rendered only when given | None: `useRender`, a `div` by default | `pn-EmptyState-action`      | `action`        |

No part has a Base UI component, because none has behaviour for Base UI to give: no focus, keys, state or popup. Each part renders through Base UI's `useRender` hook instead, so each takes `render`, as the root does and as its `slotProps` key does for an inner part.

- Decided: the title renders as a `p` by default, with no heading level of its own; a caller that wants it in the page's outline makes it a heading through `slotProps.title.render`, such as `render: <h3 />`. EmptyState sits inside panels whose heading levels it cannot know, and a wrong level breaks the outline where a `p` leaves it whole.

## Base UI parts

No Base UI component: each part renders through the `useRender` hook from `@base-ui/react/use-render`, and merges its props with `mergeProps` from `@base-ui/react/merge-props`, at the version pinned in `packages/perron/package.json` (1.9.0).

| Base UI part                | Renders | Perron sets                                                                                      | Passed through                                                        |
| --------------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `useRender` for root        | `div`   | `defaultTagName: 'div'`, `ref`, the class `pn-EmptyState`, and the parts below as children       | `render`, `className`, `style`, `ref` and the rest of the `div` props |
| `useRender` for icon        | `div`   | `defaultTagName: 'div'`, the class `pn-EmptyState-icon`, `aria-hidden: true`, `icon` as children | `slotProps.icon`                                                      |
| `useRender` for title       | `p`     | `defaultTagName: 'p'`, the class `pn-EmptyState-title`, `title` as children                      | `slotProps.title`, its `render` making it a heading                   |
| `useRender` for description | `div`   | `defaultTagName: 'div'`, the class `pn-EmptyState-description`, `children` as children           | `slotProps.description`                                               |
| `useRender` for action      | `div`   | `defaultTagName: 'div'`, the class `pn-EmptyState-action`, `action` as children                  | `slotProps.action`                                                    |

Base UI already does: swapping each part's element through `render` while keeping its class and props, joining `className` strings and `style` objects and chaining event handlers in `mergeProps`, and setting `ref` on the rendered element.

## Props

In MUI's layout. Every prop here gets this description as its JSDoc. Slots come last.

| Name                    | Type                              | Default | Base UI prop                | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ----------------------- | --------------------------------- | ------- | --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `title`                 | `ReactNode`                       |         | none                        | What is empty, in a few words: "No matches for Nørrebro st". Required. Replaces the HTML `title` attribute                                                                                                                                                               |
| `children`              | `ReactNode`                       |         | none                        | The sentence under the title: why it is empty and what to try. "Try a line number such as 5C."                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `icon`                  | `ReactNode`                       |         | none                        | An icon from Perron's set above the title, for the eye only: it is hidden from screen readers. It renders at 16 px, `icon.size.400`; for an icon drawn for another step, set `--perron-icon-size` to that step's `icon.size.*` on the icon part through `slotProps.icon` |
| `action`                | `ReactNode`                       |         | none                        | What the person can do about it, such as a button that clears the search, below the sentence                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `render`                | Base UI's `render`                |         | inherited                   | Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render.                                                                                |
| `className`             | `string`                          |         | none                        | Joined after `pn-EmptyState` on the root                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `style`                 | `CSSProperties`                   |         | none                        | Reaches the root                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `ref`                   | `Ref<HTMLDivElement>`             |         | none                        | Reaches the root element                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `slotProps.icon`        | `useRender.ComponentProps<'div'>` |         | `useRender` for icon        | Props for the `icon` part                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `slotProps.title`       | `useRender.ComponentProps<'p'>`   |         | `useRender` for title       | Props for the `title` part. Its `render` makes the title a heading: `render: <h3 />`                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `slotProps.description` | `useRender.ComponentProps<'div'>` |         | `useRender` for description | Props for the `description` part                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `slotProps.action`      | `useRender.ComponentProps<'div'>` |         | `useRender` for action      | Props for the `action` part                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |

`render`, `className`, `style`, `ref` and the other `div` props reach the root, as the contract's Root section says; `render` is inherited from `useRender` as it is, with Base UI's JSDoc, and `EmptyStateProps` does not declare it again. No owned string, so no `*Label` prop.

- Decided: `children` is the sentence under the title, the way MUI's `Alert` takes its message, rather than a separate `description` prop, so the common call reads `<EmptyState title="No departures in the next hour">Nothing leaves this stop in the next hour.</EmptyState>`. The part keeps the name `description` for its class and `slotProps` key.
- Decided: the names `title`, `icon` and `action` are taken from MUI (`CardHeader`'s `title`, `Alert`'s `icon` and `action`), and `title` is taken out of the root's props so the HTML `title` attribute never reaches the element; an EmptyState has no use for a hover tooltip.
- Decided: EmptyState ships with no `variant`, `size` or `color`, one look everywhere. The uses known now (an empty search, an empty list in a sheet, a data panel with nothing to show) share one calm look, and any of the three can join later as an optional prop without a break.

## Tokens

One row per part, state and property. EmptyState has no interactive state of its own, so every row is rest; the caller's action keeps its own states.

| Part          | State | Property             | Token                                 |
| ------------- | ----- | -------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| `root`        | rest  | `padding-block`      | `space.600`                           |
| `root`        | rest  | `padding-inline`     | `space.400`                           |
| `root`        | rest  | `gap`                | `space.100`                           |
| `icon`        | rest  | `color`              | `color.text.secondary`                |
| `icon`        | rest  | `margin-block-end`   | `space.200`                           |
| `icon`        | rest  | `--perron-icon-size` | `icon.size.400`                       |
| `title`       | rest  | `font`               | `typography.heading-sm`               |
| `title`       | rest  | `letter-spacing`     | `typography.heading-sm`, its tracking |
| `title`       | rest  | `color`              | `color.text.primary`                  |
| `description` | rest  | `font`               | `typography.body-sm`                  |
| `description` | rest  | `letter-spacing`     | `typography.body-sm`, its tracking    |
| `description` | rest  | `color`              | `color.text.secondary`                |
| `action`      | rest  | `gap`                | `space.200`                           |
| `action`      | rest  | `margin-block-start` | `space.300`                           |

The root is a flex column with `align-items: center` and `text-align: center`; the action is a flex row that wraps, centred. The spacing comes out as 12 px from icon to title (`space.100` and `space.200`), 4 px from title to sentence, and 16 px from sentence to action (`space.100` and `space.300`). Every part and the root reset the margins a `p` brings, and the icon part is a flex box so an inline SVG adds no baseline gap below it.

- Decided: the root has no fill, border, radius or shadow, so EmptyState takes the surface of the panel, sheet or popup it sits in. It is content, not a card, and a surface of its own would join no family and stack a box inside a box.
- Decided: the layout is a centred column, padded `space.600` on the block axis and `space.400` on the inline axis, with the gaps in the table above. Centred is how an empty list reads at a glance in a narrow sheet, 24 px matches the space between blocks of a pane, and 16 px inline keeps text clear of a 320 px screen's edges.
- Decided: the icon is a bare icon from Perron's set, in `color.text.secondary`, with no disc or tile behind it, and the icon part sets `--perron-icon-size` to `icon.size.400`, the 16 px step the set's default icons are drawn for, as the contract sizes an icon on the element that holds it. An icon drawn for another step gets that step's `icon.size.*` through `slotProps.icon`, by `className` or `style`; a larger icon needs a new drawing, as the icon foundation's Sizes section says, never a scaled one. The brand keeps the interface calm, and a disc would need a size token no foundation gives it.
- Decided: the title is `typography.heading-sm` in `color.text.primary`, and the sentence `typography.body-sm` in `color.text.secondary`. The roles' own uses are "card titles" and "the line under a title", and both colours meet 4.5:1 on every surface.

## Keyboard and ARIA

EmptyState has no keys of its own and is never focusable. The caller's action is reached in reading order.

| Key         | Does                                                                   | From        |
| ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------- |
| `Tab`       | Moves to the first focusable element in the action, after the sentence | The browser |
| `Shift+Tab` | Moves back out of the action, to whatever came before the EmptyState   | The browser |

| Element       | Role                                                               | Accessible name from             | States announced |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------- | ---------------- |
| `root`        | None (generic `div`)                                               | None                             | None             |
| `icon`        | Hidden: `aria-hidden="true"`                                       | None                             | None             |
| `title`       | Paragraph, or a heading when `slotProps.title.render` makes it one | Its text, from `title`           | None             |
| `description` | None (generic `div`)                                               | None                             | None             |
| `action`      | None (generic `div`); the caller's controls carry their own roles  | The caller's controls' own names | Theirs           |

- Decided: the root carries no live-region role, leaving the caller to add `role="status"` when the EmptyState replaces results while the person types or filters. An empty state shown with the page on load needs no announcement, the accessibility rules ask for live regions on changes of state only, and a search field such as SearchField announces its own empty results.

What axe won't catch, from the contract, each with how this component meets it:

- [ ] Everything the eye is told, the ear is told, for every shape each prop accepts: the icon is `aria-hidden` and decorative, and the title, read as text, says what the icon shows.
- [ ] Every landmark and named region has an accessible name: none here; the root is not a landmark or region.
- [ ] Every default label can be overridden: none here; EmptyState owns no string.
- [ ] Every shape the type accepts renders, in every variant: `title`, `children`, `icon` and `action` each render a string, an element and an array; `description` and `action` are `div`s, so block content such as a list is valid inside them, and the title takes phrasing content as a `p` or a heading does.
- [ ] A hidden copy kept for animation is `aria-hidden`, and a collapsed region is `inert`: none here; nothing animates or collapses.
- [ ] Native semantics first: a `p` for the title, made a native `h2` to `h6` through `render` when it heads a section; the action holds the caller's own `button` or `a href`.
- [ ] Focus moves in reading order and returns on close: the action follows the sentence in the DOM and on screen; EmptyState never moves focus when it appears, and nothing in it closes.
- [ ] Every target is at least `size.target-min` square: EmptyState has no target of its own; the action's targets are the caller's components, which keep their own sizes.
- [ ] Loops stop when the system asks for less motion: none here; nothing moves.

## Owned strings

No owned strings: every word EmptyState shows comes from the caller, through `title`, `children` and `action`, and the icon is hidden from screen readers.

## Component rules

Rules for this component alone, numbered so the build and the review can cite them.

- **CR-1.** The optional parts render only when given: no `icon` part without `icon`, no `description` part without `children`, no `action` part without `action`. A value that renders nothing (`null`, `undefined`, a boolean, `''`, or an array of only such values) counts as not given, so no empty wrapper takes up a gap.
- **CR-2.** The `icon` part always carries `aria-hidden="true"`, after the caller's `slotProps.icon` props, so those props cannot make the icon speak; the title says what it shows. A `render` element's own props are the caller's: `useRender` merges them last, as Base UI does, so a caller that swaps the icon's element leaves `aria-hidden` off it.
- **CR-3.** `title`, `icon`, `action`, `children`, `slotProps` and `render` are taken out of the rest props before they reach the root, so the HTML `title` attribute never reaches the element.
- **CR-4.** Each inner part's props are its `slotProps` value merged with `mergeProps`, the component's own props last, so its class, `aria-hidden` and children stay while the caller's `className` joins and its `render` swaps the element.
- **CR-5.** EmptyState never moves focus, sets no `tabindex` and adds no role to the root; the caller decides whether it is announced.
- **CR-6.** It sizes to its container, with no width or max-width of its own, and long words wrap (`overflow-wrap: anywhere`), so a long Danish stop name in the title fits a 320 px screen.
- **CR-7.** Colour sits on the parts that hold text, and the icon takes `currentColor` from its part, as the icon foundation asks.

## Stories

One per variant and state the Penpot design shows, named as Penpot names it. The design is deferred and has no variant property, so its one variant is `Default`; `TitleOnly` is the same variant with the optional props left out, and proves CR-1.

| Story       | Shows                                                                                                                                                                                  | `play` test                                                                                                                                               |
| ----------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Default`   | Every part: the `search` icon, `title` "No matches for Nørrebro st", the sentence "Try a line number such as 5C." and an action, an `outline` `neutral` Button "Clear search", at rest | The icon part is `aria-hidden`; Tab reaches the "Clear search" button and Shift+Tab leaves it, so focus ends where it started                             |
| `TitleOnly` | `title` "No departures in the next hour", with no icon, sentence or action                                                                                                             | Only the root and the title render: no `pn-EmptyState-icon`, `pn-EmptyState-description` or `pn-EmptyState-action` element, and nothing in it takes focus |

## Do and don't

For a caller using the component, with the reason.

| Do                                                                                                                                                                                     | Don't                                                                                                                                       |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Say what is empty, then what to try, in plain sentences: "No matches for Nørrebro st" over "Try a line number such as 5C."                                                             | Write "Oops! Nothing here!": content design has no exclamation marks, and the title should name what is missing                             |
| Say only what the data knows: "No departures in the next hour" when the timetable covers an hour                                                                                       | Write "No departures" when there may be some later: the brand never claims more certainty than the data has                                 |
| Use it for a list, a search or a panel with nothing in it                                                                                                                              | Use it for loading or for missing real-time data: loading says "Loading", and missing data uses the data-state words such as "No signal"    |
| Give one neutral action at most, such as clearing the search or the filters                                                                                                            | Add a `brand` action when the panel already has one: a screen has one brand action at most                                                  |
| Pick a decorative icon from Perron's set that matches the title, or none; it renders at 16 px, and one drawn for another step takes that step's `icon.size.*` through `slotProps.icon` | Let the icon carry meaning alone, or use an emoji: the icon is hidden from screen readers and Mylder uses no emoji                          |
| Make the title a heading through `slotProps.title.render` when the EmptyState stands in for a whole section                                                                            | Wrap the title in your own heading element inside `title`: the part is a `p` until `render` swaps it, and a heading inside a `p` is invalid |
| Add `role="status"` on the root when it replaces results as the person types or filters, so the change is announced                                                                    | Add a live region to an EmptyState shown on load: there is no change to announce, and it adds noise                                         |

title: Progress
markdown:
# Progress

A bar that shows how far a task has got, such as an export, with the words that name the task and the share done, such as "Exporting the report" at "45%", or, while how far is not known, that the task is under way.

<!-- run notes -->

The design is deferred (ADR 0010, `docs/adr/0010-unattended-runs-with-design-deferred.md`): there is no read-back, code map or export, and this spec decides what the drawing would, from the [contract](README.md), the [foundations](../foundations/README.md), [content design](../content-design.md), the tokens and the Base UI reference for `Progress` (`@base-ui/react` 1.9.0, installed, its source read in `node_modules/@base-ui/react/progress/`). Progress has nothing in `dependsOn`, no ROADMAP line names it (it joined the registry with the other feedback components, under Feedback), and the extracted prototype is not reachable from this branch, so nothing here rests on either.

[Meter](meter.md), the other bar along a track on Base UI's same five parts, sets the precedent Progress follows where they meet: the layout, the figure, its locale, the track and its forced-colours rule. Meter's own Do and don't sends a task's progress here. The tokens were read from this branch's `packages/perron/tokens/` files, since the Perron MCP's `list_tokens` lacks `size.meter-track`, added since the main checkout it reads.

## Anatomy

Penpot page `Components/Progress`. Family: none, since it is a static display that sits on its container's surface and joins no family's treatment: it is not pressed, takes no hover and is not one of the Rows, Fields, Popups, Panels or Tooltips. Shared parts: none; the words for a task under way reach the ear through `aria-valuetext`, not through VisuallyHidden (CR-5).

Progress takes Meter's anatomy and layout unchanged: a `root` grid with `label` and `value` on the first row and `track` across both columns on the second, `indicator` inside `track`, the label first in the DOM and on screen. A meter and a progress bar on one panel then read as the same kind of bar, and the figure sits where Meter's does.

The drawing will have a `root` board holding three layers, `label`, `value` and `track`, with `indicator` inside `track`, and one variant property, `State`, whose values `progressing`, `complete` and `indeterminate` map in the code map to Base UI's `[data-progressing]`, `[data-complete]` and `[data-indeterminate]`, and name its variants `Progressing`, `Complete` and `Indeterminate` (`penpot/README.md`, "Conventions"). It has no other variant property. The three statuses are not a prop: each is a look Base UI produces from `value` alone, and the contract maps a `State` value to an attribute, never to a prop.

| Part (Penpot layer) | What it is                                                                                                                                                                              | Base UI part         | Class                   | `slotProps` key |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------- | ----------------------- | --------------- |
| `root`              | A `div` with `role="progressbar"`, a two-column grid: the label and the figure on the first row, the track across both columns on the second                                            | `Progress.Root`      | `pn-Progress`           | none            |
| `label`             | A `span` holding the caller's `label`, the task in a few words, such as "Exporting the report"; the progress bar's accessible name                                                      | `Progress.Label`     | `pn-Progress-label`     | `label`         |
| `value`             | A `span` at the inline end of the first row holding the figure Base UI formats, "45%", and nothing while indeterminate (CR-5); `aria-hidden`, since the root's `aria-valuetext` says it | `Progress.Value`     | `pn-Progress-value`     | `value`         |
| `track`             | A `div` across the second row: the whole task, from `min` to `max`, in an inset pill                                                                                                    | `Progress.Track`     | `pn-Progress-track`     | `track`         |
| `indicator`         | A `div` inside `track`: the share done, from the track's inline start, its width set by Base UI as a percentage; while indeterminate, a segment that sweeps along the track (CR-6)      | `Progress.Indicator` | `pn-Progress-indicator` | `indicator`     |

Every part has its Base UI part, so each one's props come through its `slotProps` key and the root takes the component's own. Base UI's root also appends a `span` with `role="presentation"`, its own `visuallyHidden` style (`position: fixed`, `clip-path: inset(50%)`) and the text "x" after its children, as Meter's does. It is no part of Perron's: it has no class, no layer and no `slotProps` key, its fixed position takes it out of the grid, and `expectOwnedStrings` already skips it (CR-9).

## Base UI parts

Imported from `@base-ui/react/progress`, at the version pinned in `packages/perron/package.json` (1.9.0 installed).

| Base UI part         | Renders                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | Perron sets                                                                                                                                                                                                                | Passed through                                                                                                                        |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Progress.Root`      | `<div role="progressbar">` with `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax`, `aria-valuenow` (the value clamped to `min` and `max`, left out while indeterminate), `aria-valuetext` (the formatted value, what `getAriaValueText` returns, or the English "indeterminate progress" while indeterminate) and `aria-labelledby` the label's `id`; `data-progressing`, `data-complete` or `data-indeterminate`; its children, then the hidden "x" `span` | `className` (`pn-Progress`, then the caller's), `ref`, `value`, `locale` (the PerronProvider's when the caller gives none), `aria-valuetext` (the owned "In progress" while indeterminate, CR-5), and the four parts below | `min`, `max`, `format`, `getAriaValueText`, `aria-valuetext` (while the value is known), `render`, `style` and every other `div` prop |
| `Progress.Label`     | `<span role="presentation">` with an `id` (the caller's, or one Base UI generates) that it registers as the root's `aria-labelledby`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | `className` (`pn-Progress-label`, then the caller's), `label` as children                                                                                                                                                  | `slotProps.label`, merged with `mergeProps`, the component's own props last                                                           |
| `Progress.Value`     | `<span aria-hidden="true">` holding the formatted value, nothing while indeterminate, or what a function `children` returns from `(formattedValue, value)`, which Base UI calls with the English "indeterminate" as `formattedValue` while indeterminate                                                                                                                                                                                   | `className` (`pn-Progress-value`, then the caller's), and while indeterminate a function `children` that returns nothing (CR-5)                                                                                            | `slotProps.value`, merged the same way; its function `children` writes the figure while the value is known                            |
| `Progress.Track`     | `<div>`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | `className` (`pn-Progress-track`, then the caller's), and the indicator as children                                                                                                                                        | `slotProps.track`, merged the same way                                                                                                |
| `Progress.Indicator` | `<div>` with an inline `style` of `inset-inline-start: 0`, `height: inherit` and `width` the value's percentage of the range, clamped to 0 to 100%, while the value is known; no inline style while indeterminate                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | `className` (`pn-Progress-indicator`, then the caller's)                                                                                                                                                                   | `slotProps.indicator`, merged the same way                                                                                            |

Base UI already does: the `progressbar` role and its `aria-value*` attributes; taking `null`, `NaN` and `Infinity` alike as indeterminate and leaving `aria-valuenow` out then; clamping a known value to `min` and `max` for `aria-valuenow`, the figure and the fill; the status, `complete` when the clamped value is `max`, `progressing` below it, `indeterminate` with no value, set as a data attribute on every part; formatting the figure with `Intl.NumberFormat`, by default as the percentage of the range done (`value` 9 of `max` 20 reads "45%"), or with the caller's `format` options applied to the clamped value; keeping the shown figure and `aria-valuetext` the same text, unless `getAriaValueText` or `aria-valuetext` gives the ear a fuller one; naming the root by the label through a generated `id`; hiding the figure from screen readers, since `aria-valuetext` says it; and sizing the indicator as a percentage of the track.

## Props

In MUI's layout. Every prop Progress declares gets this description as its JSDoc; the inherited ones keep Base UI's. Slots come last, and `slotProps` itself says "Props for each inner part, merged with the part's own, which win", as Meter's does.

| Name                  | Type                                                        | Default                     | Base UI prop                           | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| --------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------- | -------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `label`               | `ReactNode`                                                 |                             | none: the children of `Progress.Label` | The task, in a few words, such as "Exporting the report": shown above the track, and the progress bar's accessible name. Required                                                                                                                           |
| `value`               | `number \| null`                                            |                             | `value`                                | Required. How far the task has got, between `min` and `max`; one outside them is shown at the nearest end. `null`, or a number that is not finite, while how far is not known: Progress then sweeps a segment along the track and says "In progress" (CR-5) |
| `min`                 | `number`                                                    | `0`                         | inherited                              | The minimum value.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `max`                 | `number`                                                    | `100`                       | inherited                              | The maximum value.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `format`              | `Intl.NumberFormatOptions`                                  |                             | inherited                              | Options to format the value.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `locale`              | `Intl.LocalesArgument`                                      | The PerronProvider's locale | `locale`                               | The locale `Intl.NumberFormat` formats the figure in: "45%" in English, "45 %" in Danish, Swedish and Norwegian. Left out, the nearest PerronProvider's                                                                                                     |
| `getAriaValueText`    | `(formattedValue: string, value: number \| null) => string` |                             | inherited                              | Accepts a function which returns a string value that provides a human-readable text alternative for the current value of the progress bar.                                                                                                                  |
| `aria-valuetext`      | `string`                                                    |                             | inherited                              | A string value that provides a user-friendly name for `aria-valuenow`, the current value of the progress bar.                                                                                                                                               |
| `render`              | Base UI's `render`                                          |                             | inherited                              | Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render.                                                                   |
| `inProgressLabel`     | `string`                                                    | The locale's                | none                                   | Overrides "In progress", heard in place of the figure while the value is indeterminate                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `className`           | `string`                                                    |                             | none                                   | Joined after `pn-Progress` on the root                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `style`               | `CSSProperties`                                             |                             | none                                   | Reaches the root                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `ref`                 | `Ref<HTMLDivElement>`                                       |                             | none                                   | Reaches the root element                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `slotProps.label`     | `Progress.Label.Props`                                      |                             | `Progress.Label`                       | Props for the `label` part                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `slotProps.value`     | `Progress.Value.Props`                                      |                             | `Progress.Value`                       | Props for the `value` part. Its function `children` writes the figure from `(formattedValue, value)` while the value is known                                                                                                                               |
| `slotProps.track`     | `Progress.Track.Props`                                      |                             | `Progress.Track`                       | Props for the `track` part                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `slotProps.indicator` | `Progress.Indicator.Props`                                  |                             | `Progress.Indicator`                   | Props for the `indicator` part                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |

`ProgressProps` extends `Progress.Root.Props` without `children` and the members it declares again, and declares `label`, `value`, `locale`, `inProgressLabel`, React's `className`, `style` and `ref`, and `slotProps`; `min`, `max`, `format`, `getAriaValueText`, `aria-valuetext` and `render` are inherited as they are, with Base UI's JSDoc and `@default`. Progress takes no `children`: its content is its four parts, and a caller's children would land after the track inside the `progressbar` role, where a screen reader never reads them.

`label` is required: it is the progress bar's accessible name, and a `progressbar` with no name fails axe's `aria-progressbar-name`. `value` is required too, as Base UI's is, so a caller says `null` on purpose when how far is not known, rather than leaving it out by mistake.

`value` is how far a task has got, not a control's value: Progress has no `defaultValue` and no `onChange`, since nothing the person does changes it. It keeps Base UI's name, as Meter and MUI's `LinearProgress` do.

Progress takes no `color`, `size` or `variant`, its fill always the neutral mark `color.text.primary`: how far a task has got is neither good nor bad news, so no status intent has a meaning to carry, `brand` has no mark, a task that fails is told by the screen's own message in its place, and one track height and one layout serve a panel and a report, as Meter's do; each can join later as an optional prop without a break.

Progress formats the figure in the PerronProvider's locale when the caller gives no `locale`, through the `useLocale()` hook in `packages/perron/src/PerronProvider.tsx`, as Meter does: Base UI's own default, the runtime locale, shows "45%" on a Danish screen in an English browser and can differ between the server's render and the browser's. A caller's `locale` still wins.

## Tokens

One row per part, state and property. Progress is never interactive, so of the contract's design states it has rest alone; Base UI's statuses are rest with `data-progressing`, `data-complete` or `data-indeterminate` on every part, and a row with no status holds in all three.

| Part        | State                                                          | Property           | Token                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ----------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `root`      | rest                                                           | `column-gap`       | `space.200`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `root`      | rest                                                           | `row-gap`          | `space.100`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `label`     | rest                                                           | `font`             | `typography.label-sm`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `label`     | rest                                                           | `letter-spacing`   | `typography.label-sm`, its tracking                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `label`     | rest                                                           | `color`            | `color.text.secondary`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `label`     | rest                                                           | `overflow-wrap`    | none: the keyword `anywhere`, so a long Danish word breaks inside its column (CR-7)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `value`     | rest                                                           | `font`             | `typography.data`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
