| `value`     | rest                                                           | `color`            | `color.text.primary`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `value`     | rest                                                           | `white-space`      | none: the keyword `nowrap`, so "45 %" never breaks from its sign                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `track`     | rest                                                           | `background-color` | `color.surface.inset`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `track`     | rest                                                           | `block-size`       | `size.meter-track`, Meter's, its description widened in `packages/perron/tokens/base.tokens.json` through the `design-tokens` skill to name a progress bar's track too, its value unchanged: a meter and a progress bar side by side read as one kind of bar at one height, so one token holds both.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `track`     | rest                                                           | `border-radius`    | `radius.full`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `track`     | rest                                                           | `overflow`         | none: the keyword `hidden`, so the fill and the sweeping segment keep inside the pill's ends                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `track`     | rest, `(forced-colors: active)`                                | `outline`          | `border.width.025`, `solid` in the system colour `CanvasText` (CR-8)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `indicator` | rest                                                           | `background-color` | `color.text.primary`, the neutral mark of the contract's [Intents](README.md#intents)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `indicator` | rest                                                           | `border-radius`    | `radius.full`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `indicator` | rest, `data-progressing`, `data-complete`                      | `transition`       | `width` with `easing.standard` over `duration.meter`, its description widened through the `design-tokens` skill to "Meter and progress bar fill change": Motion gives meters their ease to a new value, a progress bar's fill moves the same way, and a second token of the same 800 ms would only drift from it (CR-6).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `indicator` | rest, `data-complete`                                          | every property     | As `data-progressing` at 100%: the complete status keeps the progressing look, a full fill in `color.text.primary`, with no token, tint or word of its own; the figure "100%" and the full track say it, and a success tint would be colour alone, which the screen's own message ("Report ready") says better in words.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `indicator` | rest, `data-indeterminate`                                     | `inset-inline`     | none: `30%` from each end, a percentage, so the segment is `40%` of the track wide and rests at the middle wherever the sweep does not run; its `width` stays `auto`, which the fill's `width` transition cannot ease from, so a task's first figure appears at its share at once, never shrinking from the segment (CR-6)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `indicator` | rest, `data-indeterminate`                                     | `animation`        | A loop that moves `inset-inline-start` from `-40%` to `100%` and `inset-inline-end` from `100%` to `-40%`, `infinite`, with `easing.standard`, over `duration.progress-sweep`, a new loop token of `1600ms`, "Segment that sweeps along an indeterminate progress bar's track", with no reduced-motion override, added through the `design-tokens` skill and listed on [Motion](../foundations/motion.md): the eye needs a sign that the task is under way where no figure is shown, a still bar reads as stuck or empty, and 1600 ms, the selection pulse's pace, keeps it calm; it is the first loop a component runs, so it follows Motion's rule that loops keep their durations (CR-6). |
| `indicator` | rest, `data-indeterminate`, `(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` | `animation`        | none: the keyword `none`: when the system asks for less motion, the sweep stops and the segment keeps its rest at the middle of the track, `30%` from each end; the contract stops every loop under reduced motion, and a segment at the middle never reads as a share done from the inline start, so the eye still tells it from a figure (CR-6).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `indicator` | rest, `(forced-colors: active)`                                | `background-color` | none: the system colour `CanvasText`, with the keyword `forced-color-adjust: none` (CR-8)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |

The root is `display: grid` with `grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr) auto` and `align-items: baseline`, keywords and fractions all, as Meter's; the label sits in the first column, the figure in the second at the inline end, and the track spans both on the second row (`grid-column: 1 / -1`). The root takes its container's inline size, with no width, fill, border, radius, padding or shadow of its own. Every part resets the margins its element may bring. While indeterminate, the empty figure holds a strut, a zero-width space hidden from screen readers (`content: '\200b' / ''` on `.pn-Progress-value[data-indeterminate]::before`), as NormalService's first row does, so the first row keeps the figure's line and the track does not move when a value arrives.

The track is `position: relative` and the indicator `position: absolute` with `inset-block: 0`, keywords all, so Base UI's inline `inset-inline-start: 0` and `width` place the fill from the inline start in either writing direction, and the sweep's `inset-inline-start` and `inset-inline-end` move the segment the same way in right-to-left text. Its keyframes are named `pn-Progress-sweep`.

The label takes Meter's, Stat's and FactList's label look, `typography.label-sm` in `color.text.secondary`, and the figure `typography.data`, a monospaced face with tabular figures, so the figure holds its width as it counts up. The fill takes the neutral mark, `color.text.primary`, at least 3:1 on `color.surface.inset` in both themes ([Accessibility](../foundations/accessibility.md)).

## Keyboard and ARIA

Progress has no keys of its own and is never focusable: a `progressbar` is not a control.

| Key  | Does                                  | From   |
| ---- | ------------------------------------- | ------ |
| None | Progress is not focusable or operable | Perron |

| Element              | Role                                       | Accessible name from                                                                                                                                                                                      | States announced                                                                                                                                                              |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `root`               | `progressbar`, from Base UI                | `aria-labelledby`, the `label` part's `id`, so the caller's `label`. Base UI's `Progress.Label` registers its `id` on the client only, so server-rendered markup has no `aria-labelledby` until hydration | `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax`, and `aria-valuetext`: the figure, "45%"; while indeterminate no `aria-valuenow`, and `aria-valuetext` "In progress" (CR-5) |
| `label`              | `presentation`, from Base UI               | Not named; its text is the root's name                                                                                                                                                                    | None                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `value`              | Hidden: `aria-hidden="true"`, from Base UI | Not read; `aria-valuetext` says it                                                                                                                                                                        | None                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `track`, `indicator` | None (generic `div`)                       | Not named; they hold no text                                                                                                                                                                              | None                                                                                                                                                                          |
| Base UI's "x" `span` | `presentation`, visually hidden            | Chromium exposes it as the text "x" inside the progress bar, as with Meter; Progress keeps Base UI's root (CR-1)                                                                                          | None                                                                                                                                                                          |

What axe won't catch, from the contract, each with how this component meets it:

- [ ] Everything the eye is told, the ear is told, for every shape each prop accepts: the eye gets the label, the figure and the fill's length; the ear the label as the name and the figure as `aria-valuetext`, which Base UI keeps the same text as the shown figure, or a fuller one from `getAriaValueText`. While indeterminate the eye gets the sweeping segment and no figure, the ear "In progress" in place of Base UI's English "indeterminate progress" (CR-5); under reduced motion the resting segment and the words carry it.
- [ ] Every landmark and named region has an accessible name: none here; the root is a `progressbar`, named by its label, not a landmark or region.
- [ ] Every default label can be overridden: `inProgressLabel`.
- [ ] Every shape the type accepts renders, in every variant: `label` is a `ReactNode`, and a string, a number, an element and a list each render in every status; `value` renders `0`, `min`, `max`, a value outside the range (clamped), a fraction, `null`, `NaN` and `Infinity` (the last three indeterminate), which `Progress.test.tsx` renders each of.
- [ ] A hidden copy kept for animation is `aria-hidden`, and a collapsed region is `inert`: none here; the sweep moves one element, and nothing collapses. The figure is `aria-hidden` because `aria-valuetext` says it, not for animation.
- [ ] Native semantics first: no native element says "a task's progress" with Perron's look and Base UI's API (`<progress>` draws its own bar), so Base UI's `role="progressbar"` with its `aria-value*` attributes, and no ARIA of Perron's beyond the `aria-valuetext` of an indeterminate value.
- [ ] Focus moves in reading order and returns on close: Progress takes no focus and opens nothing.
- [ ] Every target is at least `size.target-min` square: no target; Progress is not pressed.
- [ ] Loops stop when the system asks for less motion: the indeterminate sweep, the one loop, stops inside `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` in a rule for `.pn-Progress-indicator[data-indeterminate]` that sets its `animation` (CR-6); the fill's change is a transition over `duration.meter`, which the tokens shorten to 0.01 ms.

## Owned strings

Every word Progress shows comes from the caller, through `label`, or from Base UI's formatting of the number, but for the one it announces while how far is not known.

| Key          | English     | Override          | Seen or heard where                                                                        |
| ------------ | ----------- | ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `inProgress` | In progress | `inProgressLabel` | The root's `aria-valuetext` while the value is indeterminate, heard after the label (CR-5) |

The word heard while indeterminate is a new key `inProgress`, "In progress", rather than the existing `loading` ("Loading") or `unknown` ("Unknown"): a progress bar tracks exports and downloads as well as loads, so "Loading" would say more than the screen knows, and "Unknown" would tell the ear the task's state is unknown when only its share is; after the label it reads "Exporting the report, In progress". Agents write its Danish, Swedish and Norwegian in the locale files, and its JSDoc in `packages/perron/src/locale/en.ts` names Progress.

The figure's digits and percent sign carry no letter, so `expectOwnedStrings` passes them in every locale; Base UI's "x" it already skips, and Base UI's English "indeterminate progress" and "indeterminate" never reach the markup (CR-5).

## Component rules

Rules for this component alone, numbered so the build and the review can cite them.

- **CR-1.** Progress composes Base UI's five parts in one order, `Progress.Root` holding `Progress.Label`, `Progress.Value` and `Progress.Track`, with `Progress.Indicator` in the track, and never rebuilds what Base UI does: the role, the `aria-value*` attributes, the clamping, the status attributes, the formatting and the label's `id` are Base UI's.
- **CR-2.** Progress sets no `data-color`, `data-size` or `data-variant`: it has none of those props. Its CSS reads Base UI's `data-progressing`, `data-complete` and `data-indeterminate` and nothing of its own. The complete status keeps the progressing look, so no rule sets a colour, a tint or a word for `data-complete` alone.
- **CR-3.** Each inner part's props are its `slotProps` value merged with `mergeProps` from `@base-ui/react/merge-props`, the component's own props last, so its data attributes and children stay, and its class is set after the merge with the `withClass` shared helper, so the caller's `className`, a string or Base UI's function of the part's state, joins after its own, as Meter's parts do. The `usePart` helper renders a plain element, not a Base UI part, so Progress's parts, which read `Progress.Root`'s context, don't go through it.
- **CR-4.** `label`, `value`, `locale`, `inProgressLabel` and `slotProps` are taken out of the rest props before they reach the root, and `{...rest}` comes before Progress's own props, as the contract's [Root](README.md#root) says; the rest, `min`, `max`, `format`, `getAriaValueText` and `aria-valuetext` among them, reach `Progress.Root`.
- **CR-5.** The value is indeterminate when `value` is `null` or a number that is not finite, what the `known` shared helper in `packages/perron/src/internal/nodes.ts` says is no value and what Base UI takes as indeterminate, so Progress tests it with `known` and writes no test of its own; it passes `value` to Base UI as it is. While indeterminate it sets the root's `aria-valuetext` to the owned "In progress", or `inProgressLabel`, after the caller's rest props, so it wins over Base UI's English "indeterminate progress" and over a caller's `aria-valuetext` and `getAriaValueText`, which describe a known value; and it gives the value part a function `children` that returns nothing, after the caller's `slotProps.value`, so Base UI's English "indeterminate" never reaches a caller's function and the row shows the label alone. `0` is a value, not indeterminate.
- **CR-6.** While the value is known, the fill's change eases: the indicator transitions `width` over `duration.meter` with `easing.standard`, which the tokens shorten to 0.01 ms under reduced motion, and the first render does not animate. While indeterminate, the indicator is a segment `40%` of the track wide, set by `inset-inline: 30%`, which rests it at the middle of the track, and runs the `pn-Progress-sweep` keyframes, `inset-inline-start` from `-40%` to `100%` and `inset-inline-end` from `100%` to `-40%`, over `duration.progress-sweep` with `easing.standard`, `infinite`; inside `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` a rule for `.pn-Progress-indicator[data-indeterminate]` sets `animation: none`, leaving it at its rest. A value arriving after the indeterminate status does not animate: the segment's `width` is `auto`, which a transition cannot ease from, so the fill appears at once at the figure the ear already hears.
- **CR-7.** The label wraps and breaks a word longer than its column (`overflow-wrap: anywhere` on `.pn-Progress-label`, a box that takes its column's width); the figure never wraps (`white-space: nowrap`); the root sizes to its container, so a long label never pushes the figure past the inline end.
- **CR-8.** Inside `@media (forced-colors: active)`, the track draws an `outline` of `border.width.025` in `CanvasText`, and the indicator sets `forced-color-adjust: none` and `background-color: CanvasText`, as Meter's do: forced colours drop backgrounds, so without these the track, the fill and the sweep would vanish. An outline takes no space, so the geometry holds.
- **CR-9.** Base UI's `Progress.Root` appends the text "x" in a visually hidden `span role="presentation"`, which `expectOwnedStrings` in `packages/perron/src/testing/owned-strings.ts` already skips, as it does Meter's. A test that reads Progress's words through the `heard` helper reads the label part, not the root, which holds the "x". `expectOwnedStrings` reads `aria-valuetext`, so the owned "In progress" is held to the dictionary in every locale.
- **CR-10.** Progress is not a live region, sets no `aria-busy` and never moves focus. A screen announces the start and the end of a task in its own polite live region, as [Accessibility](../foundations/accessibility.md#what-a-person-checks) asks, and marks the region the task fills `aria-busy` itself if it needs to.
- **CR-11.** The figure is formatted in `locale`, the caller's or the nearest PerronProvider's, so a Danish screen reads "45 %" and an English one "45%"; Progress passes it to `Progress.Root`'s `locale` and never formats the number itself.

## Stories

One per variant the deferred design will draw, named by the Penpot convention: the `State` value in PascalCase. With no `Default` story, the [subject story](README.md#root) is the alphabetically first export, `Complete`. Each story's args are Progress's alone, so the subject story's args render it alone and hold every word the caller gives.

| Story           | Shows                                                                                                                                                         | `play` test                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Complete`      | `label` "Exporting the report", `value` 100: "100%" over a full fill; the subject story, which the contract story renders, and its args pass every rule alone | The root has role `progressbar`, the accessible name "Exporting the report", `aria-valuenow` 100, `aria-valuetext` "100%" and `data-complete`; the indicator's inline width is 100% and its computed background is `color.text.primary`'s, compared through the `colour` helper; nothing in it takes focus                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `Indeterminate` | `label` "Loading the network", `value` `null`: the label alone on the first row and a segment sweeping along the track                                        | The root carries `data-indeterminate` and no `aria-valuenow`; `aria-valuetext` is "In progress"; the value part is empty; the indicator's computed `animation-name` is `pn-Progress-sweep` and its `animation-duration` `duration.progress-sweep`'s, read through `rendered`; the stylesheet's `(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` block sets `animation: none` on `.pn-Progress-indicator[data-indeterminate]`; a Progress rendered beside the story with `value` `null`, then given `value` 5, carries `data-progressing` on its indicator, which runs no animation or transition and is 5% of its track wide |
| `Progressing`   | `label` "Exporting the report", `value` 9 of `max` 20: "45%"                                                                                                  | The root carries class `pn-Progress` and `data-progressing`, and the `ref` reaches it; `aria-valuenow` is 9, `aria-valuemax` 20 and `aria-valuetext` "45%"; the value part reads "45%" and is `aria-hidden`; the indicator's inline width is 45% and its computed `transition-duration` is `duration.meter`'s; the label is first in reading order                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |

## Do and don't

For a caller using the component, with the reason.

| Do                                                                                                                              | Don't                                                                                                                                     |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Use Progress for a task the person waits on that ends, such as an export or a download                                          | Use it for a measure within a range, such as the share of vehicles reporting live: that is a Meter, a measurement rather than a task      |
| Pass `null` while how far is not known, so Progress sweeps and says "In progress"                                               | Pass `0` or a guess: an empty fill at "0%" claims a figure the task never gave                                                            |
| Name the task in a few words in `label`: "Exporting the report", "Loading the network"                                          | Leave the name to the layout: a progress bar with no name tells the ear a number and nothing about the task                               |
| Announce the start and the end of the task, such as "Report ready", in the screen's own polite live region                      | Make a Progress a live region: a figure that counts up every moment floods the screen reader                                              |
| Replace the bar with the screen's own message when the task fails, and say what happened                                        | Leave a bar at its last figure, or tint it, when the task fails: the eye reads it as still running, and colour tells no screen reader     |
| Give `getAriaValueText` the fuller words when the figure shows them, such as "3 of 12 files" through `slotProps.value.children` | Change the shown figure and leave the ear on the percentage: the eye and the ear then hear different numbers                              |
| Use DataStatePanel's loading status for a view whose data has not arrived                                                       | Put an indeterminate Progress in place of a data view's content: DataStatePanel's calm "Loading" message is the library's answer for that |

title: Checkbox

# Checkbox

A box with its words beside it that turns one setting or one answer on and off, such as "Show planned works on the map", ticked when it is on and dashed when it stands for a set that is partly on, and submitted with a form.

<!-- run notes -->

The design is deferred (ADR 0010, `docs/adr/0010-unattended-runs-with-design-deferred.md`): there is no read-back, code map or export, and this spec decides what the drawing would, from the [contract](README.md), the [foundations](../foundations/README.md), the tokens and the Base UI reference for `Checkbox` (`@base-ui/react` 1.9.0, installed). The contract names Checkbox twice, as a composite control that carries a `name` ([State and events](README.md#state-and-events)) and as the first user of the `CheckboxIndicator` shared part ([Shared parts](README.md#shared-parts)). Its registry entry lists `Checkbox.Root` and `Checkbox.Indicator` and depends on nothing; CheckboxGroup, which depends on it, composes Checkboxes inside a Fieldset.

## Anatomy

Penpot page `Components/Checkbox`. Family: none (the contract's [Families](README.md#families) have no checkable control; the box borrows the Fields family's edge and hover, see [Tokens](#tokens)). Shared parts: `CheckboxIndicator`, the box with its tick or dash.

The drawing has a `root` board holding, in reading order, an `indicator` layer, an instance of the `CheckboxIndicator` part, and a `label` text layer. Its one variant property is `State`, with the values `default`, `hover`, `focus`, `checked`, `indeterminate`, `disabled` and `invalid`, so its variants are `Default`, `Hover`, `Focus`, `Checked`, `Indeterminate`, `Disabled` and `Invalid`. There is no `variant`, `color` or `size` property (see [Props](#props)).

The label is the caller's `children`, rendered inside the root, Base UI's `<span role="checkbox">`, after the box, so the whole row is one control, named by its own text, toggled by a click anywhere on it and ringed as one when focused. A role of `checkbox` takes its name from its content, so the label needs no `<label>` element, `id` or `aria-labelledby`, and Base UI finds no label to wire; the row, not the 16 px box, is the target, so it meets `size.target-min` with any label; and the contract has visible content come from the caller as `children`. The cost is that a checkbox's content is presentational: a link inside the label would be flattened into its name and can't be reached, so a link goes beside the checkbox (see [Do and don't](#do-and-dont)). The alternative, MUI's bare box with a separate label component, would need a second component Perron doesn't have. A checkbox with no `children` is the box alone and takes its name from `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby` or a `<label htmlFor>` on its `id`.

The box is drawn by the new `CheckboxIndicator` shared part, in its own folder under `packages/perron/src/parts/`, which Checkbox renders through `Checkbox.Indicator`'s `render` callback with `keepMounted` on, passing the part a `mark` of `'tick'` while checked, `'dash'` while indeterminate and none otherwise, read from the indicator's state. The contract's [Shared parts](README.md#shared-parts) table gives the box with its tick or dash to `CheckboxIndicator`, composed in `Checkbox.Indicator` and later in `Menu.CheckboxItemIndicator`, and says the tick and the dash are in `packages/perron/icons/`, added with `CheckboxIndicator`; Base UI's `Checkbox.Indicator` unmounts while unchecked unless `keepMounted` is set, and the part has to stay to draw the empty box; Base UI passes the indicator's `data-checked`, `data-unchecked`, `data-indeterminate`, `data-disabled`, `data-readonly` and `data-invalid` onto the element the callback returns, so the part's CSS reads its states from them with no props for each; and a `mark` read from the state renders one icon, not two with one hidden. Checkbox's own CSS sets only the indicator's place in the row, on its own class `pn-Checkbox-indicator`, never a fill, edge, radius or mark, which the shared-parts check keeps in the part's folder.

| Part (Penpot layer) | What it is                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | Base UI part                                                     | Class                                                                 | `slotProps` key |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------- |
| `root`              | Base UI's `<span role="checkbox">`, focusable, with `aria-checked`: an inline flex row that holds the indicator and the label in reading order; Base UI renders the hidden `<input type="checkbox">` beside it, outside the row      | `Checkbox.Root`                                                  | `pn-Checkbox`                                                         | none            |
| `indicator`         | The box, a `<span>` that Base UI's indicator renders as the `CheckboxIndicator` part, kept mounted: the box's fill and edge, and inside it the tick while checked or the dash while indeterminate, an inline SVG icon, `aria-hidden` | `Checkbox.Indicator`                                             | `pn-Checkbox-indicator`, beside the part's own `pn-CheckboxIndicator` | `indicator`     |
| `label`             | A `<span>` that holds the caller's `children`, after the box; only rendered when `children` renders something                                                                                                                        | none: a span inside `Checkbox.Root`, which has no part for words | `pn-Checkbox-label`                                                   | none            |
| `focusRing`         | The keyboard focus ring: the `:focus-visible` outline `perron.css` draws on the root, round the box and the label together, not an element                                                                                           | `Checkbox.Root`                                                  | none                                                                  | none            |

The hidden input is Base UI's, not a part: Base UI renders it with `aria-hidden`, `tabIndex={-1}` and the visually hidden style, and the caller reaches it through `inputRef`.

## Base UI parts

Imported from `@base-ui/react/checkbox`, at the version pinned in `packages/perron/package.json` (1.9.0 installed).

| Base UI part         | Renders                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | Perron sets                                                                                                                                                                                                            | Passed through                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| -------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Checkbox.Root`      | `<span role="checkbox">` with `tabIndex` 0, `aria-checked` (`true`, `false`, or `mixed` while indeterminate), `aria-readonly` and `aria-required` when set, `aria-disabled` and `tabIndex` −1 while disabled, and `data-checked` or `data-unchecked` (neither while indeterminate), `data-indeterminate`, `data-disabled`, `data-readonly`, `data-required`, and inside a Base UI `Field.Root` `data-invalid`, `data-valid`, `data-dirty`, `data-touched`, `data-filled` and `data-focused`; beside it a hidden `<input type="checkbox">` carrying `name`, `value`, `form`, `required` and the checked state, and an `<input type="hidden">` with `uncheckedValue` while unchecked | `className` (`pn-Checkbox`, then the caller's), `style`, `ref`, `onCheckedChange` adapted from `onChange` (CR-2), and the children: the indicator and the label                                                        | `checked`, `defaultChecked`, `disabled`, `indeterminate`, `parent`, `readOnly`, `required`, `name`, `value`, `uncheckedValue`, `form`, `id`, `inputRef`, `nativeButton`, `render`, `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby` and every other prop of a `<span>`, through `{...rest}` |
| `Checkbox.Indicator` | A `<span>`, here the `CheckboxIndicator` part's, with the root's state attributes and `data-starting-style` and `data-ending-style` while it would animate                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | `keepMounted` (`true`), `render` (the part, with its `mark` from the state), `className` (`pn-Checkbox-indicator`, then the caller's from `slotProps.indicator`), merged over `slotProps.indicator` with Perron's last | `slotProps.indicator`: every prop but `keepMounted` and `render` (CR-4)                                                                                                                                                                                                    |

Base UI already does: it renders the `<span role="checkbox">` with `aria-checked`, and the hidden input beside it that a native `<form>` and `FormData` read, submitting `value`, or `"on"` with no `value`, while checked, and `uncheckedValue` while unchecked when one is given; a click on the root, anywhere on it, or Space on its keyup, clicks the hidden input, which flips the state and calls `onCheckedChange(checked, details)` with `details.reason` `'none'` before it commits, so `details.cancel()` keeps the state as it was; Space's keydown is prevented, so the page doesn't scroll; Enter never toggles, and instead clicks the form's default submit button when the checkbox is in a form; `checked` given controls the state and `defaultChecked` (default `false`) seeds it uncontrolled; `indeterminate` shows `aria-checked="mixed"` and `data-indeterminate`, and sets the hidden input's own `indeterminate`, whatever `checked` is; `readOnly` ignores clicks and Space and sets `aria-readonly`, staying focusable; `disabled` ignores them, sets `aria-disabled` and `tabIndex` −1, so the checkbox leaves the tab order, and disables the hidden input, so a form leaves it out; `required` sets `aria-required` and the input's `required`; with `id` given the hidden input takes it, and a `<label htmlFor>` on that `id`, or a `<label>` round the checkbox, names the root through an `aria-labelledby` Base UI writes, unless an `aria-label` is given; inside a Base UI `Field.Root` or `Form` it takes the field's `name`, `disabled` and validity and sets `data-invalid`; with `render` and `nativeButton`, a native `<button>` root takes the `id` and keeps the button's own keys; with `parent`, inside a Checkbox Group given `allValues`, the checkbox is ticked while the group's list holds as many values as `allValues`, indeterminate while it holds some, and unticked while it holds none, ticks or unticks the whole set when clicked, sets `aria-controls` to the ids of the checkboxes it controls and `data-parent` on itself, and has no `name`, so a form never submits it.

## Props

In MUI's layout. Every prop Checkbox declares gets this description as its JSDoc; every one it inherits from Base UI keeps Base UI's, which the inherited rows give. Slots come last.

Checkbox's state takes Base UI's and MUI's names, `checked`, `defaultChecked` and `indeterminate`, inherited as they are, and the contract's `onChange(event, value, details)`, adapted from Base UI's `onCheckedChange`, its `value` the new checked state, a boolean, and `event` being `details.event`. `value` stays Base UI's and MUI's: the string a checked box submits, as on a native checkbox, since a checkbox's state is `checked`, not a value.

Checkbox takes no `variant`, `color` or `size`, inheriting every other prop of `Checkbox.Root` as it is. One look keeps the box's ink and its 16 px with `typography.body` text everywhere a setting or an answer is asked: the [brand](../foundations/README.md#the-brand) keeps yellow for the one main action, which ticking a box never is, and a status colour on a box would say something the label should; and the API only grows, so each can join later without a break.

Checkbox inherits Base UI's `parent`, which CheckboxGroup (`docs/components/checkbox-group.md`) brings with its `allValues`: a parent checkbox inside a group given `allValues` ticks or unticks the whole set and shows the dash while some of it is ticked (CR-14). It works only inside a Base UI Checkbox Group, which CheckboxGroup's spec adds; it draws nothing new, since a parent is ticked, unticked or indeterminate, each a look Checkbox already has; and adding it is additive, so no caller breaks.

| Name                        | Type                                                                                | Default | Base UI prop         | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| --------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------- | -------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `checked`                   | `boolean`                                                                           | none    | inherited            | Whether the checkbox is currently ticked. To render an uncontrolled checkbox, use the `defaultChecked` prop instead.                                                                                                                           |
| `defaultChecked`            | `boolean`                                                                           | `false` | inherited            | Whether the checkbox is initially ticked. To render a controlled checkbox, use the `checked` prop instead.                                                                                                                                     |
| `onChange`                  | `(event: Event, value: boolean, details: Checkbox.Root.ChangeEventDetails) => void` | none    | `onCheckedChange`    | Called when a click or Space ticks or unticks the checkbox, with the new state as `value`; `details.reason` is `'none'`, and `details.cancel()` keeps the state as it was. `event` is `details.event`. Not called while disabled or read-only. |
| `indeterminate`             | `boolean`                                                                           | `false` | inherited            | Whether the checkbox is in a mixed state: neither ticked, nor unticked.                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `parent`                    | `boolean`                                                                           | `false` | inherited            | Whether the checkbox controls a group of child checkboxes. Must be used in a Checkbox Group.                                                                                                                                                   |
| `disabled`                  | `boolean`                                                                           | `false` | inherited            | Whether the component should ignore user interaction.                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `readOnly`                  | `boolean`                                                                           | `false` | inherited            | Whether the user should be unable to tick or untick the checkbox.                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `required`                  | `boolean`                                                                           | `false` | inherited            | Whether the user must tick the checkbox before submitting a form.                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `name`                      | `string`                                                                            | none    | inherited            | Identifies the field when a form is submitted.                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `value`                     | `string`                                                                            | none    | inherited            | The checkbox's value. Identifies it within a Checkbox Group, falling back to `name` when omitted. When submitting a form, a checked box submits `value`; with no `value`, it submits the native "on".                                          |
| `uncheckedValue`            | `string`                                                                            | none    | inherited            | The value submitted with the form when the checkbox is unchecked. By default, unchecked checkboxes do not submit any value, matching native checkbox behavior.                                                                                 |
| `form`                      | `string`                                                                            | none    | inherited            | Identifies the form that owns the hidden input. Useful when the checkbox is rendered outside the form.                                                                                                                                         |
| `id`                        | `string`                                                                            | none    | inherited            | The id of the input element.                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `inputRef`                  | `React.Ref<HTMLInputElement>`                                                       | none    | inherited            | A ref to access the hidden `<input>` element.                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `nativeButton`              | `boolean`                                                                           | `false` | inherited            | Whether the component renders a native `<button>` element when replacing it via the `render` prop. Set to `true` if the rendered element is a native button.                                                                                   |
| `render`                    | Base UI's `render`                                                                  | none    | inherited            | Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render.                                                      |
| `children`                  | `ReactNode`                                                                         | none    | none                 | The label: what ticking the box turns on or agrees to, in sentence case, such as "Show planned works on the map". It names the checkbox and stays the same ticked or not. Left out, give the checkbox an `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.    |
| `className`, `style`, `ref` | React's                                                                             | none    | none                 | Reaches the root, the `<span role="checkbox">`. `className` is merged after `pn-Checkbox`.                                                                                                                                                     |
| `slotProps.indicator`       | `Omit<Checkbox.Indicator.Props, 'keepMounted' \| 'render'>`                         | none    | `Checkbox.Indicator` | Props for the `indicator` part, the box, all but `keepMounted` and `render`, which stay Checkbox's.                                                                                                                                            |

No label-override props: Checkbox owns no strings.

## Tokens

One row per part, state and property. States are the contract's design states; the deferred design's `State` values map so: `default` is rest, `hover` is `:hover` inside `@media (hover: hover)` on the root, `focus` is `:focus-visible` on the root, `checked` is Base UI's `[data-checked]`, the selected design state, `indeterminate` is `[data-indeterminate]`, `disabled` is `[data-disabled]` and `invalid` is `[data-invalid]`; pressed, which the design doesn't draw, is `:active` on the root. The `indicator` rows are the `CheckboxIndicator` part's CSS, reading the attributes Base UI puts on it, its hover and press read from the element that holds it (CR-6); the `root` and `label` rows are Checkbox's.

The box's side is `size.checkbox`, a new base token of `16px`, "The box of a checkbox, and of a menu's checkbox item", added through the `design-tokens` skill and listed in the size marker on [Layout](../foundations/layout.md#other-layout-properties). No `size.*` token holds a box this small, and an `icon.size.*` token would size a control by an icon's step; 16 px is a little taller than the 14 px text of `typography.body` and fits inside its 21 px line, and with the row as the target (CR-9) it needs no extra room of its own.

The tick and the dash are two new icons, `tick` and `dash`, drawn on the 14 px grid with a 1.8 px round stroke and shown at `icon.size.325` inside the box, each a file in `packages/perron/icons/` that joins `icons.json` under a new "Controls" category. The contract's [Shared parts](README.md#shared-parts) row names the tick icon alone, and CR-5 keeps the dash in the part's folder all the same. The contract says the tick and the dash are in `packages/perron/icons/`, added with `CheckboxIndicator` following [Icons](../foundations/icons.md); `icon.size.325` is the step for marks inline with text, and on its grid the tick leaves a clear margin inside a 16 px box, where a 16 px control icon would touch the edge; `minus`, the zoom-out icon, is drawn on the 16 px grid, and scaling it to the tick's step would break the rule that an icon is never scaled off its grid; and a dash drawn beside the tick keeps one stroke weight in the box.

The box takes the Fields family's edge and hover while unticked, a `color.surface.raised` fill with a `border.width.025` edge in `color.border.control`, `color.surface.hover` laid over the fill as a `linear-gradient` background-image on hover and `color.surface.selected` while pressed, and `radius.xs`, and turns ink while ticked or indeterminate, `color.surface.inverse` with its mark in `color.text.inverse` and a `transparent` edge, `color.surface.inverse-hover` on hover and `color.surface.inverse-pressed` while pressed. [Elevation](../foundations/elevation.md#surfaces) sets inputs on `color.surface.raised`, and `color.border.control` is the edge "that shows where a control is", 3:1 or better on every surface; `radius.xs` is the radius for "small marks and ticks", where `radius.md` would round a 16 px box into a circle's look; ink, not yellow, is the [brand](../foundations/README.md#the-brand)'s interface colour and the fill [Elevation](../foundations/elevation.md#surfaces) gives pressed toggles, as FilterChip's on state is, and moves the box from about 1:1 to 17:1 against the surface; and a `transparent` edge keeps one box size while forced colours still draw it.

A disabled checkbox is drawn as FilterChip's disabled states are: unticked a `transparent` fill with a `color.border.subtle` edge, ticked or indeterminate a `color.surface.inset` fill with its mark in `color.text.tertiary` and a `transparent` edge, and its label in `color.text.tertiary`, with no hover or press. The contract makes disabled a colour, `color.text.tertiary`, never an opacity; a faint edge and an inset fill keep the ticked state readable while disabled; and FilterChip has drawn the same pair for the same states since Wave 3, so one disabled language runs across the library.

An invalid checkbox, inside a Base UI `Field.Root` that marks it so, is drawn with a `color.status.danger` edge, ticked or not, keeping its fill and mark, and no change to its label. The Fields family draws an invalid field's edge in `color.status.danger`, and a ticked box's `transparent` edge takes the same colour, so a required box ticked and still invalid on a later rule shows it; `color.status.danger` reaches 3:1 on every surface; and the error words are the field's, Field's description and error parts, never the box's colour alone.

A read-only checkbox keeps its rest look, unticked or ticked, with no hover or press, and a `default` cursor. The contract's design states have no read-only state; Base UI keeps a read-only checkbox focusable and says `aria-readonly`, so it reads as it is; and a hover that answers a pointer would promise a change the click won't make.

The label is set in `typography.body` with its tracking twin and `color.text.primary`, `space.200` after the box, breaking a word longer than its line with `overflow-wrap: anywhere`, set on the root beside the typography role as the contract's Long words rule asks and inherited by the label, with the root a `max-inline-size: 100%` inline flex row that wraps the label onto more lines beside the box, which stays on the first. [Typography](../foundations/typography.md#roles) sets "sentences and inputs" in `typography.body`, and a checkbox's label is a sentence about a setting rather than a button's name; `space.200`, 8 px, sets the words apart from a 16 px box, a step wider than FilterChip's `space.150` beside a 13 px icon; and HighlightChip's CR-7 found that in an inline flex row `break-word` leaves the words' box as wide as its longest word, where `anywhere` lets a Danish compound break inside a 320 px container.

The root's focus ring is `perron.css`'s, round the box and the label together, on a `radius.xs` root, with the root at least `size.target-min` tall and wide, its block padding `calc((size.target-min - 1lh) / 2)` so one line of label sits centred in it, and the box centred on the label's first line with a block margin of `calc((1lh - size.checkbox) / 2)`. The row is the control ([Anatomy](#anatomy)), so the ring shows what Space will toggle, and `perron.css`'s ring needs no ring of Checkbox's own; `1lh`, which the contract allows, is the root's own `typography.body` line, 21 px, so one line makes the row 24 px tall and a label-less box keeps that height; and the box on the first line stays beside the start of a label that wraps.
