## Keyboard and ARIA

From the Base UI reference for `Checkbox` and the installed `CheckboxRoot` and `useButton`. "From" says who does it.

| Key                | Does                                                                                                                  | From                                  |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| `Tab`, `Shift+Tab` | Moves focus to the checkbox and away; a disabled checkbox is skipped, a read-only one is not                          | The browser, and Base UI's `tabIndex` |
| `Space`            | Ticks or unticks the checkbox on release and calls `onChange` with the new state; its keydown doesn't scroll the page | Base UI                               |
| `Enter`            | Doesn't toggle; in a form, clicks the form's default submit button, as on a native checkbox                           | Base UI                               |

Checkbox adds no keys of its own. Checkboxes in a column are a tab stop each: each is an answer of its own.

| Element      | Role                                                                                                  | Accessible name from                                                                                                                                                                      | States announced                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `root`       | `checkbox`, from Base UI; a native `button` with the `checkbox` role when `render` gives a `<button>` | Its text content, the label's `children`; the caller's `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` win, and with no `children`, a `<label htmlFor>` on its `id` through Base UI's `aria-labelledby` | `aria-checked`, `true`, `false` or `mixed`; `aria-disabled`; `aria-readonly`; `aria-required`; `aria-invalid` inside an invalid Base UI field, on the root and the hidden input; with `parent`, `aria-controls` the ids of the checkboxes it controls |
| `indicator`  | none: presentational inside the checkbox, its mark an `aria-hidden` SVG                               | none                                                                                                                                                                                      | none                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `label`      | none: text inside the checkbox                                                                        | The checkbox's name                                                                                                                                                                       | none                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| hidden input | none: `aria-hidden`, `tabIndex` −1, from Base UI                                                      | none                                                                                                                                                                                      | none                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |

What axe won't catch, from the contract, each with how this component meets it:

- [ ] Everything the eye is told, the ear is told, for every shape each prop accepts: the tick is `aria-checked="true"`, heard as "checked", the dash `aria-checked="mixed"`, heard as "mixed" or "partially checked", the empty box `aria-checked="false"`; the marks are `aria-hidden`, since the state says them; the tertiary colour of a disabled checkbox is `aria-disabled`; the danger edge of an invalid one is the field's error text and `aria-invalid`, never the edge alone.
- [ ] Every landmark and named region has an accessible name: none here; a checkbox is neither. The group of checkboxes is CheckboxGroup's, inside a Fieldset whose legend names it.
- [ ] Every default label can be overridden: none here; Checkbox owns no strings.
- [ ] Every shape the type accepts renders, in every variant: `children` renders a string, an element and a list alike, ticked, unticked, indeterminate and disabled, and nothing at all when it renders nothing, leaving the box alone.
- [ ] A hidden copy kept for animation is `aria-hidden`, and a collapsed region is `inert`: none here; the box kept mounted is the box itself, not a copy, and nothing collapses.
- [ ] Native semantics first: Base UI's `role="checkbox"` on a `<span>`, with a native `<input type="checkbox">` beside it for the form; with `render` and `nativeButton`, a native `<button>`.
- [ ] Focus moves in reading order and returns on close: each checkbox is one tab stop in document order, focus stays on the checkbox it toggles, and it opens nothing to return from.
- [ ] Every target is at least `size.target-min` square: the smallest target is a checkbox with no label, its root `size.target-min` (24 px) square round the 16 px box; with a label, the whole row is the target.
- [ ] Loops stop when the system asks for less motion: none here; Checkbox has no loop and no transition.

## Owned strings

No owned strings: every word comes from the caller, as `children` or an `aria-label`, and the state is heard from `aria-checked`, in the screen reader's own words.

## Component rules

Rules for this component alone, numbered so the build and the review can cite them.

- **CR-1.** Base UI's Checkbox already gives the `role="checkbox"`, the click and Space toggling, Enter submitting the form, `aria-checked` with `mixed`, the hidden input and its form value, the controlled and uncontrolled state, the cancellable change, and the disabled, read-only and required behaviour, so Checkbox rebuilds none of it and adds no key or click handlers.
- **CR-2.** Checkbox adapts Base UI's `onCheckedChange(checked, details)` into `onChange(details.event, checked, details)` inside itself, and exposes neither `onCheckedChange` nor the `<span>`'s native `onChange`: its props type omits `onCheckedChange`, `onChange`, `children`, `className`, `style` and `ref` from `Checkbox.Root.Props` and declares its own `onChange`, `children`, `className` (a string), `style` and `ref`, inheriting every other Base UI prop as it is. It takes no `variant`, `color` or `size`, and sets no `data-variant`, `data-color` or `data-size`.
- **CR-3.** It takes `{...rest}` before its own attributes and its own props out of `rest` first (`onChange`, `children`, `className`, `style`, `slotProps`; an inherited Base UI prop such as `checked`, `name` or `nativeButton` stays in `rest`, keeping Base UI's default), and merges `className` after `pn-Checkbox`; `ref` reaches the root, the `<span role="checkbox">`.
- **CR-4.** The indicator is `Checkbox.Indicator` with `keepMounted` and a `render` callback that returns the `CheckboxIndicator` part with the props Base UI passes and a `mark` of `'tick'` while `state.indeterminate` is false and `state.checked` is true, `'dash'` while `state.indeterminate` is true, and none otherwise; `slotProps.indicator`, typed `Omit<Checkbox.Indicator.Props, 'keepMounted' | 'render'>` so a caller can't pass either, is merged under these with `mergeProps` (`@base-ui/react/merge-props`), as Dialog merges its Base UI parts, Checkbox's own last, and its class set after the merge by `withClass`, `pn-Checkbox-indicator` first. Checkbox's CSS sets only the indicator's `margin-block` and `flex` on `.pn-Checkbox-indicator`; the box's size, fill, edge, radius, mark and their states are the part's, in its own folder, which no other file names (`npm run gates -- shared-parts`).
- **CR-5.** The `CheckboxIndicator` part draws the box and its mark, the `tick` or the `dash` icon inlined as JSX from its file, unchanged but for `width` and `height`, with the classes `perron-icon` and `pn-CheckboxIndicator-mark`, `aria-hidden="true"` and `focusable="false"`, and draws no mark for none. It sets `--perron-icon-size` to `icon.size.325` and centres the mark (`display: inline-flex`, `align-items: center`, `justify-content: center`). The mark draws in `currentColor`, its colour set on the box. The part takes no state props of its own beyond `mark`, reading its states from Base UI's attributes, so `Menu.CheckboxItemIndicator` can render it the same way later. The build adds both icon files following [Icons](../foundations/icons.md), joins them to `icons.json`, leaves the contract's `CheckboxIndicator` row naming the tick icon alone, adds `size.checkbox` (`16px`, "The box of a checkbox, and of a menu's checkbox item") to the base tokens through the `design-tokens` skill, and runs `npm run tokens` to rebuild the icon set's table and the size marker on [Layout](../foundations/layout.md#other-layout-properties).
- **CR-6.** Hover lays its colour on the box when the pointer is over the element that holds it, the whole row, read in the part's CSS as `[role]:hover > .pn-CheckboxIndicator` inside `@media (hover: hover)`; pressed takes the pressed tokens, a step past hover, on `[role]:active > .pn-CheckboxIndicator`, in a rule after it and outside the media query, so a touch press shows. The holder is always a control with a role (`checkbox`, later `menuitemcheckbox`), which `[role]` names. Neither applies to a disabled or read-only box: both rules exclude `[data-disabled]` and `[data-readonly]`.
- **CR-7.** Focus uses the ring `perron.css` draws on the root's `:focus-visible`; the component draws no ring of its own and never removes the outline.
- **CR-8.** The states keep the geometry: hover, pressed, focus, ticked, indeterminate, disabled, read-only and invalid change colours only, never the box's size, the edge's width, the radius, the gap, the padding or the typography, so ticking a box never moves its label. Every state draws the `border.width.025` edge, `transparent` while ticked or indeterminate, so every state shares one box.
- **CR-9.** The root is the target: an inline flex row, `align-items: flex-start`, `justify-content: center`, at least `size.target-min` tall and wide, its block padding `calc((size.target-min - 1lh) / 2)` over its own `typography.body` line, and `max-inline-size: 100%`. The box keeps its size (`flex: none`) and sits centred on the label's first line through its block margin, `calc((1lh - size.checkbox) / 2)`; the label wraps beside it (`min-inline-size: 0`, and `overflow-wrap: anywhere`, set on the root beside its `typography.body` and inherited). With no label, the box sits centred in its 24 px square.
- **CR-10.** The label span renders only when `children` renders something (the `given` helper), after the indicator in reading order, so the box sits on the start side in right-to-left text. Its colour is the root's: `color.text.primary`, and `color.text.tertiary` while `[data-disabled]`; read-only and invalid don't change it.
- **CR-11.** In `@media (forced-colors: active)`, a ticked or indeterminate box that is not disabled takes `Highlight` with its mark in `HighlightText` and `forced-color-adjust: none`, since forced colours drop its ink fill and leave a `CanvasText` tick on `Canvas`, where `Highlight` keeps the ticked state as plain as the selected state [Accessibility](../foundations/accessibility.md#what-a-person-checks) asks to show. A disabled box takes a `GrayText` edge, or, ticked or indeterminate, a `GrayText` fill with a `Canvas` mark under `forced-color-adjust: none`, so a disabled ticked box still shows it is ticked; a disabled root's label takes `GrayText`, since the `<span>` isn't natively disabled and the system can't tell. An unticked box keeps the edge the system draws for its border.
- **CR-12.** Changes of state are immediate: no `duration.*` token fits a box's state change, so the CSS has no transition, and the kept-mounted indicator never animates in or out.
- **CR-13.** The cursor is `pointer` on the root, as on SegmentedControl's segments and Tabs' tabs, and `default` while `[data-disabled]` or `[data-readonly]`.
- **CR-14.** `parent` is Base UI's, inherited as it is, and used only inside a CheckboxGroup given `allValues`: Base UI gives the parent its ticked, unticked and indeterminate state from the group's list, its `aria-checked`, `aria-controls` and `data-parent`, and its click on the whole set, and Checkbox adds none of it. A parent is drawn as any checkbox, the dash while indeterminate from CR-4's `mark`, and Checkbox's CSS sets nothing on `[data-parent]`. `CheckboxProps` inherits `parent` from `Checkbox.Root.Props` with Base UI's JSDoc, since `packages/perron/src/components/Checkbox/Checkbox.tsx` doesn't omit it; the parent's story is CheckboxGroup's `SelectAll`, since a parent needs its group.

## Stories

The deferred design's page draws one variant property, `State` (`default`, `hover`, `focus`, `checked`, `indeterminate`, `disabled`, `invalid`), and each of its stories is named by its variant name (`penpot/README.md`, "Conventions"). Each renders the checkbox "Show planned works on the map"; the hover and focus stories render at rest: the visual check drives the state, and their `play` tests check it. `Default` is the [subject story](README.md#root), which the contract story renders, and its args, the label alone, render the checkbox alone and pass every rule.

A ticked and disabled checkbox, a read-only one and the ticked hover, which Base UI's attributes produce beside `data-disabled`, `data-readonly` and `:hover` but the drawing's single `State` property can't show, get stories and `play` checks with no Penpot variant of their own: `CheckedDisabled`, `ReadOnly`, and a hover check in `Checked`'s `play`. So does `Shapes`, the label as an element and as a list in each state, beside labels that render nothing. The Tokens table already gives all three, FilterChip handles its selected and disabled state the same way, and a second variant property, `checked`, would name the drawing's variants after a prop, `TrueHover`, where the `State` property already carries `checked`.

| Story             | Shows                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | `play` test                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Default`         | Unticked, at rest, "Show planned works on the map"; the subject story                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | The root is a `<span>` with `role="checkbox"`, class `pn-Checkbox`, `aria-checked="false"` and `data-unchecked`, and the `ref` reaches it; its name is "Show planned works on the map"; the indicator has `pn-Checkbox-indicator` and `pn-CheckboxIndicator` and no mark; a click on the label ticks it, sets `aria-checked="true"` and the tick, and calls `onChange` once with `true`; Space unticks it and calls `onChange` with `false`; Enter changes nothing and calls no `onChange`, ending unticked |
| `Hover`           | Unticked, hover                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | Hovering the root lays `color.surface.hover` over the box's `color.surface.raised` fill and keeps the `color.border.control` edge                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `Focus`           | Unticked, focus                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | Tab gives the root `:focus-visible` and the ring round the box and the label; Shift+Tab leaves it                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `Checked`         | Ticked, with `defaultChecked`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | The root has `aria-checked="true"` and `data-checked`; the box's computed background is `color.surface.inverse` and its mark's colour `color.text.inverse`; hovering sets `color.surface.inverse-hover`; the box's size and the label's position match an unticked checkbox's (CR-8)                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `Indeterminate`   | Indeterminate, "Show all lines", with `indeterminate`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | The root has `aria-checked="mixed"` and `data-indeterminate` and no `data-checked`; the box shows the dash and no tick, on `color.surface.inverse`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `Disabled`        | Unticked, disabled                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | The root has `aria-disabled="true"`, `data-disabled` and `tabIndex` −1, Tab skips it, and a click neither changes `aria-checked` nor calls `onChange`; the label's colour is `color.text.tertiary`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `Invalid`         | Unticked and `required`, inside a Base UI `Field.Root` with `invalid`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | The root has `data-invalid`, `aria-invalid="true"` and `aria-required="true"`, and the hidden input `aria-invalid="true"`; the box's edge is `color.status.danger`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `CheckedDisabled` | Ticked and disabled                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | The root keeps `aria-checked="true"` and has `data-disabled`; the box's computed background is `color.surface.inset` and its mark's colour `color.text.tertiary`; a click changes nothing                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `ReadOnly`        | Ticked and `readOnly`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | The root has `aria-readonly="true"` and stays in the tab order; a click and Space change nothing and call no `onChange`; hovering adds no hover colour                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `Controlled`      | A checkbox given `checked` and `onChange` from the story's state                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | A click calls `onChange` with `true` and `details.reason` `'none'`; `aria-checked` changes only once the story sets `checked`, and a checkbox whose caller ignores the change, given `checked` of `false`, stays unticked; an `onChange` that calls `details.cancel()` keeps the state; the story ends unticked                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `InForm`          | Two checkboxes in a `<form>`: "Show planned works on the map" with `name="planned"`, and "Show bus routes" with `name="routes"`, `value="bus"` and `uncheckedValue="none"`, ticked                                                                                                                     | The form's `FormData` has `planned` only once it is ticked, as `"on"`, and `routes` as `"bus"` while ticked and `"none"` once unticked; Enter on a checkbox submits the form through its submit button, which the story stops; the story ends with both as they started                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `Shapes`          | The label as an element, "Show planned works on the map" in `<strong>`, and as a list, "Show bus routes" with "bus" in `<strong>`, each unticked, ticked, indeterminate and disabled; then three boxes whose `children`, `false`, `''` and `[null, false]`, render nothing, each named by `aria-label` | Each element and list label renders in a label span and names its checkbox, with `aria-checked` `false`, `true`, `mixed` and `false` with `aria-disabled`, and the tick or the dash where its state calls for one; each box whose `children` render nothing renders no label span and is named by its `aria-label`                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `LongLabel`       | A 320 px container holding "Vis driftsforstyrrelsesmeddelelser for alle linjer i hele hovedstadsområdet"                                                                                                                                                                                               | The label wraps onto more than one line and stays inside the container (its `scrollWidth` equals its `clientWidth`); the box stays on the first line, its top above the label's second line                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `WithoutLabel`    | The box alone, named by `aria-label` "Show planned works on the map"                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | No label span renders; the name is the `aria-label`; the root is at least `size.target-min` square and a click on it ticks the box                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |

## Do and don't

For a caller using the component, with the reason.

| Do                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | Don't                                                                                                                             |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Use Checkbox for an answer or a setting that is on or off on its own, applied when the form is sent, such as agreeing to a notice                                                                                               | Use it for a filter on the map that takes effect at once: that is a FilterChip's, pressed and seen at once                        |
| Write the label as what ticking it turns on, in sentence case, the same ticked or not: "Show planned works on the map"                                                                                                          | Write it as a question or a negative ("Don't show planned works?"): a tick on a negative reads backwards                          |
| Put a link about the setting next to the checkbox, outside its `children`                                                                                                                                                       | Put a link inside the label: a checkbox's content is flattened into its name, so the link can't be reached or pressed             |
| Give `name`, and `value` where the form needs more than `"on"`, so the answer reaches the form; connect a form library through its controller                                                                                   | Read the state back from the DOM or keep a hidden input of your own: Base UI's hidden input already carries it                    |
| Use `indeterminate` for a box that stands for a set partly on, such as "All lines" over the lines below it, and set it from the set's state, or give it `parent` inside a CheckboxGroup with `allValues`, which sets it for you | Use it as a third answer to one question: "mixed" says some of a set, and Space always turns it to ticked or unticked             |
| Show why a box is invalid in words, from its field                                                                                                                                                                              | Rely on the danger edge alone: colour is never the only sign ([Accessibility](../foundations/accessibility.md#rules))             |
| Group related checkboxes in a CheckboxGroup, whose legend names the group                                                                                                                                                       | Make a list of checkboxes one tab stop, or use them for one choice among several: that is a radio group's or a SegmentedControl's |
| Keep `onChange` for the box's state, and cancel it with `details.cancel()` when the change must not happen                                                                                                                      | Set `aria-checked` yourself or toggle a class: Base UI keeps the state, the attribute and the input in step                       |

title: CheckboxGroup

# CheckboxGroup A named set of checkboxes that answer one question together, such as which modes the map shows, holding the ticked values as one list, with a line of help and an error message tied to the set, submitted with a form under one name, and, where the set needs one, a parent checkbox that ticks or unticks them all. The design is deferred (ADR 0010, `docs/adr/0010-unattended-runs-with-design-deferred.md`): there is no read-back, code map or export, and this spec decides what the drawing would, from the [contract](README.md), the [foundations](../foundations/README.md), [content design](../content-design.md), the tokens, the Base UI reference for `CheckboxGroup`, `Field` and `Fieldset` (`@base-ui/react` 1.9.0, installed) and the specs of the entries in its `dependsOn`, [Checkbox](checkbox.md) and [Fieldset](fieldset.md), and [RadioGroup](radio-group.md)'s spec, for the group's prop names. No ROADMAP line names CheckboxGroup, and the extracted prototype component is not in any branch this run can reach, so nothing here rests on it. Fieldset's spec already says how a group builds on it: CheckboxGroup renders Fieldset with Base UI's `CheckboxGroup` through `render`, so the group takes Fieldset's legend, its name and its disabled state (Fieldset's CR-5), and takes its description and error through Base UI's `Field`, as Base UI's forms guide puts `}>` inside a `Field.Root`. ## Anatomy Penpot page `Components/CheckboxGroup`. Family: none, as Fieldset's: the group draws no box, fill or border, and its checkboxes keep their own look. Shared parts: `VisuallyHidden`, through Fieldset, for a hidden legend. The drawing has a `root` board, a vertical flex column holding, in reading order, a `legend` text layer, a `description` text layer, the caller's checkboxes, each an instance of [Checkbox](checkbox.md) in a layer named `checkbox`, a parent checkbox first among them where the group has one, and an `error` text layer. Its one variant property is `State`, with the values `default`, `disabled` and `invalid`, so its variants are `Default`, `Disabled` and `Invalid`. There is no `variant`, `color` or `size` property, as Checkbox and Fieldset have none. The root is one element that is Base UI's `Field.Root`, Perron's Fieldset and Base UI's `CheckboxGroup` at once: `Field.Root` renders through `render` as the Fieldset, and the Fieldset renders through `render` as Base UI's `CheckboxGroup`, a `

Every prop CheckboxGroup declares gets this description as its JSDoc; every one it inherits from Base UI keeps Base UI's, which the inherited rows give. Slots come last. The group's state takes the contract's names: `value` and `defaultValue`, inherited from Base UI's `CheckboxGroup` as they are, and `onChange(event, value, details)`, adapted from its `onValueChange`, its `value` the new list of ticked values and `event` being `details.event`. Its form name is `name`, as the contract asks of every composite control. Its help and its error take Field's names and behaviour, `description` and `error` (CR-4), and it inherits Field's `invalid`, `validate`, `validationMode`, `validationDebounceTime`, `dirty`, `touched` and `actionsRef` from `Field.Root.Props`, as Field does, so a form library's controller and a `validate` reach Base UI with no prop of its own. Fieldset's spec left a group's description and error to CheckboxGroup and RadioGroup, through Base UI's `Field`; a set of checkboxes in a form is the common place for "Choose at least one mode", which only a `validate` on the list or a caller's `error` can say, and [Accessibility](../foundations/accessibility.md#rules) wants that said in words, never by the boxes' red edge alone; the contract's `name` on a group needs `Field.Root` anyway, since Base UI's `CheckboxGroup` has no `name` and gives its checkboxes the field's, so the group renders its own `Field.Root` and a caller can't wrap one round it, as a caller of RadioGroup, whose Base UI root takes `name` itself, can; and the same names as Field's keep one form vocabulary across the library. Its name is the `label` prop, with `hiddenLabel` to hear it without seeing it, as RadioGroup's and SearchField's are, passed to Fieldset as its `legend` and `hiddenLegend`. A checkbox group and a radio group are the two sets of choices that answer one question, and the `api-consistency` skill holds a new member to its siblings' names, so a caller who swaps one for the other changes only the component; a group with one value list is named as a field is, and a caller reads `label` on every named form control in the library; and the legend stays the part's name, its `slotProps` key and its class, where the markup shows it. CheckboxGroup takes Base UI's `allValues`, the value of every checkbox in the set, and [Checkbox](checkbox.md) takes Base UI's `parent`, so a parent checkbox inside the group ticks or unticks the whole set and shows the indeterminate dash while some are ticked. Perron's Checkbox shipped without `parent`, leaving it to this spec; a "Select all" over a list of modes or lines is the common case a group of checkboxes meets, and Base UI already keeps the parent's state, its `aria-controls` and the dash; Checkbox's indeterminate look is already drawn, so the parent needs no new state; and adding `parent` to Checkbox is additive, so no caller breaks. `allValues` is inherited as it is, and Checkbox's `parent` row, rule and the removal of `parent` from its omitted props are in [Checkbox](checkbox.md)'s spec (its CR-14), built with this component (CR-12). The group lays its checkboxes out in one column only, with no `row` or orientation prop, as RadioGroup does. Checkbox labels are sentences of different lengths that wrap ([Checkbox](checkbox.md)'s CR-9), and a row of them wraps raggedly at 320 px; a row of filters applied at once is FilterChip's, pressed and seen at once; and a `row` boolean, MUI's `FormGroup` name, can join later without a break. The group takes no `optional` mark, unlike Field. A set of checkboxes with nothing ticked is usually an answer of its own, "none of these", so the mark would sit on almost every group and say little; a group that needs at least one says so in its `description` and its `validate`; and leaving it out keeps CheckboxGroup free of owned strings, while `optional` and `optionalLabel` can join later without a break. `CheckboxGroupProps` extends `Omit` and `Pick`, so `value`, `defaultValue`, `allValues`, `render` and Field's validation props are inherited with Base UI's JSDoc, and declares `label`, `hiddenLabel`, `description`, `error`, `disabled`, `name`, `onChange`, `children`, `className`, `style`, `ref` and `slotProps`. `disabled` is declared again for its JSDoc, since it reaches more than one Base UI part, `Field.Root` and the Fieldset that hands it to Base UI's `CheckboxGroup`; `name` is declared because neither Base UI type it extends gives it: `CheckboxGroup.Props` has none, and it is not picked from `Field.Root.Props`, so it reaches `Field.Root` alone. `id`, the `aria-*` attributes and the `
    `'s others reach the root through `{...rest}` and get no row. CheckboxGroup takes no `variant`, `color` or `size`, so its root carries no `data-variant`, `data-color` or `data-size`, and Base UI's state attributes are its data attributes. States are the contract's design states; the deferred design's `State` values map so: `default` is rest, `disabled` is `[data-disabled]` and `invalid` is `[data-invalid]`, with the error mounted. The group takes no pointer or focus, so hover, focus, pressed and selected are its checkboxes' looks, drawn by [Checkbox](checkbox.md), never the group's; highlighted and open don't apply. The root keeps Fieldset's column, its reset of the browser's frame and its one `space.200` gap, and adds `align-items: flex-start`, so each checkbox keeps its own width. Fieldset's column stretches its children across it, and a stretched Checkbox, whose root is an inline flex row with `justify-content: center` so a label-less box sits centred in its 24 px square, would centre its box and label in the group's width; the legend, the description and the error then size to their text, up to the group's width, where they wrap. The group keeps Fieldset's one `space.200` gap between every part, the legend, the description, each checkbox and the error, and sets no gap of its own. Each checkbox row is already `size.target-min` tall with its label centred in it, so 8 px between rows gives 32 px a row, room for a finger between targets without loosening the set; one gap on the root keeps the parts the root's own children, as Fieldset's CR-2 asks, where Field's `space.100` between its label and its help would need a negative margin or a wrapper; and Fieldset's CR-5 leaves a group's spacing to its own class, which can tighten it later with no change to the API. The description and the error take Field's look: `typography.body-sm`, the description in `color.text.secondary` and the error in `color.text.danger`, each `color.text.tertiary` while disabled, Base UI's list of several messages with no margin and `space.400` before its items, and no `warning` icon before the error. A group's help and error read as a field's do on the same form; `typography.body-sm` is for supporting sentences; `color.text.danger` reaches 4.5:1 on every surface in both themes ([Accessibility](../foundations/accessibility.md)); and the error's words carry its meaning, the checkboxes' danger edges beside them. Field's look is written again in the group's own CSS, on its own classes, since Field's classes are Field's (CR-7). An invalid group keeps its legend and description as they are and marks each checkbox: Base UI sets `data-invalid` and `aria-invalid` on every `Checkbox.Root` inside an invalid field, and Checkbox's `CheckboxIndicator` draws its box's edge in `color.status.danger` on `[data-invalid]`, ticked or not. A disabled group's checkboxes take Checkbox's disabled look, and its legend Fieldset's. The group keeps its rest look while Base UI marks it `data-focused`, `data-filled`, `data-dirty`, `data-touched` or `data-valid`, as Field does: none is a design state the contract names, each focused checkbox already shows its ring, and a "valid" look would claim more than a check knows. A parent checkbox takes Checkbox's own looks, ticked, unticked or its indeterminate dash, and sits in the group's one column with the boxes it controls, at the same start edge and the same `space.200` gap, with no indent. Fieldset's CR-2 keeps every checkbox the root's own child, with no wrapper to indent, and an indent drawn on the boxes after the parent would need a sibling selector, which the contract's "Selectors: one class, then attributes" rules out; title: Fieldset
markdown:
# Fieldset

A named group of related controls, such as the modes shown on the map or the fields of a report form: the group's name above, the caller's controls below it, and one switch that disables them all.

<!-- run notes -->

The design is deferred (ADR 0010, `docs/adr/0010-unattended-runs-with-design-deferred.md`): there is no read-back, code map or export, and this spec decides what the drawing would, from the [contract](README.md), the [foundations](../foundations/README.md), [content design](../content-design.md), the tokens and the Base UI reference for `Fieldset` (`@base-ui/react` 1.9.0, installed). Fieldset has nothing in `dependsOn`, no ROADMAP line names it, and the extracted prototype component is not in any branch this run can reach, so nothing here rests on it. Field, the single-field wrapper, is being built beside it and its spec is not yet in a branch this run can read, so the legend's look follows [SearchField](search-field.md)'s label, the one field label that has shipped.

CheckboxGroup and RadioGroup build on Fieldset next: each renders Fieldset with its own Base UI root through `render`, as Base UI's forms guide composes `<Fieldset.Root render={<RadioGroup />}>`, so the group takes Fieldset's legend, its name and its disabled state (CR-5).

## Anatomy

Penpot page `Components/Fieldset`. Family: none, since it draws no box, fill or border and joins no family's treatment; its controls keep their own. Shared parts: `VisuallyHidden`, for a hidden legend.

The drawing has no variant property, so its one variant is `Default`; its design states are rest and disabled, since the group itself takes no pointer or focus. Its layers are the parts below.

| Part (Penpot layer) | What it is                                                                                                                                                                                 | Base UI part      | Class                | `slotProps` key |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------- | -------------------- | --------------- |
| `root`              | A native `<fieldset>`, a flex column that stacks the legend over the caller's controls and takes its container's width, named by the legend. Penpot's main instance, a vertical flex board | `Fieldset.Root`   | `pn-Fieldset`        | none            |
| `legend`            | A `<div>` holding the caller's `legend`, the group's name, first in the root; with `hiddenLegend`, a `VisuallyHidden` span the eye never sees                                              | `Fieldset.Legend` | `pn-Fieldset-legend` | `legend`        |

The caller's `children`, the controls, follow the legend straight inside the root, with no wrapper of Fieldset's own: a component that renders Fieldset as a Base UI group (CR-5) needs its items to be the group's own children, and the root's one gap spaces the legend and each control alike (CR-2).

Fieldset takes no description and no error message. Base UI's Fieldset has only `Fieldset.Root` and `Fieldset.Legend`, the two parts the registry entry lists, and its forms guide puts a group's description and error in a `Field.Root` around the fieldset, through `Field.Description` and `Field.Error`, where Base UI ties them to the group as the field's control. CheckboxGroup renders its own `Field.Root` round the fieldset and takes them as its `description` and `error` props; a RadioGroup takes them from a `Field.Root` the caller wraps round it; and either can join Fieldset later as an optional prop without a break.

## Base UI parts

Imported from `@base-ui/react/fieldset`, at the version pinned in `packages/perron/package.json` (1.9.0).

| Base UI part      | Renders                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | Perron sets                                                                                                                                                                                                | Passed through                                                                                             |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Fieldset.Root`   | `<fieldset>`, or the element `render` gives, with `aria-labelledby` the legend's id, the native `disabled` attribute and `data-disabled` while it or a fieldset round it is disabled                                      | `className` (`pn-Fieldset`, then the caller's), `ref`, `disabled` from `disabled`, and its children: the legend part, then `children`                                                                      | `render`, `style`, `name`, `form`, `id` and every other prop of a native `<fieldset>`, through `{...rest}` |
| `Fieldset.Legend` | `<div>` with an `id` (`slotProps.legend.id`, else one Base UI generates and registers with the root), and `data-disabled` while the fieldset is disabled; with `hiddenLegend`, the `VisuallyHidden` span through `render` | `className` (`pn-Fieldset-legend`, then the caller's, through `withClass`), `legend` as children, and `render: <VisuallyHidden />` when `hiddenLegend`, merged with `mergeProps`, Perron's own last (CR-4) | `slotProps.legend`                                                                                         |

Base UI already does: it gives the root the legend's id as `aria-labelledby`, whatever id the legend ends up with, so the group is named by its legend; it sets the native `disabled` attribute on the `<fieldset>`, so the browser disables every native control inside it (`<input>`, `<button>`, `<select>`, `<textarea>`) and takes them out of the tab order; it sets `data-disabled` on the root and the legend; and it shares the disabled state through its context, so a nested `Fieldset.Root`, a `Field.Root` and a `RadioGroup` inside it are disabled too, a parent's `disabled` winning over a child's `false`. With `render`, it hands the rendered element `aria-labelledby` and `disabled` as props, and an element's own props win over them.

## Props

In MUI's layout. Every prop here gets this description as its JSDoc. Slots come last.

| Name                 | Type                    | Default | Base UI prop                 | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| -------------------- | ----------------------- | ------- | ---------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `legend`             | `ReactNode`             | none    | `Fieldset.Legend`'s children | Required. The group's name, in sentence case, a few words or a short question, such as "Show on the map": shown above the controls, and the group's accessible name.                                            |
| `hiddenLegend`       | `boolean`               | `false` | none                         | Whether the legend is heard but not seen. Use it where a heading right above already names the group for the eye, so the group keeps its name for the ear.                                                      |
| `disabled`           | `boolean`               | `false` | `disabled`                   | Whether every control in the group ignores the pointer and the keys. Native controls leave the tab order; Base UI's fields and groups inside take the disabled look; a fieldset round this one disables it too. |
| `children`           | `ReactNode`             | none    | none                         | The group's controls, in reading order, below the legend: checkboxes, radios, or fields.                                                                                                                        |
| `render`             | Base UI's `render`      | none    | inherited                    | Inherited from Base UI: swaps the root element and keeps the behaviour, the class and the data attributes. CheckboxGroup and RadioGroup give their Base UI group here.                                          |
| `className`, `style` | React's                 | none    | none                         | Reaches the root. `className` is merged after `pn-Fieldset`.                                                                                                                                                    |
| `ref`                | `Ref<HTMLElement>`      | none    | none                         | Reaches the root: the `<fieldset>`, or the element `render` gives.                                                                                                                                              |
| `slotProps.legend`   | `Fieldset.Legend.Props` | none    | `Fieldset.Legend`            | Props for the `legend` part. Its `id` is the one the group's `aria-labelledby` points at.                                                                                                                       |

`FieldsetProps` extends `Fieldset.Root.Props`, so `render` comes inherited with Base UI's JSDoc and is not declared again, and declares `legend`, `hiddenLegend`, `disabled`, `children`, `ref` and `slotProps`. `disabled` is a native `<fieldset>` attribute that `Fieldset.Root.Props` already carries; Fieldset declares it again so it gets its JSDoc and its `false` default. The other attributes of a `<fieldset>`, such as `name`, `form` and `id`, reach the root through `{...rest}` and get no row, as the contract's Props section says. No owned string, so no `*Label` prop.

- The group's name is the `legend` prop, required: the name of Base UI's part and of the HTML element it stands for, and a group without a name is announced as an unnamed group. `hiddenLegend` keeps it for the ear where the eye needs none.
- Fieldset ships with no `variant`, `size` or `color`, one look everywhere, so its root carries no `data-variant`, `data-size` or `data-color`; Base UI's `data-disabled` is its one data attribute. Any of the three can join later as an optional prop without a break.
- `hiddenLegend`, a boolean, default `false`, renders the legend through the `VisuallyHidden` shared part. It follows SearchField's `hiddenLabel`, MUI's own name for a field without a visible label, with the part's name in place of "label", and works as it does: a settings group under a Section heading that already names it keeps its name for the ear without saying it twice to the eye, and CheckboxGroup and RadioGroup can pass their own `hiddenLabel` straight to it. No name here is one the contract's [Names from other libraries](README.md#names-from-other-libraries) table bans.

## Tokens

One row per part, state and property. Fieldset has no hover, focus or pressed state of its own: its controls keep theirs. Its design states are rest and disabled.

| Part     | State    | Property                      | Token                                                    |
| -------- | -------- | ----------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `root`   | rest     | `gap`                         | `space.200`                                              |
| `root`   | rest     | `border`, `margin`, `padding` | none: `0`, resetting the browser's fieldset frame (CR-1) |
| `root`   | rest     | `min-inline-size`             | none: `0`, resetting the browser's `min-content` (CR-1)  |
| `root`   | disabled | none                          | none: the controls take their own disabled look          |
| `legend` | rest     | `font`, `letter-spacing`      | `typography.label`, with its tracking twin               |
| `legend` | rest     | `color`                       | `color.text.primary`                                     |
| `legend` | rest     | `margin`, `padding`           | none: `0`                                                |
| `legend` | disabled | `color`                       | `color.text.tertiary`, on `[data-disabled]`              |

The root is a flex column (`display: flex; flex-direction: column`), so the legend and each control stack in the DOM's order, `space.200` apart, and it takes its container's width. With `hiddenLegend`, the `VisuallyHidden` span is taken out of the flow by the part's own declarations, so the first control sits at the top with no gap above it.

The legend takes `typography.label` in `color.text.primary`, as SearchField's label does, rather than `typography.label-sm`, whose description names "field and stat labels": a RadioGroup's name then reads the same as a text field's name in the same form, SearchField already set field labels in `typography.label`, its 600 weight stands out from options set in `typography.body`, and the Field spec being written beside this one should match it either way.

The root puts one gap, `space.200`, between the legend and each control, with no wrapper round the controls: 8 px is the gap the components use between items in a row and keeps options in a list close under their name, it sits between the 4 px of SearchField's label over its box and the 12 px between the parts of a panel, and one gap on the root keeps the controls the root's own children, which CheckboxGroup and RadioGroup need (CR-5); a group of fields that wants more room sets its own `gap` through `className`.

## Keyboard and ARIA

Fieldset has no keys of its own and is never focusable. Its controls are reached in reading order, and keep their own keys.

| Key         | Does                                                                                                       | From        |
| ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------- |
| `Tab`       | Moves to the first focusable control in the group, then on through the rest; skips them all while disabled | The browser |
| `Shift+Tab` | Moves back through the controls, out to what came before the group                                         | The browser |

| Element  | Role                                                                                                                           | Accessible name from                                       | States announced                                                                                                                                |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `root`   | `group`, native to `<fieldset>`; the rendered element's own role with `render`, such as `radiogroup` from Base UI's RadioGroup | `aria-labelledby`, the legend's id, from Base UI: its text | None on the group itself; the native `disabled` attribute disables each native control in it, and each control announces its own disabled state |
| `legend` | None (generic `div`, or a `span` when hidden)                                                                                  | None: its text names the root                              | None                                                                                                                                            |

What axe won't catch, from the contract, each with how this component meets it:

- [ ] Everything the eye is told, the ear is told, for every shape each prop accepts: the legend the eye reads above the controls is the group's name for the ear, through `aria-labelledby`; a hidden legend is still the name; the disabled look of the legend matches the disabled state the browser announces on each control in the group, since the native `disabled` attribute disables them all.
- [ ] Every landmark and named region has an accessible name: the root is a `group`, not a landmark, and is always named by its legend, since `legend` is required (CR-3).
- [ ] Every default label can be overridden: none here; Fieldset owns no string.
- [ ] Every shape the type accepts renders, in every variant: `legend` renders a string, an element and an array; it sits in a `<div>`, or a `<span>` when hidden, so it takes phrasing content, and a long Danish compound wraps inside the root's width (CR-1).
- [ ] A hidden copy kept for animation is `aria-hidden`, and a collapsed region is `inert`: none here; nothing animates or collapses.
- [ ] Native semantics first: a native `<fieldset>` and its `group` role, its native `disabled` attribute, and Base UI's `aria-labelledby`; Perron adds no ARIA.
- [ ] Focus moves in reading order and returns on close: the legend comes first in the DOM and on screen, then the controls in the caller's order; Fieldset never moves focus, and nothing in it closes.
- [ ] Every target is at least `size.target-min` square: Fieldset has no target of its own; its controls are the caller's components, which keep their own sizes.
- [ ] Loops stop when the system asks for less motion: none here; nothing moves.

## Owned strings

No owned strings: every word Fieldset shows or announces comes from the caller, through `legend` and `children`, and the group's name is the legend.

## Component rules

Rules for this component alone, numbered so the build and the review can cite them.

- **CR-1.** The root resets the browser's fieldset frame: `border: 0`, `margin: 0`, `padding: 0` and `min-inline-size: 0`, so it draws no box and takes its container's width rather than its widest content's, and the legend sets `margin: 0`. The legend breaks a word longer than its line (`overflow-wrap: anywhere`), so "Realtidsdataforsinkelser", about 152 px wide in `typography.label`, wraps inside the root in a 120 px column.
- **CR-2.** The root is a flex column with `gap: space.200` between the legend and each child, and the controls are the root's own children, with no wrapper of Fieldset's. Fieldset sets no `background`, `box-shadow`, `inline-size` or `max-inline-size`, and never sets `overflow`, so a focused control's ring, drawn `focus.offset` outside it, is never cut at the edge.
- **CR-3.** `legend` is required and always renders: the group always has a name. With `hiddenLegend` it renders through `render: <VisuallyHidden />`, so its text stays in the accessibility tree and names the group, and no gap opens above the first control.
- **CR-4.** `legend`, `hiddenLegend`, `disabled`, `children` and `slotProps` are taken out of `rest` before it reaches `Fieldset.Root`, and `{...rest}` comes before Fieldset's own props, so none of them reaches the `<fieldset>` as an attribute. The legend's props are `slotProps.legend` merged with `mergeProps`, Fieldset's own last, so its class and children stay while the caller's `className` joins and its `id` reaches Base UI, which points the root's `aria-labelledby` at it.
- **CR-5.** Fieldset composes with `render`: `<Fieldset render={<CheckboxGroup />} legend="Show on the map">`, with Base UI's group, keeps `pn-Fieldset` and the legend, and Base UI hands the rendered group the legend's id as `aria-labelledby` and Fieldset's `disabled` as its own prop, so the group is named by the legend and disabled with it, as Base UI's forms guide composes Fieldset with `CheckboxGroup` and `RadioGroup`. A component built this way sets its own spacing through its own class on the same element. Rendered as anything other than a `<fieldset>`, the browser's own disabling of native controls no longer applies, and only Base UI's context and the rendered component's `disabled` carry it.
- **CR-6.** Disabled is Base UI's: `disabled` reaches `Fieldset.Root`, which sets the native attribute, `data-disabled` and its context. The legend takes `color.text.tertiary` on `[data-disabled]`, never an opacity, and the root draws nothing for it; a disabled fieldset round this one disables it too, through Base UI's context, and the legend then carries `data-disabled` as well.
- **CR-7.** Fieldset never moves focus, sets no `tabindex` and adds no role beyond its native element's.

## Stories

One per variant and state the design would show. The design is deferred and has no variant property, so its one variant is `Default`; `Disabled` is its disabled state, and `HiddenLegend` the same variant with the legend for the ear only. Each sits on a `raised` Surface, as a group sits in a panel. Checkbox and the text fields are not built yet, so each story's controls are native `<label>`s, each holding an `<input type="checkbox">` and its word, set in `typography.body` with the `typography` helper; the stories move to Checkbox when it ships.

| Story          | Shows                                                                                                                                                        | `play` test                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Default`      | `legend` "Show on the map" over three checkboxes, "Bus", "Metro" and "S-tog", at rest. The subject story: its args render Fieldset alone and pass every rule | A `group` named "Show on the map" holds the three checkboxes; the legend is the root's first child and renders `typography.label` in `color.text.primary`; Tab reaches "Bus" and Shift+Tab leaves it, so focus ends where it started; `mount` renders `render={<RadioGroup />}` from Base UI with two `Radio.Root`s under the legend "Map style" and finds a `radiogroup` named "Map style" that keeps `pn-Fieldset` (CR-5); `mount` renders the legend "Realtidsdataforsinkelser" in a 120 px column and finds it wraps onto more than one line inside the root (CR-1) |
| `Disabled`     | The `Default` group with `disabled`                                                                                                                          | The `<fieldset>` has the `disabled` attribute and `data-disabled`; every checkbox is disabled, and Tab from before the group passes over them all; the legend has `data-disabled` and its colour is `color.text.tertiary`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `HiddenLegend` | The `Default` group with `hiddenLegend`, inside a [Section](section.md) titled "Show on the map" that names it for the eye                                   | The `group` is still named "Show on the map"; the legend renders as the `VisuallyHidden` span; the first checkbox sits at the root's top edge, with no gap above it                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |

## Do and don't

For a caller using the component, with the reason.

| Do                                                                                                                                      | Don't                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Group controls that answer one question, such as which modes to show, or fields that belong together, such as a report's place and time | Wrap a single control in a Fieldset: one control is named by its own label, through Field                                                                                                                                         |
| Write the legend in sentence case, a few words or a short question: "Show on the map"                                                   | Put a heading element inside `legend`, or type it in capitals: the legend is already the group's name, a heading inside it adds one to the page's outline that no section follows, and capitals come only from the overline style |
| Use CheckboxGroup or RadioGroup for a set of checkboxes or radios, once they ship: they compose Fieldset with the group's behaviour     | Render Fieldset as a Base UI group yourself in a screen: the groups hold the value, the keys and the form name for you                                                                                                            |
| Disable the whole group with `disabled`, so every control in it goes together                                                           | Disable each control by hand inside a Fieldset that stays enabled: the legend then looks live over dead controls                                                                                                                  |
| Use `hiddenLegend` where a heading right above already names the group for the eye                                                      | Leave out the legend, or replace it with an `aria-label` on the root: the legend is the group's one name, seen and heard alike                                                                                                    |
| Use Section for a titled block of content in a panel                                                                                    | Use Fieldset to title content that holds no controls: a `group` with nothing to fill in tells a screen reader there is something to fill in                                                                                       |
| Give the group's description and error through a Base UI `Field.Root`, as CheckboxGroup and RadioGroup do                               | Put a hint or an error as plain text among the controls: nothing ties it to the group for the ear                                                                                                                                 |

title: FilterChip
markdown:
# FilterChip

A pill that turns one filter on and off, such as "Delays" in the top bar's filters, with an optional icon before its words and a count after them, drawn in ink when it is on.

<!-- run notes -->

The design is deferred (ADR 0010, `docs/adr/0010-unattended-runs-with-design-deferred.md`): there is no read-back, code map or export, and this spec decides what the drawing would, from the [contract](README.md), the [foundations](../foundations/README.md), the tokens, the Base UI reference for `Toggle` and the ROADMAP line that names it (`ROADMAP.md`, "Wave 3, interactive, on Base UI": "FilterChip and HighlightChip (Toggle)"). The extracted prototype component is not in any branch this run can reach, so nothing here rests on it. The foundations already name much of its look: [Layout](../foundations/layout.md#other-layout-properties) gives `size.control` to "icon buttons and filter chips", [Semantic spacing](../foundations/semantic-spacing.md#radius) rounds "chips" with `radius.full`, [Typography](../foundations/typography.md#roles) sets "chips" in `typography.label` and "counts in chips" in `typography.data-sm`, and [Elevation](../foundations/elevation.md#surfaces) makes `color.surface.inverse`, with `color.text.inverse`, the fill of "pressed toggles".

## Anatomy

Penpot page `Components/FilterChip`. Family: none (the contract's [Families](README.md#families) have no chips; a chip is a pill-shaped toggle button, and takes Button's ink treatments on a `radius.full` edge, see Tokens). Shared parts: none (every word is the caller's, and the count is text the chip is named by).

The drawing has a `root` board holding, in reading order, a `startIcon` layer, a `label` text layer and a `count` layer, an instance of [Count](count.md). Its one variant property is `State`, with the values `default`, `hover`, `focus`, `selected` and `disabled`, so its variants are `Default`, `Hover`, `Focus`, `Selected` and `Disabled`. There is no `variant`, `color` or `size` property (see [Props](#props)).

| Part (Penpot layer) | What it is                                                                                                                                                                                 | Base UI part                                     | Class                     | `slotProps` key |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------- | --------------- |
| `root`              | The native `<button>` with `aria-pressed`: an inline flex row, centred, on a pill edge, that holds the start icon, the label and the count in reading order                                | `Toggle`                                         | `pn-FilterChip`           | none            |
| `startIcon`         | A `<span>`, `aria-hidden`, that holds the caller's `startIcon` before the label; only rendered when `startIcon` is given                                                                   | none: a span inside `Toggle`, which has no parts | `pn-FilterChip-startIcon` | none            |
| `label`             | A `<span>` that holds the caller's `children`, the filter's name                                                                                                                           | none: a span inside `Toggle`                     | `pn-FilterChip-label`     | none            |
| `count`             | A [Count](count.md), neutral, after the label, that shows the `count` prop, given the class `pn-FilterChip-count` beside its own `pn-Count`; only rendered when `count` is a finite number | none: the Count component, inside `Toggle`       | `pn-FilterChip-count`     | none            |
| `focusRing`         | The keyboard focus ring: the `:focus-visible` outline `perron.css` draws on the root, not an element                                                                                       | `Toggle`                                         | none                      | none            |

The count composes Count rather than drawing a pill of its own, so every count in a chip has Count's one shape.

FilterChip takes `count?: number`, typed as Tab's `count` is, and renders it as a neutral Count, so `Count` joins its `dependsOn` in `packages/perron/components.json`: Count's own spec names "the '3' after 'Delays' in a filter chip" as its use, and a count the caller builds into `children` would differ from screen to screen.

## Base UI parts

Imported from `@base-ui/react/toggle`, at the version pinned in `packages/perron/package.json` (1.9.0 installed).

| Base UI part | Renders                                                                                                                                                                                                                | Perron sets                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | Passed through                                                                                                     |
| ------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `Toggle`     | `<button type="button">`, with `aria-pressed` (`"true"` or `"false"`), `data-pressed` while on and `data-disabled` and the native `disabled` while disabled; with `render` and `nativeButton={false}`, `role="button"` | `className` (`pn-FilterChip`, then the caller's), `style`, `ref`, `pressed` from `selected`, `defaultPressed` from `defaultSelected`, `onPressedChange` adapted from `onChange`, `disabled`, and the children: the icon span, the label span and the Count | `render`, `nativeButton`, `onClick`, `aria-label` and every other prop of a native `<button>`, through `{...rest}` |

Base UI already does: it renders a native `<button>` with `type="button"`, and drops a caller's `type` and `form`, so a chip never submits or joins a form; a click, or Enter or Space through the browser's click, flips the pressed state and calls `onPressedChange(pressed, details)` with `details.reason` `'none'` before it commits, so `details.cancel()` keeps the state as it was; `pressed` given controls the state and `defaultPressed` (default `false`) seeds it uncontrolled; it sets `aria-pressed` from the state and `data-pressed` while pressed; when disabled it sets the native `disabled` and `data-disabled`, so the chip leaves the tab order and its clicks are stopped (Toggle has no `focusableWhenDisabled`: the installed `Toggle` sets `focusableWhenDisabled: false` in its metadata); with `render` and `nativeButton={false}` it gives a non-button element `role="button"`, a `tabIndex` and Enter and Space activation; inside a Base UI `ToggleGroup` it reads the group's value by its `value` prop instead, which FilterChip does not offer (see [Props](#props)).

## Props

In MUI's layout. Every prop here gets this description as its JSDoc. No slots: Toggle is the root and has no inner parts, and the icon span, the label span and the Count are not Base UI parts.
