FilterChip's state is `selected`, `defaultSelected` and `onChange(event, value, details)`, mapped onto Toggle's `pressed`, `defaultPressed` and `onPressedChange`, with none of Toggle's three names exposed: `selected` is MUI's ToggleButton prop and the contract's design state for a chosen item, where `pressed` is the contract's name for a momentary press (`:active`); `onChange` with `(event, value, details)` is the contract's event shape, its `value` the new `selected` state, a boolean, and `event` being `details.event`, as Tabs adapts `onValueChange`; the contract's [Names from other libraries](README.md#names-from-other-libraries) leave all three free, and `value` and `defaultValue` are kept for a string a group chooses.

FilterChip leaves out Toggle's `value`, which only identifies a toggle inside a Base UI `ToggleGroup`: Perron offers no group of filter chips, a top bar's chips each filter on their own, and outside a group `value` does nothing, so a caller who sets it would be misled; the API only grows, so a group can bring it later.

FilterChip takes `startIcon` alone, with no `endIcon`: the count is what follows the words, an icon after them would sit between the label and the count, and the disruption icons a filter shows go before its name, as the contract's `startIcon` does; `endIcon` can join later without a break.

FilterChip comes in one look, with no `variant`, `color` or `size`: [Layout](../foundations/layout.md#other-layout-properties) gives filter chips one height, `size.control`, the [brand](../foundations/README.md#the-brand) keeps the interface ink and glass with yellow for the one main action, which a filter never is, and status colours belong to the Count's figure and the caller's words, not to the chip; each prop can join later without a break.

FilterChip has no `name`: Base UI's Toggle drops `form` and has no hidden input, so a chip's state never reaches a native form, and the contract asks `name` only of a control whose value a form submits.

| Name                        | Type                                                                         | Default | Base UI prop      | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| --------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------- | ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `selected`                  | `boolean`                                                                    | none    | `pressed`         | Whether the filter is on, when the caller controls it. Announced as pressed.                                                                                                                                             |
| `defaultSelected`           | `boolean`                                                                    | `false` | `defaultPressed`  | Whether the filter is on at first, when FilterChip keeps the state itself.                                                                                                                                               |
| `onChange`                  | `(event: Event, value: boolean, details: Toggle.ChangeEventDetails) => void` | none    | `onPressedChange` | Called when a click, Enter or Space turns the filter on or off, with the new state as `value`; `details.reason` is `'none'`, and `details.cancel()` keeps the state as it was. `event` is `details.event`.               |
| `disabled`                  | `boolean`                                                                    | `false` | `disabled`        | Whether the chip ignores the pointer and the keys. A disabled chip leaves the tab order and keeps its state.                                                                                                             |
| `startIcon`                 | `ReactNode`                                                                  | none    | none              | An icon before the label, in reading order, such as the disruption icon of the kind the chip filters. Hidden from screen readers: the label names the chip.                                                              |
| `count`                     | `number`                                                                     | none    | none              | How many the filter matches, shown after the label as a [Count](count.md), such as the "3" of "Delays 3". Heard after the label. Shown for `0` too; left out when `undefined` or not a finite number.                    |
| `nativeButton`              | `boolean`                                                                    | `true`  | inherited         | Inherited from Base UI with its JSDoc: whether the component renders a native `<button>` element when replacing it via the `render` prop. Set to `false` if the rendered element is not a button (for example, `<div>`). |
| `render`                    | Base UI's `render`                                                           | none    | inherited         | Inherited from Base UI with its JSDoc: allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component.                                                                    |
| `children`                  | `ReactNode`                                                                  | none    | none              | The label: the name of what the filter shows, in sentence case, such as "Delays". It stays the same whether the filter is on or off.                                                                                     |
| `className`, `style`, `ref` | React's                                                                      | none    | none              | Reaches the root. `className` is merged after `pn-FilterChip`.                                                                                                                                                           |

No label-override props: FilterChip owns no strings.

## Tokens

One row per part, state and property. States are the contract's design states; the deferred design's `State` values map so: `default` is rest, `hover` is `:hover` inside `@media (hover: hover)`, `focus` is `:focus-visible`, `selected` is Base UI's `[data-pressed]`, `disabled` is `[data-disabled]`; pressed, which the design doesn't draw, is `:active`. Every `color` row but the `count` rows sets the root's `color`, which the label and the icon take, since icons draw in `currentColor`; a `count` row sets the Count's own `color` (CR-9).

The selected design state is read from Toggle's `[data-pressed]`, the momentary press from `:active` alone, and FilterChip sets no `data-selected` of its own: on Base UI's Toggle `data-pressed` means "on", not the press the contract's [Design states](README.md#design-states) table files it under, Base UI sets it in both controlled and uncontrolled use where a `data-selected` of Perron's would need the state FilterChip doesn't keep when uncontrolled, and the selector stays one class then an attribute, `.pn-FilterChip[data-pressed]`.

The chip takes Button's two neutral treatments on a pill: off, Button's `outline` (transparent, a `border.width.025` edge in `color.border.control`, `color.text.primary`, `color.surface.hover` on hover and `color.surface.selected` while pressed); on, Button's `solid` (`color.surface.inverse` with `color.text.inverse`, `color.surface.inverse-hover` on hover and `color.surface.inverse-pressed` while pressed); disabled, Button's disabled outline when off and disabled solid when on. [Elevation](../foundations/elevation.md#surfaces) gives `color.surface.inverse` to pressed toggles, `color.border.control` is the edge "that shows where a control is" and reaches 3:1 where an off chip on the top bar's glass would otherwise not show at all, and borrowing Button's rows keeps one ink language across the library.

The chip's icon is `icon.size.325`: [Icons](../foundations/icons.md#sizes) gives it to icons "inline with label and caption text: the disruption icons", the icons a filter of disruption kinds shows, drawn on that grid, and an icon is never scaled off its grid; a chip with a 16 px control icon is a later `size` or a new drawing.

A selected chip shows its state by its fill alone, with no tick before the label: the inverse fill moves the chip from about 1:1 to 17:1 against its surface, a change of lightness rather than hue, `aria-pressed` says the state to the ear, Windows' forced colours get a `Highlight` fill, or a `GrayText` one when the chip is disabled too (CR-11), and a tick that appears would widen the chip and move its neighbours, which CR-5 forbids.

All states:

| Part                 | State    | Property                    | Token                                                                                                                       |
| -------------------- | -------- | --------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `root`               | rest     | `cursor`                    | none: the keyword `pointer`                                                                                                 |
| `root`               | disabled | `cursor`                    | none: the keyword `default`                                                                                                 |
| `root`               | rest     | `block-size`                | `size.control`                                                                                                              |
| `root`               | rest     | `padding-inline`            | `space.300`                                                                                                                 |
| `root`               | rest     | `gap`                       | `space.150`                                                                                                                 |
| `root`               | rest     | `border-radius`             | `radius.full`                                                                                                               |
| `root`               | rest     | `border-width`              | `border.width.025`, `solid`                                                                                                 |
| `label`              | rest     | `font`, `letter-spacing`    | `typography.label`, with its tracking twin                                                                                  |
| `startIcon`          | rest     | `--perron-icon-size`        | `icon.size.325`                                                                                                             |
| `root` (`focusRing`) | focus    | `outline`, `outline-offset` | `focus.width` in `color.border.focus`, `focus.offset` (drawn by `perron.css`); the outline follows the root's `radius.full` |
| `count`              | disabled | `color`                     | `color.text.tertiary`                                                                                                       |

Off (no `data-pressed`):

| Part   | State    | Property           | Token                    |
| ------ | -------- | ------------------ | ------------------------ |
| `root` | rest     | `background-color` | `transparent`            |
| `root` | rest     | `border-color`     | `color.border.control`   |
| `root` | rest     | `color`            | `color.text.primary`     |
| `root` | hover    | `background-color` | `color.surface.hover`    |
| `root` | pressed  | `background-color` | `color.surface.selected` |
| `root` | disabled | `background-color` | `transparent`            |
| `root` | disabled | `border-color`     | `color.border.subtle`    |
| `root` | disabled | `color`            | `color.text.tertiary`    |

On (`data-pressed`, the selected design state):

| Part   | State              | Property           | Token                           |
| ------ | ------------------ | ------------------ | ------------------------------- |
| `root` | selected           | `background-color` | `color.surface.inverse`         |
| `root` | selected           | `border-color`     | `transparent`                   |
| `root` | selected           | `color`            | `color.text.inverse`            |
| `root` | selected, hover    | `background-color` | `color.surface.inverse-hover`   |
| `root` | selected, pressed  | `background-color` | `color.surface.inverse-pressed` |
| `root` | selected, disabled | `background-color` | `color.surface.inset`           |
| `root` | selected, disabled | `border-color`     | `transparent`                   |
| `root` | selected, disabled | `color`            | `color.text.tertiary`           |

Forced colours, inside `@media (forced-colors: active)`:

| Part                 | State              | Property                              | Token                                                                                                                                                         |
| -------------------- | ------------------ | ------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `root`               | selected           | `background-color`, `color`           | the system colours `Highlight` and `HighlightText` (CR-11), on hover and press too                                                                            |
| `root`               | selected           | `forced-color-adjust`                 | none: the keyword `none`, so the system keeps the fill                                                                                                        |
| `root` (`focusRing`) | selected, focus    | `outline-color`                       | the system colour `CanvasText`, which `forced-color-adjust: none` would otherwise leave in the theme's ink (CR-7, CR-11)                                      |
| `root`               | disabled           | `color`, `border-color`               | the system colour `GrayText`                                                                                                                                  |
| `root`               | selected, disabled | `background-color`, `color`           | the system colours `GrayText` and `Canvas`, so the chip still shows it is on (CR-11)                                                                          |
| `root`               | selected, disabled | `border-color`, `forced-color-adjust` | `transparent`, and the keyword `none`, so the system keeps the fill                                                                                           |
| `count`              | selected           | `forced-color-adjust`                 | auto: the keyword `auto`, since `none` is inherited, so the system draws the Count as it draws every Count, a `Canvas` pill with Count's `CanvasText` outline |
| `count`              | disabled           | `color`, `outline-color`              | the system colour `GrayText`, the outline being the edge Count draws in forced colours                                                                        |

Outside forced colours, the Count keeps its own `color.surface.inset` pill and `color.text.primary` figure in every state but disabled: on the light theme's ink fill and the dark theme's pale one alike the inset pill stands apart, and its figure reads on it. A disabled selected chip's `color.surface.inset` fill meets the count's own, so only the tertiary figure and the space before it set the count apart. In forced colours the system draws the Count, on or off, as the Forced colours table says.

Highlighted, open and invalid don't apply: a chip takes focus rather than `data-highlighted`, and opens nothing and holds no form value.

## Keyboard and ARIA

From the Base UI reference for `Toggle` and the installed `Toggle` and `useButton`. "From" says who does it.

| Key                | Does                                                                                                       | From                                           |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `Tab`, `Shift+Tab` | Moves focus to the chip and away; a disabled chip is skipped                                               | The browser, and Base UI's native `disabled`   |
| `Enter`            | Turns the filter on or off, through the button's click, and calls `onChange` with the new state            | The browser; Base UI for a non-button `render` |
| `Space`            | Turns the filter on or off on release, through the button's click, and calls `onChange` with the new state | The browser; Base UI for a non-button `render` |

FilterChip adds no keys of its own. A row of chips is a tab stop each, not one composite stop: they are separate filters, not one choice.

| Element     | Role                                                                                                                   | Accessible name from                                                                                                        | States announced                                         |
| ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `root`      | `button`, native, a toggle button by its `aria-pressed`; `role="button"` from Base UI when `render` gives a non-button | Its text content: the label's `children`, then the count, as "Delays 3"; the caller's `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` win | `aria-pressed`, `true` or `false`; the native `disabled` |
| `startIcon` | none: `aria-hidden="true"`                                                                                             | none                                                                                                                        | none                                                     |
| `count`     | none: text inside the chip, Count's generic `<span>`                                                                   | Part of the chip's name                                                                                                     | none                                                     |

What axe won't catch, from the contract, each with how this component meets it:

- [ ] Everything the eye is told, the ear is told, for every shape each prop accepts: the selected fill is `aria-pressed`, heard as "pressed" or "not pressed" after the name; the count is text in the name, heard after the label; the icon is `aria-hidden`, since it sits beside the word it shows ([Icons](../foundations/icons.md#style)); a disabled chip's tertiary colour is the native `disabled`.
- [ ] Every landmark and named region has an accessible name: none here; a chip is neither. The group of chips that holds them is the pattern's, which names it.
- [ ] Every default label can be overridden: none here; FilterChip owns no strings.
- [ ] Every shape the type accepts renders, in every variant: `children` and `startIcon` render a string, an element and a list alike, on and off and disabled; `count` renders `0` and larger numbers alike, and nothing for `undefined`, `NaN` or `Infinity`.
- [ ] A hidden copy kept for animation is `aria-hidden`, and a collapsed region is `inert`: none here; FilterChip keeps no hidden copy and collapses nothing.
- [ ] Native semantics first: a native `<button>` with `aria-pressed` from Base UI's `Toggle`; with `render` and `nativeButton={false}`, Base UI's `role="button"`.
- [ ] Focus moves in reading order and returns on close: each chip is one tab stop in document order, focus stays on the chip it toggles, and it opens nothing to return from.
- [ ] Every target is at least `size.target-min` square: the smallest target is a chip with a one-word label and no icon or count, `size.control` (34 px) tall and the word plus `space.300` on each side wide.
- [ ] Loops stop when the system asks for less motion: none here; FilterChip has no loop and no transition.

## Owned strings

No owned strings: every word comes from the caller, as `children`, the `count`, or an `aria-label`. FilterChip renders its Count only for a finite number (CR-9), so Count's own "Unknown" never shows inside a chip.

## Component rules

Rules for this component alone, numbered so the build and the review can cite them.

- **CR-1.** Base UI's Toggle already gives the native button, the click, Enter and Space toggling, `aria-pressed`, `data-pressed`, the controlled and uncontrolled state, the cancellable change and the disabled behaviour, so FilterChip rebuilds none of it and adds no key handlers.
- **CR-2.** FilterChip adapts Base UI's `onPressedChange(pressed, details)` into `onChange(details.event, pressed, details)` inside itself, passes `selected` on as `pressed` and `defaultSelected` as `defaultPressed`, and exposes none of `pressed`, `defaultPressed`, `onPressedChange` or `value`: its props type omits them from `Toggle.Props`, with the native `onChange`. It takes no `endIcon`, `variant`, `color`, `size` or `name`.
- **CR-3.** It takes `{...rest}` before its own attributes and its own props out of `rest` first (`selected`, `defaultSelected`, `onChange`, `disabled`, `startIcon`, `count`, `children`; an inherited Base UI prop such as `nativeButton` stays in `rest`, keeping Base UI's default), and merges `className` after `pn-FilterChip`; `ref` reaches the root.
- **CR-4.** The selected look reads Base UI's attribute, `.pn-FilterChip[data-pressed]`, and the momentary press `:active`; FilterChip sets no `data-selected`, `data-variant`, `data-color` or `data-size`, having none of those props.
- **CR-5.** The states keep the chip's geometry: hover, pressed, focus, selected and disabled change colours only, never the height, padding, gap, border width, radius, typography or weight, so turning a filter on never moves its neighbours. Every state draws the `border.width.025` border, `transparent` when selected, so on and off share one box. In Windows' forced colours an off chip's border takes the system's edge, while a selected one, which keeps its `transparent` border under `forced-color-adjust: none`, shows by its fill (CR-11). The selected state is the fill alone: no tick or other mark appears before the label.
- **CR-6.** Hover is read inside `@media (hover: hover)`; pressed (`:active`) takes the pressed tokens of the chip's state, off or on, a step past hover, in a rule after it and outside it, so a touch press shows. Neither applies to a disabled chip: both rules exclude `[data-disabled]`, since a native disabled button still matches `:hover`.
- **CR-7.** Focus uses the ring `perron.css` draws on `:focus-visible`; the component draws no ring of its own and never removes the outline.
- **CR-8.** The colour is set on the root's `color`; the label and the icon take it through `currentColor`, and no rule sets a colour on an icon. The icon span is `aria-hidden="true"`, rendered only when `startIcon` is given, and sets `--perron-icon-size` to `icon.size.325`.
- **CR-9.** The count is a [Count](count.md) with its default `color`, given `className="pn-FilterChip-count"`, rendered only when `count` is a finite number, `0` included, after the label with a space between in the markup, not only the CSS gap, so the chip's name is "Delays 3", which a `play` test checks. `.pn-FilterChip[data-disabled] .pn-FilterChip-count` sets its `color` to `color.text.tertiary`; besides it, only CR-11's forced-colours rules reach inside the Count, setting its `forced-color-adjust`, `color` and `outline-color`. `Count` joins FilterChip's `dependsOn` in `packages/perron/components.json`, and `npm run registry` runs after.
- **CR-10.** The label stays on one line (`white-space: nowrap`), the chip growing with it, rather than wrapping inside the fixed `size.control` height: a chip sizes to its content beside others in a row, and the row that holds the chips wraps (`flex-wrap: wrap`), which is the caller's or the pattern's.
- **CR-11.** In `@media (forced-colors: active)`, a selected chip that is not disabled takes `Highlight` with `HighlightText` and `forced-color-adjust: none`, on hover and press too, since forced colours drop its inverse fill and the selected state would vanish ([Accessibility](../foundations/accessibility.md#what-a-person-checks)), and its focus ring takes `CanvasText`, since `none` would leave the ring in the theme's ink, which a dark contrast theme's `Canvas` hides, where that page asks the ring to show. A disabled chip that is off takes a `GrayText` edge and words on `Canvas`; a disabled chip that is on takes a `GrayText` fill with `Canvas` words, under `forced-color-adjust: none`, so the selected state still shows when the chip is disabled. Since `forced-color-adjust` is inherited, the count of a selected chip sets it back to `auto`, and the system draws it as every Count, in system colours; a disabled chip's count takes `GrayText` for its figure and the outline that is its edge in forced colours.
- **CR-12.** Changes of state are immediate: no `duration.*` token fits a chip's state change, so the CSS has no transition.
- **CR-13.** The chip sizes to its content (`display: inline-flex`, `align-items: center`), with `box-sizing: border-box`, so the border sits inside `size.control`. Placing chips in the top bar and hiding the "Later" ones under `breakpoint.desktop` belong to the pattern that uses them.

## Stories

The deferred design's page draws one variant property, `State` (`default`, `hover`, `focus`, `selected`, `disabled`), and each of its stories is named by its variant name (`penpot/README.md`, "Conventions"). Each renders the chip "Delays" with `packages/perron/icons/`'s `warning` icon as `startIcon` and a `count` of 3; the hover and focus stories render at rest: the visual check drives the state, and their `play` tests check it. `Default` is the [subject story](README.md#root), which the contract story renders, and its args, "Delays", the icon and the count, render the chip alone and pass every rule.

The selected chip's hover and its disabled look, which Base UI's `data-pressed` produces beside `:hover` and `data-disabled` but the drawing's single `State` property can't show, get the `SelectedDisabled` story below and a hover check in `Selected`'s `play`, with no Penpot variant of their own: the Tokens table already gives both, and a second variant property, `selected`, would name the drawing's variants after a prop the caller sets, `TrueHover`, where Tabs' `State` already carries `selected`.

| Story              | Shows                                                                                                                                                                                         | `play` test                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Default`          | Off, at rest: the warning icon, "Delays" and a count of 3; the subject story                                                                                                                  | The root is a `<button>` with class `pn-FilterChip`, `aria-pressed="false"` and no `data-pressed`, and the `ref` reaches it; its name is "Delays 3"; the icon span is `aria-hidden`; a click sets `aria-pressed="true"` and `data-pressed` and calls `onChange` once with `true`; Space sets it back and calls `onChange` with `false`; Enter turns it on and calls `onChange` with `true`, and Enter again turns it off and calls `onChange` with `false`, ending off |
| `Hover`            | Off, hover                                                                                                                                                                                    | Hovering lays `color.surface.hover` over the transparent fill and keeps the `color.border.control` edge                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `Focus`            | Off, focus                                                                                                                                                                                    | Tab gives the chip `:focus-visible` and the ring; Shift+Tab leaves it                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `Selected`         | On, with `defaultSelected`                                                                                                                                                                    | The chip has `aria-pressed="true"` and `data-pressed`, and its computed background is `color.surface.inverse`; hovering sets `color.surface.inverse-hover`; its height and width match an off chip's with the same content (CR-5)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `Disabled`         | Off, disabled                                                                                                                                                                                 | The chip has the native `disabled` and `data-disabled`, Tab skips it, and a click neither changes `aria-pressed` nor calls `onChange`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `SelectedDisabled` | On and disabled                                                                                                                                                                               | The chip keeps `aria-pressed="true"` and `data-pressed`, has `data-disabled`, its computed background is `color.surface.inset`, and a click changes nothing                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `Controlled`       | A chip given `selected` and `onChange` from the story's state                                                                                                                                 | A click calls `onChange` with `true` and `details.reason` `'none'`; `aria-pressed` changes only once the story sets `selected`, and a chip whose caller ignores the change, given `selected` of `false`, stays off; an `onChange` that calls `details.cancel()` keeps the state; the story ends off                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `LabelOnly`        | "Planned works", with no icon and no count                                                                                                                                                    | No icon span and no count render, nor does a count for a `count` of `NaN` or `Infinity`; the name is "Planned works"; the chip is at least `size.target-min` square                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `Row`              | Three chips in a 320 px container that wraps: "Delays" with a count of 3 and the `warning` icon, "Diversions" with 2 and the `diversion` icon, "Planned works" with 0 and the `calendar` icon | Each label stays on one line; the chips wrap onto a second row rather than overflow (the container's `scrollWidth` equals its `clientWidth`); the count of 0 shows; Tab moves through the three chips in reading order                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |

## Do and don't

For a caller using the component, with the reason.

| Do                                                                                                                                       | Don't                                                                                                                           |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Use FilterChip for a filter people turn on and off on its own, such as showing delays on the map                                         | Use it to pick one of several views or modes: that is one choice, a SegmentedControl's, and chips would let two be on at once   |
| Keep the label the filter's name, the same on and off, in sentence case: "Delays", "Planned works"                                       | Change the label to say the state ("Delays on"): `aria-pressed` and the fill already say it, and a changing label moves the row |
| Give the count as `count`, so every chip's count has Count's shape and is heard after the label                                          | Build a count into `children`, or pass a guess when the number is unknown: leave `count` out, and the chip shows none           |
| Use the [content design](../content-design.md) words for kinds of disruption and data states, so the chips agree with the rest of Mylder | Coin a filter name of your own for a kind the table names                                                                       |
| Lay a row of chips out with `flex-wrap: wrap` and a gap, and name the group in the pattern that holds it                                 | Put chips in a [Toolbar](toolbar.md) or make them one tab stop: each is a filter of its own, reached with Tab                   |
| Use a [Tag](tag.md) to mark a property that can't be pressed                                                                             | Use a FilterChip as a label: a chip invites a press, and one that does nothing misleads                                         |
| Disable a chip only while its filter can't apply, and say why nearby                                                                     | Disable a chip to show a count of 0: show the 0, since a disabled chip leaves the tab order and can't explain itself            |
| Keep `onChange` for the filter's state, and cancel it with `details.cancel()` when the change must not happen                            | Set `aria-pressed` yourself or toggle a class: Base UI keeps the state and the attribute in step                                |

title: HighlightChip
markdown:
# HighlightChip

A pill that floats over the map on glass and turns one highlight of the map on and off, such as line 5C in focus with everything outside it dimmed; while it is selected, the map shows the highlight.

<!-- run notes -->

The design is deferred (ADR 0010, `docs/adr/0010-unattended-runs-with-design-deferred.md`): there is no read-back, code map or export, and this spec decides what the drawing would, from the contract, the foundations, the tokens, the Base UI reference and the ROADMAP line that names it (`ROADMAP.md`, "Wave 3, interactive, on Base UI": "FilterChip and HighlightChip (Toggle)"). The extracted prototype component is not in any branch this run can reach. The foundations already place it: [Layout](../foundations/layout.md#stacking) stacks "the highlight chip" above the overview sheet and below the detail panel, with `z-index.highlight`; [Accessibility](../foundations/accessibility.md#rules) has Esc close "a dialog, then a detail panel, then a highlight"; and [Map](../foundations/map.md#focus-and-dimming) gives the dimming a line in focus brings.

## Anatomy

Penpot page `Components/HighlightChip`. Family: none (the contract's [Families](README.md#families) have no toggle; the chip takes the glass of a floating panel from [Elevation](../foundations/elevation.md#surfaces) and the pressed toggle's `color.surface.inverse` from the same page). Shared parts: none (every word is the caller's, and the selected state is told by `aria-pressed`, not by a hidden word).

HighlightChip is the one toggle that floats alone over the map and turns one map highlight on and off, such as a line in focus or the delayed vehicles; the screen places it (`z-index.highlight`, `size.panel-gap`) and clears it on Esc, while FilterChip is the chip in the top bar's filters that changes what the map and the lists show. Layout's stacking names one "highlight chip" between the sheet and the detail panel, Map's "Focus and dimming" is the highlight it turns on, a highlight keeps every vehicle on the map where a filter takes some away, and the registry gives both chips Base UI's `Toggle`, so they differ in what they change and where they sit, not in their behaviour.

The chip shows no close mark while selected: its selected state is told to the eye by the `color.surface.inverse` fill and to the ear by `aria-pressed`. The `close` icon is drawn only in the `CloseButton` shared part's folder (the contract's [Shared parts](README.md#shared-parts), held by the `shared-parts` check), a `CloseButton` can't sit inside the chip's `<button>`, and a chip whose press clears the highlight needs no second target; a close mark can join later as a shared part of its own.

The drawing has a `root` board holding one text layer, `label`, and no variant properties, so its variants are the values of its `State` property alone: `default`, `hover`, `focus`, `disabled`, `selected`, `selected-hover` and `selected-disabled`, named `Default`, `Hover`, `Focus`, `Disabled`, `Selected`, `SelectedHover` and `SelectedDisabled` (`penpot/README.md`, "Conventions"). `selected` is the chip turned on, Base UI's `[data-pressed]`; the press itself, `:active`, is drawn as hover.

| Part (Penpot layer) | What it is                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | Base UI part             | Class              | `slotProps` key |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------ | ------------------ | --------------- |
| `root`              | The native `<button>`: an inline flex row on a `radius.full` pill, glass at rest and `color.surface.inverse` while selected, holding the caller's `children`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | `Toggle`                 | `pn-HighlightChip` | none            |
| `label`             | The words, and any badge or icon beside them, from the caller's `children`, set in `typography.label`. The `label` layer is the root's own content, with no element, class or `slotProps` key of its own, as Tag's and LineBadge's are: the root's flex `gap` spaces the nodes of `children` given as a list, such as a LineBadge and its words, which a wrapping span would make one flex item with no gap between them | none: the root's content | none               | none            |
| `focusRing`         | The keyboard focus ring on the root: the `:focus-visible` outline `perron.css` draws, not an element                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | `Toggle`                 | none               | none            |

## Base UI parts

Imported from `@base-ui/react/toggle`, at the version pinned in `packages/perron/package.json` (1.9.0 installed).

| Base UI part | Renders                                                                                                                                                                                                        | Perron sets                                                                                                                                                                                                               | Passed through                                                                                                 |
| ------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Toggle`     | `<button type="button">`, with `aria-pressed`, `data-pressed` while selected, and `data-disabled` and the native `disabled` attribute while disabled; outside a `ToggleGroup`, as here, it keeps its own state | `className` (`pn-HighlightChip`, then the caller's), `style`, `ref`, `pressed` from `selected`, `defaultPressed` from `defaultSelected`, `onPressedChange` adapted from `onChange` (CR-3), `disabled`; `value` left unset | `nativeButton`, `render`, `onClick`, `aria-*` and every other prop of a native `<button>`, through `{...rest}` |

Base UI already does: toggling the pressed state on a click, Enter or Space, through the native button or, for a `render` that isn't a `<button>` with `nativeButton={false}`, through its own key handling; keeping the state itself when uncontrolled (`defaultPressed`) or following `pressed` when controlled; setting `aria-pressed` and `data-pressed` from that state; passing `onPressedChange` the next state and `details` whose `cancel()` stops the change; making a disabled toggle natively `disabled` (`focusableWhenDisabled` is fixed off in the installed `Toggle`), so it leaves the tab order and ignores clicks; and fixing `type="button"`, so the chip never submits a form it sits in.

## Props

In MUI's layout. Every prop the component declares gets this description as its JSDoc; the inherited rows keep Base UI's. No slots.

The chip takes `selected`, `defaultSelected` and `onChange(event, value, details)`, where `value` is the next selected state, a `boolean`, mapped onto Toggle's `pressed`, `defaultPressed` and `onPressedChange`, with none of Toggle's three names exposed. In the contract's [Design states](README.md#design-states), `pressed` names the momentary press (`:active`) and `selected` a chosen item; MUI's ToggleButton takes `selected`; FilterChip, built on the same `Toggle`, takes `selected` and `defaultSelected`; and the `props` check (`scripts/checks/props.ts`) takes `onChange` only with the parameters `(event, value, details)` or `(event)`. The contract's [Names from other libraries](README.md#names-from-other-libraries) leaves all three free, and Base UI's `onPressedChange` is adapted once, inside the chip, as its [State and events](README.md#state-and-events) asks.

Base UI's `value`, the string that names a toggle inside a `ToggleGroup`, is left out of the props type, and so is the native button's `value` with it: a HighlightChip stands alone, and SegmentedControl is the group of toggles. Base UI's function forms of `className` and `style` are left out too, so both are React's, as on every Perron component.

The chip comes in one look, with no `variant`, `color`, `size` or `startIcon`. The brand keeps colour for the map and its vehicles and the yellow for the one main action, a screen has one highlight chip, a badge or an icon beside the words goes in `children` (such as a LineBadge before "Line 5C"), and each prop can join later without a break.

`children` is required: a chip with no words has no name, and the selected fill alone would say nothing. The chip takes no form `name` of its own and renders no hidden input: its state changes the map, not what a form sends, and the native button's `name`, which reaches the `<button>` with the other native props, is never sent, since a `type="button"` never submits.

| Name                        | Type                                                                         | Default | Base UI prop      | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| --------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------- | ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `selected`                  | `boolean`                                                                    | none    | `pressed`         | Whether the highlight is on, when the caller controls it. Announced as pressed.                                                                                                                                            |
| `defaultSelected`           | `boolean`                                                                    | `false` | `defaultPressed`  | Whether the highlight is on at first, when the chip keeps the state itself.                                                                                                                                                |
| `onChange`                  | `(event: Event, value: boolean, details: Toggle.ChangeEventDetails) => void` | none    | `onPressedChange` | Called when a click, Enter or Space turns the chip on or off, with the next selected state: `true` turns the highlight on, `false` clears it. `event` is `details.event`, and `details.cancel()` keeps the chip as it was. |
| `disabled`                  | `boolean`                                                                    | `false` | `disabled`        | Whether the chip ignores the pointer and the keys. A disabled chip leaves the tab order, and a selected one still shows that the highlight is on.                                                                          |
| `nativeButton`              | `boolean`                                                                    | `true`  | inherited         | Whether the component renders a native `<button>` element when replacing it via the `render` prop. Set to `false` if the rendered element is not a button (for example, `<div>`).                                          |
| `render`                    | Base UI's `render`                                                           | none    | inherited         | Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render.                                  |
| `children`                  | `ReactNode`                                                                  | none    | none              | Required. What the chip highlights, in a word or two in sentence case, such as "Line 5C" or "Delayed vehicles": the chip's name. A string, an element such as a LineBadge, or a list of both.                              |
| `className`, `style`, `ref` | React's                                                                      | none    | none              | Reaches the root. `className` is merged after `pn-HighlightChip`.                                                                                                                                                          |

## Tokens

One row per part, state and property. States are the contract's design states, and Penpot's `State` values map to them: `default` is rest, no selector; `hover` is `:hover` inside `@media (hover: hover)`, and the press, `:active`, takes the same values; `focus` is `:focus-visible`; `disabled` is `[data-disabled]`; `selected` is Base UI's `[data-pressed]`, which the installed `Toggle` sets for as long as the chip is on, so here it is the selected state and the press itself is `:active` alone. Every `color` row sets the root's `color`, which the label and any icon in it take.

The chip is glass at rest, as a floating panel is (`color.surface.overlay` with `effect.glass-blur` and `effect.glass-saturate`, `shadow.panel` and a `border.width.025` edge in `color.border.subtle`), and `color.surface.inverse` with `color.text.inverse` while selected, keeping its shadow and turning its edge `transparent`. The chip floats alone over the map, where [Elevation](../foundations/elevation.md#surfaces) puts everything on glass and lets only floating panels cast `shadow.panel`, and the same page gives "pressed toggles" `color.surface.inverse`, so a selected chip reads as on over land, water and parks alike.

The chip is `size.control` tall at least and as wide at least, with `space.300` at the sides, `space.150` between the nodes of its `children`, `typography.label` and `icon.size.400` for an icon in it. `size.control` is the height of "icon buttons and filter chips" and of the map controls' buttons beside which the chip floats, `space.300` is a small button's and a segment's inline padding, `typography.label`'s description names chips, and `icon.size.400` is the step for icons "inside controls".

A selected chip that is disabled takes `color.surface.inset` with `color.text.tertiary`, as Button's disabled solid button does, while a disabled chip at rest keeps its glass with `color.text.tertiary`. The contract makes disabled a colour, never an opacity; the inset fill still sets a selected chip apart from the glass of one at rest, so a highlight held on, such as while the map follows a vehicle, still shows; and `color.text.tertiary` on `color.surface.inverse` would read as a live chip with faint words.

| Part                 | State              | Property                    | Token                                                                                                                                                            |
| -------------------- | ------------------ | --------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `root`               | rest               | `cursor`                    | none: the keyword `pointer`                                                                                                                                      |
| `root`               | disabled           | `cursor`                    | none: the keyword `default`                                                                                                                                      |
| `root`               | rest               | `display`                   | none: the keyword `inline-flex`, with `align-items: center` and `justify-content: center`                                                                        |
| `root`               | rest               | `box-sizing`                | none: the keyword `border-box`, so the padding and the edge count inside `max-inline-size` (CR-7)                                                                |
| `root`               | rest               | `max-inline-size`           | none: `100%`, so the chip never runs past its container (CR-7)                                                                                                   |
| `root`               | rest               | `min-block-size`            | `size.control`                                                                                                                                                   |
| `root`               | rest               | `min-inline-size`           | `size.control`                                                                                                                                                   |
| `root`               | rest               | `padding-block`             | `space.100`, so a label that wraps keeps clear of the edge                                                                                                       |
| `root`               | rest               | `padding-inline`            | `space.300`                                                                                                                                                      |
| `root`               | rest               | `gap`                       | `space.150`, between the nodes of `children` given as a list                                                                                                     |
| `root`               | rest               | `border-radius`             | `radius.full`                                                                                                                                                    |
| `root`               | rest               | `border-width`              | `border.width.025`                                                                                                                                               |
| `root`               | rest               | `border-style`              | none: the keyword `solid`                                                                                                                                        |
| `root`               | rest               | `border-color`              | `color.border.subtle`                                                                                                                                            |
| `root`               | rest               | `background-color`          | `color.surface.overlay`                                                                                                                                          |
| `root`               | rest               | `backdrop-filter`           | `effect.glass-blur` (blur) and `effect.glass-saturate` (saturate)                                                                                                |
| `root`               | rest               | `box-shadow`                | `shadow.panel`                                                                                                                                                   |
| `root`               | rest               | `color`                     | `color.text.primary`                                                                                                                                             |
| `root`               | rest               | `font`, `letter-spacing`    | `typography.label`, with its tracking twin                                                                                                                       |
| `root`               | rest               | `overflow-wrap`             | none: the keyword `anywhere`, so a word longer than the line breaks within the chip, even as the anonymous flex item its words make (CR-7)                       |
| `root`               | rest               | `text-align`                | none: the keyword `center`                                                                                                                                       |
| `root`               | rest               | `--perron-icon-size`        | `icon.size.400`, for an icon in `children`                                                                                                                       |
| `root`               | hover              | `background-image`          | `color.surface.hover`, laid over the glass as a `linear-gradient`                                                                                                |
| `root`               | pressed            | `background-image`          | `color.surface.selected`, laid over the glass as a `linear-gradient`                                                                                             |
| `root` (`focusRing`) | focus              | `outline`, `outline-offset` | `focus.width` in `color.border.focus`, `focus.offset` (drawn by `perron.css`)                                                                                    |
| `root`               | disabled           | `color`                     | `color.text.tertiary`                                                                                                                                            |
| `root`               | disabled           | `background-image`          | none: the keyword `none`, so hover lays no layer (CR-6)                                                                                                          |
| `root`               | selected           | `background-color`          | `color.surface.inverse`                                                                                                                                          |
| `root`               | selected           | `border-color`              | none: the keyword `transparent`, so the edge keeps its width (CR-4); in forced colours the system fill, `Highlight` or `GrayText`, draws the pill's shape (CR-5) |
| `root`               | selected           | `color`                     | `color.text.inverse`                                                                                                                                             |
| `root`               | selected           | `box-shadow`                | `shadow.panel`, unchanged                                                                                                                                        |
| `root`               | selected, hover    | `background-color`          | `color.surface.inverse-hover`                                                                                                                                    |
| `root`               | selected, hover    | `background-image`          | none: the keyword `none`                                                                                                                                         |
| `root`               | selected, pressed  | `background-color`          | `color.surface.inverse-pressed`                                                                                                                                  |
| `root`               | selected, pressed  | `background-image`          | none: the keyword `none`, so the rest press layer doesn't lie over the inverse fill                                                                              |
| `root`               | selected, disabled | `background-color`          | `color.surface.inset`                                                                                                                                            |
| `root`               | selected, disabled | `color`                     | `color.text.tertiary`                                                                                                                                            |

The words take the pairs [Semantic colours](../foundations/semantic-colours.md) sets: `color.text.primary` on the glass, as on every floating panel, and `color.text.inverse` on `color.surface.inverse`, the pair that page gives "pressed toggles", with `color.surface.inverse-hover` under it on hover, as on Button's solid neutral button.

Highlighted, open and invalid don't apply: the chip takes focus rather than `data-highlighted`, opens nothing and holds no form value. Its place on the map is not here: `z-index.highlight` and `size.panel-gap` belong to the screen that places it (CR-8).

## Keyboard and ARIA

From the Base UI reference for `Toggle` and the installed `Toggle`, which builds on Base UI's button hook. "From" says who does it.

| Key              | Does                                                                                                                           | From                                                   |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `Tab`            | Moves focus to the chip, in reading order; a disabled chip is skipped                                                          | The browser                                            |
| `Shift+Tab`      | Moves focus back out of the chip                                                                                               | The browser                                            |
| `Enter`, `Space` | Toggle the chip and call `onChange` with the next state                                                                        | The browser's click; Base UI for a non-button `render` |
| `Esc`            | Nothing on the chip: the screen clears the highlight on Esc, after a dialog and a detail panel, and sets `selected` to `false` | The screen                                             |

| Element | Role                                      | Accessible name from                 | States announced                                                |
| ------- | ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `root`  | `button`, a toggle through `aria-pressed` | Its content: the caller's `children` | `aria-pressed` (pressed or not pressed), disabled when disabled |

The chip tells its state with `aria-pressed` and the selected fill, with no word of its own, leaving the caller free to change `children` with the state, as "Follow" and "Following" do. [Accessibility](../foundations/accessibility.md#rules) wants a toggle's state "in words as well as in looks", and `aria-pressed` puts it in words for the ear; what the chip highlights is the caller's to say, an owned "On" would read beside "Line 5C" as a second name, and a selected-state label can join later as a new optional prop.

What axe won't catch, from the contract, each with how this component meets it:

- [ ] Everything the eye is told, the ear is told, for every shape each prop accepts: the caller's `children` name what the chip highlights, and the selected state the eye gets from the inverse fill the ear gets from `aria-pressed`; a LineBadge or icon in `children` brings its own text or is `aria-hidden` beside words that say it.
- [ ] Every landmark and named region has an accessible name: none here; the chip is a button, not a region.
- [ ] Every default label can be overridden: none here; the chip owns no strings.
- [ ] Every shape the type accepts renders, in every variant: `children` as a string, an element, or a list of an element and a string, each inside the one root, in every `State`.
- [ ] A hidden copy kept for animation is `aria-hidden`, and a collapsed region is `inert`: none here; the chip doesn't animate.
- [ ] Native semantics first: a native `<button type="button">` from Base UI's `Toggle`, with `aria-pressed`, the one ARIA attribute, set by Base UI.
- [ ] Focus moves in reading order and returns on close: the chip is one tab stop where the screen puts it in the document; it opens nothing, so nothing returns focus, and toggling it keeps focus on it.
- [ ] Every target is at least `size.target-min` square: the chip is at least `size.control` tall and wide, above `size.target-min`.
- [ ] Loops stop when the system asks for less motion: none here; the chip has no motion.

## Owned strings

No owned strings: every word comes from the caller, as `children`.

## Component rules

- **CR-1.** HighlightChip renders Base UI's `Toggle` as its root, with `{...rest}` first and its own `className`, `style`, `ref` and state props after, as the contract's [Root](README.md#root) asks, so `className` reads `pn-HighlightChip` and then the caller's. `selected`, `defaultSelected`, `onChange` and `disabled` are taken out of `rest` before the spread and given to `Toggle` as `pressed`, `defaultPressed`, `onPressedChange` (CR-3) and `disabled`, and `className`, `style` and `ref` are taken out and given to it as they are, `className` merged.
- **CR-2.** The chip keeps no state of its own: Base UI's `Toggle` holds it, uncontrolled from `defaultSelected` or controlled by `selected`, and sets `aria-pressed` and `data-pressed` from it. The CSS reads the selected state from `[data-pressed]` alone, never from a class or a prop.
- **CR-3.** `onChange(event, value, details)` is Base UI's `onPressedChange(pressed, details)` adapted once, inside the chip: `event` is `details.event`, `value` is the next selected state, and `details` is passed through unchanged, so `details.cancel()` keeps the chip as it was. The props type declares none of `pressed`, `defaultPressed`, `onPressedChange` and `value`.
- **CR-4.** Every state keeps one geometry: the root draws its `border.width.025` edge in every state, `color.border.subtle` at rest and `transparent` while selected, and the same padding and minimum size, so turning the chip on never moves it or what floats beside it.
- **CR-5.** In Windows' forced colours, where fills are dropped, a selected chip that is not disabled sets `background-color: Highlight`, `color: HighlightText` and `forced-color-adjust: none` inside `@media (forced-colors: active)`, on hover and press too, so the system keeps the fill and the selected and unselected chip still look apart; a selected disabled chip sets a `GrayText` fill with `Canvas` words under `forced-color-adjust: none`, as FilterChip's and SegmentedControl's do, so the selected state still shows when the chip is disabled; and, since `forced-color-adjust: none` keeps the focus ring in its token's colour too, a selected chip's `:focus-visible` ring sets `outline-color: CanvasText`, so it still shows ([Accessibility](../foundations/accessibility.md#what-a-person-checks)).
- **CR-6.** Hover is `:hover` inside `@media (hover: hover)`, and it and `:active` lay no layer on a disabled chip: the hover rule reads `.pn-HighlightChip:not([data-disabled])`.
- **CR-7.** The chip never cuts its words off: it sets no `white-space: nowrap` and no `text-overflow`. Alone in a container narrower than it, at 320 px or at 200% zoom, it wraps inside itself and grows taller, a word longer than the line breaking within it with `overflow-wrap: anywhere`, since `break-word` leaves the anonymous flex item that holds the words as wide as its longest word, and stays inside the container through `max-inline-size: 100%` ([Accessibility](../foundations/accessibility.md#what-a-person-checks), zoom and reflow).
- **CR-8.** The chip sets no `position`, `z-index` or margin: the screen that floats it over the map places it, with `z-index.highlight`, which the contract's [Token families](README.md#token-families) keep for patterns, and `size.panel-gap`, the distance a floating panel keeps from the viewport's edge and from the other panels, which the chip can't measure from inside itself, since where it sits is the screen's. The chip's CSS reads only the component row's tokens.
- **CR-9.** The chip doesn't listen for Esc and doesn't clear itself: clearing the highlight on Esc, after a dialog and a detail panel, is the screen's ([Accessibility](../foundations/accessibility.md#rules)), which sets `selected` to `false`.
- **CR-10.** The chip's own props are only those [Props](#props) gives: `children` is required in the type, Toggle's `pressed`, `defaultPressed`, `onPressedChange` and `value` and the function forms of `className` and `style` are left out, and there is no `variant`, `color`, `size`, `startIcon` or `slotProps`.
- **CR-11.** The chip renders only the caller's `children` inside its root: no close mark while selected, no `close` icon, which the `CloseButton` shared part alone draws, and no owned or visually hidden word for its state, which the selected fill tells the eye and `aria-pressed` the ear.

## Stories

One per value of the deferred design's `State` property, named by its variant name (`penpot/README.md`, "Conventions"), each with the label "Line 5C". Each `play` test reads the accessibility tree and the DOM, not the pixels, and ends with the chip in the state its story shows.

| Story              | Shows                                                                                      | `play` test                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Default`          | At rest, not selected: glass, "Line 5C". The subject story: its args render the chip alone | The chip is a button named "Line 5C" with `aria-pressed="false"`; Tab focuses it; Space selects it, `aria-pressed` turns `true`, `data-pressed` is set and `onChange` is called once with `true`; Enter clears it again, `aria-pressed` turns `false` and `onChange` is called with `false`; Shift+Tab returns focus; a chip with `selected={false}` whose `onChange` calls `details.cancel()` stays unselected; with the canvas narrowed to a few characters' width the chip wraps onto more than one line and stays inside the canvas, then the canvas is restored, and a single word longer than a container a dozen characters wide breaks within the chip, which stays inside the container with nothing overflowing (CR-7); `children` as an element and as a list of an element and a string each render inside the one root |
| `Hover`            | At rest, hovered                                                                           | Hovering lays `color.surface.hover` over the glass as a `background-image`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `Focus`            | At rest, focused from the keyboard                                                         | Tab gives the root `:focus-visible` and the ring                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `Disabled`         | At rest, disabled                                                                          | The chip has `disabled` and `data-disabled`, Tab skips it, and a click calls no `onChange` and leaves `aria-pressed` `false`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `Selected`         | Selected (`defaultSelected`): `color.surface.inverse` with `color.text.inverse`            | `aria-pressed` is `true` and `data-pressed` is set; the chip's border box has the same width and height as the unselected chip's with the same words (CR-4)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `SelectedHover`    | Selected, hovered                                                                          | Hovering sets the `color.surface.inverse-hover` fill                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
