| `SelectedDisabled` | Selected and disabled: `color.surface.inset` with `color.text.tertiary`                    | `aria-pressed` is `true`, the chip has `disabled`, and a click calls no `onChange`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |

## Do and don't

For a caller using the component, with the reason.

| Do                                                                                                                                 | Don't                                                                                                                                                    |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Name what the chip highlights in a word or two: "Line 5C", "Delayed vehicles".                                                     | Write an instruction such as "Click to highlight": `aria-pressed` already says it is a toggle and whether it is on.                                      |
| Float one chip over the map, placed by the screen with `z-index.highlight`, and clear it on Esc after a dialog and a detail panel. | Put a row of highlight chips in a panel or the top bar: a filter people turn on and off there is a FilterChip, and a choice of views a SegmentedControl. |
| Control it with `selected` when the map can change the highlight too, such as a click on another line.                             | Keep a second copy of the state beside an uncontrolled chip: the two drift apart, and the chip says the highlight is on when it is not.                  |
| Put a LineBadge or an icon in `children` beside the words when it helps the eye find the line.                                     | Give the chip a badge or an icon alone: its content is its name, and a screen reader needs the words.                                                    |
| Change the words with the state when the action reads better that way, as "Follow" and "Following" do.                             | Restyle the selected chip through `className` to look like the unselected one: the inverse fill is what tells the eye the highlight is on.               |
| Let the chip wrap in a narrow container: it grows taller and keeps every word.                                                     | Cut its words off with `nowrap` and an ellipsis through `className`: a Danish line name at 320 px would lose its end.                                    |

# NumberField The box a person types a number into, or steps up and down with its minus and plus buttons and the arrow keys, such as how many departures a board shows, framed by the [Field](field.md) that gives it its label, its line of help and its error message. The design is deferred (ADR 0010, `docs/adr/0010-unattended-runs-with-design-deferred.md`): there is no read-back, code map or export, and this spec decides what the drawing would, from the [contract](README.md), the [foundations](../foundations/README.md), the tokens, the Base UI reference for `NumberField` (`@base-ui/react` 1.9.0, installed, its keys, labels and button semantics confirmed in the installed `NumberFieldInput`, `NumberFieldRoot` and `useNumberFieldStepperButton`), the [Field](field.md) spec, the entry NumberField's registry entry names in `dependsOn`, and its siblings in the Fields family, [TextField](text-field.md) and [SearchField](search-field.md). No ROADMAP line names NumberField, and the extracted prototype component is not in any branch this run can reach. ## Anatomy Penpot page `Components/NumberField`. Family: Fields, for the box. Shared parts: `VisuallyHidden`, through Field, for a hidden label. NumberField composes the [Field](field.md) component for the frame, and Base UI's `NumberField.Root`, `NumberField.Group`, `NumberField.Input`, `NumberField.Decrement` and `NumberField.Increment`, the parts its registry entry lists, for the control. Field's `Field.Root`, `Field.Label`, `Field.Description` and `Field.Error` are reached through Field's props and `slotProps`, as TextField reaches them, so the frame is drawn once, in Field's folder. Base UI's `NumberField.ScrubArea` and `NumberField.ScrubAreaCursor` are left out, as the registry entry leaves them out: dragging a label to change a number is a design tool's gesture, the cursor takes the pointer lock, and the keys and the buttons already step the value. NumberField's root is Base UI's `NumberField.Root`, with Field rendered round it as the frame and reached through `slotProps.field`, as TextField's root is its control and its frame `slotProps.field`. `NumberField.Root` is where Base UI takes the value and every number prop (`min`, `max`, `step`, `format`, `name`, `required`, `readOnly`), so `{...rest}` reaches them with no prop of NumberField's own; the contract's "Native text" rule doesn't apply, since the value is a number Base UI keeps, submitted through its hidden ``, which makes NumberField a composite control whose `name` goes to Base UI's root (the contract's "Forms"); and TextField's `field` key is then the one way into the frame in both siblings. The parts sit in the order the frame gives, label, description, the box, error, and inside the box the input, then the decrement button, then the increment button. | Part (Penpot layer) | What it is | Base UI part | Class | `slotProps` key | | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- | --------------- | | `root` | A `
` that holds the box and gives the number's state to every part; Base UI renders its hidden `` beside it, for a form | `NumberField.Root` | `pn-NumberField` | none | | `field` | The frame round the control: Field's root `

title: RadioGroup
markdown:
# RadioGroup

A named set of two to six choices of which exactly one holds at a time, such as the theme the map is drawn in, each a round mark beside its words.

<!-- run notes -->

The design is deferred (ADR 0010, `docs/adr/0010-unattended-runs-with-design-deferred.md`): there is no read-back, code map or export, and this spec decides what the drawing would, from the [contract](README.md), the [foundations](../foundations/README.md), [content design](../content-design.md), the tokens, the Base UI reference for `RadioGroup` and `Radio` (`@base-ui/react` 1.9.0, installed) and the spec of the one entry in `dependsOn`, [Fieldset](fieldset.md). No ROADMAP line names RadioGroup; it joined the registry with the form components, with `baseUiParts` `RadioGroup`, `Radio.Root` and `Radio.Indicator`. The extracted prototype component is not in any branch this run can reach, so nothing here rests on it. [Switch](switch.md), the other two-state form control, and [Field](field.md), the frame round one form control, have shipped and are in this branch: the radio's look follows Switch's where the two meet (the on fill, the hover, the disabled, read-only and invalid looks, the cursor), and what Field means for the group is in Anatomy.

The foundations already name most of the look: [Elevation](../foundations/elevation.md#surfaces) puts inputs on `color.surface.raised` and pressed toggles on `color.surface.inverse`; [Accessibility](../foundations/accessibility.md#rules) asks every target to be `size.target-min` and every control's edge to reach 3:1, which `color.border.control` does; [Semantic spacing](../foundations/semantic-spacing.md) gives round marks `radius.full`; and Fieldset's spec says RadioGroup renders Fieldset with Base UI's `RadioGroup` through `render`, so the group takes Fieldset's legend, its name and its disabled state (Fieldset CR-5).

## Anatomy

Penpot page `Components/RadioGroup`. Family: none (the contract's [Families](README.md#families) have no round choice mark; a radio is not a Row, since it takes no fill on hover, and its mark's surfaces come from [Elevation](../foundations/elevation.md#surfaces)). Shared parts: `VisuallyHidden`, through Fieldset, for a hidden label.

The control is written as two components, `RadioGroup` for the named group and `Radio` for each choice, both exported with their props types from `RadioGroup.tsx`, an exception to the contract's "one component per folder" as SegmentedControl, Tabs and Toolbar are. Base UI's `Radio.Root` reads `RadioGroup`'s context for its checked state, so a radio can't be shown apart from its group; the caller writes a radio many times, so it is a component of its own; a child component takes a `ReactNode` label where an `options` array would need a shape of its own; MUI writes `<RadioGroup>` round its radios too; and the registry's one entry, with `baseUiParts` `RadioGroup`, `Radio.Root` and `Radio.Indicator`, stays one entry. The `props` check reads both props types, and the `api-compatibility` check only `RadioGroupProps`, so the review holds `RadioProps` to the contract's Change rules.

A radio's root is Base UI's `Radio.Root` itself, the `<span role="radio">` holding the round mark and the words as one row, rather than a `<label>` wrapped round a bare `Radio.Root`, as Checkbox's root, which has shipped, is its `Checkbox.Root`. The row is then the radio: one element takes the `ref`, the class, the rest props, `render` and the focus ring; a click anywhere on it, mark or words, selects it through Base UI's own click; its words are its accessible name, as a radio's role takes its name from its content; the whole row is the target, so it passes `size.target-min` with room to spare; and `slotProps` has one key, `indicator`, named for the one inner Base UI part. A wrapping `<label>` would be an element with no Base UI part as the component's root, which takes `className` and `ref` while `render` and the rest props would reach a part inside it.

| Part (Penpot layer) | What it is                                                                                                                                                                                                                | Base UI part                                               | Class                                                          | `slotProps` key           |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------- |
| `root`              | `RadioGroup`: a `<div role="radiogroup">`, Fieldset's flex column, that stacks the legend over the caller's `Radio`s, owns the value and is named by the legend                                                           | `RadioGroup`, rendered by `Fieldset.Root` through `render` | `pn-RadioGroup`, beside Fieldset's `pn-Fieldset`               | none                      |
| `legend`            | Fieldset's legend: a `<div>` holding the caller's `label`, the group's name, first in the root; with `hiddenLabel`, a `VisuallyHidden` span the eye never sees                                                            | `Fieldset.Legend`, through Fieldset                        | `pn-RadioGroup-legend`, beside Fieldset's `pn-Fieldset-legend` | `legend`                  |
| `radio`             | `Radio`: the `<span role="radio">` of one choice, a flex row, as wide as its words up to the group's width, that holds the indicator and the label and takes focus                                                        | `Radio.Root`                                               | `pn-Radio`                                                     | none (`Radio`'s own root) |
| `indicator`         | The round mark at the radio's inline start: a circle with a control edge, filled and holding a dot while the radio is checked; always mounted                                                                             | `Radio.Indicator`, with `keepMounted`                      | `pn-Radio-indicator`                                           | `indicator` (on `Radio`)  |
| `label`             | A `<span>` after the indicator that holds the caller's `children`, the radio's one text flex item, so a label given as text and an element flows and wraps as one run of text, as `pn-Segment-label` does                 | none: a span inside `Radio.Root`                           | `pn-Radio-label`                                               | none                      |
| `input`             | Not drawn: the visually hidden `<input type="radio">` Base UI renders beside each radio's root, `aria-hidden` and out of the tab order, that a native `<form>` reads; out of the flow, so the group's gap never counts it | `Radio.Root`                                               | none                                                           | none                      |
| `focusRing`         | The keyboard focus ring round a radio's whole row: the `:focus-visible` outline `perron.css` draws, following the row's radius, not an element                                                                            | `Radio.Root`                                               | none                                                           | none                      |

The indicator is the whole circle, not only its dot: Base UI's `Radio.Indicator` with `keepMounted` stays in the DOM while the radio is unchecked and carries the radio's state attributes (`data-checked`, `data-unchecked`, `data-disabled`, `data-readonly`, `data-invalid`), so the mark is drawn by one element whose own attributes select each state, one class then attributes; the dot is its `::before`, drawn only on `[data-checked]`. The `input` has no class and no `slotProps` key: Base UI renders it inside `Radio.Root`'s fragment and gives the caller `inputRef`, `id` and the group's `name` and `form` to reach it.

RadioGroup takes no description and no error of its own, though Perron's [Field](field.md) has shipped with a required `label` it always renders as `Field.Label`: a caller who needs either wraps the group in Base UI's `Field.Root` with `Field.Description` and `Field.Error` and no `Field.Label`, never in Perron's Field, until Field can frame a group. In the installed Base UI a `Field.Label` at the field's root renames every radio in it, though not the group: the group's own default `aria-labelledby` takes the field's label id before the legend's (`radio-group/RadioGroup.js`), but `Fieldset.Root` hands the rendered group the legend's id as an element prop (`fieldset/root/FieldsetRoot.js`), which wins over that default, so the group keeps its legend as its name; each `Radio.Root`, though, takes the field's label id as its `aria-labelledby` in place of its own words (`radio/root/RadioRoot.js`, through `useAriaLabelledBy`), so inside Perron's Field every radio would be heard as the field's label; Base UI's forms guide frames a radio group with a `Field.Root` and no label at its root, which keeps the legend the group's name and each radio's words its own, while Base UI still ties the description and the error to the group and marks each radio invalid; a `description` and an `error` on RadioGroup would build Field's parts, look and validation props a second time, and again on CheckboxGroup, where one change to Field would serve both; and either prop can join RadioGroup later without a break. The `Invalid` story uses Base UI's `Field.Root` that way.

## Base UI parts

Imported from `@base-ui/react/radio-group` and `@base-ui/react/radio`, at the version pinned in `packages/perron/package.json` (1.9.0 installed), and Perron's own [Fieldset](fieldset.md), which brings `Fieldset.Root` and `Fieldset.Legend`.

| Base UI part      | Renders                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | Perron sets                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | Passed through                                                                                                                        |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Fieldset.Root`   | Through Perron's Fieldset, rendered as Base UI's `RadioGroup` through `render`: it hands the group `aria-labelledby` (the legend's id), `disabled`, `data-disabled`, the class and the children                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | Through Fieldset: `legend` from `label`, `hiddenLegend` from `hiddenLabel`, `disabled`, `className` (`pn-RadioGroup`, then the caller's), `ref`, `slotProps.legend` with `pn-RadioGroup-legend` joined to its class, `render` the Base UI group below, and the caller's `children` | none: every caller's prop reaches the group below                                                                                     |

a disabled group, or a checked radio disabled alone, keeps the group's one tab stop, a focusable radio announced as dimmed that Space and a click don't change (the installed `RadioGroup` keeps its roving `tabIndex` of 0 while disabled), and from a checked radio disabled alone the arrow keys move on to the enabled radios; a read-only group keeps its tab stop and lets the arrows move focus but checks nothing, and sets `aria-readonly`; `onValueChange` passes `details` whose `cancel()` keeps an uncontrolled group as it was; each hidden input carries the group's `name`, so a native `<form>` submits the checked radio's `value` and `FormData` reads it; `required` makes the hidden inputs required, so a native form won't submit with none checked; the group takes the legend's id as its `aria-labelledby` from the Fieldset round it; inside a Base UI `Field.Root` it takes the field's name, disabled state and validation, joins the field's description and error into the group's `aria-describedby` and each radio's, and sets `aria-invalid` on the group and on each radio, and `data-invalid` on each, while the field is invalid; a `Field.Label` at that field's root becomes the `aria-labelledby` of each radio, in place of its own words, but not of the group, whose legend's id `Fieldset.Root` passes as an element prop, which wins over the group's own default; Left and Right swap only under Base UI's `DirectionProvider` set to `rtl`, which Perron doesn't set up, as all four locales run left to right.

## Props

In MUI's layout. Every prop the props types declare gets this description as its JSDoc; every inherited one keeps Base UI's. Slots come last.

The group's name is the `label` prop, with `hiddenLabel` to hear it without seeing it, as SearchField's are, passed to Fieldset as its `legend` and `hiddenLegend`. A radio group is one form control with one value, named as a field is, and SearchField already ships `label` and `hiddenLabel` for a field's name; MUI's form controls take `label` for their name; Fieldset's spec expects RadioGroup to pass its own `hiddenLabel` straight to Fieldset's `hiddenLegend`; and `legend` would name the group by the HTML element it renders through, which a caller of a radio group never writes. The prop is required, as Fieldset's `legend` is, so the group is never announced unnamed.

The value is a `string`, and no radio is checked while neither `value` nor `defaultValue` is given. Base UI's `RadioGroup` takes any value, but a `string` is what a hidden input submits and what `onChange` narrows without a cast, as SegmentedControl's value is; Base UI checks nothing by default and has no fallback, and building one would mean reading the radios' values out of `children`; and a group with nothing checked is the caller's choice, such as a question not yet answered, which `required` then holds to an answer.

The group comes in one look, a vertical column, with no `variant`, `size`, `color` or `orientation`. The [brand](../foundations/README.md#the-brand) keeps the interface to ink and neutral surfaces, and a radio is never the main action, so it takes no `brand`; a row is `size.target-min` tall, the smallest target, so a `small` would miss it; Mylder's choices sit in panels and sheets, where a column reads each choice in full and wraps a long Danish one, and a row of radios is what SegmentedControl draws better; Base UI's group takes no orientation of its own and its arrow keys already run all four ways; and each prop can join later without a break.

The group passes Base UI's `form` and `inputRef` through unchanged and declares `name`, `disabled`, `readOnly` and `required` with Perron's own descriptions: the contract's [State and events](README.md#state-and-events) asks a radio group for `name`, and names `required` and `readOnly` among its booleans. A radio passes Base UI's `nativeButton`, `readOnly`, `required` and `inputRef` through; a radio's own `readOnly` or `required` adds to the group's, which Base UI joins with an "or". No label-override props: the component owns no strings.

RadioGroup takes no `description` and no `error`: a hint or an error reaches the group through Base UI's `Field.Root` round it, with `Field.Description` and `Field.Error` and no `Field.Label`, as Anatomy says, never through Perron's [Field](field.md), whose required label would rename every radio in it (CR-12); either prop can join later without a break.

`Radio` takes no description line of its own: `children` is phrasing content in one span, so a caller who needs a second line can set one in it, and a `description` prop, with its own typography and `aria-describedby`, can join later without a break.

## Tokens

One row per part, state and property. States are the contract's design states: rest is no selector (an unchecked radio, `[data-unchecked]`), hover is `:hover` on the radio inside `@media (hover: hover)`, pressed is `:active` on the radio, focus is `:focus-visible` on the radio, disabled is `[data-disabled]`, selected is Base UI's `[data-checked]` (the radio checked), and invalid is `[data-invalid]`, which Base UI sets only inside a `Field.Root` whose field is invalid. Highlighted and open don't apply: a radio takes focus rather than `data-highlighted`, and opens nothing. The indicator reads its own state attributes; hover and pressed are the radio's, read on the indicator inside it as Checkbox's indicator reads its row (`[role]:hover > .pn-Radio-indicator`), with the disabled and read-only guard on the indicator's own attributes, so hovering the words lights the mark.

The group itself sets nothing Fieldset doesn't, but its disabled legend's `GrayText` under forced colours (CR-11): Fieldset's root is the flex column with its `space.200` gap between the legend and each radio, and its legend is `typography.label` in `color.text.primary`, tertiary while disabled. RadioGroup's CSS draws the radios.

The indicator is a 16 px circle, `icon.size.400`, with a dot half its size, centred on the first line of the label in `typography.body`. `icon.size.400` is the size of the marks inside Perron's controls, and a radio's circle is one; 16 px beside 14 px body text is the size Base UI's own demo and most systems draw, and the size of Checkbox's shipped box, which takes it from `size.checkbox`, a token of its own, so the two marks agree in size though not in token; a dot of half the circle, `calc()` over the same token, keeps the proportion if the token changes; and `margin-block` of half the line less half the circle (`1lh`, the contract's one line of the element's own typography) keeps the mark on the first line when a long label wraps. A size token of its own, such as `size.choice-mark`, would go through the `design-tokens` skill instead.

A checked radio is a `color.surface.inverse` circle and edge with a `color.surface.raised` dot, and an unchecked one a `color.surface.raised` circle with a `border.width.025` edge in `color.border.control`. [Elevation](../foundations/elevation.md#surfaces) puts inputs on `color.surface.raised` and pressed toggles on `color.surface.inverse`, the fill FilterChip's selected state, Switch's on track and Checkbox's ticked box take; `color.border.control` is the edge that shows where a control is, 3:1 or better on every surface ([Accessibility](../foundations/accessibility.md#controls-focus-and-status-fills-on-surfaces)), so an unchecked circle shows on a raised panel; a checked radio differs in its fill and in its dot, never in colour alone; and the edge keeps its width when checked, in the fill's colour, so the geometry holds (CR-6). A thick ink ring with an ink dot, the classic look `border.width.050` could give, would be a second way to show a pressed control.

A disabled radio unchecked is a `color.surface.inset` circle with a `color.border.subtle` edge, and checked a `color.text.tertiary` circle and edge with a `color.surface.raised` dot, its words `color.text.tertiary`, with no hover or pressed layer, as Switch's are; Checkbox draws its own disabled box, a transparent one with a `color.border.subtle` edge unticked and a `color.surface.inset` one with a `color.text.tertiary` mark ticked. The contract makes disabled a colour, `color.text.tertiary`, never an opacity; a disabled control is exempt from 3:1, so the edge steps down to the decorative `color.border.subtle`; and a disabled group still shows which choice it holds, as a disabled segmented control keeps its choice.

Read-only and invalid are states Base UI's parts produce (`data-readonly`, `data-invalid`) that no drawing shows: a read-only radio looks as at rest, checked or not, with no hover or pressed layer and the default cursor, and an invalid one turns its edge `color.status.danger`, checked or not, with its fills unchanged and disabled winning over it, as Switch's are and Checkbox's are. A read-only group keeps its tab stop, so a dimmed look would read as disabled, which it isn't; the contract's [Families](README.md#families) give the Fields' edge `color.status.danger` when invalid, a radio group sits in a Field beside them, and the message that says why is the Field's; and Base UI drops `aria-invalid` while a control is disabled, which is exempt from 3:1 and shows no error.

The focus ring goes round the radio's whole row, the outline `perron.css` draws on its `:focus-visible`, with the row's `radius.md`, rather than round the circle alone. The row is the element that takes focus and the target a click lands on, so the ring shows what Space will check; `perron.css` already draws it, so the component draws no ring of its own and removes no outline, as [Accessibility](../foundations/accessibility.md#rules) asks; and `radius.md` is the radius of a button and a row, so the ring reads as theirs. A ring round the circle alone would hide the row's outline and draw a second ring on the indicator with `focus.width`, `focus.offset` and `color.border.focus`.

A single-line radio is `size.target-min` tall: the `typography.body` line is 21 px, and the block padding adds the rest. A radio is as wide as its indicator, the gap and its words, and never wider than the group, so its hover and its ring end where its words do. The indicator's dot is centred inside its edge (`display: grid; place-items: center`, with `box-sizing: border-box`). Required changes no look: Base UI's `data-required` sets nothing, and the label or the Field says the choice is required. Base UI's other field attributes, `data-dirty`, `data-touched`, `data-filled` and `data-focused`, set nothing either.

Nothing moves: a radio's fill and dot change at once. [Motion](../foundations/motion.md) says motion explains a change of place, and nothing in a radio changes place, where a switch's thumb slides to its other end; the contract's [CSS](README.md#css) says a state with no fitting duration changes at once; and `duration.switch`, the one short duration, is described as the switch's thumb slide and track fill.

What axe won't catch, from the contract, each with how this component meets it:

- [ ] Everything the eye is told, the ear is told, for every shape each prop accepts: the checked radio's filled circle and dot are `aria-checked="true"` and every other radio's `"false"`; a disabled radio's tertiary colours are `aria-disabled`, heard as dimmed, on each radio of a disabled group; a read-only group is `aria-readonly`; an invalid radio's danger edge is `aria-invalid`, with the Field's message as its description; the label the eye reads above the radios is the group's name, and a hidden label still is.
- [ ] Every landmark and named region has an accessible name: the root is a `radiogroup`, not a landmark, and is always named by its `label`, which is required (CR-2).
- [ ] Every default label can be overridden: none here; the component owns no strings.
- [ ] Every shape the type accepts renders, in every variant: `label` and a radio's `children` render a string, an element and a list alike: `Default` names its group with a string, and `LabelShapes` with a list and, in its `play` test, an element, each heard as one run, over radios whose words are a string, an element and a list; a radio's words sit in one span, so text and elements flow and wrap as one run beside the mark.
- [ ] A hidden copy kept for animation is `aria-hidden`, and a collapsed region is `inert`: the hidden inputs are Base UI's, `aria-hidden` and out of the tab order; the indicator kept mounted while unchecked holds no text, so it adds nothing to the tree; nothing collapses.
- [ ] Native semantics first: Base UI's `radiogroup` and `radio` roles with `aria-checked`, with a native `<input type="radio">` beside each for the form; with `render` and `nativeButton`, a native `<button>`. Perron adds no ARIA.
- [ ] Focus moves in reading order and returns on close: the arrow keys move through the radios in document order, below their label, and Tab leaves the group after its one stop; focus stays on the radio it checks; the group opens nothing to return from.
- [ ] Every target is at least `size.target-min` square: the smallest target is a radio with a one-letter label, `size.target-min` (24 px) tall and the 16 px circle, the `space.200` gap and the letter (at least 24 px) wide.
- [ ] Loops stop when the system asks for less motion: no loop, and no transition; a radio's state changes at once.

## Owned strings

No owned strings: every word RadioGroup shows or announces comes from the caller, through `label` and each radio's `children`. Base UI's roles say checked or not checked, and a radio's place in its group, in every locale with no word of Perron's.

## Component rules

Rules for this component alone, numbered so the build and the review can cite them.

- **CR-1.** Base UI's group and radios already give the roles, `aria-checked`, the one tab stop and its roving `tabIndex`, the arrow keys that move and check, Space, the click, disabled and read-only, the hidden inputs and the Field integration, so the component rebuilds none of it and adds no key or click handlers. Perron forces no `tabIndex`: a disabled group, or a checked radio disabled alone, keeps Base UI's one focusable stop, announced as dimmed, that changes nothing, and the arrow keys skip disabled radios.
- **CR-2.** RadioGroup renders Perron's [Fieldset](fieldset.md) with Base UI's `RadioGroup` as its `render`, as Base UI's forms guide composes `<Fieldset.Root render={<RadioGroup />}>`: `label` is Fieldset's required `legend` and `hiddenLabel` its `hiddenLegend`, so the group is always named by its legend's id through `aria-labelledby` and a hidden label stays in the tree; `disabled` reaches Fieldset, which hands it to the group and shares it through Base UI's context. The root keeps Fieldset's `pn-Fieldset` and its column and gap, and RadioGroup's CSS sets no `gap`, `padding` or `border` on it.
- **CR-3.** RadioGroup adapts Base UI's `onValueChange(value, details)` into `onChange(details.event, value, details)` inside itself and exposes no `onValueChange`. It passes `value` only when given, so a group given neither `value` nor `defaultValue` is uncontrolled with nothing checked. A click on the radio already checked changes nothing and calls no `onChange`, as Base UI's hidden input fires no change.
- **CR-4.** Each component takes `{...rest}` before its own attributes and its own props out of `rest` first: RadioGroup takes `label`, `hiddenLabel`, `value`, `defaultValue`, `onChange`, `name`, `disabled`, `readOnly`, `required`, `children`, `className`, `style`, `slotProps` and `ref`, and gives `rest` (with `form`, `inputRef`, `render` and the caller's `aria-*`) to Base UI's `RadioGroup`; Radio takes `value`, `disabled`, `children`, `className`, `style`, `slotProps` and `ref`, and gives `rest` (with `readOnly`, `required`, `inputRef`, `nativeButton` and `render`) to `Radio.Root`. `ref` reaches the root of each: the `<div role="radiogroup">` and the `<span role="radio">`. Class order is the component's own first, then the caller's: `pn-RadioGroup` (with Fieldset's `pn-Fieldset`), `pn-RadioGroup-legend` (with Fieldset's `pn-Fieldset-legend`), `pn-Radio`, `pn-Radio-indicator`, through `withClass` where the caller's `className` may be a function of the state.
- **CR-5.** A radio renders `Radio.Indicator` with `keepMounted`, so the circle is drawn while the radio is unchecked, from the indicator's own state attributes; `slotProps.indicator`, typed `Omit<Radio.Indicator.Props, 'keepMounted'>` so a caller can't pass it, as Checkbox's slot leaves out what Checkbox sets (Checkbox sets `render` too, which Radio leaves to the caller), merges under Perron's props with `mergeProps`, Perron's `keepMounted` last. After the indicator comes the label span holding `children`; the radio's root has no other child.
- **CR-6.** The states keep the geometry: hover, pressed, focus, selected, disabled, read-only and invalid change the indicator's fill, its edge's colour and the dot only, never the circle's size, the edge's width or the row's padding, and the indicator never shrinks in its row (`flex-shrink: 0`), so a long label wraps beside it rather than squeezing it.
- **CR-7.** A radio's words break a word longer than their line (`overflow-wrap: anywhere`, on `.pn-Radio`, which sets the typography): a radio is never wider than its group, and "Realtidsdataforsinkelser", wider than 120 px in `typography.body`, wraps beside the circle in a 120 px group, the circle staying on the first line.
- **CR-8.** Hover is read inside `@media (hover: hover)`; pressed (`:active`) takes the pressed fill, a step past hover, in a rule after it and outside it, so a touch press shows. Neither applies to a disabled or a read-only radio: both rules exclude `[data-disabled]` and `[data-readonly]`. Selected is `.pn-Radio-indicator[data-checked]`, one class then attributes, from the indicator's own state attributes.
- **CR-9.** A read-only radio looks as at rest, checked or not, with no hover or pressed layer and the default cursor; the label or the Field's description says why it can't change. An invalid one turns its indicator's edge `color.status.danger`, checked or not, and a disabled one keeps its disabled edge even inside an invalid Field.
- **CR-10.** Focus uses the ring `perron.css` draws on the radio's `:focus-visible`, which follows its `radius.md`; the component draws no ring of its own and never removes the outline. Nothing in RadioGroup or Radio sets `overflow`, so a ring drawn `focus.offset` outside a radio is never cut at the group's edge.
- **CR-11.** In `@media (forced-colors: active)`, where the browser drops the fills, the indicator sets `forced-color-adjust: none` and draws its states in system colours: unchecked, a `Canvas` circle with a `ButtonText` edge; checked, a `Highlight` circle and edge with a `HighlightText` dot; disabled, a `GrayText` edge unchecked, and a `GrayText` circle and edge with a `Canvas` dot checked. A disabled radio's words and a disabled group's legend take `GrayText` too, since neither the radio's `<span>` nor the legend's `<div>` is natively disabled, so the system can't tell their words are, as Checkbox's disabled root does (Checkbox CR-11). So the checked state, which would otherwise vanish into the forced `Canvas`, still shows, as [Accessibility](../foundations/accessibility.md#what-a-person-checks) asks.
- **CR-12.** RadioGroup declares no `description` or `error` prop and renders no Field of its own, Perron's or Base UI's. A hint or an error comes from a Base UI `Field.Root` the caller puts round the group, with `Field.Description` and `Field.Error` and no `Field.Label`, as the `Invalid` story does: inside it the group keeps its legend as its name and each radio its own words, while Base UI joins the description and the error into the group's `aria-describedby` and each radio's and marks the group and each radio invalid. No story and no example wraps the group in Perron's [Field](field.md), whose `Field.Label` would become the `aria-labelledby` of every radio, in place of its own words; the group alone keeps its legend, since `Fieldset.Root` passes the legend's id as an element prop, which wins over the group's own default.

## Stories

The deferred design's page draws two things, the group, `Default`, and the radio, with one variant property, `State` (`default`, `hover`, `focus`, `checked`, `disabled`), its stories prefixed `Radio` as SegmentedControl's segment stories are prefixed `Segment`. The group has no variant property of its own, so its one variant is `Default`; a radio's states are what the drawing has to show; one `State` property names its variants by state alone; and the on state is `checked`, the word of Base UI's `data-checked` and `aria-checked` that a caller looks for, where the contract's design-state name `selected` is a row's.

Every story names its group with `label` "Theme" and gives three radios, "Match the system" (`'system'`), "Light" (`'light'`) and "Dark" (`'dark'`), with `defaultValue` `'system'`, unless its row gives other choices, and then a label that names the question those choices answer, as `LabelShapes` and `LongLabels` do; each sits on a `raised` Surface, as a group sits in a panel. The radio stories put the state on "Light"; the hover and focus stories render at rest: the visual check drives the state, and their `play` tests check it. `Default` is the [subject story](README.md#root), which the contract story renders, and its args hold the label and the radios, so they pass every rule alone and hold every word the caller gives. The group's disabled, read-only and invalid looks and a disabled radio checked, which Base UI's attributes produce beside the drawn states, get stories of their own with no Penpot variant.

| Story           | Shows                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | `play` test                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| --------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Default`       | The group: "Theme" over three radios, "Match the system" checked; the subject story                                                                                                                                                                                              | The root has `role="radiogroup"`, `pn-RadioGroup` and `pn-Fieldset`, and is named "Theme"; the `ref` reaches it; each radio has `role="radio"` and `pn-Radio` and is named by its words; Tab focuses "Match the system"; ArrowDown checks "Light", sets its `aria-checked` to `true` and "Match the system"'s to `false`, and calls `onChange` once with `'light'` and `details.reason` `'none'`; ArrowRight checks "Dark"; ArrowDown from "Dark" wraps to "Match the system"; ArrowUp wraps back to "Dark", and ArrowLeft goes to "Light"; Enter changes nothing; a click on the words "Match the system" checks it; Shift+Tab leaves the group, which ends with "Match the system" checked |
| `RadioDefault`  | A radio at rest, unchecked                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | "Light"'s indicator is `icon.size.400` square with a `border.width.025` edge in `color.border.control` on `color.surface.raised`, its row is `size.target-min` tall, and its words render `typography.body` in `color.text.primary`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `RadioHover`    | A radio, hover                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | Hovering "Light" lays `color.surface.hover` over its indicator's fill and keeps the edge; hovering the checked "Match the system" sets its indicator to `color.surface.inverse-hover`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `RadioFocus`    | A radio, focus, with `defaultValue` `'light'`, since focus rests on the checked radio                                                                                                                                                                                            | Tab gives "Light" `:focus-visible` and the ring round its whole row, following its `radius.md`; Shift+Tab leaves the group, which ends with "Light" checked                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `RadioChecked`  | A radio, checked, with `defaultValue` `'light'`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | "Light" has `aria-checked="true"` and its indicator `data-checked`, a `color.surface.inverse` fill and edge and a `color.surface.raised` dot half its size; its indicator is the same size as an unchecked one's (CR-6)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `RadioDisabled` | A radio, disabled                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | "Light" has `aria-disabled="true"` and `data-disabled`, its words are `color.text.tertiary` and its indicator has a `color.border.subtle` edge on `color.surface.inset`; ArrowDown from "Match the system" goes to "Dark"; a click on "Light" checks nothing and calls no `onChange`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `Disabled`      | The whole group disabled, "Match the system" checked, with a Button after it                                                                                                                                                                                                     | Every radio has `aria-disabled="true"`; Tab reaches "Match the system", heard as dimmed and checked, and the next Tab reaches the Button; "Match the system" keeps `aria-checked="true"` and a `color.text.tertiary` circle with a `color.surface.raised` dot; the legend has `data-disabled`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `ReadOnly`      | The group read-only, "Match the system" checked                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | The root has `aria-readonly="true"`; Tab reaches "Match the system"; ArrowDown moves focus to "Light" without checking it; Space and a click check nothing and call no `onChange`; hovering adds no fill                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `Invalid`       | The group, nothing checked and `required`, in a Base UI `Field.Root` marked invalid, with no `Field.Label` and its `Field.Error` "Choose a theme"                                                                                                                                | Each radio has `aria-invalid="true"`, is described by "Choose a theme" and is still named by its own words, and its indicator has `data-invalid` and a `color.status.danger` edge; the group is still named "Theme", has `aria-invalid="true"` and is described by "Choose a theme"                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `HiddenLabel`   | The `Default` group with `hiddenLabel`, inside a [Section](section.md) titled "Theme" that names it for the eye                                                                                                                                                                  | The group is still named "Theme"; the legend renders as the `VisuallyHidden` span; the first radio sits at the root's top edge, with no gap above it                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `Controlled`    | A group given `value` and `onChange` from the story's state                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | A click on "Dark" calls `onChange` with `'dark'`; the check moves only once the story sets `value`, and a group whose caller ignores the change stays on "Match the system"; an uncontrolled group whose `onChange` calls `details.cancel()` stays as it was; the story ends on "Match the system"                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `LabelShapes`   | A group whose `label` is a list, "Show on" then "map" in a `<span>`, over three radios whose words are a string ("Planned works"), an element ("Diversions" in a `<span>`) and a list, text then an element ("Data feed", then "problems" in a `<span>`), in a 320 px wide group | The group is named "Show on map", its list label read as one run, and a group whose `label` is an element, "Show on map" in a `<span>`, is named the same; each radio holds two elements, its indicator and its `pn-Radio-label`; the list's words read as one run, "Data feed problems", in its accessible name                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `LongLabels`    | A Danish group, `lang` `da`, "Vis på kort" over three radios, "Omkørsler", "Planlagt arbejde" and "Realtidsdataforsinkelser", in a 120 px wide group                                                                                                                             | The long word wraps onto more than one line inside its radio (`lines`), which is no wider than the group; the group doesn't scroll sideways (its `scrollWidth` equals its `clientWidth`); the indicator stays `icon.size.400` square and its top sits within the first line (CR-6, CR-7)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `InForm`        | A native `<form>` holding the group with `name` "theme" and a submit button                                                                                                                                                                                                      | `FormData` has "theme" of "system"; after ArrowDown to "Light", it has "theme" of "light"; with `required` and no `defaultValue`, the form reports itself invalid until a radio is checked; the story ends on "Match the system"                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |

## Do and don't

For a caller using the component, with the reason.

| Do                                                                                                                                            | Don't                                                                                                                                                                 |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Use a RadioGroup for one answer of two to six that a person reads in full before choosing, such as the theme or the language                  | Use it for more choices than fit a panel, or for choices that need a search: a select or a search field keeps a long list out of the way                              |
| Switch how one view shows its content with a [SegmentedControl](segmented-control.md), and filter the map with a [FilterChip](filter-chip.md) | Use a row of radios for a view's mode or the top bar's filters: a radio is a form answer, read down a column                                                          |
| Name the group with `label`, in sentence case, a word or a short question: "Theme"                                                            | Leave out the label, or name the group with `aria-label` where there is room to show one: a sighted person can't tell what an unnamed set of choices answers          |
| Write each radio's words as a short noun phrase in sentence case, of a similar length and shape: "Match the system", "Light", "Dark"          | Put a link or a button inside a radio's words: a radio's content is presentational, so a screen reader never reaches it, and a click on it checks the radio too       |
| Check the safest or most common choice with `defaultValue`, or leave all unchecked with `required` when the person must decide                | Check a choice the person never made and then treat it as their answer: a pre-checked radio is easy to pass by                                                        |
| Disable the whole group with `disabled`, or one radio that can't be chosen now, and say why in the label or the Field's description           | Disable a radio with no word of why, or hide it: a dimmed choice can't explain itself, and a missing one moves the others                                             |
| Give a hint or an error through Base UI's `Field.Root` round the group, with `Field.Description` and `Field.Error` and no `Field.Label`       | Put a hint or an error as plain text among the radios: nothing ties it to the group for the ear, and the arrow keys never reach it                                    |
| Name the group with its own `label`                                                                                                           | Wrap the group in Perron's [Field](field.md): its label renames every radio in it, so each radio is heard as the field's label, never its own words                   |
| Use a checkbox for a choice that can be on or off on its own, or several at once                                                              | Use a RadioGroup of one radio, or of "Yes" and "No" for a setting that takes effect at once: one radio can't be unchecked, and a setting that applies now is a switch |

title: SearchField

# SearchField

The field that finds a line or a stop: a labelled text input with the search icon, a clear button while it holds text, and a list of suggestions under it that narrows as the person types.

<!-- run notes -->

The design is deferred (ADR 0010, `docs/adr/0010-unattended-runs-with-design-deferred.md`): there is no read-back, code map or export, and this spec decides what the drawing would, from the [contract](README.md), the [foundations](../foundations/README.md), the tokens and the Base UI reference for `Field` and `Autocomplete` (`@base-ui/react` 1.9.0, installed). The extracted prototype component is not in any branch this run can reach.

## Anatomy

Penpot page `Components/SearchField`. Family: Fields, for the input group; Popups, for the list's popup; Rows, for its suggestions. Shared parts: `VisuallyHidden`, for a hidden label; `CloseButton`, for the clear button.

SearchField is a text field whose value is the words typed, with suggestions under it: Base UI's Autocomplete, not its Combobox, which keeps a chosen item as its value. It composes the parts the registry entry lists, `Field.Root`, `Field.Label` and the ten `Autocomplete` parts from `Autocomplete.Root` to `Autocomplete.Empty`, and none of Autocomplete's others: no `Autocomplete.Trigger` or `Autocomplete.Icon`, since the list opens as the person types; no `Group`, `GroupLabel`, `Separator`, `Row` or `Collection`, since the suggestions are one flat list; no `Status`, `Backdrop` or `Arrow`. Groups can join later, as an optional prop, without a break.

The suggestions are data, `items`, and SearchField draws each row, so the caller never writes a row and there is no `SearchFieldItem` component: the contract's rule of a component per child applies to a child the caller writes many times.

| Part (Penpot layer) | What it is                                                                                                                                                                            | Base UI part              | Class                        | `slotProps` key |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------- | ---------------------------- | --------------- |
| `root`              | A `<div>`, a flex column that stacks the label over the input group and takes its container's width                                                                                   | `Field.Root`              | `pn-SearchField`             | none            |
| `label`             | The `<label>` that holds the caller's `label` and names the input; with `hiddenLabel`, a `VisuallyHidden` span the eye never sees                                                     | `Field.Label`             | `pn-SearchField-label`       | `label`         |
| `inputGroup`        | The field's box, `size.input` tall: a flex row on the Fields family's fill and edge that holds the icon, the input and the clear button, and the box the list is placed against       | `Autocomplete.InputGroup` | `pn-SearchField-inputGroup`  | `inputGroup`    |
| `icon`              | The `search` icon at the start of the box, an inline SVG hidden from screen readers                                                                                                   | none: an `<svg>`          | `pn-SearchField-icon`        | none            |
| `input`             | The native `<input>` the person types in, transparent inside the box, growing to fill it                                                                                              | `Autocomplete.Input`      | `pn-SearchField-input`       | `input`         |
| `clear`             | The `CloseButton` at the end of the box, named by the owned "Clear"; rendered only while the input holds text and the field is not disabled                                           | `Autocomplete.Clear`      | `pn-SearchField-clear`       | `clear`         |
| `portal`            | Not drawn: the `<div>` Base UI appends to `<body>` while the list is open                                                                                                             | `Autocomplete.Portal`     | `pn-SearchField-portal`      | `portal`        |
| `positioner`        | Not drawn: the box Base UI places under the input group, flipping above it when there is no room, and that carries the stacking and the gap                                           | `Autocomplete.Positioner` | `pn-SearchField-positioner`  | `positioner`    |
| `popup`             | The list's glass panel, as wide as the input group, that scrolls when the suggestions are taller than the room                                                                        | `Autocomplete.Popup`      | `pn-SearchField-popup`       | `popup`         |
| `empty`             | The message the popup shows when no suggestion matches, the owned "No matches", a polite live region that stays mounted and holds nothing while there are matches                     | `Autocomplete.Empty`      | `pn-SearchField-empty`       | `empty`         |
| `list`              | The `<div role="listbox">` that holds one row per matching item                                                                                                                       | `Autocomplete.List`       | `pn-SearchField-list`        | `list`          |
| `item`              | One suggestion: a row, a flex row of the item's `startIcon` and its text, highlighted under the pointer or the arrow keys                                                             | `Autocomplete.Item`       | `pn-SearchField-item`        | `item`          |
| `startIcon`         | A `<span>` before the text that holds the item's `startIcon`, such as a [StationIcon](station-icon.md) or a [LineBadge](line-badge.md); rendered only when the item gives one         | none: a `<span>`          | `pn-SearchField-startIcon`   | none            |
| `text`              | A `<span>`, a flex column that holds the item's label and description                                                                                                                 | none: a `<span>`          | `pn-SearchField-text`        | none            |
| `itemLabel`         | A `<span>` that holds the item's `label`, the words the input takes when the item is chosen                                                                                           | none: a `<span>`          | `pn-SearchField-itemLabel`   | none            |
| `description`       | A `<span>` under the label that holds the item's `description`, such as "Metro, S-tog and bus"; rendered only when the item gives one                                                 | none: a `<span>`          | `pn-SearchField-description` | none            |
| `focusRing`         | The keyboard focus ring round the input group while the input has `:focus-visible`, drawn on the group so it rings the whole box rather than the bare input inside it; not an element | `Autocomplete.InputGroup` | none                         | none            |

`Autocomplete.Root` groups the Autocomplete parts and holds the value and the open state; it renders no element, so it has no layer, class or `slotProps` key. The item's inner spans are named for the item fields they show, `itemLabel` rather than `label`, since `label` is the field's own part.

The clear button composes the `CloseButton` shared part, rendered through `Autocomplete.Clear`'s `render` as `<Autocomplete.Clear render={<CloseButton label={strings.clear} />} />`. It keeps the part's own `size.control` square and looks, SearchField's CSS sets only its place in the row, it is left out entirely while the field is disabled, and the build adds `Autocomplete.Clear` to the part's "Composed in" cell in the contract's Shared parts table. The contract's `shared-parts` check keeps the `close` icon inside `CloseButton`'s folder, so SearchField can't draw a cross of its own; a 34 px square sits inside the 38 px box with a pixel to spare above and below; and the part has no disabled look (Dialog CR-6), while a disabled field takes no clearing, so the button is not rendered rather than shown live.

## Base UI parts

Imported from `@base-ui/react/field` and `@base-ui/react/autocomplete`, at the version pinned in `package.json` (1.9.0 installed).

| Base UI part              | Renders                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | Perron sets                                                                                                                                                                                | Passed through                                                                                                            |
| ------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Field.Root`              | A `<div>`, with `data-disabled`, `data-filled`, `data-focused`, `data-dirty`, `data-touched` and `data-valid`                                                                                                                                                                             | `className` (`pn-SearchField`, then the caller's), `ref`, and the parts below as children                                                                                                  | `name`, `disabled`, `render`, `style` and every other prop of a `<div>`, through `{...rest}`                              |
| `Field.Label`             | A `<label>`, its id the input's `aria-labelledby`; with `hiddenLabel`, the `VisuallyHidden` span through `render`, with `nativeLabel={false}`                                                                                                                                             | `className` (`pn-SearchField-label`, then the caller's), an `id` from React's `useId` that the list's `aria-labelledby` reads, and `label` as children                                     | `slotProps.label`                                                                                                         |
| `Autocomplete.Root`       | No element                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | `items`, `filter`, `value`, `defaultValue`, `open` and `defaultOpen` from SearchField's props; `onValueChange`, turned into `onChange`; `onOpenChange`, turned into `onOpen` and `onClose` | none                                                                                                                      |
| `Autocomplete.InputGroup` | `<div role="group">`, with `data-popup-open`, `data-list-empty`, `data-disabled`, `data-filled` and `data-focused`                                                                                                                                                                        | `className` (`pn-SearchField-inputGroup`, then the caller's), and the icon, the input and the clear button as children                                                                     | `slotProps.inputGroup`                                                                                                    |

Base UI already does: it filters `items` against the typed words, as the person types, with a collator in the runtime's locale that ignores case and accents (`contains`), matching each item's `label`; it opens the list when the person types words that aren't blank (reason `'input-change'`) or presses an arrow key (`'list-navigation'`), and closes it when typing empties the input (`'input-clear'`), on Esc (`'escape-key'`), on a press outside the field and the list (`'outside-press'`), when focus leaves (`'focus-out'`) and when an item is chosen (`'item-press'`); it moves a virtual highlight through the rows with the arrow keys, looping back to the input, keeping focus in the input with `aria-activedescendant`, and highlights a row under the pointer; on an item's press, or Enter on a highlighted row, it fills the input with the item's label, calls the item's `onClick` and closes the list; on Enter with no row highlighted it closes the list (`'none'`) and lets a form around it submit; on Esc with the list closed it empties the input; it shows the clear button only while the input holds text, keeps it out of the tab order and, when it is pressed, empties the input (`'clear-press'`), keeps focus in the input and leaves an open list open, now showing every item, with no `onClose`; it places the popup against the input group, below it, flipping above it when there is no room, and gives it `--anchor-width` and `--available-height`; it names the input by the label, puts the field's `name` on the input itself, so the typed words reach a form's `FormData`, and passes `disabled` from `Field.Root` to the input and the clear button; and it announces the empty message politely when it appears. While the list is open it also adds two screen-reader-only `Dismiss` controls and hides the rest of the page from the ear, the label and the clear button among them (see Keyboard and ARIA, Base UI's known exceptions).

## Props

In MUI's layout. Every prop here gets its description as its JSDoc. Slots come last.

SearchField is a composite control: its root is `Field.Root`'s `<div>`, and its value is the typed words, reported as `onChange(event, value, details)` adapted from `Autocomplete.Root`'s `onValueChange`, not React's own `onChange` on an `<input>` root. The contract's "Native text" rule fits a value only the `<input>` changes, but Base UI also changes this one from outside the input's own events (it fills the input with a chosen item's label, empties it on Esc and on the clear button, each with a `details.reason`), which React's `onChange(event)` never reports; the contract's Forms rule names a combobox among the composite controls; and the root must hold the label as well as the input. The field's `name` still reaches the `<input>`, so a native form submits the typed words, and form libraries connect through their controller.

From `Autocomplete.Root`, SearchField offers only `items`, `filter`, `value`, `defaultValue`, `onChange`, `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpen` and `onClose`. It keeps Base UI's defaults for the rest (`mode` `'list'`, `autoHighlight` `false`, `openOnInputClick` `false`, `submitOnItemClick` `false`, `loopFocus` `true`, `limit` `-1`) and leaves out `readOnly`, `required`, `inline`, `grid`, `virtualized`, `modal`, `itemToStringValue`, `filteredItems`, `onItemHighlighted`, `actionsRef` and `inputRef`. These are what a search for a line or a stop needs; with `autoHighlight` off, Enter on the typed words submits a form around the field, as a search does, and a row is chosen by the arrow keys or the pointer; each prop left out can join later as an optional prop without a break.

`SearchFieldProps` extends `Field.Root.Props` without `children`, `ref`, `invalid`, `validate`, `validationMode`, `validationDebounceTime`, `actionsRef`, `dirty` and `touched`, so `name`, `disabled`, `render`, `className` and `style` are inherited with Base UI's JSDoc, and SearchField has no invalid state. The registry gives SearchField no `Field.Error` or `Field.Description`, so an invalid field could only say so by its red edge, which [Accessibility](../foundations/accessibility.md) forbids as colour alone; a search is never wrong, only empty of matches; and without `required` (left out above), Base UI never marks the field invalid on its own, so `[data-invalid]` never appears and the Fields family's invalid edge is not drawn.

A suggestion is a `SearchFieldItem`, exported from `SearchField.tsx`, of the shape `{ value: string; label: string; description?: ReactNode; startIcon?: ReactNode }`, with `items` typed `ReadonlyArray<SearchFieldItem>` and `filter` typed `((item: SearchFieldItem, query: string) => boolean) | null`. `value` identifies the item and keys its row, so two stops with the same name stay apart; Base UI reads `label` from a `{ value, label }` object on its own, for filtering and to fill the input; `description` is the Rows family's second line; and `startIcon` follows the contract's name for a mark before a label, here a [StationIcon](station-icon.md) or a [LineBadge](line-badge.md). No `disabled` per item: a suggestion that can't be chosen is left out of `items`.

A chosen suggestion is reported by `onItemSelect(event, item)`, called from the item's `onClick` with the click event and the `SearchFieldItem` itself, on a press or on Enter with the row highlighted. `onChange` then carries only the words, with `details.reason` `'item-press'` when an item filled them, and a caller who moves the map to the stop needs the item, not its label, which two items can share. `onSelect` is not used because the root's `<div>` already takes React's `onSelect`, the text-selection event, and no row is ever "selected" in the Rows family's sense: Autocomplete keeps no chosen item.

SearchField takes a required `label` (`ReactNode`) and a `hiddenLabel` boolean, default `false`, that keeps the label for the ear only, rendering it through the `VisuallyHidden` shared part. Every input needs a name, and the label is the only one that never disappears as the placeholder does; Mylder's top bar search shows only the icon and the placeholder, so `hiddenLabel` is how it keeps the name; `hiddenLabel` is MUI's own name for a field without a visible label.

SearchField takes no `variant`, `size`, `color` or `fullWidth`: its root takes its container's width and its box is `size.input` tall. There is one search field look, `size.input` is the one height the layout tokens give a search field, and the contract has a component size to its container, so a caller sets the width on the container or through `className`.

The default filter keeps Base UI's own collator, in the runtime's locale, rather than PerronProvider's locale. PerronProvider exposes no locale to components, only their owned strings, and adding a hook is a change to every component's provider for one prop; the runtime's locale is the person's own; a caller who wants another collator passes it through `filter`.
