| `Escape`                                            | With the list open: closes it (`onClose`, `'escape-key'`). With it closed: empties the box (`onChange`, `''`, `'escape-key'`)                                                                                                                 | Base UI |
| `Home`, `End`                                       | Move the caret to the start or end of the words                                                                                                                                                                                               | Base UI |
| `Tab`, `Shift+Tab`                                  | Move focus out of the field, closing the list (`onClose`, `'focus-out'`); the clear button is not a tab stop, since Esc empties the box from the keyboard                                                                                     | Base UI |
| A screen reader's activation of a `Dismiss` control | Closes the list (`onClose`, `'close-press'`); neither control is a tab stop                                                                                                                                                                   | Base UI |

| Element                      | Role                                                                                                                          | Accessible name from                                                                  | States announced                                                                                     |
| ---------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `label`                      | none: a native `<label>`, or a hidden span                                                                                    | Its text, the caller's `label`                                                        | `aria-hidden="true"` while the list is open, from Base UI: a known exception (below)                 |
| `inputGroup`                 | `group`, from Base UI                                                                                                         | none                                                                                  | none                                                                                                 |
| `input`                      | `combobox`, from Base UI                                                                                                      | `aria-labelledby` the `label`                                                         | `aria-expanded`, `aria-autocomplete="list"`, `aria-activedescendant` the highlighted row, `disabled` |
| `clear`                      | `button`, native                                                                                                              | The owned "Clear", or `clearLabel`, in the `CloseButton`'s `VisuallyHidden` span      | `aria-hidden="true"` while the list is open, from Base UI: a known exception (below)                 |
| `list`                       | `listbox`, from Base UI                                                                                                       | `aria-labelledby` the `label`, which Perron sets                                      | none                                                                                                 |
| `item`                       | `option`, from Base UI                                                                                                        | Its text: the item's `label`, then its `description`, and the text of its `startIcon` | Highlighted through the input's `aria-activedescendant`                                              |
| `empty`                      | `status`, from Base UI                                                                                                        | none: its text, "No matches", announced politely when it appears                      | none                                                                                                 |
| `positioner`, `popup`        | `presentation`, from Base UI                                                                                                  | none                                                                                  | none                                                                                                 |
| Base UI's `Dismiss` controls | `button`, from Base UI: two screen-reader-only `<span>`s while the list is open, one before the input and one after the popup | `aria-label="Dismiss"`, Base UI's own English: a known exception (below)              | none                                                                                                 |

**Base UI's known exceptions.** While the list is open, Base UI 1.9.0 adds two `<span role="button" aria-label="Dismiss">` controls, from `ComboboxInput` and `ComboboxPopup`, that a screen reader can activate to close the list, named in hard-coded English that no owned string or `*Label` prop reaches; and its modal focus manager sets `aria-hidden` on everything outside the input, the popup and those controls, the label and the clear button included, until the list closes. SearchField keeps Base UI's behaviour and neither hides nor relabels them: the input stays named by the label through `aria-labelledby`, which reads hidden text; Esc and the arrow keys stay the field's keys; and both controls sit outside the popup, so the open list's owned-strings check never sees them. The `Open` story asserts them, and a Direction finding asks Base UI for a label prop.

What axe won't catch, from the contract, each with how this component meets it:

- [ ] Everything the eye is told, the ear is told, for every shape each prop accepts: the search icon is `aria-hidden` beside a field the label names; the clear button's `aria-hidden` cross has the owned "Clear" as its text; a hidden label is still the input's and the list's name; "No matches" is announced as it appears; a row reads its label, its description and its start icon's own text, as a [StationIcon](station-icon.md) or a [LineBadge](line-badge.md) gives one. Base UI's known exceptions, which the `Open` story asserts: while the list is open, its modal focus manager hides the label and the clear button from the ear, the input keeping its name, and its two `Dismiss` controls are heard in its own English.
- [ ] Every landmark and named region has an accessible name: none here; SearchField is not a landmark, and a caller puts it in a `<search>` element when it is the screen's search (see Do and don't).
- [ ] Every default label can be overridden: `clearLabel` and `noMatchesLabel`. Base UI's two `Dismiss` controls are its known exception: no prop reaches their hard-coded English.
- [ ] Every shape the type accepts renders, in every variant: `label`, an item's `description` and its `startIcon` render a string, an element and a list alike; a long Danish compound wraps in the label, the rows and the empty message (CR-11).
- [ ] A hidden copy kept for animation is `aria-hidden`, and a collapsed region is `inert`: none here; the closed list renders nothing, and the clear button is unmounted while the box is empty.
- [ ] Native semantics first: a native `<label>` and `<input>`, a native `<button>` for the clear button, and Base UI's `combobox`, `listbox`, `option` and `status` roles; Perron adds only the listbox's `aria-labelledby`. Base UI's `Dismiss` controls are `<span role="button">`s, its known exception.
- [ ] Focus moves in reading order and returns on close: the label, then the input, are the field's one tab stop; the highlight in the list is virtual, so focus never leaves the input, and closing the list, choosing a row or pressing the clear button leaves it there.
- [ ] Every target is at least `size.target-min` square: the clear button, `size.control` (34 px) square; a row, at least `size.target-min` tall and as wide as the list; the input, `size.input` tall. Base UI's `Dismiss` controls are screen-reader-only, with no box to press, and take no tab stop.
- [ ] Loops stop when the system asks for less motion: none here; SearchField has no loop and no transition (CR-12).

## Owned strings

| Key         | English      | Override         | Seen or heard where                                                                                           |
| ----------- | ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `clear`     | "Clear"      | `clearLabel`     | `clear`, heard as the clear button's name from the `CloseButton`'s `VisuallyHidden` span; never seen          |
| `noMatches` | "No matches" | `noMatchesLabel` | `empty`, seen in the list when no suggestion matches the words, and announced politely by its `status` region |

`clear` is the key `packages/perron/src/locale/en.ts` already has, "A button that clears a field or a filter". `noMatches` is new.

The new key is `noMatches`, "No matches", described in `en.ts` as "A search field's list: shown and announced when no suggestion matches the words typed", with the Danish, Swedish and Norwegian written by the build. It says what happened in plain words and no more than the data knows, in sentence case, as [Content design](../content-design.md) asks; it doesn't address the person, since a hint such as "Try a line number such as 5C." is the caller's, in the placeholder; and it stays apart from `noData`, "No data to show", which a data view says when its data came back empty.

Every other word is the caller's, through `label`, `placeholder` and `items`, but Base UI's `Dismiss`, the name of its two screen-reader-only controls while the list is open: its hard-coded English, a known exception (see Keyboard and ARIA).

## Component rules

Rules for this component alone, numbered so the build and the review can cite them.

- **CR-1.** Base UI's Autocomplete already gives the filtering, the opening and closing with their reasons, the virtual highlight and the arrow keys, Enter and Esc, filling the box with a chosen label, the clear button's visibility and its focus keeping, the placement and its flipping, the combobox, listbox and option roles and the live empty message, so the component rebuilds none of it and adds no key or pointer handlers.
- **CR-2.** SearchField renders `Field.Root`, holding `Field.Label` and then `Autocomplete.Root`; `Autocomplete.Root` holds `Autocomplete.InputGroup` (the search icon, `Autocomplete.Input`, then `Autocomplete.Clear`) and `Autocomplete.Portal`, which holds `Autocomplete.Positioner`, `Autocomplete.Popup`, and in the popup `Autocomplete.Empty` and then `Autocomplete.List`. The list's child is a function of each matching item that renders an `Autocomplete.Item` with `value` the item and `key` its `value`, holding the start icon span (only when the item gives `startIcon`), then the text span with the label span and the description span (only when the item gives `description`). `SearchField.tsx` exports `SearchFieldItem` beside `SearchField` and `SearchFieldProps`, so the package's barrel gives it to callers.
- **CR-3.** `{...rest}` reaches `Field.Root` before SearchField's own attributes, and SearchField's own props are taken out of `rest` first (`label`, `hiddenLabel`, `placeholder`, `items`, `filter`, `value`, `defaultValue`, `onChange`, `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpen`, `onClose`, `onItemSelect`, `clearLabel`, `noMatchesLabel`, `slotProps`), so none reaches the `<div>`; `name`, `disabled` and `render` stay in `rest` for `Field.Root`. `ref`, `style` and `data-testid` land on the root, and `className` is merged after `pn-SearchField`.
- **CR-4.** SearchField turns `onValueChange(value, details)` into `onChange(details.event, value, details)`, and `onOpenChange(open, details)` into `onOpen(details.event, details)` when `open` is `true` and `onClose(details.event, details.reason, details)` when it is `false`, and exposes neither. It passes `filter` to `Autocomplete.Root` as given, keeping a left-out `filter` (Base UI's collator in the runtime's locale) apart from `null` (no filtering), and passes `items` as given.
- **CR-5.** Each `slotProps` value is merged with Base UI's `mergeProps` (`@base-ui/react/merge-props`), SearchField's own props last, so a caller's handler runs beside SearchField's and its `className` joins after the part's class. Each part's class is set after the merge, with the shared `withClass` helper from `packages/perron/src/internal/nodes.ts`, as Dialog, Sheet and MapTooltip do, because `mergeProps` joins only class strings and puts the rightmost first: `pn-SearchField-<part>` first, then the caller's `className`, a string or a function of the part's state. On an item, `onItemSelect(event, item)` runs first, then the caller's `slotProps.item.onClick`, which can't cancel it.
- **CR-6.** The label gets an `id` from React's `useId`, given to `Field.Label` as its own prop so Base UI registers it as the field's label; the input reads it through Base UI's `aria-labelledby`, and SearchField sets the same id as `aria-labelledby` on `Autocomplete.List`, which Base UI leaves unnamed. With `hiddenLabel`, `Field.Label` renders through `render={<VisuallyHidden />}` with `nativeLabel={false}`, keeping the id and the label's text for the ear.
- **CR-7.** The search icon is an inline `<svg>` drawn from `packages/perron/icons/search.svg`, with the classes `perron-icon` and `pn-SearchField-icon`, `aria-hidden="true"` and `focusable="false"`, in `currentColor`. The clear button is `<Autocomplete.Clear render={<CloseButton label={strings.clear} />} />`, with `const strings = useOwnedStrings({ clear: clearLabel, noMatches: noMatchesLabel })`; it is not rendered while the field is `disabled`, `slotProps.clear` takes every prop but `disabled` (typed `Omit<Autocomplete.Clear.Props, 'disabled'>`, as Dialog's `slotProps.close` is), so the button is never disabled, and SearchField's CSS sets only its place in the row (`flex: none`), never its size or colours. The build adds `Autocomplete.Clear` to `CloseButton`'s "Composed in" cell in the contract's Shared parts table.
- **CR-8.** The input keeps the text type Base UI gives it by setting no `type`, never `type="search"`, whose browser cancel button would sit beside the clear button, and SearchField gives it `enterKeyHint="search"`, so a phone's keyboard labels its Enter key as a search; `slotProps.input` replaces it.
- **CR-9.** The input group is a flex row, `align-items: center`, the input growing (`flex: 1`, `min-inline-size: 0`) and the icon and the clear button keeping their size (`flex: none`). The input draws no outline of its own (`outline: none`): the ring is the input group's, on `:has(.pn-SearchField-input:focus-visible)`, with `focus.width`, `focus.offset` and `color.border.focus`, as the contract asks of a component that draws its own ring. The group's hover lays `color.surface.hover` over its fill as a `linear-gradient` background-image, inside `@media (hover: hover)` and not while `[data-disabled]`; an open field keeps its rest look.
- **CR-10.** The positioner takes `z-index.dialog` and `padding-block: space.100`, the gap on whichever side the list sits; SearchField passes no `sideOffset` and keeps Base UI's positioning defaults, which `slotProps.positioner` replaces. The popup is `box-sizing: border-box`, `inline-size: var(--anchor-width)`, at most `calc(var(--available-height) - 2 * var(--perron-space-100))` tall, and scrolls (`overflow-y: auto`, `overscroll-behavior: contain`). It draws its `border.width.025` edge as a border, so Windows' forced colours keep an edge round it when they drop its glass and shadow.
- **CR-11.** Long words: the label, a row's label and description, and the empty message wrap (`overflow-wrap: anywhere`), since each box takes its container's width; the input keeps its words on one line (`white-space: nowrap`) and scrolls them, as a native input does.
- **CR-12.** The list opens and closes at once: no `duration.*` token fits a list under a field, so the CSS has no transition or animation and styles neither `data-starting-style` nor `data-ending-style`.
- **CR-13.** In forced colours a highlighted row draws `Highlight` with `HighlightText`, its description too, inside `@media (forced-colors: active)` and with `forced-color-adjust: none`, since forced colours drop `color.surface.hover` and the highlight would vanish, and the browser's Canvas backing behind each line of text would hide the label's `HighlightText`.
- **CR-14.** The empty message is always rendered inside the popup, as Base UI asks for its live region, with the owned `noMatches` string as its child, a key the build adds to `en.ts`, with its description, and to `da.ts`, `sv.ts` and `nb.ts`; Base UI shows that child only while no item matches. Its padding is drawn on `:not(:empty)` only, and it is never hidden with `display: none`, `hidden` or `aria-hidden`.
- **CR-15.** The portal renders nothing on the server, so the contract story's owned-strings check sees only the label, the input and its placeholder. The stories that open the list check its words in the live DOM: `expectOwnedStrings(popup.outerHTML, locale, callerWords)`, in English and in Danish with no override.
- **CR-16.** The stories' meta sets `parameters: { docs: { story: { inline: false, height: '360px' } } }`, as the contract's [Stories](README.md#stories) asks of an overlay, and each story that shows the list opens it at first render with `defaultOpen` and words in `defaultValue`, beside the field that opens it again.

The input gets `enterKeyHint="search"` from SearchField, as CR-8 says: Mylder is used on phones, the hint costs nothing on a desktop, and `slotProps.input` lets a caller change it.

The list opens and closes at once, with no transition, as CR-12 says: the motion tokens hold the sheet's, the meter's and the map's durations and none for a popup, and Dialog and MapTooltip open at once for the same reason; a new duration goes through the `design-tokens` skill when a design asks for one.

## Stories

The deferred drawing has no variant property and a `State` property with the values `default`, `hover`, `focus`, `open` and `disabled`, so its variants, and the stories that carry their names, are `Default`, `Hover`, `Focus`, `Open` and `Disabled`. These are the CSS states the field's parts produce that change its look; whether the box holds words is the value, not a state, so `Filled` is a story beside them, as are the stories of content and behaviour; the Penpot conventions name a variant by its property values, and a `State` of `default` gives `Default`, the subject story.

The stories render the field on its own in a 320 px wide container, in a `PerronProvider` in English unless the story says otherwise, with `fn()` handlers for `onChange`, `onOpen`, `onClose` and `onItemSelect`, and these items: "Nørreport St." ("Metro, S-tog and bus"), "Nørrebro St." ("S-tog and bus"), "Nørrebros Runddel" ("Bus"), "Nordhavn St." ("S-tog") and "5C" ("Bus, Husum Torv to Lufthavnen"). The `Default` story's args, which the contract story renders, hold every word the caller gives: the label "Search lines and stops", the placeholder "Line or stop, such as 5C" and the items ([Content design](../content-design.md)). The `Hover` and `Focus` stories render at rest; their `play` tests drive the state. Each `play` that opens the list finds it through `screen`, outside `canvasElement`, and ends with it closed and focus where it started.

| Story          | Shows                                                                                                                                                                  | `play` test                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| -------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Default`      | The subject story: State default, the empty field with its visible label, icon and placeholder, the list closed; its args pass every rule alone                        | The input has the role `combobox`, is named "Search lines and stops" and has `aria-expanded="false"`; no clear button is rendered; Tab focuses the input, Shift+Tab moves focus back out                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `Hover`        | State hover: the empty field, at rest at first render                                                                                                                  | Hovering the box lays `color.surface.hover` over its fill as a background image                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `Focus`        | State focus: the empty field, at rest at first render                                                                                                                  | Tab gives the input `:focus-visible`; the input group draws an outline `focus.width` wide in `color.border.focus` and the input none                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `Open`         | State open: the words "Nørre" in `defaultValue` and the list open by `defaultOpen`, showing the three items that contain them                                          | The list has the role `listbox`, is named by the label, and holds three options; ArrowDown highlights "Nørreport St." through `aria-activedescendant` with focus still on the input; ArrowDown again highlights "Nørrebro St."; Enter calls `onItemSelect` once with that item, fills the box with "Nørrebro St." (`onChange`, `'item-press'`) and closes the list (`onClose`, `'item-press'`); the open list's words pass `expectOwnedStrings` in `en`; while it is open, Base UI's known exceptions hold: two `Dismiss` controls, and `aria-hidden` on the label and the clear button with the input still named; once it closes, both controls are gone and the label is heard again |
| `Disabled`     | State disabled: the field with `disabled` and the words "5C", in `color.text.tertiary`                                                                                 | The input is `disabled`, Tab passes it by, no clear button is rendered, and typing changes nothing and calls no handler                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `Filled`       | The field holding the words "5C", with the clear button                                                                                                                | The clear button is named "Clear" and is not a tab stop; pressing it empties the box (`onChange`, `''`, `'clear-press'`), unmounts the button and leaves focus on the input; typing "5C" again and pressing Esc with the list closed empties it again (`'escape-key'`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `NoMatches`    | The words "Xyz" and the list open, with no item matching, showing "No matches"                                                                                         | The popup's `status` region holds "No matches" and the list no option; rendered in `da` with no override, it shows the Danish dictionary's word, and `expectOwnedStrings` passes in `en` and `da`; with `noMatchesLabel` "No lines or stops match", it shows that; Esc closes the list (`'escape-key'`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `HiddenLabel`  | The field with `hiddenLabel`, as in the top bar: the icon and the placeholder, no label in view                                                                        | No label is visible, and the input and, once open, the list are still named "Search lines and stops"                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `WithMarks`    | The list open on "5", with rows that give a `startIcon` (a [LineBadge](line-badge.md) for "5C" and a [StationIcon](station-icon.md) for a stop) and a description each | Each option's name holds its label, its description and its mark's text; the start icon sits before the text on the inline axis; Esc closes the list                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `CallerFilter` | The list open with `filter={null}` and the words "zz", showing every item as given                                                                                     | All five options render though none contains "zz"; Esc closes the list                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `Controlled`   | `value` and `open` held in the story's state, with the list closed at first                                                                                            | Typing "N" calls `onChange` with `'input-change'` and `onOpen` with `'input-change'`, and the story sets both; ArrowDown moves the highlight; Esc calls `onClose` with `'escape-key'` and the story clears `open`; a press outside calls `onClose` with `'outside-press'`; ends with the list closed and the input blurred, focus where it started                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `LongWords`    | The label and an item's label and description each hold a long Danish compound, the list open, in the 320 px container                                                 | The label, the row's label and its description wrap onto more than one line and stay inside the popup; the popup is no wider than the box; nothing overflows; Esc closes the list                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |

## Do and don't

For a caller using the component, with the reason.

| Do                                                                                                                                   | Don't                                                                                                                                        |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Give a `label` that names what is searched, "Search lines and stops", and hide it with `hiddenLabel` only where the icon says enough | Leave the placeholder as the field's only words: it vanishes as the person types, and it is not a name                                       |
| Put a hint in the placeholder as an instruction with an example, "Line or stop, such as 5C"                                          | Put anything the person must remember in the placeholder: it is gone once they type, and drawn in `color.text.tertiary`, below text contrast |
| Act on `onItemSelect`, which gives the item, to move the map to the stop or show the line                                            | Find the chosen item from `onChange`'s words with `'item-press'`: two stops can share a name                                                 |
| Pass `filter={null}` when the suggestions come already matched, such as from a server                                                | Leave Base UI's filter on server results: it hides a match whose label doesn't contain the words, such as a stop found by its old name       |
| Give a short `label` and a `description` that tells two rows apart, "Bus, Husum Torv to Lufthavnen"                                  | Put a link, a button or a field in a row: an option is chosen as a whole, and the keys never reach a control inside it                       |
| Use a [StationIcon](station-icon.md) or a [LineBadge](line-badge.md) as an item's `startIcon`, which carries its own text            | Use colour alone to tell a line from a stop: the mark needs its words, and the row its description                                           |
| Put the field in a `<search>` element, or a `<form role="search">`, when it is the screen's search                                   | Expect SearchField to be a landmark: it is one field, and a screen may hold more than one                                                    |
| Set the width on the container, or through `className` on the root                                                                   | Give the input or the box a width through `slotProps`: the list takes the box's width, and the label the root's                              |
| Keep the field in a `PerronProvider` with the screen's locale, so "Clear" and "No matches" speak it                                  | Translate them with `clearLabel` and `noMatchesLabel` on every instance: those are for one instance's own words                              |

title: SegmentedControl
markdown:
# SegmentedControl

A row of two to five segments on an inset track, one of them selected, that picks how one view shows its content, such as a stop's departures by mode.

<!-- run notes -->

The design is deferred (ADR 0010, `docs/adr/0010-unattended-runs-with-design-deferred.md`): there is no read-back, code map or export, and this spec decides what the drawing would, from the contract, the foundations, the tokens, the Base UI reference and the ROADMAP line that names it (`ROADMAP.md`, "Wave 3, interactive, on Base UI": "SegmentedControl (ToggleGroup)"). The extracted prototype component is not in any branch this run can reach. The foundations already name its look: [Elevation](../foundations/elevation.md#surfaces) puts the track on `color.surface.inset` and the selected segment on `color.surface.raised` with `shadow.thumb`, the only shadow outside a floating panel; [Layout](../foundations/layout.md) gives a segment `size.segment`; and [Semantic spacing](../foundations/semantic-spacing.md) gives segments `radius.md`.

## Anatomy

Penpot page `Components/SegmentedControl`. Family: none (the contract's [Families](README.md#families) have no inset track of choices; its surfaces come from [Elevation](../foundations/elevation.md#surfaces)). Shared parts: none (every word is the caller's, and the selected segment is told by `aria-pressed`, not by a hidden word).

The control is written as two components, `SegmentedControl` for the track and `Segment` for each choice, both exported with their props types from `SegmentedControl.tsx`, an exception to the contract's "one component per folder", as Tabs and Toolbar are. Base UI's `Toggle` reads `ToggleGroup`'s context for its pressed state, so a segment can't be shown apart from its control; the caller writes a segment many times, so it is a component of its own; a child component takes a `ReactNode` label where an `options` array would need a shape of its own; and the registry's one entry, with `baseUiParts` `ToggleGroup` and `Toggle`, stays one entry. The `props` check reads both props types, and the `api-compatibility` check only `SegmentedControlProps`, so the review holds `SegmentProps` to the contract's Change rules.

| Part (Penpot layer) | What it is                                                                                                                       | Base UI part  | Class                 | `slotProps` key |
| ------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------- | --------------------- | --------------- |
| `root`              | `SegmentedControl`: the track, an inline flex row on `color.surface.inset` that holds the caller's `Segment`s and owns the value | `ToggleGroup` | `pn-SegmentedControl` | none            |
| `segment`           | `Segment`: the native `<button>` of one choice, an inline flex row, centred, that holds its label                                | `Toggle`      | `pn-Segment`          | none            |
| `label`             | The `<span>` that holds the caller's `children`, the segment's one flex item, its text centred                                   | none          | `pn-Segment-label`    | none            |
| `focusRing`         | The keyboard focus ring on a segment: the `:focus-visible` outline `perron.css` draws, not an element                            | `Toggle`      | none                  | none            |

`Segment` wraps its `children` in its label, as Tab does with `pn-Tab-label`: held directly, a label given as text and an element would be two flex items, set side by side as two columns and broken mid-word in a narrow track, where in one span they flow and wrap as one run of text, centred (CR-9). The label holds the typography and its long-word rule.

## Base UI parts

Imported from `@base-ui/react/toggle-group` and `@base-ui/react/toggle`, at the version pinned in `package.json` (1.9.0 installed).

| Base UI part  | Renders                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | Perron sets                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | Passed through                                                                                                         |
| ------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ToggleGroup` | `<div role="group">`, with `data-orientation` (always `horizontal` here) and `data-disabled` while disabled; inside a Base UI `Toolbar.Root` it renders a plain `<div>` that joins the toolbar's roving focus instead of keeping its own                         | `className` (`pn-SegmentedControl`, then the caller's), `ref`, `value` and `defaultValue` as one-item arrays, `onValueChange` adapted from `onChange` (CR-4), `disabled`; `multiple` and `orientation` left at Base UI's `false` and `'horizontal'` | `loopFocus`, `render`, `style`, `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby` and every other prop of a `<div>`, through `{...rest}` |
| `Toggle`      | `<button type="button">`, with `aria-pressed`, `data-pressed` while pressed (here: selected), `data-disabled` and the native `disabled` attribute while it or its group is disabled, and a roving `tabIndex` of 0 on the group's one tab stop and −1 on the rest | `className` (`pn-Segment`, then the caller's), `ref`, `value`, `disabled`, and `children`, the caller's wrapped in the label                                                                                                                        | `nativeButton`, `render`, `style`, `onClick` and every other prop of a native `<button>`, through `{...rest}`          |

Base UI already does: one tab stop for the whole group, a roving `tabIndex` that rests on the first enabled segment until another one is focused and then stays where focus last was (not on the selected segment: `ToggleGroup` keeps no link between the two and exposes no `highlightedIndex`); Left and Right move focus between segments, wrapping at the ends while `loopFocus` is on, and Home and End go to the first and the last enabled segment (`enableHomeAndEndKeys` is fixed on in the installed `ToggleGroup`); moving focus doesn't select, and Enter, Space or a click toggles the focused segment; with `multiple` off, pressing one segment unpresses the others; a disabled segment is natively `disabled` (`focusableWhenDisabled` is fixed off in the installed `Toggle`), so it leaves the tab and arrow-key order and ignores clicks; a disabled group disables every segment in it; `aria-pressed` follows the group's value; `onValueChange` passes `details` whose `cancel()` stops both the group's and the toggle's change (the installed `Toggle` checks `details.isCanceled` after the group's handler); Left and Right swap only under Base UI's `DirectionProvider` set to `rtl`, not from the `dir` attribute, and Perron doesn't set one up yet, as all four locales run left to right.

## Props

In MUI's layout. Every prop here gets this description as its JSDoc. Slots come last.

The control holds one choice, its value a `string` rather than Base UI's `string[]`, with Base UI's `multiple` and `orientation` left out, so it only runs horizontally. A segmented control picks one of a few ways to show one view, and FilterChip (on Base UI's `Toggle`, in the same wave) is the on-and-off filter that takes several; a `string` narrows in the caller's `onChange` where a one-item array has to be unpacked; Mylder's controls sit across a panel or a sheet, where a vertical stack of segments would read as a list; and the API only grows, so a later `orientation` costs nothing now.

With neither `value` nor `defaultValue` given, no segment is selected, with no fallback to the first one. Base UI's `ToggleGroup` has no fallback, unlike Tabs, and building one would mean reading the segments' values out of `children`; every story and the Do and don't table give `defaultValue` or `value`, so a control with nothing selected is the caller's choice, such as before a person has picked a mode.

The control takes no `name` and renders no hidden input, so its value never reaches a native `<form>`. Base UI's `ToggleGroup` renders no input to submit, unlike the composite controls the contract's Forms line names; Mylder's segmented controls change how a view shows its content, not what a form sends; and a later `name` with a hidden input only grows the API.

The control takes no `fullWidth`, so it is as wide as its segments' labels, up to its container's width. Tabs takes none for the same reason: a control sized to its labels keeps each segment's target as wide as its word, the API can grow one, and leaving it out keeps the CSS to one layout. A control in a narrow container still fits it (CR-9).

Each segment is a `ReactNode` label and no icon prop: Mylder's segments are words such as "Bus" and "Metro", and an icon-only segment would need a name of its own, so `startIcon` waits until a screen needs it. No `variant`, `size` or `color`: the tokens give one look, an inset track and a raised selected segment at `size.segment`, as the brand keeps colour for the map and the one main action. No `slotProps`: each component renders one Base UI part as its own root. No label-override props: the control owns no strings.

`Segment` leaves out Base UI's `pressed`, `defaultPressed` and `onPressedChange`: inside a group the installed `Toggle` reads its pressed state from the group's value and ignores `pressed`, so the root's `value`, `defaultValue` and `onChange` are the one way in.

### SegmentedControl

| Name                        | Type                                                                             | Default | Base UI prop    | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------- | --------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `value`                     | `string`                                                                         | none    | `value`         | The selected segment's `value`, when the caller controls it. A value no segment has selects none.                                                                                                                |
| `defaultValue`              | `string`                                                                         | none    | `defaultValue`  | The segment selected at first, when the control keeps the value itself. Left out, with no `value`, no segment is selected until one is chosen.                                                                   |
| `onChange`                  | `(event: Event, value: string, details: ToggleGroup.ChangeEventDetails) => void` | none    | `onValueChange` | Called when another segment is selected, by a click, Enter or Space (`details.reason` `'none'`), with that segment's `value`. Not called when the selected segment is pressed again. `event` is `details.event`. |
| `disabled`                  | `boolean`                                                                        | `false` | `disabled`      | Whether every segment ignores the pointer and the keys. The selected segment still shows, and the control leaves the tab order.                                                                                  |
| `loopFocus`                 | `boolean`                                                                        | `true`  | inherited       | Inherited from Base UI with its JSDoc: whether to loop keyboard focus back to the first segment when the end is reached with the arrow keys.                                                                     |
| `render`                    | Base UI's `render`                                                               | none    | inherited       | Inherited from Base UI: swaps the root element and keeps the behaviour, the class and the data attributes.                                                                                                       |
| `children`                  | `ReactNode`                                                                      | none    | none            | The control's `Segment`s, in reading order.                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `className`, `style`, `ref` | React's                                                                          | none    | none            | Reaches the root. `className` is merged after `pn-SegmentedControl`.                                                                                                                                             |

### Segment

| Name                        | Type               | Default | Base UI prop | Description                                                                                                              |
| --------------------------- | ------------------ | ------- | ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `value`                     | `string`           | none    | `value`      | Required. The value that selects this segment, unique within its control.                                                |
| `disabled`                  | `boolean`          | `false` | `disabled`   | Whether the segment ignores the pointer and the keys. It leaves the tab and arrow-key order, and is announced as dimmed. |
| `nativeButton`              | `boolean`          | `true`  | inherited    | Inherited from Base UI with its JSDoc: set it to `false` when `render` gives an element that isn't a `<button>`.         |
| `render`                    | Base UI's `render` | none    | inherited    | Inherited from Base UI: swaps the segment's element and keeps the behaviour, the class and the data attributes.          |
| `children`                  | `ReactNode`        | none    | none         | The label: a word or two that names the choice, in sentence case, such as "Metro".                                       |
| `className`, `style`, `ref` | React's            | none    | none         | Reach the segment's `<button>`. `className` is merged after `pn-Segment`.                                                |

## Tokens

One row per part, state and property. States are the contract's design states: rest is no selector, hover is `:hover` inside `@media (hover: hover)`, pressed is `:active`, focus is `:focus-visible`, disabled is `[data-disabled]`, and selected is Base UI's `[data-pressed]` on the segment. The contract's Design states table lists `[data-pressed]` under Pressed, but Base UI's `Toggle` sets it for as long as the toggle is on, which in a segmented control is the selected segment, so here the press itself is `:active` alone. Every `color` row on `segment` sets the segment's `color`, which its label takes.

The track is `radius.lg` with `space.100` padding and a `space.100` gap between segments, each segment `radius.md` with `space.300` inline padding. A segment's `radius.md` plus the track's `space.100` padding is `radius.lg` (8 + 4 = 12 px), so the corners nest, each token used as its description says ("Cards and inset boxes", "segments"); the padding is `focus.offset` plus `focus.width`, so a focused segment's ring reaches the track's edge and no further; the track is 40 px tall, `size.segment` plus the padding; a segment's `space.050` block padding keeps a wrapped label's lines off the raised fill's top and bottom edges, and leaves a one-line segment `size.segment` tall; and `space.300` is a tab's inline padding, the label sizing the target as it does there. The other way, a `space.050` padding with `radius.sm` segments, would make the track `size.button` tall but give segments the line badges' radius.

A selected segment that is disabled, alone or with its whole control, keeps its `color.surface.raised` fill and `shadow.thumb`, with only its label turning `color.text.tertiary`. The contract makes disabled a colour, never an opacity, and the choice a disabled control holds is still worth seeing, such as a mode that can't change while the map follows a vehicle; dropping the fill would leave a disabled control showing no choice at all.

| Part                    | State              | Property                    | Token                                                                         |
| ----------------------- | ------------------ | --------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `root`                  | rest               | `background-color`          | `color.surface.inset`                                                         |
| `root`                  | rest               | `border-radius`             | `radius.lg`                                                                   |
| `root`                  | rest               | `padding`                   | `space.100`                                                                   |
| `root`                  | rest               | `gap`                       | `space.100`                                                                   |
| `root`                  | disabled           | `background-color`          | `color.surface.inset`, unchanged: the segments show the state                 |
| `segment`               | rest               | `min-block-size`            | `size.segment`                                                                |
| `segment`               | rest               | `padding-block`             | `space.050`                                                                   |
| `segment`               | rest               | `padding-inline`            | `space.300`                                                                   |
| `segment`               | rest               | `border-radius`             | `radius.md`                                                                   |
| `label`                 | rest               | `font`, `letter-spacing`    | `typography.label`, with its tracking twin                                    |
| `segment`               | rest               | `background-color`          | `transparent`                                                                 |
| `segment`               | rest               | `color`                     | `color.text.secondary`                                                        |
| `segment`               | rest               | `cursor`                    | none: the keyword `pointer`                                                   |
| `segment`               | hover              | `background-color`          | `color.surface.hover`                                                         |
| `segment`               | hover              | `color`                     | `color.text.primary`                                                          |
| `segment`               | pressed            | `background-color`          | `color.surface.selected`                                                      |
| `segment`               | pressed            | `color`                     | `color.text.primary`                                                          |
| `segment`               | selected           | `background-color`          | `color.surface.raised`                                                        |
| `segment`               | selected           | `box-shadow`                | `shadow.thumb`                                                                |
| `segment`               | selected           | `color`                     | `color.text.primary`                                                          |
| `segment`               | disabled           | `color`                     | `color.text.tertiary`                                                         |
| `segment`               | disabled           | `cursor`                    | none: the keyword `default`                                                   |
| `segment`               | selected, disabled | `background-color`          | `color.surface.raised`                                                        |
| `segment`               | selected, disabled | `box-shadow`                | `shadow.thumb`                                                                |
| `segment`               | selected, disabled | `color`                     | `color.text.tertiary`                                                         |
| `segment` (`focusRing`) | focus              | `outline`, `outline-offset` | `focus.width` in `color.border.focus`, `focus.offset` (drawn by `perron.css`) |

A selected segment shows no hover or pressed layer: pressing it again changes nothing (CR-4), so it doesn't look as if it would. Highlighted, open and invalid don't apply: a segment takes focus rather than `data-highlighted`, and the control opens nothing and holds no form value.

## Keyboard and ARIA

From the Base UI reference for `ToggleGroup` and `Toggle` and the installed `ToggleGroup`, `Toggle` and the composite root and item they build on. "From" says who does it.

| Key              | Does                                                                                                                                                                                                         | From                                                   |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `Tab`            | Moves focus into the control, to its one tab stop: the first enabled segment, or the segment focused last; the next `Tab` leaves the control                                                                 | Base UI                                                |
| `Shift+Tab`      | Moves focus out of the control, backwards                                                                                                                                                                    | Base UI                                                |
| `ArrowRight`     | Moves focus to the next enabled segment, wrapping from the last to the first while `loopFocus` is on, without selecting it; the previous one under an `rtl` `DirectionProvider`, which Perron doesn't set up | Base UI                                                |
| `ArrowLeft`      | Moves focus to the previous enabled segment, wrapping from the first to the last while `loopFocus` is on, without selecting it; the next one under an `rtl` `DirectionProvider`                              | Base UI                                                |
| `Home`, `End`    | Move focus to the first and the last enabled segment                                                                                                                                                         | Base UI                                                |
| `Enter`, `Space` | Select the focused segment and call `onChange`; nothing on the selected segment, whose change Perron cancels (CR-4)                                                                                          | The browser's click; Base UI for a non-button `render` |

`ArrowUp` and `ArrowDown` do nothing: the control runs horizontally, and the component adds no keys of its own.

| Element   | Role                                                                   | Accessible name from                           | States announced                                  |
| --------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `root`    | `group`, from Base UI                                                  | The caller's `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` | none                                              |
| `segment` | `button`, a native `<button>`, announced as a toggle by `aria-pressed` | Its text content: the caller's `children`      | `aria-pressed`; disabled by the native `disabled` |

What axe won't catch, from the contract, each with how this component meets it:

- [ ] Everything the eye is told, the ear is told, for every shape each prop accepts: the selected segment, which the raised fill and the shadow show, is `aria-pressed="true"` and every other segment `"false"`; a disabled segment's tertiary colour is the native `disabled`, announced as dimmed; a disabled control shows it on each of its segments, which Base UI disables.
- [ ] Every landmark and named region has an accessible name: the control is a `group`, not a landmark, named by the caller's `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`, which every story sets, so a screen reader says what the choice is about before its segments.
- [ ] Every default label can be overridden: none here; the control owns no strings.
- [ ] Every shape the type accepts renders, in every variant: a segment's `children` render a string, an element and a list alike, as one label whose text and elements flow and wrap as one run of text, as the `LabelShapes` story shows.
- [ ] A hidden copy kept for animation is `aria-hidden`, and a collapsed region is `inert`: none here; the control keeps no copy and collapses nothing.
- [ ] Native semantics first: native `<button>`s from `Toggle`, with `aria-pressed`, in Base UI's `group`, with ARIA from the caller only for the group's name.
- [ ] Focus moves in reading order and returns on close: the arrow keys move through the segments in document order, and Tab leaves the control after its one stop; the control opens and closes nothing, and focus stays on the segment it selects.
- [ ] Every target is at least `size.target-min` square: the smallest target is a segment with a one-letter label, `size.segment` (32 px) tall and its label plus `space.300` on each side (at least 24 px) wide.
- [ ] Loops stop when the system asks for less motion: none here; the control has no loop and no transition.

## Owned strings

No owned strings: every word comes from the caller, as a segment's `children` or the control's `aria-label`.

## Component rules

Rules for this component alone, numbered so the build and the review can cite them.

- **CR-1.** Base UI's toggle group already gives the one tab stop, the roving `tabIndex`, the arrow, Home and End keys, the wrap, the single selection, `aria-pressed` and the disabled segments leaving the key order, so the components rebuild none of it and add no key handlers.
- **CR-2.** `Segment` only renders inside a `SegmentedControl`: outside one, Base UI's `Toggle` is a lone toggle with a pressed state of its own, which no story shows. Every story renders segments in a control, and the `Default` story's args hold a whole control, its `aria-label`, its `defaultValue` and its segments, so the contract story renders it alone.
- **CR-3.** Each of the two takes `{...rest}` before its own attributes and its own props out of `rest` first (`value`, `defaultValue`, `onChange`, `disabled`, and `Segment`'s `children`, which it wraps in its label; an inherited Base UI prop such as `loopFocus` or `nativeButton` stays in `rest`, keeping Base UI's default), and merges `className` after its own `pn-` class; `ref` reaches its one element.
- **CR-4.** `SegmentedControl` adapts between its `string` and Base UI's `string[]` inside itself and exposes neither `onValueChange`, `multiple` nor `orientation`. It passes `value` as `[value]` and `defaultValue` as `[defaultValue]`, each only when given, so a control given neither is uncontrolled with nothing selected. Its `onValueChange(next, details)` calls `details.cancel()` and returns when `next` is empty, the one change Base UI makes when the selected segment is pressed again, so the selection stays and `onChange` isn't called; otherwise it calls `onChange(details.event, next[0], details)`.
- **CR-5.** The states keep the segment's geometry: hover, pressed, focus, selected and disabled change the fill, the shadow and the colour only, never the height, padding, radius, typography or weight, so selecting a segment never moves its neighbours.
- **CR-6.** Hover is read inside `@media (hover: hover)`; pressed (`:active`) takes the colour and a denser fill, `color.surface.selected`, a step past hover, in a rule after it and outside it, so a touch press shows. Neither applies to a selected or a disabled segment: both rules exclude `[data-pressed]` and `[data-disabled]`. Selected is `.pn-Segment[data-pressed]`, one class then attributes.
- **CR-7.** Focus uses the ring `perron.css` draws on `:focus-visible`; the component draws no ring of its own and never removes the outline. The ring sits inside the track's padding (CR-9's container clips nothing). Under forced colours the selected segment, which opts out of the forced adjustment (CR-10), sets only the ring's colour, `outline-color: CanvasText`: out of the adjustment the browser no longer forces the ring's `color.border.focus` to a system colour, and `CanvasText` is the colour it forces every other ring to.
- **CR-8.** Changes of state are immediate: no `duration.*` token fits a segment's state change or the selected fill's move, so the CSS has no transition, and the raised fill jumps to the selected segment.
- **CR-9.** The control is `display: inline-flex` with `max-inline-size: 100%`, so it is as wide as its segments and never wider than its container. When the labels outrun the container, the segments shrink and each label, one `pn-Segment-label` whatever shape the caller gives it, wraps inside its segment, centred, with `overflow-wrap: anywhere` on `.pn-Segment-label`, the segment growing taller than `size.segment`, rather than the labels being cut off or the control scrolling sideways. [Accessibility](../foundations/accessibility.md#what-a-person-checks) lets nothing be cut off at 320 px and only the map scroll sideways; a Danish compound is longer than its English word; and a segment that grows keeps every segment on one track, where segments wrapping onto a second row, as tabs do, would read as two controls.
- **CR-10.** In `@media (forced-colors: active)`, where the fill and the shadow are dropped, the selected segment takes `Highlight` with `HighlightText` and a disabled segment `GrayText`, so the selected and disabled states still show, as [Accessibility](../foundations/accessibility.md#what-a-person-checks) asks. The selected segment sets `forced-color-adjust: none`, since the `Canvas` backplate the browser draws behind forced text would hide `HighlightText` on the `Highlight` fill. A segment both selected and disabled takes a `GrayText` fill with `Canvas` text: `Highlight` would show it as a choice that can still change, and `GrayText` text on `Highlight` may not be legible, while a grey fill still shows which segment the disabled control holds, as the raised fill does outside forced colours ([Tokens](#tokens)).
- **CR-11.** The tab stop is Base UI's: the first enabled segment, then the one focused last, not the selected one. The component doesn't move it, since `ToggleGroup` exposes no `highlightedIndex`, and `aria-pressed` tells which segment is selected wherever focus lands.

## Stories

The deferred design's page draws two things: the control, `Default`, four segments ("All", "Bus", "S-tog" and "Metro") with "All" selected; and the segment, with one variant property, `State` (`default`, `hover`, `focus`, `selected`, `disabled`). Each story is named by its variant name (`penpot/README.md`, "Conventions"); the segment's are prefixed `Segment`, as `SegmentHover`, beside the control's `Default`, since the conventions name a variant by its property values alone.

Every story names its control with `aria-label` ("Mode"). The segment stories render a control of three segments, "All", "Bus" and "Metro", with "All" selected and the state on "Bus" (on "Bus" selected, for `SegmentSelected`); the hover and focus stories render at rest: the visual check drives the state, and their `play` tests check it. `Default` is the story the contract story renders, and its args pass every rule alone.

| Story             | Shows                                                                                                                                                                                                         | `play` test                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Default`         | The control: four segments, "All" selected; the subject the contract story renders                                                                                                                            | Tab focuses "All"; ArrowRight moves focus to "Bus" without selecting it; Enter selects it, sets its `aria-pressed` to `true` and "All"'s to `false`, and calls `onChange` once with `'bus'` and `details.reason` `'none'`; Enter again keeps "Bus" selected and doesn't call `onChange`; End and Home go to the last and first segment; ArrowLeft from the first wraps to the last; Shift+Tab leaves the control |
| `SegmentDefault`  | A segment at rest, not selected                                                                                                                                                                               | none                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `SegmentHover`    | A segment, hover                                                                                                                                                                                              | Hovering "Bus" sets its fill to `color.surface.hover` and its colour to `color.text.primary`; hovering the selected "All" leaves its fill `color.surface.raised`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `SegmentFocus`    | A segment, focus                                                                                                                                                                                              | Tab, then ArrowRight, gives "Bus" `:focus-visible` and the ring                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `SegmentSelected` | A segment, selected, raised with `shadow.thumb`                                                                                                                                                               | "Bus" has `aria-pressed="true"` and `data-pressed`, its fill is `color.surface.raised` and its shadow `shadow.thumb`; "All" and "Metro" have `aria-pressed="false"`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `SegmentDisabled` | A segment, disabled                                                                                                                                                                                           | "Bus" is natively `disabled` with `data-disabled`; ArrowRight from "All" goes to "Metro"; a click on "Bus" doesn't select it or call `onChange`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `Disabled`        | The whole control disabled, "All" selected and still raised, every label tertiary                                                                                                                             | Every segment is natively `disabled`; Tab passes the control by; "All" keeps `aria-pressed="true"` and its `color.surface.raised` fill                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `Controlled`      | A control given `value` and `onChange` from the story's state                                                                                                                                                 | A click on "Metro" calls `onChange` with `'metro'`; the selection moves only once the story sets `value`; setting `value` from outside moves the raised fill                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `LongLabels`      | Three segments with long labels ("Planned works", "Data feed problems", "Omkørsler") in a 320 px wide container                                                                                               | The control is no wider than its container, which doesn't scroll sideways (its `scrollWidth` equals its `clientWidth`); the longest label wraps onto more than one line inside its segment, which is taller than `size.segment`                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `LabelShapes`     | Three segments whose labels are a string ("Planned works"), an element ("Diversions" in a `<span>`) and a list, text then an element ("Data feed", then "problems" in a `<span>`), in a 320 px wide container | Each segment holds one element, its `pn-Segment-label`, no wider than the segment; the list's segment is taller than `size.segment`, and its element sits below the text before it in one line box, unbroken                                                                                                                                                                                                     |

## Do and don't

For a caller using the component, with the reason.

| Do                                                                                                                                                     | Don't                                                                                                                                                      |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Use a SegmentedControl to pick how one view shows its content, such as departures by mode or a chart by day or week                                    | Use it to switch between views of one thing: [Tabs](tabs.md) change which view shows, a segmented control changes how one view shows                       |
| Use it for one choice of two to five                                                                                                                   | Use it for filters that turn on and off apart, or for more than five choices: filter chips take several, and a long row of segments outgrows a phone       |
| Name the control with `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`, such as "Mode", so a screen reader says what the choice is about                              | Leave the control unnamed: its segments' words alone don't say what they choose between                                                                    |
| Give it a `defaultValue` or a `value`, so one segment is always selected                                                                               | Leave nothing selected without a reason: a control with no raised segment reads as broken                                                                  |
| Keep each label to a word or two, in sentence case: "Bus", "Planned works"                                                                             | Write a sentence in a segment, or rely on a label's colour or an icon alone to say what it chooses                                                         |
| Show a segment whose view is empty, and say so in the view with an [EmptyState](empty-state.md) or a [DataStatePanel](../patterns/data-state-panel.md) | Disable a segment because its view has no data: a disabled segment can't say why, and leaves the key order                                                 |
| Run an action with a [Button](button.md), and group actions in a [Toolbar](toolbar.md)                                                                 | Use a segment as an action or as navigation: pressing one selects it and keeps it selected, and a link to another screen is a [LinkButton](link-button.md) |

title: Select
