# Select

The field that picks one value from a short, fixed list: a labelled box showing the chosen option, or a placeholder, that opens a list of options under it, with the field's help and error round it.

<!-- run notes -->

The design is deferred (ADR 0010, `docs/adr/0010-unattended-runs-with-design-deferred.md`): there is no read-back, code map or export, and this spec decides what the drawing would, from the [contract](README.md), the [foundations](../foundations/README.md), the tokens, the Base UI reference for `Select` (`@base-ui/react` 1.9.0, installed) and the spec of [Field](field.md), which the registry entry's `dependsOn` names. The extracted prototype component is not in any branch this run can reach.

## Anatomy

Penpot page `Components/Select`. Family: Fields, for the trigger, the box the person presses; Popups, for the list's popup; Rows, for its options. Shared parts: `VisuallyHidden`, through Field, for a hidden label; `SelectedMark`, for the tick beside the chosen option.

Select composes the [Field](field.md) component for its label, its description, its error and its optional mark, and Base UI's `Select` for the rest: the fourteen parts the registry entry lists, from `Select.Root` to `Select.Separator`. It uses none of Select's others: not `Select.Label`, since Field's label already names the trigger through Base UI's field context; not `Select.Backdrop` or `Select.Arrow`; not `Select.ScrollUpArrow` or `Select.ScrollDownArrow`, since the list scrolls as any list does, by wheel, touch and the keys.

The options are data, `items`, that Select draws as rows, with no item component: each is a `SelectItem` of the shape `{ value: string; label: string; disabled?: boolean }`, and grouped options a `SelectGroup` of the shape `{ label: string; items: ReadonlyArray<SelectItem> }`, with no `startIcon` or `description` on an item for now. SearchField takes its suggestions as data for the same reason, so the two fields read alike; the contract's rule of a component per child applies to a child the caller writes many times, and an option is a value and its words; the trigger shows the chosen option's `label`, so a `label` is a plain string, which Base UI also matches the typed letters against; a start icon and a second line can join later as optional fields without a break.

Select draws a separator between two groups, and none in a flat list or before the first group. The group labels already divide the list for the ear, and a hairline divides it for the eye at the same place; the registry lists `Select.Separator` for this; a caller never places a separator, since the list is data.

Base UI already does: it opens the list on a press of the trigger (on `mousedown`, so a press, a drag and a release on an option chooses it in one gesture), on Enter or Space on the trigger (`'trigger-press'`), and on ArrowDown or ArrowUp (`'list-navigation'`), and closes it when an option is chosen (`'item-press'`), on Esc (`'escape-key'`), on a press outside the trigger and the list (`'outside-press'`), on a second press of the trigger (`'trigger-press'`), when focus leaves (`'focus-out'`) and when a press on the closed trigger is dragged off and released outside the trigger and the list (`'cancel-open'`); on open from the keys it highlights and focuses the chosen option, or, with nothing chosen, the first, or the last on ArrowUp, and, opened by a press or by `defaultOpen` with nothing chosen, focuses the popup and highlights no row until a key or the pointer reaches one; it moves the highlight and focus through the rows with the arrow keys, without wrapping, and to the first and last with Home and End; it highlights the row under the pointer; it moves the highlight to the next option whose label starts with the letters typed while the list is open, and chooses it at once, without opening the list, while the trigger is focused and closed; it chooses the highlighted option on Enter, Space or a press, sets it as the value, closes the list and returns focus to the trigger; it skips a disabled option when letters are typed, lets the keys reach it, and never chooses it; it keeps the value while `readOnly`, letting the list open and the person browse it; it shows the chosen option's label in the value, from `items`, and the placeholder while nothing is chosen; it names the trigger by Field's label through `aria-labelledby`, and names each group by its label; it locks the page's scroll and blocks presses outside while the list is open (`modal`, by default); it places the list against the trigger, below it, flipping above it when there is no room, and gives the positioner `--anchor-width` and `--available-height`; it puts the field's `name` and the chosen value on its hidden input, so a native form's `FormData` reads them, and marks it `required`; and, inside Field, it takes `disabled` and `name` from `Field.Root`, marks the trigger `aria-invalid` and `data-invalid` while the field is invalid, runs the field's checks on the value, and sets the field's state attributes on the trigger.

Select sets `alignItemWithTrigger={false}` on `Select.Positioner`, as its own prop that a caller's `slotProps.positioner` can't turn back on, so the list always opens under the trigger, as wide as it, as SearchField's does. Base UI's default lays the popup over the trigger with the chosen option on top of the value, for a mouse only, so the list would sit in two places by the input it was opened with; one place under the box is the Fields family's and SearchField's, and keeps the trigger in view; the Tokens table's width, gap and height are drawn for a list under the box, and Base UI ignores `sideOffset` and closes the list on a window resize while it aligns the item.

The list is named by the label, as SearchField's is: Select gives Field's label an `id` from React's `useId` through `slotProps.label`, which Base UI registers as the field's label, and sets the same id as `aria-labelledby` on `Select.List`, which Base UI leaves unnamed.

## Props

In MUI's layout. Every prop here gets its description as its JSDoc. Slots come last.

Select is a composite control: its root is Field's `<div>`, and its value is the chosen option's `value`, reported as `onChange(event, value, details)` adapted from `Select.Root`'s `onValueChange`, as the contract's [State and events](README.md#state-and-events) asks of a select. Its `name` reaches both `Field.Root` and `Select.Root`, as the contract's Forms rule asks, so Base UI's hidden input carries it and a native form submits the chosen value, and form libraries connect through their controller.

`SelectProps` extends Field's props, `FieldProps`, without `children`, `slotProps`, `onChange` and `defaultValue`, so `label`, `hiddenLabel`, `optional`, `optionalLabel`, `description`, `error`, `ref`, and Field's inherited `name`, `disabled`, `invalid`, `validate`, `validationMode`, `validationDebounceTime`, `dirty`, `touched`, `actionsRef`, `render`, `className` and `style`, come with Field's JSDoc, and `slotProps` takes Field's three keys beside Select's. `name` also reaches `Select.Root`, as the contract's Forms rule asks, so Base UI's hidden input reaches `FormData`. Select is a Field round a Base UI control, which is what `dependsOn` says; extending Field's props keeps every field's label, help, error and optional mark one API, reaching Field unchanged, and a prop Field gains reaches Select with no edit; `onChange` and `defaultValue` are a `<div>`'s with another type, and Select declares its own; `children` is the control, which is Select's own; `actionsRef` stays Field's, whose `validate` action a form library calls, and `Select.Root`'s, which closes the list, is left out, the two sharing one name.

Select takes one value only, a `string`, or `null` while nothing is chosen, leaving out Base UI's `multiple`, and leaves out `Select.Root`'s `modal`, `highlightItemOnHover`, `autoComplete`, `form`, `id`, `inputRef`, `actionsRef`, `isItemEqualToValue`, `itemToStringLabel`, `itemToStringValue` and `onOpenChangeComplete`, keeping Base UI's defaults for them. A Mylder select picks one mode, one operator or one order, and the options' values are strings, which a form submits as they are, so no comparison or conversion is needed; Base UI's `modal` default locks the page while the list is open, as a native select does; with `highlightItemOnHover` on, the pointer and the keys share one highlight, the Rows family's; a widened value type (`string[]` for `multiple`) and each prop left out can join later as an optional prop without a break.

Select declares `required` and `readOnly`, both default `false`, passed to `Select.Root`, with `required` apart from Field's `optional`: Select derives neither from the other, and a caller sets one at most. `required` lets Base UI's hidden input fail a form's check while nothing is chosen and tells the ear through `aria-required`, which `optional` can't, since it only draws words; `optional` marks the few fields a person may leave empty, which `required` can't, since Field draws no required mark; Field's own spec asks each dependent to say how the two relate, and the Do and don't says to set one at most, since a required field marked optional contradicts itself; `readOnly` shows a chosen value that the screen won't let the person change while still letting them see the options, which `disabled` hides from the keys.

`placeholder` is a `string`, the caller's, with no owned default, so the trigger shows nothing but its icon while no option is chosen and no placeholder is given. SearchField's `placeholder` is a string, and both are words in a box; a default such as "Choose" would be an owned word that says nothing about the field, which its label already names; Base UI's `Select.Value` shows it in `color.text.tertiary`, a hint beside the label, never the field's name.

Select takes no `variant`, `size`, `color` or `fullWidth`: its root takes its container's width and its trigger is `size.input` tall, the Fields family's one height. So the root carries no `data-variant`, `data-size` or `data-color`, and Base UI's state attributes are its data attributes. No name here is one the contract's [Names from other libraries](README.md#names-from-other-libraries) table bans: `onValueChange` and `onOpenChange` stay inside the component.

## Tokens

One row per part, state and property. The design states the deferred drawing shows are, for the trigger, rest, hover, focus, open, disabled and invalid, and, for a row, rest, hover, highlighted, pressed, selected and disabled. The Fields family keeps the trigger's rest look while the list is open, so open is the popup's look, not the box's. The label, the optional mark, the description and the error take Field's tokens, as [Field](field.md) gives them, and Select sets none of their properties.

The trigger takes `space.300` at its start and end, `space.200` between the value and the icon, the value in `typography.body` and `color.text.primary` on one line that ends in an ellipsis, the placeholder in `color.text.tertiary`, and the icon at `icon.size.400` in `color.text.secondary`. `space.300` is SearchField's start padding, and with the trigger's hairline it sets the value 13 px in, where a row's text starts inside the popup (its hairline, the list's `space.100` and the row's `space.200`), so the chosen word sits over its row; `typography.body` is the contract's type for a field's words; the box is one `size.input` tall, as an input is, so a long label is cut with an ellipsis rather than wrapped, its whole text still in the trigger for the ear; the chevron is decoration beside the value, so it takes the secondary ink SearchField's icon takes.

The chevron is a new icon, `chevron-down`, drawn on a 16 px grid for `icon.size.400` and joining the Actions category of `packages/perron/icons/icons.json` as "Open a select's list". The tick the `SelectedMark` part needs is the set's `tick`, which Checkbox added, drawn on a 14 px grid for `icon.size.325`: the `SelectedMark` shows it at that size, no `check` icon is drawn, and its use in `icons.json` widens to name the chosen option in a list. The set has no chevron; [Icons](../foundations/icons.md) asks a new icon to be drawn near the size it shows at, and the chevron sits inside a control, which is `icon.size.400`'s use; a single down chevron says the list opens under the box, which it always does (see Base UI parts); the contract's shared parts name the tick in `packages/perron/icons/` as the one tick, so a second drawing of it would be a copy.

The list, not the popup, takes the Popups family's `space.100` padding, the popup taking none, so the focus ring round a row the keys reach is drawn inside the scrolling list rather than cut by it. `Select.List` is the box that scrolls, and a scroll box clips what reaches past its padding, so a row's ring, `focus.width` and `focus.offset` outside it, needs room inside the list; `space.100` is that room exactly (2 px and 2 px), so the ring is never cut and the rows' `radius.md` still nests in the popup's `radius.lg`; the popup still looks padded `space.100`, as the family asks.

A row keeps `perron.css`'s focus ring on `:focus-visible`, beside its highlight fill. Base UI moves real focus to the row the keys reach, and [Accessibility](../foundations/accessibility.md) says never to remove an outline without drawing the ring another way; the highlight fill, `color.surface.hover`, is too faint to be the only mark of focus; the pointer moves the highlight and focus too, but `:focus-visible` matches only after a key, so a pointer sees the fill alone.

The chosen row takes `color.surface.selected` with the `SelectedMark`, in `color.text.primary` at `icon.size.325` (the `tick`'s drawn size), at its end, and a highlighted chosen row lays `color.surface.hover` over that fill as a `linear-gradient` background-image. The Rows family gives a selected row `color.surface.selected` with the `SelectedMark`; at the row's end the tick never moves the labels, which all start on one line with the group labels and the value in the box, and Base UI mounts it on the chosen row only; the list opens with the highlight on the chosen row, so the highlight must show over the selected fill, and a gradient over it is how the Fields family lays the hover over a fill.

A group label takes `typography.overline` in `color.text.secondary`, padded `space.150` above, `space.100` below and `space.200` at its sides, and a separator is a `border.width.025` line in `color.border.subtle`, `space.100` above and below. A group label heads a short section, which is `typography.overline`'s use, and its capitals come from the style, so a caller writes it in sentence case, as [Content design](../content-design.md) asks; `space.200` at its sides starts it on the rows' line; the Rows family divides rows with `border.width.025` in `color.border.subtle`, and `space.100` keeps the line apart from the rows on either side.

The trigger's cursor is `pointer`, and `default` while disabled (`[data-disabled]`) or read-only (`[data-readonly]`). It has no pressed look: while pressed (`[data-pressed]`, `:active`) it keeps its rest look, under its hover layer while the pointer is on it, for the reason CR-9 gives. A read-only trigger keeps its rest look and takes no hover, as the contract's [Pointer feedback](README.md#pointer-feedback) asks of a read-only part, though its list still opens. The Fields family has no pressed look, and a press opens the list at once, whose popup is the change the person sees; a read-only field's value reads at full strength, so a quieter look would say it is disabled when it isn't, and the ear hears `aria-readonly`; a read-only look can join later as a look, without a prop.

A disabled row takes `color.text.tertiary` and the `default` cursor, takes neither the hover nor the pressed look, keeps the highlight look where Base UI puts the highlight, and never takes the selected look. Disabled is a colour, never an opacity, as the contract says; the contract's pointer feedback keeps hover and pressed off a disabled part; Base UI lets the keys reach a disabled option so the person can hear it is there, so the place the keys are at must stay visible, and the highlight is that place, not a hover; a disabled option is never chosen, so it is never the selected one.

A row the pointer presses lays `color.surface.selected` in place of the hover fill, on `:active`, outside `@media (hover: hover)` and after the hover and highlight rules; a pressed chosen row lays a second `color.surface.selected` over its selected fill as a `linear-gradient` background-image, in place of its hover layer (CR-17). A row's cursor is `pointer`, and `default` on a disabled row and in a read-only list, where no row takes the hover or the pressed look. A row is a quiet part, transparent at rest, and the contract's [Pointer feedback](README.md#pointer-feedback) gives a quiet part `color.surface.hover`, then `color.surface.selected`, a step the eye sees past hover that keeps the label's contrast; the chosen row's hover is already a layer over its fill, so its press is the denser layer over the same fill and still steps past its hover; Base UI's `Select.Item` sets no `data-pressed`, so `:active` alone marks the press, and outside the query a touch press shows too. Base UI marks no row read-only: the list carries `aria-readonly="true"` while the field is read-only, so the rules read the list's attribute, as CR-14 lets a rule read a part inside another.

## Keyboard and ARIA

From the Base UI reference for `Select` and the installed `SelectRoot`, `SelectTrigger`, `SelectPopup`, `SelectList`, `SelectItem`, `SelectGroup`, `SelectGroupLabel` and `SelectSeparator`, and Field's for the label. "From" says who does it.

| ---------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------- |
| `Enter`, `Space`       | On the closed trigger: open the list (`onOpen`, `'trigger-press'`), highlighting and focusing the chosen option, or the first. On a highlighted row: choose it (`onChange`, `'item-press'`), close the list (`onClose`, `'item-press'`) and return focus to the trigger                                                            | Base UI |
| `ArrowDown`, `ArrowUp` | On the closed trigger: open the list (`onOpen`, `'list-navigation'`), highlighting and focusing the chosen option, or, with nothing chosen, the first on ArrowDown and the last on ArrowUp. | `Home`, `End`          | In the open list: move the highlight and focus to the first or the last row                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | Base UI |

What axe won't catch, from the contract, each with how this component meets it:

- [ ] Everything the eye is told, the ear is told, for every shape each prop accepts: the chevron is `aria-hidden` beside a trigger the `combobox` role and `aria-expanded` describe; the selected mark is `aria-hidden` on a row whose `aria-selected` says it is chosen; a hidden label still names the trigger and the list; a group label is heard as its group's name; a disabled row is `aria-disabled`, not only grey; an invalid field is `aria-invalid` and its error is words, never only the trigger's red edge.
- [ ] Every landmark and named region has an accessible name: none here; Select is not a landmark, and its list is named by the label.
- [ ] Every default label can be overridden: `optionalLabel`, Field's, overrides "(optional)", the one owned string Select shows (see Owned strings).
- [ ] Every shape the type accepts renders, in every variant: `label`, `description` and `error` render a string, an element and a list alike, as Field's do; `items` renders a flat list and groups alike; a long Danish compound wraps in a row and a group label and ends in an ellipsis in the box (CR-11).
- [ ] A hidden copy kept for animation is `aria-hidden`, and a collapsed region is `inert`: none here; the closed list renders nothing, and Base UI makes the positioner `inert` while it closes; Base UI's hidden input is `aria-hidden`.
- [ ] Native semantics first: a native `<button>` for the trigger, and Base UI's `combobox`, `listbox`, `group` and `option` roles; Perron adds only the listbox's `aria-labelledby`. The label is a `<div>` rather than a `<label>`, as Base UI advises for a `<button>` control, and names the trigger through `aria-labelledby`.
- [ ] Focus moves in reading order and returns on close: the trigger is the field's one tab stop; opening moves focus to the chosen row, and choosing, Esc, Tab and a press outside return it to the trigger, through Base UI's popup.
- [ ] Every target is at least `size.target-min` square: a row, at least `size.target-min` tall and as wide as the list; the trigger, `size.input` tall and as wide as the field.
- [ ] Loops stop when the system asks for less motion: none here; Select has no loop and no transition (CR-12).

`optional` is the key `packages/perron/src/locale/en.ts` already has, "A field's label: after the words of a field the person may leave empty", which Field reads and Select passes `optionalLabel` to. Select adds no key.

Every other word is the caller's, through `label`, `description`, `error`, `placeholder` and `items`, or Base UI's message for a failing check, which is the caller's `validate` result or the browser's own, Field's known exception: a `required` select with nothing chosen fails the hidden input's native check, whose message the browser writes in its own interface language, unless the caller gives `error` or `slotProps.error.match` with its own words.

## Component rules

Rules for this component alone, numbered so the build and the review can cite them.

- **CR-1.** Base UI's Select already gives the opening and closing with their reasons, the highlight and focus moving through the rows, Home and End, the typed-letter matching on the closed trigger and in the open list, choosing on Enter, Space and a press, focus moving into the list and back to the trigger, the placement and its flipping, the page's scroll lock while open, the combobox, listbox, group and option roles, the hidden input for forms, and, inside Field, the field's validity on the trigger, so the component rebuilds none of it and adds no key or pointer handlers.
- **CR-2.** Select renders the [Field](field.md) component, given every Field prop it takes, holding `Select.Root` as its `children`; `Select.Root` holds `Select.Trigger` (`Select.Value`, then `Select.Icon`) and `Select.Portal`, which holds `Select.Positioner`, `Select.Popup` and, in the popup, `Select.List`. With a flat `items`, the list holds one `Select.Item` per item; with groups, one `Select.Group` per group, each holding its `Select.GroupLabel` and then its items, with a `Select.Separator` before each group but the first. Each `Select.Item` has `value` and `key` the item's `value`, `label` the item's `label` and `disabled` the item's, and holds `Select.ItemText` with the label, then `Select.ItemIndicator`. `Select.tsx` exports `SelectItem` and `SelectGroup` beside `Select` and `SelectProps`, so the package's barrel gives them to callers.
- **CR-3.** `{...rest}` reaches Field before Select's own props, and Select's own props are taken out of `rest` first (`items`, `placeholder`, `value`, `defaultValue`, `onChange`, `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpen`, `onClose`, `required`, `readOnly`, `slotProps`), so none reaches the `<div>`; `label`, `hiddenLabel`, `optional`, `optionalLabel`, `description`, `error`, `name`, `disabled`, `invalid`, `validate`, `validationMode`, `validationDebounceTime`, `dirty`, `touched`, `actionsRef` and `render` stay in `rest` for Field. Select also reads `name`, without taking it out of `rest`, and gives it to `Select.Root`, so the hidden input carries it whether or not Base UI's field context reaches it. `ref`, `style` and `data-testid` land on the root, and `className` reaches Field as `pn-Select` then the caller's, a string or a function of the root's state, so the root reads `pn-Field pn-Select`, then the caller's.
- **CR-4.** Select turns `onValueChange(value, details)` into `onChange(details.event, value, details)`, and `onOpenChange(open, details)` into `onOpen(details.event, details)` when `open` is `true` and `onClose(details.event, details.reason, details)` when it is `false`, and exposes neither. It gives `Select.Root` the options flattened, groups and all, into Base UI's `{ value, label }` list, so `Select.Value` shows the chosen option's label; a key Select doesn't set is left out of `Select.Root`'s props, never set to `undefined`, so `value` stays uncontrolled when the caller leaves it out.
- **CR-5.** Each `slotProps` value of a part Select sets props on (`label`, `value`, `icon`, `positioner`, `list`, `item` and `itemIndicator`) is merged with Base UI's `mergeProps` (`@base-ui/react/merge-props`), Select's own props last, so a caller's handler runs beside Select's and its `className` joins after the part's class; a part Select sets nothing on but its class (`trigger`, `portal`, `popup`, `group`, `groupLabel`, `separator` and `itemText`) takes its `slotProps` value spread as it is, `{...slotProps?.portal}`. Each Select part's class is set after the merge with the shared `withClass` helper from `packages/perron/src/internal/nodes.ts`: `pn-Select-<part>` first, then the caller's `className`, a string or a function of the part's state. `slotProps.label`, `slotProps.description` and `slotProps.error` go to Field's own `slotProps`, which merges and classes them itself; Select's own props for the label, `render={<div />}`, `nativeLabel={false}` and its `id`, are merged after the caller's `slotProps.label`, so the label stays a non-native `<div>` that the list's `aria-labelledby` names, and Field's `hiddenLabel` wins over both.
- **CR-6.** The label gets an `id` from React's `useId`, given through Field's `slotProps.label`, so Base UI registers it as the field's label; the trigger reads it through Base UI's `aria-labelledby`, and Select sets the same id as `aria-labelledby` on `Select.List`, which Base UI leaves unnamed. A caller's `slotProps.label.id` gives way to it, so the trigger and the list always read the same id.
- **CR-7.** The chevron is an inline `<svg>` drawn from the new `chevron-down.svg` in the icons folder, inside `Select.Icon`, with the classes `perron-icon`, `aria-hidden="true"` and `focusable="false"`, in `currentColor`; the build adds the file and its `icons.json` entry, following [Icons](../foundations/icons.md). The selected mark is `<Select.ItemIndicator render={<SelectedMark />} />`; the build adds the `SelectedMark` shared part, with the set's `tick.svg`, its only icon, at `icon.size.325`, as the contract's [Shared parts](README.md#shared-parts) table says, draws no `check` icon, and widens the tick's `use` in `icons.json` to name the chosen option in a list too; and Select's CSS sets only its place in the row (`flex: none`), never its size or colour.
- **CR-8.** `Select.Positioner` takes `alignItemWithTrigger={false}`, Select's own, last, and `slotProps.positioner` is typed `Omit<Select.Positioner.Props, 'alignItemWithTrigger'>`, so the list always opens under the trigger. The positioner takes `z-index.dialog` and `padding-block: space.100`, the gap on whichever side the list sits; Select passes no `sideOffset` and keeps Base UI's other positioning defaults, which `slotProps.positioner` replaces.
- **CR-9.** The trigger is a flex row, `align-items: center`, `box-sizing: border-box`, the value growing (`flex: 1`, `min-inline-size: 0`) and the icon keeping its size (`flex: none`), with `text-align: start` and `margin: 0`. Its focus ring is `perron.css`'s, on `:focus-visible`, never redrawn. Its hover lays `color.surface.hover` over its fill as a `linear-gradient` background-image, inside `@media (hover: hover)` and not while `[data-disabled]` or `[data-readonly]`; its cursor is `pointer`, and `default` while `[data-disabled]` or `[data-readonly]`. It has no pressed look, the reason the contract's [Pointer feedback](README.md#pointer-feedback) asks for: the Fields family has no pressed look, and a press opens the list at once, whose popup is the change the person sees, so while pressed (`[data-pressed]`, `:active`) it keeps its rest look, under its hover layer while the pointer is on it. While open or read-only it keeps its rest look too.
- **CR-10.** The popup is `box-sizing: border-box`, `inline-size: var(--anchor-width)`, at most `calc(var(--available-height) - 2 * var(--perron-space-100))` tall, and a flex column, with no padding of its own; the list fills it, scrolls (`overflow-y: auto`, `overscroll-behavior: contain`, `min-block-size: 0`) and carries the `space.100` padding and `scroll-padding-block`, so a row's focus ring is never cut. The popup draws its `border.width.025` edge as a border, so Windows' forced colours keep an edge round it when they drop its glass and shadow.
- **CR-11.** Long words: a row's text and a group label wrap (`overflow-wrap: anywhere`), since each takes the list's width; the value in the trigger keeps its words on one line (`white-space: nowrap`) and ends in an ellipsis (`overflow: hidden`, `text-overflow: ellipsis`), as an input's words stay on one line. The label, the description and the error wrap, as Field's do.
- **CR-12.** The list opens and closes at once, and the chevron doesn't turn: no `duration.*` token fits a list under a field, as SearchField's CR-12 says, so the CSS has no transition or animation and styles neither `data-starting-style` nor `data-ending-style`.
- **CR-13.** A row is a flex row, `align-items: center`: the item text grows (`flex: 1`, `min-inline-size: 0`) and the selected mark sits after it at the row's end. Each row keeps `perron.css`'s focus ring on `:focus-visible`; the hover and highlight fill is `color.surface.hover`, on `:hover` inside `@media (hover: hover)`, never on a disabled row or in a read-only list (CR-17), and on `[data-highlighted]`, disabled rows included, since the highlight shows where the keys are, not a hover; the chosen row's fill is `color.surface.selected`, and a hovered or highlighted chosen row lays `color.surface.hover` over it as a `linear-gradient` background-image. In forced colours a highlighted row draws `Highlight` with `HighlightText`, inside `@media (forced-colors: active)`, with `forced-color-adjust: none` and a selector that reads the list's class, `.pn-Select-list .pn-Select-item[data-highlighted]`, so it outweighs the hover and pressed rules (CR-17), as SearchField's CR-13 does, since forced colours drop `color.surface.hover`; the chosen row keeps its tick. Forced colours also drop `color.text.tertiary`, so there a disabled row draws `GrayText`, as Checkbox's CR-11 does, and a highlighted one, disabled or not, keeps `HighlightText`, the rule for it coming after.
- **CR-14.** A rule that styles a part inside another reads one class under its part's class and attribute, as Field's CR-13 allows: the icon's disabled colour is `.pn-Select-trigger[data-disabled] .pn-Select-icon`, and the placeholder's colour is `.pn-Select-value[data-placeholder]`, which draws `GrayText` in forced colours, so the placeholder never reads as a chosen value.
- **CR-15.** The portal renders nothing on the server, so the contract story's owned-strings check sees only the label and the trigger, with the option `Default` chooses. The stories that open the list check its words in the live DOM: `expectOwnedStrings(popup.outerHTML, locale, callerWords)`, from `packages/perron/src/testing/owned-strings.ts`, in English. The `Optional` story's render gets its own test, which runs `expectOwnedStrings` on its server-rendered markup in `en`, `da`, `sv` and `nb`, as Field's CR-12 does.
- **CR-16.** The stories' meta sets `parameters: { docs: { story: { inline: false, height: '480px' } } }`, as the contract's [Stories](README.md#stories) asks of an overlay, a height that fits the tallest open list, `Groups`' two group labels and ten options, without its scrolling, and each story that shows the list opens it at first render with `defaultOpen`, beside the trigger that opens it again. The `Disabled` story turns off axe's `color-contrast` rule for itself alone, with its reason, as Field's does: axe flags the disabled trigger's `color.text.tertiary`, which [Accessibility](../foundations/accessibility.md) lists as a deliberate miss and WCAG 1.4.3 exempts for an inactive control. The placeholder is the stories' one other exception: drawn as text in `color.text.tertiary`, the contract's colour for a placeholder and a miss Accessibility lists by name, it is checked by axe where a native input's placeholder is not, so the meta narrows axe's `color-contrast` rule to every element but `.pn-Select-value[data-placeholder]`, for the stories that show the placeholder, and checks the rest. The contract story `Root` renders `Default`'s args without Select's meta, so `Default` chooses "Metro" by `defaultValue` and renders no placeholder; no rule in the shared `.storybook/preview.ts` passes over it.
- **CR-17.** A row answers the pointer as the contract's [Pointer feedback](README.md#pointer-feedback) asks of a quiet part. Its cursor is `pointer`, and `default` on `[data-disabled]` and in a read-only list. Pressed, it lays `color.surface.selected` as its `background-color`, on `:active`, since Base UI's `Select.Item` sets no `data-pressed`, in a rule after the hover and highlight rules and outside `@media (hover: hover)`; a pressed chosen row keeps its `color.surface.selected` fill and lays a second `color.surface.selected` over it as a `linear-gradient` background-image, in place of its hover layer, so it steps past its hover as an unchosen row does. Neither the hover rule nor the pressed one applies to `[data-disabled]` or to a row in a read-only list: Base UI marks the list, not the row, so they read `:where(.pn-Select-list:not([aria-readonly='true'])) .pn-Select-item`, as CR-14 lets a rule read a part inside another, the list's test inside `:where()` so it adds no weight and CR-13's forced-colours highlight, `.pn-Select-list .pn-Select-item[data-highlighted]` after them, still wins over a hovered or pressed row; and the cursor's `default` reads `.pn-Select-list[aria-readonly='true'] .pn-Select-item`. The `Open` story's `play` checks, with `stateFill` and `pressedAfterHover`, that the pressed fill, as written, renders apart from the hover one and its rule comes after the hover rule.

## Do and don't

For a caller using the component, with the reason.

| Do                                                                                                                                       | Don't                                                                                                                                    |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Use Select for one choice from a short, fixed list, such as a transport mode or an order                                                 | Use it to find a line or a stop among hundreds: use [SearchField](search-field.md), which narrows the list as the person types           |
| Give a `label` that names the value, "Transport mode", and hide it with `hiddenLabel` only where the screen already says it              | Let the placeholder stand in for the label: it is gone once an option is chosen, and drawn in `color.text.tertiary`, below text contrast |
| Write the placeholder as an instruction, "Choose a transport mode"                                                                       | Put an option's words in the placeholder: the person reads it as a value already chosen                                                  |
| Give short `label`s that the person can tell apart by their first letters, so typing on the closed box finds them                        | Start every option with the same word ("Line M1", "Line M2"): typing finds nothing, and the box's ellipsis cuts the words that differ    |
| Group options with `SelectGroup` when the list mixes kinds, such as metro and S-tog lines, and write each group's label in sentence case | Write a group label in capitals: its style sets the capitals, and the ear hears the words as written                                     |
| Set `required` or `optional`, whichever the form needs                                                                                   | Set both: the field is marked optional while the form refuses it empty                                                                   |
| Give `error` whenever the field is `invalid`                                                                                             | Set `invalid` with no message: the trigger's red edge alone tells only the eye, and only by its colour                                   |
| Leave an option that can't be chosen out of `items`, or give it `disabled` when the person should see it is there                        | Disable the whole field to say one option isn't available                                                                                |
| Keep the field in a `PerronProvider` with the screen's locale, so "(optional)" speaks it                                                 | Translate it with `optionalLabel` on every instance: that is for one instance's own words                                                |

title: Switch
markdown:
# Switch

A two-state control that turns one setting on or off at once, such as showing vehicle trails on the map.

<!-- run notes -->

The design is deferred (ADR 0010, `docs/adr/0010-unattended-runs-with-design-deferred.md`): there is no read-back, code map or export, and this spec decides what the drawing would, from the [contract](README.md), the [foundations](../foundations/README.md), [content design](../content-design.md), the tokens and the Base UI reference for `@base-ui/react` 1.9.0. No ROADMAP line names Switch; it joined the registry with the form components, with `baseUiParts` `Switch.Root` and `Switch.Thumb` and nothing in `dependsOn`. The extracted prototype component is not in any branch this run can reach, so nothing here rests on it. The foundations already name its look: [Elevation](../foundations/elevation.md#surfaces) puts tracks on `color.surface.inset` and pressed toggles on `color.surface.inverse`, [Accessibility](../foundations/accessibility.md#rules) asks every target to be `size.target-min` and every control's edge to reach 3:1, which `color.border.control` does, and [Semantic spacing](../foundations/semantic-spacing.md#radius) gives pills `radius.full`.

## Anatomy

Penpot page `Components/Switch`. Family: none (the contract's [Families](README.md#families) have no two-state track; its surfaces come from [Elevation](../foundations/elevation.md#surfaces), as FilterChip's do). Shared parts: none (every word is the caller's, and the state is told by `role="switch"` with `aria-checked`, not by a hidden word).

| Part (Penpot layer) | What it is                                                                                                                                                                             | Base UI part   | Class             | `slotProps` key |
| ------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------- | ----------------- | --------------- |
| `root`              | The track: a `<span role="switch">`, an inline flex row in a pill, that holds the thumb and takes focus                                                                                | `Switch.Root`  | `pn-Switch`       | none            |
| `thumb`             | The `<span>` circle inside the track, at its inline start when off and its inline end when on                                                                                          | `Switch.Thumb` | `pn-Switch-thumb` | `thumb`         |
| `input`             | The visually hidden `<input type="checkbox">` Base UI renders beside the root, `aria-hidden` and out of the tab order, that a `<label>` targets and a native `<form>` reads; not drawn | `Switch.Root`  | none              | none            |
| `focusRing`         | The keyboard focus ring on the root: the `:focus-visible` outline `perron.css` draws, following the pill's radius, not an element                                                      | `Switch.Root`  | none              | none            |

The `input` has no class and no `slotProps` key: Base UI renders it inside `Switch.Root` and gives the caller `inputRef`, `id`, `name`, `form`, `value` and `uncheckedValue` to reach it, with no props of its own. A second hidden input, `type="hidden"`, renders while the switch is off and both `name` and `uncheckedValue` are given, so the form submits the off value.

## Base UI parts

Imported from `@base-ui/react/switch`, at the version pinned in `package.json` (1.9.0 installed).

| Base UI part   | Renders                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | Perron sets                                                                                                                                                                                                     | Passed through                                                                                                                                                                  |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Switch.Root`  | `<span role="switch">` with `aria-checked`, `tabIndex` 0, `aria-readonly`, `aria-required`, `aria-disabled` and `tabIndex` −1 while disabled, `aria-labelledby` from a wrapping or associated `<label>`, `data-checked` or `data-unchecked`, `data-disabled`, `data-readonly`, `data-required`; and the hidden input beside it | `className` (`pn-Switch`, then the caller's), `ref`, `checked`, `defaultChecked`, `onCheckedChange` adapted from `onChange` (CR-2), `disabled`, `readOnly`, `required`, `name`, and the thumb as its only child | `value`, `uncheckedValue`, `form`, `inputRef`, `id`, `nativeButton`, `render`, `style`, `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby` and every other prop of a `<span>`, through `{...rest}` |
| `Switch.Thumb` | `<span>`, with the root's state attributes: `data-checked` or `data-unchecked`, `data-disabled`, `data-readonly`, `data-required`, and inside a Base UI `Field.Root` `data-invalid` and the other field attributes                                                                                                             | `className` (`pn-Switch-thumb`, then the caller's, a string or a function of the thumb's state), through `withClass`, as Dialog's parts                                                                         | `slotProps.thumb`, merged under Perron's own props with `mergeProps`                                                                                                            |

Base UI already does: `role="switch"` and `aria-checked` following the state; one tab stop, through `tabIndex` 0 on the `<span>`; Space (on release) and Enter (on press) toggle it, as a click does, through the hidden input's click, so `onCheckedChange` fires once with the new state and its details; a `<label>` wrapping the switch, or one whose `htmlFor` names its `id`, gives it `aria-labelledby` and toggles it when clicked, since the `id` lands on the hidden input; `aria-label` wins over an associated label, as on native inputs; a disabled switch sets `aria-disabled`, leaves the tab order (`tabIndex` −1) and ignores clicks and keys; a read-only one keeps focus but ignores clicks and keys, and sets `aria-readonly`; `details.cancel()` in `onCheckedChange` keeps an uncontrolled switch as it was; the hidden input submits `value` (default `"on"`) when on, and `uncheckedValue` when off and given; inside a Base UI `Field.Root` it takes the field's name, disabled state, label and validation, setting `aria-invalid` and `data-invalid` when the field is invalid.

## Props

In MUI's layout. Every prop the props type declares gets this description as its JSDoc; every inherited one keeps Base UI's. Slots come last. The props type extends `Switch.Root.Props` without `checked`, `defaultChecked`, `onCheckedChange`, `disabled`, `readOnly`, `required`, `name`, `className`, `style`, `children` and `ref`: it declares its own `checked`, `defaultChecked`, `disabled`, `readOnly`, `required`, `name`, `className`, `style` and `ref`, with the descriptions below, maps `onCheckedChange` to `onChange`, and renders the thumb as the only child.

The switch's state is `checked`, `defaultChecked` and `onChange(event, value, details)`, whose `value` argument is the new `checked`, and the `value` prop stays the value a form submits when it is on. These are MUI's Switch names and Base UI's own `checked` and `defaultChecked`; the contract's [State and events](README.md#state-and-events) keeps `value`, `defaultValue` and `onChange` for a value a control chooses, but a switch's value is a boolean, and MUI and Base UI both give `value` to the submitted string, so a caller coming from either reads them as they do there; `onChange` keeps the contract's `(event, value, details)` shape, its value the new `checked`; and the contract's [Names from other libraries](README.md#names-from-other-libraries) leave all three free, where FilterChip's `selected` names a toggle button's pressed state, not a switch's.

The switch takes no label of its own: the caller names it with a `<label>` around it or beside it, a Field's label, or `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`. MUI's Switch takes no label (its `FormControlLabel` adds one) and Base UI's `Switch.Root` takes none, labelling itself from a native `<label>` or a `Field.Label`; Field, registered beside Switch, is where a label, a description and an error sit for every form control; one switch's setting row, a label at the start and the switch at the end, varies between a settings list and a panel; and the API only grows, so a `label` prop can join later without a break.

The switch comes in one look, with no `variant`, `size` or `color`. The [brand](../foundations/README.md#the-brand) keeps the interface to ink, glass and neutral surfaces, with yellow for the one main action, which a switch never is; the on track is `color.surface.inverse`, the pressed toggle's fill, as FilterChip's selected fill is; the track is `size.target-min` tall, the smallest target, so a `small` would miss it; and each prop can join later without a break.

The switch passes every other prop of `Switch.Root` through unchanged (`value`, `uncheckedValue`, `form`, `inputRef`, `id`, `nativeButton` and `render`), and declares `readOnly`, `required` and `name` with Perron's own descriptions. Each is a form or labelling hook a caller of Base UI's switch has, none changes the look, the contract asks `name` of every control a form submits and names `required` and `readOnly` among its booleans, and leaving one out now would only make a caller wrap the switch to reach it.

Switch takes no `children`: its one child is the thumb, which it renders itself, and the caller's words go in the label beside it. No label-override props: the switch owns no strings.

| Name                        | Type                                                                              | Default | Base UI prop      | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| --------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------- | ----------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `checked`                   | `boolean`                                                                         | none    | `checked`         | Whether the switch is on, when the caller controls it. Announced as on or off.                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `defaultChecked`            | `boolean`                                                                         | `false` | `defaultChecked`  | Whether the switch is on at first, when it keeps its state itself.                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `onChange`                  | `(event: Event, value: boolean, details: Switch.Root.ChangeEventDetails) => void` | none    | `onCheckedChange` | Called when a click, Space or Enter, or a click on its label, turns the switch on or off, with the new state as `value`; `details.reason` is `'none'`, and `details.cancel()` keeps the state as it was. `event` is `details.event`, the hidden input's change. |
| `disabled`                  | `boolean`                                                                         | `false` | `disabled`        | Whether the switch ignores the pointer and the keys. It leaves the tab order, keeps its state, and is announced as dimmed.                                                                                                                                      |
| `readOnly`                  | `boolean`                                                                         | `false` | `readOnly`        | Whether the switch shows its state but can't be changed. It keeps its place in the tab order and is announced as read-only.                                                                                                                                     |
| `required`                  | `boolean`                                                                         | `false` | `required`        | Whether the switch must be on before its form submits. Announced as required; the label says so to the eye.                                                                                                                                                     |
| `name`                      | `string`                                                                          | none    | `name`            | The name the switch's value is submitted under in a native `<form>`. Inside a Base UI `Field.Root`, the field's name wins.                                                                                                                                      |
| `value`                     | `string`                                                                          | none    | inherited         | Inherited from Base UI with its JSDoc: the value submitted with the form when the switch is on. By default, switch submits the "on" value, matching native checkbox behavior.                                                                                   |
| `uncheckedValue`            | `string`                                                                          | none    | inherited         | Inherited from Base UI with its JSDoc: the value submitted with the form when the switch is off. By default, unchecked switches do not submit any value, matching native checkbox behavior.                                                                     |
| `form`                      | `string`                                                                          | none    | inherited         | Inherited from Base UI with its JSDoc: identifies the form that owns the hidden input. Useful when the switch is rendered outside the form.                                                                                                                     |
| `inputRef`                  | `React.Ref<HTMLInputElement>`                                                     | none    | inherited         | Inherited from Base UI with its JSDoc: a ref to access the hidden `<input>` element.                                                                                                                                                                            |

When `nativeButton` is `true`, the id is applied to the root element.                                                                                                                |
| `nativeButton`              | `boolean`                                                                         | `false` | inherited         | Inherited from Base UI with its JSDoc: whether the component renders a native `<button>` element when replacing it via the `render` prop. Set to `true` if the rendered element is a native button.                                                             |
| `render`                    | Base UI's `render`                                                                | none    | inherited         | Inherited from Base UI with its JSDoc: allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component.                                                                                                           |
| `className`, `style`, `ref` | React's                                                                           | none    | none              | Reaches the root. `className` is merged after `pn-Switch`.                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `slotProps.thumb`           | `Switch.Thumb.Props`                                                              | none    | `Switch.Thumb`    | Props for the thumb part, merged under Perron's own; its `className` joins after `pn-Switch-thumb`.                                                                                                                                                             |

## Tokens

One row per part, state and property. States are the contract's design states: rest is no selector (the switch off, `[data-unchecked]`), hover is `:hover` inside `@media (hover: hover)`, pressed is `:active`, focus is `:focus-visible`, disabled is `[data-disabled]`, selected is Base UI's `[data-checked]` (the switch on), and invalid is `[data-invalid]`, which Base UI sets only inside a `Field.Root` whose field is invalid. Highlighted and open don't apply: the switch takes focus rather than `data-highlighted`, and opens nothing.

The track is 40 × 24 px and the thumb 18 px, from the tokens with no new size token: the root is `size.target-min` tall and `size.target-min` plus `space.400` wide, with a `border.width.025` border and `space.050` padding inside it, so the thumb is `size.target-min` less twice the padding and the border, and travels `space.400`. The track is the target, so `size.target-min` tall meets [Accessibility](../foundations/accessibility.md#rules) on its own; the width is the height plus the travel, a common switch's proportion beside `typography.label` text; the thumb is 18 px inside a 1 px edge and a 2 px gap, so it reads as a separate mark; the travel, 40 − 6 − 18, is exactly `space.400`; and [Layout](../foundations/layout.md#other-layout-properties) keeps a measure only one component reads in that component's CSS, as `calc()` over the tokens.

The switch off is a `color.surface.inset` track with a `border.width.025` edge in `color.border.control` and a `color.text.secondary` thumb, and on a `color.surface.inverse` track and edge with a `color.surface.raised` thumb; hover lays `color.surface.hover` over the off track and turns the on track `color.surface.inverse-hover`, and pressed, a step past it, lays `color.surface.selected` and turns it `color.surface.inverse-pressed`, and there is no shadow. [Elevation](../foundations/elevation.md#surfaces) puts tracks on `color.surface.inset` and pressed toggles on `color.surface.inverse`; `color.surface.inset` stands only 1.17:1 from `color.surface.raised`, so the off track needs `color.border.control`'s 3:1 edge to show where it is ([Accessibility](../foundations/accessibility.md#controls-focus-and-status-fills-on-surfaces)); the thumb's colour reaches well past 3:1 on its track in both states and both themes (`color.text.secondary` is 6.77:1 on light inset and 5.71:1 on dark), so on and off differ in the thumb's place, the thumb's colour and the track's fill, never in colour alone; the hover fills are the ones FilterChip and the Fields take; the edge keeps its width when on, in the fill's colour, so the geometry holds (CR-5); and [Elevation](../foundations/elevation.md#shadows) gives `shadow.thumb` to the selected segment alone, where the thumb needs no shadow to stand out.

A disabled switch off is a `color.surface.inset` track with a `color.border.subtle` edge and a `color.text.tertiary` thumb, and on a `color.text.tertiary` track and edge with a `color.surface.raised` thumb, with no hover or pressed layer. The contract makes disabled a colour, `color.text.tertiary`, never an opacity; a disabled control is exempt from 3:1, so the edge steps down to the decorative `color.border.subtle`; and a disabled switch still shows whether its setting is on, by the thumb's place and the track's fill, as a disabled segmented control keeps its choice.

Inside an invalid Base UI `Field.Root`, a state Base UI produces (`data-invalid`) that no drawing shows, the track's edge turns `color.status.danger`, on and off, with the fills unchanged. The contract's [Families](README.md#families) give the Fields' edge `color.status.danger` when invalid, a switch sits in a Field beside them, and the message that says why is the Field's, not the switch's. Disabled wins over invalid: a disabled switch in an invalid Field keeps its disabled edge, `color.border.subtle` or `color.text.tertiary`, since Base UI drops `aria-invalid` while the control is disabled (`field/root/useFieldValidation.js`), and a disabled control is exempt from 3:1 and shows no error.
