title: Section
markdown:
# Section

A titled group of content inside a panel or a page, such as a stop's departures or the lines that call at it: a small heading in capitals, an optional action beside it, and the caller's content below.

<!-- run notes -->

The design is deferred (ADR 0010, `docs/adr/0010-unattended-runs-with-design-deferred.md`): this spec decides what the drawing would, from the [contract](README.md), the [foundations](../foundations/README.md), [content design](../content-design.md) and the tokens. Section has no Base UI component and nothing in `dependsOn`, and the extracted prototype is not reachable from this branch, so nothing here rests on it. Its one firm source is the token `typography.overline`, whose description is "Section headings and tags, set in capitals".

## Anatomy

Penpot page `Components/Section`. Family: none, since it is content on its container's surface and joins no family's treatment. Shared parts: none.

The drawing has no variant property, so its one variant is `Default`, and no `State` property, since Section is not interactive and has only its rest state. Its layers are the parts below.

| Part (Penpot layer) | What it is                                                                                                                      | Base UI part                              | Class                | `slotProps` key |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- | -------------------- | --------------- |
| `root`              | A `section` stacking the header above the content, named by its title. Penpot's main instance, a vertical flex board            | None: `useRender`, a `section` by default | `pn-Section`         | none            |
| `header`            | A `div` laying out the title and the action in a row                                                                            | None: `useRender`, a `div` by default     | `pn-Section-header`  | `header`        |
| `title`             | An `h3` holding the caller's `title`, set in capitals: what the section is about                                                | None: `useRender`, an `h3` by default     | `pn-Section-title`   | `title`         |
| `action`            | A `div` at the end of the header holding the caller's `action`, such as a link to everything the section shows; only when given | None: `useRender`, a `div` by default     | `pn-Section-action`  | `action`        |
| `content`           | A `div` holding the caller's `children`; only when given                                                                        | None: `useRender`, a `div` by default     | `pn-Section-content` | `content`       |

No part has a Base UI component, because none has behaviour for Base UI to give: no focus, keys, state or popup. Each part renders through Base UI's `useRender` hook instead, as EmptyState's do ([EmptyState](empty-state.md)), so each takes `render`: the root through the `render` prop, an inner part through its `slotProps` key.

- The root is a `section` named by its own title, through `aria-labelledby` pointing at the title's `id`, so it is a named region a screen reader can list and jump to. A `section` is the native element for a group under its own heading, the contract's checklist asks a named region for its name "from the component's own heading through `aria-labelledby` where it has one", and a caller who wants a plain group renders the root as a `div` through `render`, which drops the region and keeps the heading.
- The title is an `h3` by default, its level changed through `slotProps.title.render` (`render: <h2 />`, `<h4 />`), with no `level` prop. Sections sit inside a detail panel whose title is always an `h2` ([DetailHeader](../patterns/detail-header.md)), so `h3` is the level the commonest use needs; `render` is the contract's one way to swap an element, as EmptyState's title is swapped, and a `level` prop would be a second way.
- Section wraps its `children` in a `content` part, rather than laying them straight into the root. The root's gap then sits once between the header and the content, however many children the caller gives, and the content's own layout (a list, a grid, a run of paragraphs) stays the caller's, with `slotProps.content` to reach it.

## Base UI parts

No Base UI component: each part renders through the `useRender` hook from `@base-ui/react/use-render`, and merges its props with `mergeProps` from `@base-ui/react/merge-props`, at the version pinned in `packages/perron/package.json` (1.9.0). `baseUiParts` stays empty in `packages/perron/components.json`.

| Base UI part            | Renders   | Perron sets                                                                                                                                        | Passed through                                                            |
| ----------------------- | --------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `useRender` for root    | `section` | `defaultTagName: 'section'`, `ref`, the class `pn-Section`, `aria-labelledby` with the title's `id` (CR-2), and the header and content as children | `render`, `className`, `style`, `ref` and the rest of the `section` props |
| `useRender` for header  | `div`     | `defaultTagName: 'div'`, the class `pn-Section-header`, the title and action as children                                                           | `slotProps.header`                                                        |
| `useRender` for title   | `h3`      | `defaultTagName: 'h3'`, the class `pn-Section-title`, `id` (`slotProps.title.id`, else one from React's `useId`), `title` as children              | `slotProps.title`, its `render` changing the heading's level              |
| `useRender` for action  | `div`     | `defaultTagName: 'div'`, the class `pn-Section-action`, `action` as children; left out when `action` renders nothing (CR-1)                        | `slotProps.action`                                                        |
| `useRender` for content | `div`     | `defaultTagName: 'div'`, the class `pn-Section-content`, `children` as children; left out when `children` renders nothing (CR-1)                   | `slotProps.content`                                                       |

Base UI already does: swapping each part's element through `render` while keeping its class and props, joining `className` strings and `style` objects and chaining event handlers in `mergeProps`, setting `ref` on the rendered element, and rendering nothing for a part whose `enabled` is `false`.

## Props

In MUI's layout. Every prop here gets this description as its JSDoc. Slots come last.

| Name                | Type                              | Default | Base UI prop            | Description                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------- | ------- | ----------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `title`             | `ReactNode`                       |         | none                    | What the section is about, in a word or two and in sentence case: "Departures". Set in capitals by the style; it names the section for screen readers. Required. Replaces the HTML `title` attribute |
| `children`          | `ReactNode`                       |         | none                    | The section's content, below the title                                                                                                                                                               |
| `action`            | `ReactNode`                       |         | none                    | One small action at the end of the header, such as a small `outline` LinkButton to everything the section lists                                                                                      |
| `render`            | Base UI's `render`                |         | inherited               | Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render.            |
| `className`         | `string`                          |         | none                    | Joined after `pn-Section` on the root                                                                                                                                                                |
| `style`             | `CSSProperties`                   |         | none                    | Reaches the root                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `ref`               | `Ref<HTMLElement>`                |         | none                    | Reaches the root element, whichever element `render` makes it                                                                                                                                        |
| `slotProps.header`  | `useRender.ComponentProps<'div'>` |         | `useRender` for header  | Props for the `header` part                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `slotProps.title`   | `useRender.ComponentProps<'h3'>`  |         | `useRender` for title   | Props for the `title` part. Its `render` changes the heading's level, `render: <h2 />`, and its `id` is the one the root's `aria-labelledby` points at                                               |
| `slotProps.action`  | `useRender.ComponentProps<'div'>` |         | `useRender` for action  | Props for the `action` part                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `slotProps.content` | `useRender.ComponentProps<'div'>` |         | `useRender` for content | Props for the `content` part                                                                                                                                                                         |

`render`, `className`, `style`, `ref` and the other `section` props reach the root, as the contract's Root section says; `render` is inherited from `useRender.ComponentProps<'section'>` as it is, with Base UI's JSDoc, and `SectionProps` does not declare it again. `title` and `children` are left out of the inherited props and declared again, as EmptyState does. No owned string, so no `*Label` prop. The names `title` and `action` are MUI's (`CardHeader`) and EmptyState's, and none of the names is one the contract's [Names from other libraries](README.md#names-from-other-libraries) table bans.

- Section takes an `action`, one node at the end of its header. A list in a panel often leads to the whole of itself ("All departures", "Show on map"), and a slot keeps that link beside the heading it belongs to, aligned the same way in every section, where a caller's own row would differ from one screen to the next.
- Section ships with no `variant`, `size` or `color`, one look everywhere. The uses known now (the groups of a stop, line or vehicle panel, a settings sheet) share one heading style, `typography.overline` has one size, and any of the three can join later as an optional prop without a break.

## Tokens

One row per part, state and property. Section has no interactive state of its own, so every row is rest; the caller's action and content keep their own states.

| Part      | State | Property         | Token                                                             |
| --------- | ----- | ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `root`    | rest  | `gap`            | `space.300`                                                       |
| `header`  | rest  | `gap`            | `space.200`                                                       |
| `title`   | rest  | `font`           | `typography.overline`                                             |
| `title`   | rest  | `letter-spacing` | `typography.overline`, its tracking                               |
| `title`   | rest  | `color`          | `color.text.secondary`                                            |
| `title`   | rest  | `text-transform` | none: the keyword `uppercase`, as the role's class sets it (CR-7) |
| `action`  | rest  | `gap`            | `space.200`                                                       |
| `content` | rest  | none             | none: the content's look and layout are the caller's              |

The root is a flex column; the header is a flex row that wraps, its items centred on the cross axis, the title growing and the action keeping its size at the inline end; the action is a flex row that wraps. Every part resets the browser's margins to 0 and adds none of its own, so the `h3` brings no browser margin and the caller spaces sections.

- The title is `typography.overline` in `color.text.secondary`. The role's own use is "Section headings and tags, set in capitals"; its 11 px semibold capitals sit under a panel's `heading-md` title and above `label` rows without competing with either, and `color.text.secondary` reaches 4.5:1 on every opaque surface in both themes (6.77:1 at its lowest in light, on `color.surface.inset`, and 5.71:1 in dark, on [Accessibility](../foundations/accessibility.md#text-on-surfaces)), where `color.text.primary` would make every group heading as loud as the rows under it.
- The header and the content are `space.300` apart, and the title and the action `space.200`. [Semantic spacing](../foundations/semantic-spacing.md#space) sets the parts of a detail panel 12 px apart and the blocks of a pane 24 px apart, so a heading sits nearer its own content than the section before it, which reads as belonging to what follows. The header is as tall as its tallest item, with the title centred in it: with no action the header is the title's own line, 12 px above the content, and beside a small LinkButton (`size.button-sm`, 30 px) the header is 30 px tall and the title's text sits about 20 px above the content. The 8 px between title and action is the gap the components use between items in a row, such as EmptyState's actions.
- Section draws no surface, divider or padding of its own, and adds no margin, so sections take the panel's surface and the caller spaces them. It is content, not a card: a box of its own would join no family and stack a box inside the panel's, a box is Surface's job ([Surface](surface.md)) and a caller wraps a section in one when it needs one; the space between sections, `space.600` for blocks of a pane, is the caller's layout, as the contract has components size to their container.

## Keyboard and ARIA

Section has no keys of its own and is never focusable. The caller's action, then the caller's content, are reached in reading order.

| Key         | Does                                                                               | From        |
| ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------- |
| `Tab`       | Moves to the first focusable element in the action, then on into the content       | The browser |
| `Shift+Tab` | Moves back through the content and the action, out to what came before the Section | The browser |

| Element   | Role                                                                                       | Accessible name from                                     | States announced |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------- |
| `root`    | `region`, from a `section` with an accessible name; generic when `render` makes it a `div` | `aria-labelledby`, the title's `id`: its text            | None             |
| `header`  | None (generic `div`)                                                                       | None                                                     | None             |
| `title`   | `heading`, level 3, or the level `slotProps.title.render` gives                            | Its text, from `title`, read as written in sentence case | None             |
| `action`  | None (generic `div`); the caller's controls carry their own roles                          | The caller's controls' own names                         | Theirs           |
| `content` | None (generic `div`); the caller's content carries its own roles                           | None                                                     | None             |

What axe won't catch, from the contract, each with how this component meets it:

- [ ] Everything the eye is told, the ear is told, for every shape each prop accepts: the eye gets a grouping under a heading, and the ear the same heading and a region named by it; the capitals are style over sentence-case text (CR-7), so a screen reader reads the word, not its letters.
- [ ] Every landmark and named region has an accessible name: the root is a `section` named by its own title through `aria-labelledby` (CR-2), and the `Default` story's `play` checks the region's name.
- [ ] Every default label can be overridden: none here; Section owns no string.
- [ ] Every shape the type accepts renders, in every variant: `title`, `action` and `children` each render a string, an element and an array; the title is a heading, so it takes phrasing content, and `content` and `action` are `div`s, so block content such as a list is valid inside them.
- [ ] A hidden copy kept for animation is `aria-hidden`, and a collapsed region is `inert`: none here; nothing animates or collapses.
- [ ] Native semantics first: a native `section` and `h3`, with `aria-labelledby` the only ARIA, naming the region from the heading that is already there; the action holds the caller's own `a href` or `button`.
- [ ] Focus moves in reading order and returns on close: the title, the action and the content follow each other in the DOM as on screen, including when the header wraps (CR-6); Section never moves focus, and nothing in it closes.
- [ ] Every target is at least `size.target-min` square: Section has no target of its own; the action's targets are the caller's components, which keep their own sizes (a small LinkButton is `size.button-sm`).
- [ ] Loops stop when the system asks for less motion: none here; nothing moves.

## Owned strings

No owned strings: every word Section shows or announces comes from the caller, through `title`, `action` and `children`, and the region's name is the title.

## Component rules

Rules for this component alone, numbered so the build and the review can cite them.

- **CR-1.** The optional parts render only when given: no `action` part without `action`, no `content` part without `children`. A value that renders nothing (`null`, `undefined`, a boolean, `''`, or an array of only such values) counts as not given, so no empty wrapper takes up a gap. The root, the header and the title always render: `title` is required.
- **CR-2.** The title's `id` is `slotProps.title.id` when given, else one from React's `useId`, and the root's `aria-labelledby` is set to it after the caller's rest props, so the region is always named by its own heading.
- **CR-3.** `title`, `action`, `children`, `slotProps` and `render` are taken out of the rest props before they reach the root, so the HTML `title` attribute never reaches the element and a hover tooltip never repeats the heading.
- **CR-4.** Each inner part's props are its `slotProps` value merged with `mergeProps`, the component's own props last, so its class, `id` and children stay while the caller's `className` joins and its `render` swaps the element, such as the title's heading level. An element given as `render` is merged over all of these, as Base UI's `useRender` merges its element's own props last, so the element carries no `id` or children of its own: an `id` on it replaces the title's, and the root's `aria-labelledby` then points at nothing.
- **CR-5.** Section sets no `background`, `border`, `padding`, `box-shadow`, `inline-size` or `max-inline-size`, and every part sets `margin: 0`, resetting the browser's margins and adding none of its own: it sizes to its container on the surface it sits on, and the space between sections is the caller's.
- **CR-6.** The header wraps: the title grows to fill its line and the action keeps its own size at the inline end (`margin-inline-start: auto`). When the title's text and the action don't fit on one line together, the action moves onto its own line below the title, still at the inline end and in the same reading order, so beside "Driftsforstyrrelser" on a 320 px screen the action sits under the title. The title can shrink below its longest word (`min-inline-size: 0`) and breaks a word longer than its line (`overflow-wrap: anywhere`), so a single long word never overflows the section.
- **CR-7.** The title sets `text-transform: uppercase`, as the `perron-typography-overline` class does; the source text stays in sentence case, as content design asks, and the DOM and the region's name keep it.
- **CR-8.** Section never sets `overflow`, so a focused child's ring, drawn `focus.offset` outside it, is never cut at the edge.
- **CR-9.** Section never moves focus, sets no `tabindex` and adds no role beyond its native elements.

## Stories

One per variant and state the design would show. The design is deferred and has no variant property, so its one variant is `Default`; `TitleOnly` is the same variant with the optional props left out, and proves CR-1; `HeadingLevel` is the same variant with the title's level changed, and proves CR-4. Each sits on a `raised` Surface, as a section sits in a panel.

| Story          | Shows                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | `play` test                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| -------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Default`      | Every part: `title` "Departures", `action` a small `outline` LinkButton "All departures" with an `href`, and `children` a list of three departures, such as "5C Husum Torv 08:14", at rest. The subject story: its args render Section alone and pass every rule | A `region` named "Departures" holds a heading of level 3 named "Departures"; the title's computed `text-transform` is `uppercase` while its DOM text is the sentence case; Tab reaches "All departures" and Shift+Tab leaves it, so focus ends where it started |
| `TitleOnly`    | `title` "Lines here" and `children` a sentence, with no action                                                                                                                                                                                                   | No `pn-Section-action` element renders; the `pn-Section-content` part holds the sentence; nothing in the section takes focus                                                                                                                                    |
| `HeadingLevel` | `title` "Planned works", `slotProps.title.render` an `h2`, and `children` a sentence about planned works on a line                                                                                                                                               | The title is a heading of level 2 that keeps `pn-Section-title`, and the `region` is still named "Planned works"                                                                                                                                                |

## Do and don't

For a caller using the component, with the reason.

| Do                                                                                                                                               | Don't                                                                                                                                 |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Write the title in sentence case, a word or two, and let the style set the capitals: "Departures"                                                | Type the title in capitals: a screen reader may spell it out letter by letter, and content design writes source text in sentence case |
| Give the title the level that fits the page's outline through `slotProps.title.render`: `h3` under a panel's `h2`, `h4` inside an `h3`'s section | Skip a level, or wrap a heading element inside `title`: the part is already a heading, and a heading inside a heading is invalid      |
| Put one small, neutral action in the header, such as a small `outline` LinkButton to the whole list                                              | Put the panel's main action, or a `brand` button, in a section's header: a screen has one brand action, and it belongs to the panel   |
| Space sections apart in the caller's layout, `space.600` between blocks of a pane                                                                | Add margins or padding to Section with raw values, or rely on it for the space between sections: it adds none                         |
| Wrap a section in a Surface when it needs a card or a box of its own                                                                             | Add a fill, border or shadow to Section through `className`: a box is Surface's job, and the ladder lives there                       |
| Render the root as a `div` through `render` when the group is too small to be worth a region of its own                                          | Leave a screen full of tiny named regions: a screen reader's landmark list then says less than its headings                           |
| Leave a group that opens and closes to a collapsible component, built on Base UI's Collapsible                                                   | Build a collapsible group from Section by hiding its content: it brings no button, state or keys                                      |
| Set the title's `id` through `slotProps.title.id`                                                                                                | Put an `id` on the element in `slotProps.title.render`: it replaces the generated one and the region loses its name                   |

title: Separator
markdown:
# Separator

A hairline that divides two groups of content, across a column (horizontal) or down a row (vertical), and tells a screen reader there is a break there.

<!-- run notes -->

The design is deferred (ADR 0010, `docs/adr/0010-unattended-runs-with-design-deferred.md`): there is no read-back, code map or export, and this spec decides what the drawing would, from the [contract](README.md), the [foundations](../foundations/README.md), the tokens, the Base UI reference for `Separator` (`@base-ui/react` 1.9.0, installed) and the three separators already merged, [Toolbar](toolbar.md)'s `ToolbarSeparator`, [Select](select.md)'s separator between groups and [Menu](menu.md)'s `MenuSeparator`, whose line it shares. Its registry entry has no `dependsOn`. No ROADMAP line names Separator, and the extracted prototype component is not in any branch this run can reach, so nothing here rests on it. The factory's brief for this slot put it in the Layout category, asked for a minimal API, and asked the spec to say whether the merged separators should later render it (CR-8).

## Anatomy

Penpot page `Components/Separator`. Family: none: the contract's [Families](README.md#families) have no divider of its own, and the line is the one the Rows family divides rows with, `border.width.025` in `color.border.subtle`. Shared parts: none.

The drawing has one board, `root`, a line with no content. Its one variant property is `orientation`, with the values `horizontal` and `vertical`, so its variants are `Horizontal` and `Vertical`. It has no `State` property: a separator is never interactive (CR-6) and has only its rest state.

| Part (Penpot layer) | What it is                                                                                                                                                         | Base UI part | Class          | `slotProps` key |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------ | -------------- | --------------- |
| `root`              | The line: a `<div role="separator">` of no size, drawn by one border, running across its container's width when horizontal and down its row's height when vertical | `Separator`  | `pn-Separator` | none            |

## Base UI parts

Imported from `@base-ui/react/separator`, at the version pinned in `packages/perron/package.json` (1.9.0).

| Base UI part | Renders                                                                                                           | Perron sets                                            | Passed through                                                                                                    |
| ------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Separator`  | `<div role="separator" aria-orientation>`, with `data-orientation`, its `orientation` (`'horizontal'` by default) | `className` (`pn-Separator`, then the caller's), `ref` | `orientation`, `render`, `style`, `id`, `data-*`, `aria-*` and every other `<div>` attribute, through `{...rest}` |

Base UI already does: the `separator` role and `aria-orientation` from `orientation`, set before the caller's props so nothing Perron writes is needed for the ear; `data-orientation` for the CSS; no `tabIndex`, so the separator is not a tab stop; swapping the element for the `render` element or function while keeping the role, the class and the data attribute.

## Props

In MUI's layout. Every prop here gets this description as its JSDoc. No slots: the separator has no inner part.

| Name          | Type                         | Default        | Base UI prop | Description                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ------------- | ---------------------------- | -------------- | ------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `orientation` | `'horizontal' \| 'vertical'` | `'horizontal'` | inherited    | The orientation of the separator.                                                                                                                                                         |
| `render`      | Base UI's `render`           |                | inherited    | Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render. |
| `className`   | `string`                     |                | none         | Joined after `pn-Separator` on the root                                                                                                                                                   |
| `style`       | `CSSProperties`              |                | none         | Reaches the root                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `ref`         | `Ref<HTMLDivElement>`        |                | none         | Reaches the root, the `role="separator"` element                                                                                                                                          |

`SeparatorProps` extends Base UI's `Separator.Props` without its `className`, `style`, `children` and `ref`, as `ToolbarSeparatorProps` does, and declares `className`, `style` and `ref` as React's; `orientation` and `render` are inherited as they are, with Base UI's JSDoc and `@default`, and `SeparatorProps` declares neither. It takes no `children` (CR-5). No `*Label` props: Separator owns no strings.

Separator ships one look, with no `variant`, `color`, `size` or inset prop. The API stays minimal; every divider Perron draws today, ToolbarSeparator's, Select's and MenuSeparator's, is the same hairline in the same colour, `color.border.subtle` is the one colour [Semantic colours](../foundations/semantic-colours.md#borders) gives dividers, and a line that only decorates carries no meaning an intent could add. An inset, as MUI's `variant="middle"`, is the container's padding; the props API only grows, so any of these can join later as an optional prop.

Separator is always announced as a separator, with no `decorative` prop that swaps its role for `none`. Base UI's `Separator` always sets `role="separator"`, and a caller's `role="none"` would leave its `aria-orientation` on an element with no role, which axe's `aria-allowed-attr` fails; a break the eye is shown is a break the ear is told, as the contract's checklist asks; and a line that is only decoration, such as a panel's edge, is that element's own border, not a Separator.

## Tokens

One row per part, state and property. Separator has one part, `root`, and one design state, rest (CR-6). The line is a border on a box of no size, never a background, so forced colours keep it (CR-3), and its colour is a token [Semantic colours](../foundations/semantic-colours.md#borders) gives for both themes, so it needs no rule for the dark theme. `color.border.subtle` is exempt from the 3:1 non-text contrast, as a line that decorates ([Accessibility](../foundations/accessibility.md#what-the-build-checks)): the separator's meaning reaches the ear through its role, not the eye through its contrast.

| Part               | State                | Property              | Token                                                                                                                         |
| ------------------ | -------------------- | --------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `root`, horizontal | rest                 | `border-block-start`  | `border.width.025` solid in `color.border.subtle`                                                                             |
| `root`, vertical   | rest                 | `border-inline-start` | `border.width.025` solid in `color.border.subtle`                                                                             |
| `root`             | rest                 | `flex`                | none: the keyword `none`, so a flex container never squeezes the line away                                                    |
| `root`             | rest                 | `align-self`          | none: the keyword `stretch`, so a vertical line takes its row's height and a horizontal one its column's width                |
| `root`             | rest                 | `margin`              | none: `0`, the space on either side of the line coming from its container                                                     |
| `root`             | rest                 | `border`              | none: `0`, set before the orientation's side, so a `render={<hr />}` drops the user agent's inset border                      |
| `root`, either     | rest, forced colours | `border`              | none: the same border, which Windows' contrast themes paint in the text colour, so the line stays where every fill is dropped |

Separator takes no margin of its own, leaving the space on either side of the line to its container's `gap` or padding. A component sizes to its container and the screen or pattern that uses it places it, as Toolbar's CR-13 says of the bar; the three merged separators get their space from where they sit, ToolbarSeparator from the bar's `space.100` gap, and Select's and MenuSeparator from `space.100` set on their own classes inside the list and the popup; and a margin on Separator would add to every container's `gap`, doubling the space in a flex column that already has one. A caller wanting Select's spacing gives the container `gap: var(--perron-space-100)`.

## Keyboard and ARIA

From the Base UI reference for `Separator` and the installed `Separator.js`. "From" says who does it.

No keys: the separator is not focusable and does nothing (CR-6).

| Element | Role                      | Accessible name from                                  | States announced                                   |
| ------- | ------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `root`  | `separator`, from Base UI | none: a separator that is not focusable needs no name | `aria-orientation`, from `orientation`, by Base UI |

What axe won't catch, from the contract, each with how this component meets it:

- [ ] Everything the eye is told, the ear is told, for every shape each prop accepts: the line the eye sees is the `separator` role the ear is told, in both orientations, with `aria-orientation` saying which.
- [ ] Every landmark and named region has an accessible name: none here; a separator is neither.
- [ ] Every default label can be overridden: none here; Separator owns no strings.
- [ ] Every shape the type accepts renders, in every variant: both `orientation` values draw the line on their side; Separator takes no `ReactNode` prop.
- [ ] A hidden copy kept for animation is `aria-hidden`, and a collapsed region is `inert`: none here; nothing animates or collapses.
- [ ] Native semantics first: Base UI renders a `<div>` with the `separator` role, the role an `<hr>` gives natively, and `render={<hr />}` stays open to a caller who wants the native element, drawn the same (CR-3); no other ARIA.
- [ ] Focus moves in reading order and returns on close: the separator is never a tab stop, so Tab passes from the content before it to the content after it.
- [ ] Every target is at least `size.target-min` square: none here; the separator is not a target.
- [ ] Loops stop when the system asks for less motion: none here; nothing moves.

## Owned strings

No owned strings: the separator shows and announces no words, only its role.

## Component rules

- **CR-1.** The root is Base UI's `Separator` from `@base-ui/react/separator`, which sets `role="separator"`, `aria-orientation` and `data-orientation` from `orientation`. Separator sets none of the three itself, and passes `orientation` through `{...rest}` untouched, so Base UI's default, `'horizontal'`, holds.
- **CR-2.** `{...rest}` comes first, then `ref`, then `className` from the shared `classes` helper in `packages/perron/src/internal/nodes.ts`: `pn-Separator` first, then the caller's.
- **CR-3.** The line is drawn as one border on a box of no size: `.pn-Separator` clears every border with `border: 0`, so an `<hr>` from `render` keeps none of the user agent's, then `border-block-start` on `.pn-Separator[data-orientation='horizontal']`, `border-inline-start` on `.pn-Separator[data-orientation='vertical']`, as ToolbarSeparator's CR-11 draws its own, never as a background or a `block-size` of `border.width.025`, which forced colours would drop.
- **CR-4.** The root sets `flex: none`, `align-self: stretch` and `margin: 0`, and no size of its own, its spacing coming from its container's `gap` or padding (Tokens), so a vertical separator in a flex row is as tall as the row and a horizontal one in a block or a flex column is as wide as its container. A vertical separator outside a flex or grid row, and a horizontal one inside a flex row, have no length and draw nothing; the stories and Do and don't show the right container.
- **CR-5.** `SeparatorProps` omits `children`, so a caller can't put words in the line: the `separator` role makes its children presentational, and a labelled break, such as "Earlier today", is a heading, which a screen reader can move to.
- **CR-6.** Separator is never interactive: no `tabIndex`, no handler, no hover, focus or pressed look, and no cursor. A focusable separator is ARIA's window splitter, which takes a value and arrow keys, and is a component of its own if a screen needs one.
- **CR-7.** The line's two tokens, `border.width.025` and `color.border.subtle`, are the ones `ToolbarSeparator`, Select's separator and `MenuSeparator` draw with, so the four dividers look alike in both themes. A change to one is a change to all four, in the same pull request.
- **CR-8.** ToolbarSeparator, Select's separator and MenuSeparator keep their own Base UI parts and never render Separator, with no follow-up change. `Toolbar.Separator` reads the toolbar's context to run across the bar's orientation, which Separator can't; Select's separator is Base UI's `Select.Separator`, a `role="presentation"` inside a `listbox`, where a `separator` role is not an allowed child and axe's `aria-required-children` fails; and MenuSeparator is Base UI's `Menu.Separator`, the same Base UI `Separator` under the menu's name, kept as its own component because its look is the menu's: it leaves out `orientation`, a menu being a column, and its margins run it across the popup's padding to its edge with `space.100` above and below, where Separator takes no margin. Each keeps its Base UI part and its own class, and shares Separator's look through CR-7; Separator is for content outside those three, such as between a panel's facts and its actions.
- **CR-9.** Separator has one look and one role: `SeparatorProps` declares no `variant`, `color`, `size`, inset or `decorative` prop (Props), and Separator sets no `role` of its own, so Base UI's `separator` is the one it announces.

## Stories

One per variant the drawing has, `Horizontal` and `Vertical`. Each story's `render` places the separator between two short lines of text in the container its orientation needs (CR-4), set in `typography.body` with the shared `typography` helper; the args hold only `orientation`, so the contract story renders the separator alone.

| Story        | Shows                                                                                                                                                              | `play` test                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `Horizontal` | `orientation: 'horizontal'`, the default, between "Line 5C to Husum Torv" and "Next departure in 4 min" in a flex column with a `space.100` gap; the subject story | The root has the `separator` role and `aria-orientation="horizontal"`, `pn-Separator` and `data-orientation="horizontal"`; its `border-block-start` renders as `border.width.025` in `color.border.subtle` (`resolve`, `colour`) and it has no other border; it is as wide as its column; it has no `tabindex`, and `focus()` on it leaves `document.activeElement` where it was; a `render={<hr />}` mounted in the column is an `<hr>` with the same one border, none of the user agent's, and `border.width.025` tall |
| `Vertical`   | `orientation: 'vertical'` between "Bus" and "Metro" in a flex row with a `space.100` gap                                                                           | The root has `aria-orientation="vertical"` and `data-orientation="vertical"`; its `border-inline-start` renders as `border.width.025` in `color.border.subtle`; it is as tall as the row and `border.width.025` wide                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |

## Do and don't

For a caller using the component, with the reason.

| Do                                                                                                                                                           | Don't                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Put a Separator where two groups of content meet and the layout doesn't already set them apart, such as between a vehicle's facts and its actions in a panel | Put one between every row of a list or after every paragraph: the interface around the map stays calm, and white space sets most things apart without a line                        |
| Space the line with its container's `gap` or padding, from the `space.*` scale                                                                               | Give the separator a margin of its own: it adds to the container's gap, and two screens end up with two spacings                                                                    |
| Put a vertical Separator in a flex row, and a horizontal one in a block or a flex column, so the line runs the container's length                            | Put a vertical one in block flow or a horizontal one in a flex row, where it has no length and draws nothing                                                                        |
| Use `ToolbarSeparator` inside a `Toolbar` and `MenuSeparator` inside a `Menu`, and let Select draw its own between groups                                    | Put a Separator in a toolbar, where it doesn't run across the bar, in a menu, where it isn't the menu's own part, or in a list, where a `separator` is not a listbox's child (CR-8) |
| Give a break that needs words a heading                                                                                                                      | Put text in the separator, or swap its role for `none` to hide it: a break the eye sees is one the ear is told                                                                      |
| Draw a panel's or card's edge with its own border                                                                                                            | Use a Separator as an element's edge: it announces a break between two groups, which an edge is not                                                                                 |

title: Surface
markdown:
# Surface

A box that sets content on one step of the surface ladder: glass or an opaque panel floating over the map, a raised card inside a panel, or an inset box, each with its fill, edge, radius, shadow and padding from the tokens.

## Anatomy

Penpot page `Components/Surface`. Family: none. Shared parts: none.

The design is deferred (ADR 0010, `docs/adr/0010-unattended-runs-with-design-deferred.md`), so this spec decides the drawing: the layers below are the ones the drawing will name, and the variants are the steps of the surface ladder on [Elevation](../foundations/elevation.md#surfaces). Surface has no Base UI part: it is a box with no behaviour, so its root renders through Base UI's `useRender` hook (`@base-ui/react/use-render`), which gives it the `render` prop.

Surface is not one of the contract's [families](README.md#families): it is the box the ladder is drawn on, which patterns such as a detail panel or a disruption card compose. Its `glass` variant draws the Panels row's treatment (the Popups' glass, `radius.xl`), so a panel a pattern builds from it matches the Dialog and Sheet beside it.

| Part (Penpot layer) | What it is                                                                                                                                       | Base UI part                            | Class        | `slotProps` key |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------- | ------------ | --------------- |
| `root`              | The box: a `<div>` with the variant's fill, edge, radius, shadow and padding, holding the caller's content. Penpot's main instance, a flex board | none: a `<div>` rendered by `useRender` | `pn-Surface` | none            |

The content is the caller's: Surface draws no heading, divider or inner part, so the drawing's one layer is `root`, holding a placeholder content slot that the code map does not map to a part.

Surface's one Penpot variant property is `variant`, with the values `raised`, `inset`, `glass` and `opaque` in that order, so `raised` is the default (the contract's first value), and the variants are `Raised`, `Inset`, `Glass` and `Opaque`. They are the four steps of [Elevation](../foundations/elevation.md#surfaces) a box sits on, named by what they look like rather than by their token (`overlay` and `default` would collide with the floating-panel words and with Penpot's `State` value `default`); `raised` comes first because cards inside a panel are the commonest box, and a floating panel is usually a pattern that chooses `glass` on purpose. `color.surface.hover`, `selected`, `inverse` and the tinted intent surfaces are state layers, buttons and messages, not boxes, so they are not variants.

## Base UI parts

Surface imports no Base UI component. It uses two Base UI utilities, at the version pinned in `package.json`: `useRender` (`@base-ui/react/use-render`) for the root and `mergeProps` (`@base-ui/react/merge-props`) to merge the caller's props with its own.

| Base UI part                     | Renders | Perron sets                                                                                                              | Passed through                                                    |
| -------------------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `useRender` (a hook, not a part) | `<div>` | `defaultTagName: 'div'`, `className` (`pn-Surface` first, then the caller's), `data-variant` from `variant` (CR-1, CR-2) | `render`, `ref`, `children`, `className`, `style`, the rest props |

Base UI already does: swapping the root element for the one `render` gives, keeping the class and data attribute; merging the caller's `ref` with the element's; and merging event handlers, `className` and `style` through `mergeProps`.

Surface renders a `<div>` by default, with no role, and leaves a landmark or region to the caller through `render` (`render={<section aria-labelledby="…" />}`, `<aside>`, `<article>`). Most surfaces are cards and boxes inside a panel, which are not landmarks; a `<section>` or `<aside>` by default would add an unnamed region to every card, and the contract asks every landmark and named region for a name only the caller's heading can give.

## Props

In MUI's layout. Every prop Surface declares gets this description as its JSDoc. It declares `variant`, `children`, `className`, `style` and `ref`, and inherits `render` from `useRender`'s props type as it is, with Base UI's description; a caller renders it as `<section>` or `<aside>` with `aria-labelledby` for a named region. Surface has no `slotProps`, because the contract keys `slotProps` by inner Base UI part and Surface has none; a caller restyles it through `className` on the root.

| Name                 | Type                                         | Default    | Base UI prop         | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| -------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | ---------- | -------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `variant`            | `'raised' \| 'inset' \| 'glass' \| 'opaque'` | `'raised'` | none                 | The step of the surface ladder: `raised` for a card inside a panel, `inset` for a box or track set into one, `glass` for a panel floating over the map, `opaque` for a floating panel full of text on a phone, where glass would let the map show through. |
| `render`             | Base UI's `render`                           |            | inherited            | Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render.                                                                  |
| `children`           | `ReactNode`                                  |            | none                 | The content the surface holds                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `className`, `style` | React's                                      |            | through `mergeProps` | Reaches the root; `className` is merged after `pn-Surface`                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `ref`                | `Ref<HTMLElement>`                           |            | `useRender`'s `ref`  | Reaches the root element, whichever element `render` makes it                                                                                                                                                                                              |

No `size`: padding follows the variant (see [Tokens](#tokens)). No label props: Surface owns no strings.

Surface has no `color`, so no variant is tinted with an intent's surface (`color.surface.success` and the rest). A tinted box says something only colour tells, and colour is never alone ([Accessibility](../foundations/accessibility.md#rules)): a status surface belongs to a component that also gives the word or icon, such as a notice, which can add the tints then. `color` can join Surface later without a break.

## Tokens

Surface is not interactive, so its one design state is rest; each row names the `variant` it applies to. Every variant has the same edge width, so the four share one geometry and swapping variants never shifts the content.

Each variant takes the treatment below: `raised` a `color.surface.raised` card with a `color.border.subtle` edge, `radius.lg` and no shadow; `inset` a `color.surface.inset` box with a transparent edge and `radius.lg`; `glass` the Panels' glass (`color.surface.overlay`, the glass blur and saturation, a `color.border.subtle` edge, `shadow.panel`) at `radius.xl`; and `opaque` the same as glass with `color.surface.default` and no blur. It is [Elevation](../foundations/elevation.md) and [Semantic spacing](../foundations/semantic-spacing.md) as written: floating panels are glass with `shadow.panel` and `radius.xl`, and on phones opaque; cards and inset boxes take `radius.lg`; card and panel edges are `border.width.025` in `color.border.subtle`; an inset box reads without a border; and nothing else casts a shadow.

Surface pads its content by variant, `space.400` for `glass` and `opaque` and `space.300` for `raised` and `inset`, with no prop to change it, so a caller who needs another inset (rows running to the edge, a flush image) sets `padding` through `className` with a `space.*` token. A box with no padding is never used as it comes, and a padding prop would grow a scale before any caller needs one; `space.300` is the gap between parts of a detail panel, and a floating panel one step wider sets its blocks off from the map. A `padding` prop can join later without a break.

| Part   | State                    | Property           | Token                                                                                                                                  |
| ------ | ------------------------ | ------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `root` | rest, every `variant`    | `color`            | `color.text.primary`                                                                                                                   |
| `root` | rest, every `variant`    | `border-width`     | `border.width.025`                                                                                                                     |
| `root` | rest, every `variant`    | `border-style`     | none: the keyword `solid`                                                                                                              |
| `root` | rest, `variant='raised'` | `background-color` | `color.surface.raised`                                                                                                                 |
| `root` | rest, `variant='raised'` | `border-color`     | `color.border.subtle`                                                                                                                  |
| `root` | rest, `variant='raised'` | `border-radius`    | `radius.lg`                                                                                                                            |
| `root` | rest, `variant='raised'` | `padding`          | `space.300`                                                                                                                            |
| `root` | rest, `variant='raised'` | `box-shadow`       | none: the keyword `none`                                                                                                               |
| `root` | rest, `variant='inset'`  | `background-color` | `color.surface.inset`                                                                                                                  |
| `root` | rest, `variant='inset'`  | `border-color`     | none: the keyword `transparent`, so the edge shows only in forced colours (CR-5)                                                       |
| `root` | rest, `variant='inset'`  | `border-radius`    | `radius.lg`                                                                                                                            |
| `root` | rest, `variant='inset'`  | `padding`          | `space.300`                                                                                                                            |
| `root` | rest, `variant='inset'`  | `box-shadow`       | none: the keyword `none`                                                                                                               |
| `root` | rest, `variant='glass'`  | `background-color` | `color.surface.overlay`                                                                                                                |
| `root` | rest, `variant='glass'`  | `backdrop-filter`  | `effect.glass-blur` and `effect.glass-saturate`: `blur(var(--perron-effect-glass-blur)) saturate(var(--perron-effect-glass-saturate))` |
| `root` | rest, `variant='glass'`  | `border-color`     | `color.border.subtle`                                                                                                                  |
| `root` | rest, `variant='glass'`  | `border-radius`    | `radius.xl`                                                                                                                            |
| `root` | rest, `variant='glass'`  | `padding`          | `space.400`                                                                                                                            |
| `root` | rest, `variant='glass'`  | `box-shadow`       | `shadow.panel`                                                                                                                         |
| `root` | rest, `variant='opaque'` | `background-color` | `color.surface.default`                                                                                                                |
| `root` | rest, `variant='opaque'` | `border-color`     | `color.border.subtle`                                                                                                                  |
| `root` | rest, `variant='opaque'` | `border-radius`    | `radius.xl`                                                                                                                            |
| `root` | rest, `variant='opaque'` | `padding`          | `space.400`                                                                                                                            |
| `root` | rest, `variant='opaque'` | `box-shadow`       | `shadow.panel`                                                                                                                         |

Every text colour reaches 4.5:1 on `color.surface.default`, `raised` and `inset` in both themes, as [Accessibility](../foundations/accessibility.md#text-on-surfaces) measures, except `color.text.tertiary`, which stays for hints beside stronger text. The build measures text on the three opaque surfaces only. `color.surface.overlay` is `color.surface.default`'s colour at 0.9 opacity in light and 0.88 in dark, behind the glass blur, so text on `glass` reads close to its contrast on `color.surface.default`.

## Keyboard and ARIA

Surface is a box: it takes no focus, and no key does anything. Focus moves through the caller's content in reading order. A caller who makes it a link or button through `render` brings that element's own keys.

| Key  | Does                                                          | From   |
| ---- | ------------------------------------------------------------- | ------ |
| none | Surface is not focusable or operable; Tab reaches its content | Perron |

| Element | Role                    | Accessible name from                                                                                                               | States announced |
| ------- | ----------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------- |
| `root`  | none: a generic `<div>` | Not named. Through `render`, a `<section>`, `<aside>` or `<article>` takes its name from the caller's heading by `aria-labelledby` | none             |

What axe won't catch, from the contract, each with how this component meets it:

- [ ] Everything the eye is told, the ear is told, for every shape each prop accepts: the surface tells the eye only grouping and depth, which the content's own headings and order tell the ear; Surface carries no colour that means a state (no `color` prop).
- [ ] Every landmark and named region has an accessible name: the root is a generic `<div>` and no landmark; a caller who renders it as `<section>`, `<aside>` or `<article>` names it with `aria-labelledby` pointing at its heading, as the `Nested` story shows.
- [ ] Every default label can be overridden: none here; Surface owns no label.
- [ ] Every shape the type accepts renders, in every variant: `children` as a string, an element and a list all render in each of the four variants, shown by the variant stories.
- [ ] A hidden copy kept for animation is `aria-hidden`, and a collapsed region is `inert`: none here; Surface does not animate or collapse.
- [ ] Native semantics first: a `<div>` with no role and no ARIA; the caller picks `<section>`, `<aside>` or `<article>` through `render` when the box is a region.
- [ ] Focus moves in reading order and returns on close: Surface takes no focus and does not reorder its content; it does not clip, so a focused child's ring shows in full (CR-4).
- [ ] Every target is at least `size.target-min` square: no target; Surface is not pressed.
- [ ] Loops stop when the system asks for less motion: none here; Surface has no motion.

## Owned strings

No owned strings: Surface shows and announces no words of its own; every word inside it is the caller's.

## Component rules

- **CR-1.** The root renders through `useRender` with `defaultTagName: 'div'` and `mergeProps`: Surface's own props (`className` starting with `pn-Surface`, `data-variant`) win over the caller's rest props, and `variant` is taken out of the rest before the merge, so it never reaches the DOM.
- **CR-2.** The root always carries `data-variant` with the `variant` value, `raised` by default, and the CSS reads the treatment from it: `.pn-Surface[data-variant='glass']`.
- **CR-3.** Surface sets no `display`, `inline-size`, `block-size`, `margin`, `gap` or typography: it is a block box that sizes to its container, and its content and the caller's layout decide the rest. It sets `color` to `color.text.primary` so content reads on every variant in both themes.
- **CR-4.** Surface never sets `overflow`: content stays unclipped, so a focused child's ring, drawn `focus.offset` outside it, is never cut at the edge. A caller who must clip (a scrolling panel body) does so on its own inner element.
- **CR-5.** Every variant has a `border.width.025` edge, `inset` a transparent one, so in `(forced-colors: active)`, where the system paints borders and drops shadows and translucent fills, every surface keeps a visible edge with no rule of its own.
- **CR-6.** `glass` is for a panel floating over the map. Surface has no breakpoint query, as the contract's [Media queries](README.md#media-queries) allow none: a caller whose panel fills with text on a phone chooses `opaque` there, as [Elevation](../foundations/elevation.md#surfaces) says.
- **CR-7.** Surfaces nest down the ladder: `raised` and `inset` sit inside `glass` or `opaque`, and `inset` inside `raised`. `glass` and `opaque` are never nested in another surface, and a `raised` or `inset` surface casts no shadow, since only floating panels do.

## Stories

No Penpot design yet, so the stories are named by the variant names the design will have: the `variant` value in PascalCase (the Conventions of `penpot/README.md`), and `Nested` shows the ladder together. Each `play` test reads the DOM and the accessibility tree, not the pixels.

| Story    | Shows                                                                                                                                               | `play` test                                                                                                                                                                        |
| -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Raised` | `variant='raised'`, a card holding a heading, a line of text and a Button, on `color.surface.default`                                               | The root is a `<div>` with `pn-Surface` and `data-variant='raised'`, no role and no name; Tab moves straight to the Button inside it                                               |
| `Inset`  | `variant='inset'`, a box holding a line of text, on `color.surface.raised`                                                                          | `data-variant` is `inset`                                                                                                                                                          |
| `Glass`  | `variant='glass'`, a panel holding a heading and text, over a busy coloured backdrop that shows the blur                                            | `data-variant` is `glass`                                                                                                                                                          |
| `Opaque` | `variant='opaque'`, the same panel over the same backdrop                                                                                           | `data-variant` is `opaque`                                                                                                                                                         |
| `Nested` | A `glass` panel rendered as `<section aria-labelledby>` with its heading, holding a `raised` card that holds an `inset` box, over the busy backdrop | The outer root is a `region` named by its heading, keeps `pn-Surface` and `data-variant='glass'`; the inner surfaces carry `raised` and `inset`; a `ref` on each lands on its root |

## Do and don't

For a caller using the component, with the reason.

| Do                                                                                                                         | Don't                                                                                                                                          |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Use `glass` for a panel that floats over the map, and `opaque` for one full of text on a phone, as Elevation says.         | Use `glass` over a plain background or inside another panel: the blur has nothing to soften, and glass on glass loses its edge.                |
| Put `raised` cards and `inset` boxes inside a panel, stepping down the ladder.                                             | Nest a floating `glass` or `opaque` surface inside another surface, or add a shadow to a card with `className`: only floating panels cast one. |
| Render it as `<section>` or `<aside>` with `aria-labelledby` on its heading when the box is a region someone navigates to. | Give every card a landmark element: a screen of unnamed regions is noisier than plain boxes.                                                   |
| Use Dialog or Sheet for a panel that opens and closes over the screen, since they bring the focus, Esc and scrim.          | Build a dialog from a `glass` Surface: it would look right and trap no focus.                                                                  |
| Say a state in words or with an icon inside the surface.                                                                   | Tint a surface with a status colour through `className` to mean warning or success: colour is never alone.                                     |
| Change the padding through `className` with a `space.*` token when rows must run to the edge.                              | Set raw pixel padding, radius or colours on it, which leave the ladder and the themes behind.                                                  |

It sets no outline, so `perron.css`'s focus ring shows on `:focus-visible`, and no `text-decoration-color`, so the underline follows the text's colour. - **CR-5.** The CSS reads only the component layer's [token families](README.md#token-families), with no `opacity`, no `text-transform`, no transition and no `[data-theme]` selector: the credits read in the case the caller wrote them, in both themes through the semantic tokens. - **CR-6.** Attribution places nothing: no `position`, `inset`, `z-index` or `margin`. The screen that holds the map puts it in a corner of the map with `size.panel-gap` from the edge and stacks it at `z-index.map-controls`, the pattern row's tokens, as [Layout](../foundations/layout.md#stacking) stacks it with the legend, the map controls and the scale. ## Stories One per variant the deferred design will draw. Attribution has no variant property, so its one variant is `Default`; `PlainText` and `Wrapping` are the same variant with other credits, and prove the shapes `children` takes and CR-3. Each sits on a `color.map.land` backdrop, so the glass is seen over what it sits on in Mylder. Each `play` test reads the DOM and the accessibility tree, not the pixels. | Story | Shows | `play` test | | ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `Default` | "Map data © OpenStreetMap contributors", with "OpenStreetMap contributors" a link to `https://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright`; the contract story renders it as the subject, and its args pass every rule alone | The root is a `` with `pn-Attribution`, no role, no ARIA attribute and no `data-*`; its accessible text is the whole credit; the link has the `link` role, its name "OpenStreetMap contributors", and a computed `text-decoration-line` of `underline`; Tab moves focus to the link and Shift+Tab back, and the root itself never takes focus | | `PlainText` | "Departures from Rejseplanen", a string with no link | The root's text is the string; nothing in it takes focus; the root's computed `color` is `color.text.secondary`'s | | `Wrapping` | Two credits, "Map data © OpenStreetMap contributors" and "Departures from Rejseplanen", each with its link, as a list of children in a 200 px wide column | The root wraps onto more than one line; it stays inside its column (its `scrollWidth` is no more than its `clientWidth`, and its right edge no further than the column's); both links are in the accessible text, in order | ## Do and don't For a caller using the component, with the reason. | Do | Don't | | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | | Credit each source as its terms ask, with a link to those terms: "Map data © OpenStreetMap contributors" | Shorten a credit a source's terms set, or leave the link out where the terms ask for one | | Place one Attribution in a corner of the map, `size.panel-gap` from the edge and stacked at `z-index.map-controls`, clear of the map controls and the scale | Put it in a panel, a dialog or the page's footer, away from the map it credits, or cover it with a sheet or a panel | | Give it phrasing content: text, links and inline elements | Put a heading, a paragraph or a list in it; a `` holds phrasing content only | | Write each link's text as the source's name or the credit itself | Write "Click here" or "Read more", or a bare URL; the link's text is what a screen reader hears | | Keep it to the credits | Use it for a disclaimer, a data-state note or a status message; a status belongs in words beside what it is about, in its own component, with its own colour |

# MapControls

The map's zoom in, zoom out and centre buttons, in one glass bar that is one tab stop, named and labelled in the reader's language.

<!-- run notes -->

The design is deferred (ADR 0010, `docs/adr/0010-unattended-runs-with-design-deferred.md`): there is no read-back, code map or export, and this spec decides what the drawing would, from the contract, the foundations, the tokens, the Base UI reference and the spec of [Toolbar](toolbar.md), the one entry it depends on, and of [IconButton](icon-button.md), which it does not use (see Anatomy). The extracted prototype component is not in any branch this run can reach.

## Anatomy

Penpot page `Components/MapControls`. Family: none (the contract's [Families](README.md#families) have no bar of actions; the bar is Toolbar's, on the Popups' glass). Shared parts: none (each button is an icon-only `ToolbarButton`, named by its `aria-label` from an owned string, as Toolbar's icon-only buttons are).
