| `TabDisabled` | A tab, disabled                                                                               | "Lines" has `aria-disabled` and `data-disabled`, the arrow keys still reach it, and a click or Enter doesn't select it or call `onChange`                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `Count`       | Three tabs with counts of 12, 0 and 2                                                         | Each tab's accessible name is its label, a space and its count ("Disruptions 2"), and the tab with `0` shows its count                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `Controlled`  | Tabs given `value` and `onChange` from the story's state                                      | A click on "Lines" calls `onChange` with `'lines'`; the panel changes only once the story sets `value`; setting `value` from outside moves the underline                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `Wrapping`    | Five tabs in a 320 px wide container                                                          | The tabs wrap onto a second row, the list doesn't scroll sideways (its `scrollWidth` equals its `clientWidth`), and the underline sits under the selected tab on the second row                                                                                                                                                                       |

## Do and don't

For a caller using the component, with the reason.

| Do                                                                                                                                                  | Don't                                                                                                                                       |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Use Tabs to switch between views of one thing, such as a stop's departures, lines and disruptions                                                   | Use Tabs to filter or sort one view, such as departures by mode: a segmented control or filter chips change a view, tabs change which one   |
| Name the tab list with `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`, such as the stop's name, so a screen reader tells it from the next one                    | Leave the list unnamed beside another set of tabs                                                                                           |
| Keep each label to a word or two, in sentence case: "Departures", "Planned works"                                                                   | Write a sentence on a tab, or put a count in the label's text: give it as `count`, so every count has one shape                             |
| Give every `Tab` a `TabsPanel` with the same `value`                                                                                                | Leave a tab without a panel: its `aria-controls` points at nothing, and selecting it shows nothing                                          |
| Show a tab whose view is empty, and say so in its panel with an [EmptyState](empty-state.md) or a [DataStatePanel](../patterns/data-state-panel.md) | Disable a tab because its view has no data: a disabled tab can't say why, and the empty view is what Mylder should tell                     |
| Use `keepMounted` on a panel that holds state the caller would lose, such as a scrolled list                                                        | Keep every panel mounted by default: hidden panels still render, and update with the live data                                              |
| Link to another screen with a [LinkButton](link-button.md)                                                                                          | Use tabs as navigation between pages: a tab selects a panel on this screen, and a link is what goes elsewhere                               |
| Let the tabs size to their labels and wrap on a narrow screen                                                                                       | Set the list to scroll sideways or give the tabs fixed widths: only the map scrolls sideways, and a translated label outgrows a fixed width |

title: MapTooltip
markdown:
# MapTooltip

The map's hover card: a small inverse card of the caller's words, placed against a point on the map or an element, shown while the pointer rests on a vehicle or a stop.

<!-- run notes -->

The design is deferred (ADR 0010, `docs/adr/0010-unattended-runs-with-design-deferred.md`): there is no read-back, code map or export, and this spec decides what the drawing would, from the contract, the foundations, the tokens and the Base UI reference. The extracted prototype component is not in any branch this run can reach.

## Anatomy

Penpot page `Components/MapTooltip`. Family: Tooltips. Shared parts: none (the card holds the caller's words and draws no mark of its own).

MapTooltip is a controlled card with no trigger: it is placed against its `anchorEl` (a virtual element at a point the map projects, or an element) and opened and closed by the caller through `open`, so it composes `Tooltip.Root`, `Tooltip.Portal`, `Tooltip.Positioner` and `Tooltip.Popup` and not `Tooltip.Provider` or `Tooltip.Trigger`, which the build takes out of the entry's `baseUiParts`. The vehicles and stops are drawn on the map canvas, not as elements a `Tooltip.Trigger` could wrap, so only the map knows what is under the pointer; and without triggers there is no hover delay for a `Tooltip.Provider` to share.

The popup is the component's root, taking `ref`, `className`, `style`, `render` and the rest props. `Tooltip.Root`'s props other than `open`, `defaultOpen` and `onOpenChange` (as `onClose`) are not offered, and `slotProps` has keys for the portal and the positioner only. The popup is the element the eye sees and the one a caller restyles, and `Tooltip.Root` renders no element; its other props (`actionsRef`, `handle`, `triggerId`, `trackCursorAxis`, `disabled`, `disableHoverablePopup`, `onOpenChangeComplete`) serve triggers, cursor tracking and exit animations this card doesn't have.

The card leaves out Base UI's `Tooltip.Arrow` and `Tooltip.Viewport`. The Tooltips family draws no arrow, and the content swaps at once, with no transition for a viewport to run (see Component rules).

| Part (Penpot layer) | What it is                                                                                                             | Base UI part         | Class                      | `slotProps` key |
| ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------- | -------------------------- | --------------- |
| `root`              | The card: an inverse box that holds the caller's `children`, a block that wraps its text                               | `Tooltip.Popup`      | `pn-MapTooltip`            | none            |
| `positioner`        | Not drawn: the box Base UI places against the anchor, above it by default, and that carries the stacking               | `Tooltip.Positioner` | `pn-MapTooltip-positioner` | `positioner`    |
| `portal`            | Not drawn: the `<div>` Base UI appends to `<body>` while the card is open, so no panel's overflow or stacking clips it | `Tooltip.Portal`     | `pn-MapTooltip-portal`     | `portal`        |

`Tooltip.Root` groups the parts and holds the open state; it renders no element, so it has no layer, class or `slotProps` key.

## Base UI parts

Imported from `@base-ui/react/tooltip`, at the version pinned in `package.json` (1.9.0 installed).

| Base UI part         | Renders                                                                                                                                                                     | Perron sets                                                                                                                                                                                                 | Passed through                                                                                                                                     |
| -------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Tooltip.Root`       | No element                                                                                                                                                                  | `open` and `defaultOpen` from MapTooltip's props, and `onOpenChange`, turned into `onClose(event, reason, details)` when it reports `false`                                                                 | none                                                                                                                                               |
| `Tooltip.Portal`     | A `<div>` appended to `<body>`, rendered only while the card is open                                                                                                        | `className` (`pn-MapTooltip-portal`, then the caller's)                                                                                                                                                     | `slotProps.portal`: `container`, `keepMounted` and the rest of its props                                                                           |
| `Tooltip.Positioner` | A `<div role="presentation">`, placed by Base UI, with `data-side`, `data-align`, `data-open` or `data-closed`, `data-anchor-hidden`, and the `--available-width` variables | `className` (`pn-MapTooltip-positioner`, then the caller's), `anchor` from MapTooltip's `anchorEl`, and the defaults `sideOffset` and `collisionPadding` (see Props), which `slotProps.positioner` replaces | `slotProps.positioner`: `side`, `align`, `sideOffset`, `alignOffset`, `collisionPadding`, `collisionAvoidance`, `sticky` and the rest of its props |
| `Tooltip.Popup`      | A `<div tabindex="-1">` with no role, with `data-side`, `data-align`, `data-open` or `data-closed`, `data-starting-style`, `data-ending-style` and `data-instant`           | `className` (`pn-MapTooltip`, then the caller's), `ref`, and the caller's `children`                                                                                                                        | `render`, `style`, `id`, `onPointerEnter`, `onPointerLeave` and every other prop of a `<div>`, through `{...rest}`                                 |

Base UI already does: it renders the card only while it is open; it places the card against the anchor, on the side asked for, flipping to the opposite side when that one has no room and shifting it along the edge so it stays inside the viewport; it re-reads the anchor when an ancestor scrolls, the anchor or the card resizes or the layout shifts, though not on every frame; it marks the positioner `data-anchor-hidden` when the anchor is out of view or a virtual one measures nothing (a 0 by 0 rect at 0, 0); it reports Esc, from anywhere in the document while the card is open, as `onOpenChange(false)` with the reason `'escape-key'`, and a press outside the card as `'outside-press'`; it leaves the card readable but out of the tab order (`tabindex="-1"`) and makes the positioner `inert` while the card is closed; and it sets the variables `--available-width` and `--available-height`, the room between the anchor and the viewport's edge.

## Props

In MUI's layout. Every prop here gets this description as its JSDoc. Slots come last.

The prop that places the card is named `anchorEl`, MUI Popper's name for what a popper sits against, and it is required. MUI's `anchorEl` takes an element or a virtual element, an object whose `getBoundingClientRect()` gives a point with no element behind it, as this one does. Its type is Base UI's for `Tooltip.Positioner`'s `anchor` without `undefined`, since the prop is required, onto which it maps one to one, so it also takes a ref and a function. It is not named `anchor`, because Sheet, MapTooltip's sibling in Overlays, already ships `anchor` as the edge it slides from (Sheet CR-3), and one name has one type and default across the library. With no trigger, a card without an anchor has nothing to sit against.

MapTooltip leaves out `onOpen`. Nothing inside the component opens the card: Base UI reports an opening only from a trigger's hover or focus, and MapTooltip has no trigger, so an `onOpen` would never fire. It can join later as an optional prop without a break.

MapTooltip leaves the side and alignment to `slotProps.positioner`, keeping Base UI's `side` of `'top'` and `align` of `'center'`, and sets two defaults read in script, since Base UI takes numbers: a `sideOffset` of `space.200` and a `collisionPadding` of `size.panel-gap`. Their pixel lengths are read at run time by the shared helper `positionerOffsets`, which [Tooltip](tooltip.md) imports too, from the tokens' custom properties, `--perron-space-200` and `--perron-size-panel-gap`, in the document's computed style, because the tokens' `numeric` values in `@mylder/perron/tokens.ts` sit outside the package build's `rootDir`, so a component under `src/` cannot import them. A card above the point leaves the vehicle under the pointer in view, `space.200` keeps it clear of the largest dot, and `size.panel-gap` keeps it as far from the screen edge as the panels are; a caller who needs another side gives it through `slotProps.positioner`, which the contract makes the way inside.

| Name                   | Type                                                                                                                 | Default | Base UI prop                     | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ---------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------- | -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `children`             | `ReactNode`                                                                                                          | none    | none                             | The card's content: a few words on what is under the pointer, in sentence case, such as "Bus 5C to Husum". It takes the card's inverse text colour.                                                                      |
| `anchorEl`             | `Element \| VirtualElement \| React.RefObject<Element \| null> \| (() => Element \| VirtualElement \| null) \| null` | none    | `anchor` on `Tooltip.Positioner` | Required. What the card sits against: a virtual element whose `getBoundingClientRect()` gives the point the map projects for a vehicle or stop, or an element. Pass a new one when the point moves, so the card follows. |
| `open`                 | `boolean`                                                                                                            | none    | `open`                           | Whether the card is shown. Set it while the pointer rests on what the card describes, and clear it in `onClose`.                                                                                                         |
| `defaultOpen`          | `boolean`                                                                                                            | `false` | `defaultOpen`                    | Whether the card is shown at first, when `open` is not set.                                                                                                                                                              |
| `onClose`              | `(event, reason, details) => void`                                                                                   | none    | `onOpenChange`                   | Called when the card asks to close: `reason` is `'escape-key'` on Esc or `'outside-press'` on a press outside it, and `details.cancel()` keeps it open.                                                                  |
| `render`               | Base UI's `render`                                                                                                   | none    | inherited                        | Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render.                                |
| `className`            | `string \| ((state: Tooltip.Popup.State) => string \| undefined)`                                                    | none    | inherited                        | CSS class applied to the element, or a function that returns a class based on the component's state.                                                                                                                     |
| `style`                | `CSSProperties \| ((state: Tooltip.Popup.State) => CSSProperties \| undefined)`                                      | none    | inherited                        | Style applied to the element, or a function that returns a style object based on the component's state.                                                                                                                  |
| `ref`                  | `Ref<HTMLDivElement>`                                                                                                | none    | none                             | Reaches the root, the card.                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `slotProps.portal`     | `Tooltip.Portal.Props`                                                                                               | none    | `Tooltip.Portal`                 | Props for the `portal` part, such as `container` to render the card inside the map's own element.                                                                                                                        |
| `slotProps.positioner` | `Tooltip.Positioner.Props`                                                                                           | none    | `Tooltip.Positioner`             | Props for the `positioner` part, such as `side`, `align` or `sideOffset`. Its `sideOffset` and `collisionPadding` replace MapTooltip's defaults.                                                                         |

`MapTooltipProps` extends `Tooltip.Popup.Props` without its `children` and `ref`, so `render`, `className` and `style` are inherited with Base UI's JSDoc, and declares `children`, `anchorEl`, `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onClose`, `ref` and `slotProps`. No `variant`, `size` or `color`: the card has one look, the Tooltips family's. No owned string, so no `*Label` prop. None of the names is one the contract's [Names from other libraries](README.md#names-from-other-libraries) table bans; `onOpenChange` stays inside the component.

## Tokens

One row per part, state and property. The card has one design state, open: it renders only while open, and takes no hover, focus, press, selection or disabled look, since it holds no control. Rest below is the open card.

The card takes the Tooltips family's treatment: `color.surface.inverse` with `color.text.inverse`, no shadow, no border, `radius.md`, text in `typography.label-sm`. The positioner takes `z-index.dialog`, as the contract's CSS section asks of everything that renders in a portal, so a dialog opened after the card paints over it; the screen's `z-index.tooltip` is a pattern's token, outside a component's [families](README.md#token-families).

The card is padded `space.150` on the block axis and `space.200` on the inline axis. The family sets no padding; `space.150` above and below keeps a line of `typography.label-sm` and a `size.badge` line badge comfortable, and `space.200` at the sides matches the offset from the point.

The card's width follows its content, capped at `--available-width`, Base UI's room between the anchor and the viewport's edge, with no token for a largest width. The card holds a few words, and the cap keeps it on screen at 320 px wide; a fixed largest width would need a new token through the `design-tokens` skill for no use yet.

In forced colours, the card draws a `border.width.025` outline in `CanvasText`, so its edge still shows on the map. Forced colours replace the inverse fill with `Canvas`, the map's own colour there, and an outline, unlike a border, keeps the card's size.

When Base UI marks the positioner `data-anchor-hidden`, the card is hidden with `visibility: hidden` until its anchor is back in view. The card speaks of a point the reader can no longer see, such as a vehicle panned off the map.

| Part         | State          | Property                 | Token                                                                          |
| ------------ | -------------- | ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `positioner` | rest           | `z-index`                | `z-index.dialog`                                                               |
| `positioner` | anchor hidden  | `visibility`             | `hidden`, on `[data-anchor-hidden]`                                            |
| `root`       | rest           | `background-color`       | `color.surface.inverse`                                                        |
| `root`       | rest           | `color`                  | `color.text.inverse`                                                           |
| `root`       | rest           | `font`, `letter-spacing` | `typography.label-sm`, with its tracking twin                                  |
| `root`       | rest           | `border-radius`          | `radius.md`                                                                    |
| `root`       | rest           | `padding-block`          | `space.150`                                                                    |
| `root`       | rest           | `padding-inline`         | `space.200`                                                                    |
| `root`       | rest           | `max-inline-size`        | `var(--available-width)`, Base UI's variable                                   |
| `root`       | rest           | `box-shadow`             | `none`                                                                         |
| `root`       | forced colours | `outline`                | `border.width.025` solid `CanvasText`, inside `@media (forced-colors: active)` |

The defaults MapTooltip gives the positioner in script, read from the tokens' custom properties at run time:

| Part         | State | Property           | Token            |
| ------------ | ----- | ------------------ | ---------------- |
| `positioner` | rest  | `sideOffset`       | `space.200`      |
| `positioner` | rest  | `collisionPadding` | `size.panel-gap` |

Hover, highlighted, focus, pressed, disabled, selected and invalid don't apply: the card is not a control. Base UI's `data-starting-style` and `data-ending-style` take no look, as the card has no transition.

## Keyboard and ARIA

From the Base UI reference for `Tooltip` and the installed `TooltipRoot`, `TooltipPositioner`, `TooltipPopup` and the dismiss hook they build on. "From" says who does it.

| Key      | Does                                                                                                                                                                                     | From    |
| -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------- |
| `Escape` | While the card is open, from anywhere in the document: calls `onClose(event, 'escape-key', details)`; an uncontrolled card closes, a controlled one closes when the caller clears `open` | Base UI |

No other key: the card is out of the tab order (`tabindex="-1"`) and holds no control, so Tab passes it by. Opening it from the keyboard is the map's, which moves focus between vehicles in the vehicle list rather than on the canvas.

The card keeps no role and stays in the accessibility tree, with neither `role="tooltip"` nor `aria-hidden`. Base UI sets no role on `Tooltip.Popup`, and `role="tooltip"` describes a trigger through `aria-describedby`, which the card has none of; left readable, a screen reader's reading cursor still finds its words, while the map's text alternative, the vehicle list, carries the same facts.

| Element      | Role                                   | Accessible name from                  | States announced |
| ------------ | -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- | ---------------- |
| `positioner` | `presentation`, from Base UI           | none                                  | none             |
| `root`       | none: a `<div>` that reads as its text | none: its `children` are read as text | none             |

What axe won't catch, from the contract, each with how this component meets it:

- [ ] Everything the eye is told, the ear is told, for every shape each prop accepts: the card shows only the caller's `children`, read as text in the accessibility tree; it draws no mark, and the facts it shows are also in the vehicle list and the detail panel, the map's text alternative.
- [ ] Every landmark and named region has an accessible name: none here; the card is not a landmark or a region.
- [ ] Every default label can be overridden: none here; the card owns no strings.
- [ ] Every shape the type accepts renders, in every variant: `children` renders a string, an element and a list alike, as the `Content` story shows.
- [ ] A hidden copy kept for animation is `aria-hidden`, and a collapsed region is `inert`: none here; the card leaves the document when it closes, and Base UI makes the positioner `inert` while it is closed.
- [ ] Native semantics first: a plain `<div>` for words, with no role, since the card is neither a control nor a description tied to one.
- [ ] Focus moves in reading order and returns on close: the card never takes focus, so opening and closing it leaves focus where it was.
- [ ] Every target is at least `size.target-min` square: none here; the card takes no press.
- [ ] Loops stop when the system asks for less motion: none here; the card has no loop and no transition.

## Owned strings

No owned strings: every word on the card comes from the caller, as `children`.

## Component rules

Rules for this component alone, numbered so the build and the review can cite them.

- **CR-1.** MapTooltip renders `Tooltip.Root`, then `Tooltip.Portal`, `Tooltip.Positioner` and `Tooltip.Popup`, and no `Tooltip.Provider`, `Tooltip.Trigger`, `Tooltip.Arrow` or `Tooltip.Viewport`. The caller opens and closes it; the component adds no pointer or key handlers of its own.
- **CR-2.** Base UI already places the card, flips and shifts it inside the viewport, re-reads the anchor on scroll, resize and layout shift, reports Esc and a press outside, and marks the hidden anchor, so the component rebuilds none of it.
- **CR-3.** The popup is the root: `{...rest}` comes before its own attributes, `ref` reaches it, and `className` is merged after `pn-MapTooltip`. `children`, `anchorEl`, `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onClose` and `slotProps` are taken out of `rest` first, so none reaches the `<div>`.
- **CR-4.** `onOpenChange(open, details)` is adapted once, inside the component: when `open` is `false` it calls `onClose(details.event, details.reason, details)`; MapTooltip exposes no `onOpenChange`, and `onClose` is never called for an opening.
- **CR-5.** `slotProps.portal` and `slotProps.positioner` are spread through `mergeProps` (`@base-ui/react/merge-props`), the component's own props last, so the positioner's `anchor` is MapTooltip's `anchorEl`; the portal has no props of the component's own to merge, so its `mergeProps` call, kept in the form Dialog uses, passes the caller's props as they are. Each part's class is set after the merge, by `withClass`, because `mergeProps` joins class strings rightmost first and joins only strings, not a function of state: `pn-MapTooltip-portal` and `pn-MapTooltip-positioner` come first, then the caller's `className`, a string or a function of the part's state. The positioner's `sideOffset` and `collisionPadding` are defaults: the component passes `space.200` and `size.panel-gap` only when `slotProps.positioner` gives none, reading their pixel lengths in script, through the shared helper `positionerOffsets`, from the tokens' custom properties, `--perron-space-200` and `--perron-size-panel-gap`, in the document's computed style, never a literal. With no document, as on a server, or before a token stylesheet has given both properties in pixels, it passes neither, so Base UI's own defaults apply, and it keeps the first reading that gives both for the life of the page.
- **CR-6.** The positioner takes `z-index.dialog`, and hides the card with `visibility: hidden` while it carries `[data-anchor-hidden]`.
- **CR-7.** The card's look is the Tooltips family's and nothing more: `color.surface.inverse`, `color.text.inverse`, `radius.md`, `typography.label-sm` with its tracking twin, no shadow and no border. The family sets no padding, so the card's is its own: `space.150` on the block axis and `space.200` on the inline axis. Its text wraps (`overflow-wrap: break-word`) inside `max-inline-size: var(--available-width)`, with `box-sizing: border-box` so the padding stays inside that cap, and its width otherwise follows its content.
- **CR-8.** The card is a block: `children` flow as the caller writes them, and the component sets no flex or grid on them. Content takes the card's colour through `currentColor`.
- **CR-9.** Opening and closing are immediate: no `duration.*` token fits a hover card, so the CSS has no transition or animation, and `data-starting-style` and `data-ending-style` take no look.
- **CR-10.** In forced colours the card draws a `border.width.025` solid `CanvasText` outline, inside `@media (forced-colors: active)`, so its geometry doesn't change.
- **CR-11.** The popup keeps no role and no `aria-hidden`, and the component adds none.

## Stories

The deferred drawing has no variant property and no `State`: the card has one look and one design state, open, so its one variant is `Default` (`penpot/README.md`, "Conventions"). The other stories are behaviour, which the `play` tests check.

The meta sets `parameters: { docs: { story: { inline: false, height: '480px' } } }`, since the card portals to `<body>`, and each story renders in its own frame. A virtual anchor in a story is a point inside the frame, such as `{ getBoundingClientRect: () => DOMRect.fromRect({ x: 240, y: 240, width: 0, height: 0 }) }`, never one at 0, 0, which Base UI reads as hidden, except in the two stories that test the hidden anchor: `AnchorHidden`, at 0, 0, and `MovingPoint`, whose point leaves the frame. Each `play` finds the card through `screen`, outside `canvasElement`, and ends with it closed.

| Story          | Shows                                                                                                                                                                                                         | `play` test                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Default`      | The subject story: the card open (`defaultOpen`) against a virtual point, with one line of text, "Bus 5C to Husum"; its args pass every rule alone                                                            | The card has `pn-MapTooltip`, no role, and the text; its positioner has `data-side="top"`, and the card's bottom edge sits above the point; Esc with `details.cancel()` in `onClose` leaves the card open; Esc again calls `onClose` with `'escape-key'` and the card leaves the document                                                                                              |
| `Controlled`   | The card with `open` held in the story's state, against an element (a small dot standing in for a stop), beside a button "Show the card" that opens it again                                                  | Esc calls `onClose` once with `'escape-key'` and the story clears `open`; the button opens it again; a press outside the card calls `onClose` with `'outside-press'`; focus stays on the button throughout; ends closed                                                                                                                                                                |
| `Content`      | The card open against a virtual point, with an element and a list as `children`: a bold line, "Bus 5C to Husum", and a second line, "Live, on time"                                                           | Both lines render inside the card in `color.text.inverse`, and the card stays inside the viewport                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `NearTopEdge`  | The card open against a virtual point near the top of the frame, where there is no room above it                                                                                                              | The positioner flips to `data-side="bottom"`, and the card's top edge stays at least `size.panel-gap` from the top of the viewport                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `MovingPoint`  | The card with `open` held in the story's state, against a virtual point the story holds, beside a button "Move the bus" that moves the point to another place in the frame, then off its left edge, then back | The card sits centred `space.200` above the point; Enter on the button passes a new `anchorEl`, and the same card, still open, sits centred `space.200` above the new point; Enter again moves the point off the frame, the positioner takes `data-anchor-hidden` and the card has `visibility: hidden`; Enter again brings the point back, and the card shows above it; Esc closes it |
| `AnchorHidden` | The card open (`defaultOpen`) against a virtual point that measures nothing, 0 by 0 at 0, 0, as a map gives before it has projected the vehicle                                                               | The positioner has `data-anchor-hidden`, and the card has `visibility: hidden` and is not visible (CR-6); Esc calls `onClose` with `'escape-key'` and the card leaves the document                                                                                                                                                                                                     |

## Do and don't

For a caller using the component, with the reason.

| Do                                                                                                                                 | Don't                                                                                                                                             |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Open the card while a mouse pointer rests on a vehicle or a stop, and select it on a tap or a click, opening its detail panel      | Open the card on touch: a tap has no hover, and Accessibility asks that anything shown on hover is also reached by selecting the item             |
| Keep the card open while the pointer is over it, using the card's `onPointerEnter` and `onPointerLeave`, and close it in `onClose` | Close it the moment the pointer leaves the dot: Accessibility asks that a hover card stays while the pointer is over it                           |
| Give a few words: the line and its destination, the data state                                                                     | Put a link, a button or a field in the card: it is out of the tab order, so the keys can't reach them; use a panel or a popover                   |
| Pass a new `anchorEl` when the vehicle moves, so the card moves with it                                                            | Expect the card to follow a moving point on its own: Base UI re-reads the anchor on scroll, resize and layout shift, not on every frame           |
| Let the card's words take its inverse colour, and use components that draw their own colours on a fill, such as a line badge       | Put text that sets its own secondary or tertiary colour in the card: those colours are measured on light surfaces, not on `color.surface.inverse` |
| Give the same facts in the vehicle list or the detail panel                                                                        | Put anything only in the card: screen reader, keyboard and touch users never see it                                                               |
| Change the side through `slotProps.positioner`, such as `side: 'bottom'`                                                           | Move the card with a margin or a `transform`: Base UI's placement and flipping no longer match what is drawn                                      |
| Show one card at a time                                                                                                            | Open a card for each vehicle at once: the cards cover the map they describe                                                                       |

title: Menu
markdown:
# Menu

A list of actions and settings that opens from a button, such as the top bar's menu of kiosk mode, help and the map's display settings, moved through with the arrow keys and closed with Esc, a choice or a press outside it.

<!-- run notes -->

The design is deferred (ADR 0010, `docs/adr/0010-unattended-runs-with-design-deferred.md`): there is no read-back, code map or export, and this spec decides what the drawing would, from the contract, the foundations, the tokens and the Base UI reference. The extracted prototype component is not in any branch this run can reach, and no ROADMAP line names Menu. The [Dialog](dialog.md) spec gives the trigger and the open state their shape, the [Toolbar](toolbar.md) spec the compound components, the [SearchField](search-field.md) spec the rows of a popup, and the [Switch](switch.md) spec a checked state's props.

## Anatomy

Penpot page `Components/Menu`. Family: Popups, for the popup and the submenu's popup; Rows, for every item. Shared parts: `CheckboxIndicator`, in `Menu.CheckboxItemIndicator`, and `SelectedMark`, in `Menu.RadioItemIndicator`, as the contract's [Shared parts](README.md#shared-parts) table composes them.

Menu is nine components, `Menu`, `MenuItem`, `MenuLinkItem`, `MenuCheckboxItem`, `MenuRadioGroup`, `MenuRadioItem`, `MenuGroup`, `MenuSeparator` and `MenuSubmenu`, each exported with its props type from `Menu.tsx`, in the one `Menu` folder and the one registry entry, as the Toolbar spec's exception to the contract's "one component per folder". The contract makes a child the caller writes many times, such as a menu's item, a component of its own, and every Base UI part after `Menu.Root` reads `Menu.Root`'s context, so the items can't be built, shown or tested apart from a menu; the registry gives Menu one entry for all seventeen parts; MUI's Menu takes its items as `MenuItem` children; and a data prop, as SearchField's `items`, can't hold checkbox items, radio groups and submenus without a second, typed language for each. The `props` check reads every `*Props` `Menu.tsx` exports, and the `docs` check holds `MenuProps` alone to the first Props table, so the review holds the other eight to their tables.

`Menu` renders every part of the menu itself, `Menu.Root`, `Menu.Trigger`, `Menu.Portal`, `Menu.Positioner` and `Menu.Popup`, with the popup as its root, the element `ref`, `className`, `style` and the rest props reach, as Dialog does: `Menu.Root` renders no element, and the popup is the one element a caller would style or measure. `MenuSubmenu` does the same for a submenu, with its trigger row as its root, since that row is what sits in the parent menu. Each item component renders one Base UI part as its root.

The checkbox item's box is the `CheckboxIndicator` part and the radio item's tick the `SelectedMark` part, each in its own folder under `packages/perron/src/parts/`. Both parts and the `tick` icon they draw are on `main`, the `CheckboxIndicator` drawn for [Checkbox](checkbox.md) and the `SelectedMark` for [Select](select.md), and Menu composes each unchanged. The build adds only the submenu's `chevron-right` icon, following [Icons](../foundations/icons.md) and joining `icons.json` (CR-8).

| `trigger`               | The caller's `trigger`, such as a [Button](button.md), rendered in place of the menu through `Menu.Trigger`'s `render`. `Menu.Root` and `Menu.SubmenuRoot` render no element: they hold the open state and the props of [Props](#props) that map to them. The registry's other Base UI parts are each one component's root or inner part, as the table gives. Base UI's `Menu.Backdrop`, `Menu.Arrow`, `Menu.Viewport`, `Menu.FilterProvider`, `Menu.Input`, `Menu.List`, `Menu.Clear`, `Menu.Empty` and `Menu.createHandle` are not used: the registry doesn't name them, a Mylder menu is short enough to need no filter, a modal menu already blocks the page without a backdrop of its own, the Popups family draws no arrow, and one trigger opens one menu. Each can join later as a new optional component or prop, which the contract's [Change](README.md#change) rule allows.

## Base UI parts

Base UI already does: it opens the menu on a press of the trigger, or on Enter, Space, ArrowDown or ArrowUp with the trigger focused, and gives the trigger `aria-haspopup="menu"`, `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`; it portals the positioner and the popup to `<body>`, and renders nothing there, on the server or the client, while the menu is closed, unless the portal's `keepMounted` is set; it places the popup against the trigger and flips it to the other side, or shifts it along, when there is no room; it names the popup from the trigger with `aria-labelledby`, unless the caller gives `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`; opened from the keys it moves focus to the first item (to the last on ArrowUp), and opened by the pointer to the popup itself; it moves focus between the items with the arrow keys, wrapping at the ends while `loopFocus` is on, jumps to the first and last with Home and End, and to the next item whose text starts with the letters typed; moving the pointer over an item highlights and focuses it (`highlightItemOnHover`); a disabled item stays focusable and in the arrow-key order, with `aria-disabled`, and ignores presses; a press of an item, by the pointer, Enter or Space, runs its `onClick` and closes the menu (`closeOnClick` is `true` on `Menu.Item` and `false` on the checkbox, radio and link items); a checkbox item toggles itself and a radio item chooses itself, each keeping the menu open; a radio group keeps one value for its items; a submenu opens on ArrowRight, Enter or Space on its row, or on hover after `delay`, and closes on ArrowLeft or Esc, which closes only the submenu unless `closeParentOnEsc` is set; Esc closes the menu, as do a press outside it and Tab; while open the modal menu locks the page's scroll and blocks the pointer outside it; on close it returns focus to the trigger, unless `finalFocus` says otherwise; it reports each change of open with its reason (`trigger-press`, `trigger-hover`, `outside-press`, `escape-key`, `item-press`, `focus-out`, `list-navigation`, `close-press`, `sibling-open`, `cancel-open`, `imperative-action`, `none`) and a `cancel()` that keeps the menu as it is; Left and Right swap only under Base UI's `DirectionProvider` set to `rtl`, not from the `dir` attribute, and Perron doesn't set one up yet, as all four locales run left to right.

## Props

In MUI's layout, as MUI's Menu takes `open` and `onClose` with `MenuItem` children, and with the trigger as a prop, as Dialog takes it. Every prop a props type declares gets this description as its JSDoc; every inherited one keeps Base UI's. Slots come last.

Menu leaves out `Menu.Root`'s `modal`, `loopFocus`, `orientation`, `highlightItemOnHover`, `closeParentOnEsc`, `onItemHighlighted`, `actionsRef`, `handle`, `onOpenChangeComplete`, `triggerId` and `defaultTriggerId` (the last two set by Menu itself from the trigger, CR-5), and `MenuSubmenu` leaves out every prop of `Menu.SubmenuRoot`, its open state included. Menu leaves these out, each keeping Base UI's default (a modal, vertical menu that wraps, highlights on hover and closes one submenu at a time on Esc): no Mylder screen asks for any of them yet, each changes behaviour the contract's checklist relies on rather than the look, the Dialog spec leaves out the same kind of root props, and each can join later as a new optional prop, which the contract's [Change](README.md#change) rule allows.

Menu takes `disabled`, given to `Menu.Root`, which Base UI passes to the trigger so the menu can't open. A caller's `trigger` element is rendered through `Menu.Trigger`, whose own `disabled` decides whether it opens and sets `data-disabled`, so a `disabled` on the caller's Button alone would leave Base UI's trigger enabled; the contract names `disabled` among its booleans; and it matches Toolbar's and Switch's `disabled`.

`MenuGroup` and `MenuRadioGroup` take their heading as `label: ReactNode`, rendered in `Menu.GroupLabel`, and `MenuSubmenu` its row's words as `label: ReactNode`, leaving out `Menu.SubmenuTrigger`'s own `label`, while `MenuItem`, `MenuLinkItem`, `MenuCheckboxItem` and `MenuRadioItem` inherit Base UI's `label: string`, the text for typeahead. The Base UI part is a group's label, and SearchField and Field call a control's visible name `label`; a submenu's row has no `children` of its own, since its `children` are the submenu's items; Base UI's typeahead reads a row's rendered text when its `label` is absent, so the submenu loses nothing by leaving it out; and an item's words are its `children`, as a Button's are, so its inherited `label` only ever overrides typeahead, as Base UI's JSDoc says.

`MenuRadioGroup`'s `value` and `defaultValue`, the `value` of its `onChange` and `MenuRadioItem`'s `value` are typed `string`, where Base UI takes `any`. A menu's choices, a theme or a language, are names, a string types the `onChange` a caller writes without a cast, and the API only grows, so a wider type can join later without a break; Switch's `value` is a string too.

A row offers only `startIcon` (on `MenuItem`, `MenuLinkItem` and `MenuSubmenu`), with no `endIcon`, `color`, `description` or shortcut, and the checkbox and radio items no `startIcon`. The end of a row holds the box, the tick or the chevron; the [brand](../foundations/README.md#the-brand) keeps the interface to ink and glass, and no Mylder menu holds a destructive action that a `danger` row would mark; a start icon beside the box would put two marks on one row; and each can join later as a new optional prop.

`MenuCheckboxItem` takes Switch's state, `checked`, `defaultChecked` and `onChange(event, value, details)`, whose `value` is the new `checked`, and `MenuRadioGroup` the contract's `value`, `defaultValue` and `onChange(event, value, details)`: the contract's [State and events](README.md#state-and-events) and the [Switch](switch.md) spec, with Base UI's `onCheckedChange` and `onValueChange` adapted inside (CR-4). No item takes `name`: a menu's choices act at once and submit no form.

Menu, `MenuItem`, `MenuLinkItem`, `MenuCheckboxItem`, `MenuRadioItem` and `MenuSubmenu` each declare `id` themselves, passed to their Base UI part as it is, where every other Base UI prop is inherited. Base UI's JSDoc marks `id` `@ignore` on `Menu.Popup`, `Menu.Item`, `Menu.LinkItem`, `Menu.CheckboxItem`, `Menu.RadioItem` and `Menu.SubmenuTrigger`, and the docs page's props table drops a prop whose JSDoc carries `@ignore`, so an inherited `id` would be missing from it.

No label-override props: Menu owns no strings ([Owned strings](#owned-strings)).

## Tokens

One row per part, state and property. States are the contract's design states: rest is no selector; hover is `:hover` inside `@media (hover: hover)`; highlighted is `[data-highlighted]`, a row under the pointer or the keys; focus is `:focus-visible`; disabled is `[data-disabled]`; selected is `[data-checked]` on a checkbox or radio item; open is `[data-open]` on a popup and `[data-popup-open]` on a submenu's row. The trigger is the caller's element and keeps its own tokens in every state, open included: Menu styles no `[data-popup-open]` on it. The portals and positioners are never seen; the positioners carry only the stacking.

The popup and the submenu's popup take the Popups family's treatment ([Families](README.md#families)): `color.surface.overlay` with a `backdrop-filter` of `effect.glass-blur` and `effect.glass-saturate`, `shadow.panel`, a `border.width.025` edge in `color.border.subtle`, and `radius.lg` padded `space.100`, so the rows' `radius.md` nests. Both popups share one rule, `.pn-Menu, .pn-MenuSubmenu-popup`.

The popup is at least as wide as its trigger and at most as wide and as tall as the room Base UI measures, scrolling inside when taller: `min-inline-size: var(--anchor-width)`, `max-inline-size: var(--available-width)` and `max-block-size: var(--available-height)`, over Base UI's variables, with `overflow-y: auto`, `overscroll-behavior: contain` and a `scroll-padding-block` of `space.100` (see the focus ring below). A menu as wide as the button above it reads as that button's own, as SearchField's list does; the positioner keeps `size.panel-gap` from the screen's edge as its `collisionPadding`, read through the shared `positionerOffsets` helper as Popover's, Tooltip's and MapTooltip's are (CR-9), and Base UI leaves that gap out of the room it measures, so the popup never runs off a 320 px screen and sits as far from its edge as every other popup; no width token fits a menu, and [Layout](../foundations/layout.md#other-layout-properties) keeps a measure only one component reads in that component's CSS; and the popup grows with its longest label until the room runs out, where the labels wrap (CR-11).

Every row, `MenuItem`, `MenuLinkItem`, `MenuCheckboxItem`, `MenuRadioItem` and `MenuSubmenu`, takes the Rows family's treatment and SearchField's row metrics, in one rule over the five classes: `space.150` above and below and `space.200` at its sides, `space.200` between its parts, `radius.md`, `typography.label` in `color.text.primary`, at least `size.target-min` tall, transparent at rest, `color.surface.hover` on hover and while highlighted, `color.surface.selected` while pressed, a step past hover ([Pointer feedback](README.md#pointer-feedback)), and `color.surface.selected` while checked, with the cursor `pointer`, and `default` while disabled. Rows of `typography.label` at `space.150` stand about 29 px tall, above `size.target-min`, and the same metrics in SearchField's list and here make Perron's popups read as one family.

A row's marks, the start icon, the box, the tick and the chevron, sit at its top (`align-items: flex-start`), each centred on the label's first line by a `margin-block` of half of `1lh` less its own size, as Checkbox centres its box on its label's first line. A label that wraps, such as a long Danish word on a phone, then keeps every mark level with its first words, where centring them on the row would set them between two lines; and a one-line row looks the same either way, its label one `1lh` tall.

A disabled row is `color.text.tertiary` and takes no hover, highlighted or pressed fill, as the contract makes disabled a colour; it stays focusable (Base UI's `focusableWhenDisabled`), so the focus ring still shows where the keys are. A checked row that is highlighted lays `color.surface.hover` over `color.surface.selected` as a `linear-gradient` background-image, as the Fields family lays hover over a fill, so the highlight shows on a chosen row too, and lays `color.surface.selected` over it while pressed, a step past that. A submenu's row keeps the highlighted fill while its submenu is open, so the path from the menu to the submenu shows.

The focus ring is `perron.css`'s, kept on a focused row beside the highlighted fill: [Accessibility](../foundations/accessibility.md#rules) asks for the ring on every interactive element unless another mark reaches 3:1, and `color.surface.hover` doesn't. The popup's `space.100` padding leaves the ring, `focus.offset` plus `focus.width` out from the row, inside the popup's scrolling box at its ends, as the Toolbar spec's CR-7 does for its bar, and its `scroll-padding-block` of `space.100` keeps it there when Base UI scrolls a highlighted row into view, which would otherwise set the row flush with the visible edge and clip its ring, as Select's list does. The popups draw no ring of their own, `outline: none` on their `:focus-visible`: Base UI focuses the popup itself when the pointer opens it or at first render, and a ring round the whole menu marks no row the keys would act on, so the rows alone draw it.

The checkbox item's box and the radio item's tick sit at the row's end, after the label, with the label growing between them and the row's start. Every label in a menu then starts at one edge, whether the row is an action, a setting or an option, as long as every row has a start icon or none does, which the stories keep and [Do and don't](#do-and-dont) asks, and a tick that appears and disappears shifts no words; a menu's settings read as a list of settings with their state at the end, as the submenu's chevron sits at the end; and Select and Combobox, which compose the same `SelectedMark`, can place it to suit a list of options.

The checkbox item's box is the `CheckboxIndicator` part as `main` draws it for Checkbox ([Checkbox](checkbox.md)), unchanged: a `size.checkbox` square with a `border.width.025` `color.border.control` edge and `radius.xs` on `color.surface.raised` while unticked, `color.surface.inverse` with the `tick` icon in `color.text.inverse` while ticked, and its disabled colours; Menu sets none of its tokens. The contract draws a shared part once and has every component compose it, so a menu's setting and a form's checkbox read as one control, and the part already reads its states from the attributes `Menu.CheckboxItemIndicator` sets, as `Checkbox.Indicator` does. The `SelectedMark` draws the same `tick` icon.

The group label is `typography.overline` in `color.text.secondary`, set in capitals with `text-transform: uppercase`, `space.200` at its sides as a row's text is, with `space.200` above and `space.100` below. [Typography](../foundations/typography.md) gives `overline` to section headings, which a group's label is; `color.text.secondary` is supporting text that still reaches 4.5:1; the label starts where the rows below it start their content, at `space.200`, level with their start icons or, in rows with none, their labels; and the space above parts it from the group before more than from its own rows.

`MenuSeparator` is a `border.width.025` hairline in `color.border.subtle`, drawn as a border so forced colours keep it, across the popup's padding box, a `margin-inline` of minus `space.100` running it over the popup's padding to its edge, with `space.100` above and below: the Toolbar spec's separator, and `color.border.subtle` is the dividers' colour, a divider only decorating.

The chevron is `chevron-right` at `icon.size.400` in `color.text.secondary`, `color.text.tertiary` on a disabled row, each set on its holder span, never on the `<svg>`, as [Icons](../foundations/icons.md) asks and Select's `icon` holds its chevron; the start icon is the caller's at `icon.size.400`, taking the row's colour, an icon drawn on the 16 px grid for that step, such as `locate`, `plus` or `minus`, never one drawn for `icon.size.450`, such as `monitor` or `info`, whose stroke would fall under 1.5 px ([Icons](../foundations/icons.md#sizes)); the tick is the `SelectedMark` part's `tick` at `icon.size.325`, the step its 14 px grid is drawn for ([Icons](../foundations/icons.md)), in the row's colour: the same drawing at the same size as the box's tick.

## Keyboard and ARIA

From the Base UI reference for `Menu` and the installed `MenuRoot`, `MenuTrigger`, `MenuPopup`, `useMenuItemCommonProps`, `MenuCheckboxItem`, `MenuRadioItem`, `MenuGroupLabel`, `MenuRadioGroup`, `MenuSubmenuTrigger` and the list navigation they build on. "From" says who does it.

| Key                                               | Does                                                                                                                                                       | From                                                            |
| ------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Enter`, `Space`, `ArrowDown` on the trigger      | Open the menu, calling `onOpen` with reason `'trigger-press'` or `'list-navigation'`, and move focus to the first item                                     | The browser activates the button; Base UI opens and moves focus |
| `ArrowUp` on the trigger                          | Opens the menu and moves focus to the last item                                                                                                            | Base UI                                                         |
| `ArrowDown`, `ArrowUp`                            | Move focus to the next and the previous item, disabled items included, skipping group labels and separators, and wrap from the last to the first and back  | Base UI                                                         |
| `Home`, `End`                                     | Move focus to the first and the last item                                                                                                                  | Base UI                                                         |
| A letter or letters                               | Move focus to the next item whose text, or `label`, starts with them                                                                                       | Base UI                                                         |
| `Enter`, `Space` on an item                       | Run its `onClick` and close the menu, calling `onClose` with reason `'item-press'`, and return focus to the trigger; on a disabled item, nothing           | Base UI                                                         |
| `Enter`, `Space` on a link item                   | Follow the link                                                                                                                                            | The browser; Base UI for `Space`                                |
| `Enter`, `Space` on a checkbox item               | Turn it on or off, calling `onChange` with the new `checked`, and keep the menu open                                                                       | Base UI                                                         |
| `Enter`, `Space` on a radio item                  | Choose it, calling the group's `onChange` with its `value`, and keep the menu open                                                                         | Base UI                                                         |
| `ArrowRight`, `Enter`, `Space` on a submenu's row | Open the submenu and move focus to its first item                                                                                                          | Base UI                                                         |
| `ArrowLeft` in a submenu                          | Closes the submenu and returns focus to its row                                                                                                            | Base UI                                                         |
| `Escape`                                          | Closes the innermost open menu, a submenu first, returning focus to its row or to the trigger; closing the menu calls `onClose` with reason `'escape-key'` | Base UI                                                         |
| `Tab`, `Shift+Tab`                                | Move focus out of the menu, on past the trigger or back to it, and close the menu, calling `onClose` with reason `'focus-out'`                             | Base UI                                                         |

A press outside the popup closes the menu too, with reason `'outside-press'`, and focus returns to the trigger.
