| `Bottom`         | `anchor` `bottom`, with a trigger, open at the `size.sheet-peek` snap point                          | The body at the peek ends on screen, takes focus and scrolls; `onClose` is called with reason `escape-key` on Esc, the sheet closes and focus returns to the trigger; `title` and `children` show a string, an element and a list alike                                                                                                                                                |
| `BottomExpanded` | `anchor` `bottom`, with a trigger, open at `defaultSnapPoint` `1`, with a body long enough to scroll | The content scrolls and the header stays in place; Esc closes it with reason `escape-key` and focus returns to the trigger                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `Modal`          | `anchor` `left`, `modal`, with a trigger, open by `defaultOpen` over the scrim                       | A click on the backdrop closes it with reason `outside-press`; clicking the trigger opens it again; Tab wraps inside the sheet; Esc closes it and focus returns to the trigger                                                                                                                                                                                                         |

## Do and don't

For a caller using the component, with the reason.

| Do                                                                                                                                                    | Don't                                                                                                                                              |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Use a sheet for a panel beside the map, left open while the rider pans and picks vehicles: it is not modal by default                                 | Use a modal sheet to ask for a decision; that is a Dialog, which needs no swipe or snap points (Base UI's own advice)                              |
| Pick `anchor` `bottom` on a phone, under `breakpoint.phone`, in the screen's code                                                                     | Expect the sheet to turn into a bottom sheet on its own; it sizes to its viewport and holds no media query                                         |
| Name the sheet with `title`: the stop, line or destination it shows                                                                                   | Leave the title out, or draw a heading of your own in `children`: the dialog takes its name from `title`                                           |
| Handle `onClose` and let Esc close the topmost sheet, as [Accessibility](../foundations/accessibility.md#rules) orders: a dialog, then a detail panel | Cancel every close of a sheet the rider can't otherwise leave; cancel only the reasons a screen must refuse, such as `swipe` on the overview sheet |
| Mark a horizontal carousel or slider inside a bottom sheet with `data-base-ui-swipe-ignore`, so its drags don't swipe the sheet                       | Let a control that drags sideways fight the sheet's swipe                                                                                          |
| Keep one primary action per sheet                                                                                                                     | Put two brand buttons in one sheet; a screen has one brand action at most                                                                          |

title: Tooltip
markdown:
# Tooltip

A short visual label beside a control, such as "Zoom in" over the map's zoom button, shown while a mouse pointer rests on the control or the keyboard focuses it, for sighted mouse and keyboard users.

<!-- run notes -->

The design is deferred (ADR 0010, `docs/adr/0010-unattended-runs-with-design-deferred.md`): there is no read-back, code map or export, and this spec decides what the drawing would, from the contract, the foundations, the tokens and the Base UI reference. The ROADMAP names no Tooltip line of its own: Base UI's Tooltip is the part under the MapTooltip line of Wave 3, and this component is its trigger-bound sibling. The extracted prototype component is not in any branch this run can reach. It shares the Tooltips family's treatment with [MapTooltip](map-tooltip.md), which places a card against a point the caller holds, where this one sits against the control it labels.

## Anatomy

Penpot page `Components/Tooltip`. Family: Tooltips. Shared parts: none (the popup holds the caller's words and draws no mark of its own).

Tooltip is one component that takes its trigger as a `trigger` prop (a `ReactElement`, required) and its words as `children`, with the popup as its root, the way [Dialog](dialog.md) and [Sheet](sheet.md) take `trigger` and [MapTooltip](map-tooltip.md) takes `children` as the card's words, rather than MUI's `title` for the words and `children` for the trigger. In Perron `title` is already a heading (Dialog, Sheet, Section, EmptyState) and `children` is what an overlay shows, so one name keeps one meaning across the Overlays category; the trigger is required because a tooltip with nothing to label is MapTooltip's job; and the popup is the root, as in its three siblings, so `ref`, `className`, `style` and the rest props reach the element the eye sees.

Tooltip renders `Tooltip.Root`, `Tooltip.Trigger`, `Tooltip.Portal`, `Tooltip.Positioner` and `Tooltip.Popup`. It leaves out `Tooltip.Arrow`, which the entry's `baseUiParts` don't name: the Tooltips family draws no arrow, and MapTooltip, its other member, has none, so the family keeps one treatment. It leaves out `Tooltip.Viewport` too, which the entry doesn't name: one tooltip has one trigger, and its words swap with no transition for a viewport to run.

`PerronProvider` (`packages/perron/src/PerronProvider.tsx`) wraps its children in `Tooltip.Provider`, with Base UI's own delays, so that once one tooltip is open the next one the pointer reaches opens at once, while Tooltip itself renders no provider. A provider around each tooltip groups nothing, and a second exported component would need a spec and a registry entry of its own; the map's controls set three tooltips side by side, and Base UI's demos wrap such a row in one provider. `Tooltip.Provider` renders no element, so the app's markup doesn't change; the entry keeps `Tooltip.Provider` in its `baseUiParts`, since Tooltip relies on it.

| Part (Penpot layer) | What it is                                                                                                                             | Base UI part         | Class                   | `slotProps` key |
| ------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------- | ----------------------- | --------------- |
| `root`              | The popup: an inverse box that holds the caller's `children`, a block that wraps its text; rendered only while open                    | `Tooltip.Popup`      | `pn-Tooltip`            | none            |
| `trigger`           | The caller's `trigger`, such as an [IconButton](icon-button.md), rendered in place of the tooltip through `Tooltip.Trigger`'s `render` | `Tooltip.Trigger`    | `pn-Tooltip-trigger`    | `trigger`       |
| `positioner`        | Not drawn: the box Base UI places against the trigger, above it by default, and that carries the stacking                              | `Tooltip.Positioner` | `pn-Tooltip-positioner` | `positioner`    |
| `portal`            | Not drawn: the `<div>` Base UI appends to `<body>` while the tooltip is open, so no panel's overflow or stacking clips it              | `Tooltip.Portal`     | `pn-Tooltip-portal`     | `portal`        |
| `provider`          | Not drawn: the shared delay group, rendered once by `PerronProvider` around the app, never by Tooltip                                  | `Tooltip.Provider`   | none                    | none            |

`Tooltip.Root` groups the parts and holds the open state; it renders no element, so it has no layer, class or `slotProps` key. The trigger keeps the caller's element and its look: Tooltip adds its class beside the element's own and no style.

## Base UI parts

Imported from `@base-ui/react/tooltip`, at the version pinned in `package.json` (1.9.0 installed).

| Base UI part         | Renders                                                                                                                                                                     | Perron sets                                                                                                                                                                                     | Passed through                                                                                                                                     |
| -------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Tooltip.Provider`   | No element                                                                                                                                                                  | Rendered by `PerronProvider` around its children, with no props: Base UI's `delay`, `closeDelay` and `timeout` of 400 ms hold                                                                   | none                                                                                                                                               |
| `Tooltip.Root`       | No element                                                                                                                                                                  | `open` and `defaultOpen` from Tooltip's props, `onOpenChange` adapted to `onOpen` and `onClose` (CR-4), and `defaultTriggerId`, or `triggerId` when `open` is set, from the trigger's id (CR-5) | none: Tooltip declares the root props it offers                                                                                                    |
| `Tooltip.Trigger`    | The caller's `trigger` element through `render`, a `<button>` by default, with `data-popup-open` while its tooltip is open and `data-trigger-disabled` while it can't open  | `render` (the `trigger` prop), `className` (`pn-Tooltip-trigger`, beside the trigger's own), `id` (the trigger's own, then `slotProps.trigger.id`, or one from `useId`, CR-5)                   | `slotProps.trigger`: `delay`, `closeDelay`, `closeOnClick`, `disabled` and the rest of `Tooltip.Trigger.Props`                                     |
| `Tooltip.Portal`     | A `<div>` appended to `<body>`, rendered only while the tooltip is open                                                                                                     | `className` (`pn-Tooltip-portal`, then the caller's)                                                                                                                                            | `slotProps.portal`: `container`, `keepMounted` and the rest of its props                                                                           |
| `Tooltip.Positioner` | A `<div role="presentation">`, placed by Base UI, with `data-side`, `data-align`, `data-open` or `data-closed`, `data-anchor-hidden`, and the `--available-width` variables | `className` (`pn-Tooltip-positioner`, then the caller's), and the defaults `sideOffset` and `collisionPadding` (see Props), which `slotProps.positioner` replaces                               | `slotProps.positioner`: `side`, `align`, `sideOffset`, `alignOffset`, `collisionPadding`, `collisionAvoidance`, `sticky` and the rest of its props |
| `Tooltip.Popup`      | A `<div tabindex="-1">` with no role, with `data-side`, `data-align`, `data-open` or `data-closed`, `data-starting-style`, `data-ending-style` and `data-instant`           | `className` (`pn-Tooltip`, then the caller's), `ref`, and the caller's `children`                                                                                                               | `render`, `style`, `id` and every other prop of a `<div>`, through `{...rest}`                                                                     |

Base UI already does: it opens the tooltip when a mouse pointer rests on the trigger for the open delay, 600 ms unless the trigger's or the provider's `delay` says otherwise, and never on touch, since its hover listens to the mouse only; it opens it at once when the trigger takes keyboard focus that matches `:focus-visible`, and not on a tap or a click that focuses it; inside a provider, once one tooltip is open, the next trigger the pointer reaches within the provider's 400 ms `timeout` opens its tooltip at once, marked `data-instant="delay"`; it keeps the tooltip open while the pointer travels from the trigger onto the popup and rests there, so its words can be read and selected; it closes it when the pointer leaves both, when the trigger loses focus, on Esc from anywhere in the document, on a press outside, and on a press of the trigger itself while `closeOnClick` is on, its default; it reports each change with its reason (`trigger-hover`, `trigger-focus`, `trigger-press`, `outside-press`, `escape-key`, `disabled`, `imperative-action`, `none`) and a `cancel()` that keeps it as it is; it portals the popup to `<body>` and renders nothing there while closed; it places the popup against the trigger, above it by default, flipping to the opposite side when that one has no room and shifting it along the edge so it stays inside the viewport, and re-reads the trigger when an ancestor scrolls, either one resizes or the layout shifts; it marks the positioner `data-anchor-hidden` when the trigger is scrolled out of view; it leaves the popup out of the tab order (`tabindex="-1"`) and makes the positioner `inert` while closed; and it sets the variables `--available-width` and `--available-height`, the room between the trigger and the viewport's edge. Base UI sets no role on the popup and no `aria-describedby` on the trigger: its guidelines make a tooltip a visual label only, with the trigger named on its own.

## Props

In MUI's layout. Every prop the component declares gets this description as its JSDoc; the inherited rows keep Base UI's. Slots come last.

Tooltip offers only `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpen` and `onClose` of `Tooltip.Root`'s props, and leaves out `disabled`, `trackCursorAxis`, `disableHoverablePopup`, `actionsRef`, `handle` and `onOpenChangeComplete` (with `triggerId` and `defaultTriggerId` set by Tooltip itself, CR-5). A tooltip that should not open is one the caller doesn't render, or one whose `slotProps.trigger.disabled` is set; a popup that can't be hovered fails [Accessibility](../foundations/accessibility.md#rules)'s rule that a hover card stays while the pointer is over it; cursor tracking, detached triggers and exit animations serve no Mylder screen yet; and each can join later as a new optional prop, which the contract's [Change](README.md#change) rule allows.

Tooltip sets two positioner defaults read in script, since Base UI takes numbers: a `sideOffset` of `space.200` and a `collisionPadding` of `size.panel-gap`, as [MapTooltip](map-tooltip.md) does, so the Tooltips family sits the same distance from what it labels and from the screen's edge. It keeps Base UI's `side` of `'top'` and `align` of `'center'`, and Base UI's open and close delays, for which no token exists; a caller changes any of them through `slotProps.positioner` or `slotProps.trigger`. Both read the two lengths through one shared helper, `positionerOffsets` (CR-6).

| Name                   | Type                                                                                                       | Default | Base UI prop                 | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ---------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------- | ---------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `children`             | `ReactNode`                                                                                                | none    | none                         | The tooltip's words: a short label in sentence case that matches the trigger's accessible name, such as "Zoom in". It takes the popup's inverse text colour.                                                         |
| `trigger`              | `ReactElement`                                                                                             | none    | `Tooltip.Trigger`'s `render` | Required. The control the tooltip labels, such as an IconButton, rendered in place of the tooltip. It must take a ref and spread the props it is given, as Perron's buttons do, and carry its own accessible name.   |
| `open`                 | `boolean`                                                                                                  | none    | `open`                       | Whether the tooltip is shown. Set it to control the tooltip, with `onOpen` and `onClose` to hear when it asks to change; leave it out for a tooltip its trigger opens.                                               |
| `defaultOpen`          | `boolean`                                                                                                  | `false` | `defaultOpen`                | Whether the tooltip is shown at first, when `open` is left out.                                                                                                                                                      |
| `onOpen`               | `(event: Event, details: Tooltip.Root.ChangeEventDetails) => void`                                         | none    | `onOpenChange`               | Called when the tooltip asks to open: `reason` in `details` is `'trigger-hover'` when the pointer rests on the trigger or `'trigger-focus'` when the keyboard focuses it, and `details.cancel()` keeps it closed.    |
| `onClose`              | `(event: Event, reason: Tooltip.Root.ChangeEventReason, details: Tooltip.Root.ChangeEventDetails) => void` | none    | `onOpenChange`               | Called when the tooltip asks to close: `reason` is `'trigger-hover'`, `'trigger-focus'`, `'trigger-press'`, `'escape-key'`, `'outside-press'` or another of Base UI's reasons, and `details.cancel()` keeps it open. |
| `render`               | Base UI's `render`                                                                                         | none    | inherited                    | Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render.                            |
| `className`            | `string \| ((state: Tooltip.Popup.State) => string \| undefined)`                                          | none    | inherited                    | CSS class applied to the element, or a function that returns a class based on the component's state.                                                                                                                 |
| `style`                | `CSSProperties \| ((state: Tooltip.Popup.State) => CSSProperties \| undefined)`                            | none    | inherited                    | Style applied to the element, or a function that returns a style object based on the component's state.                                                                                                              |
| `ref`                  | `Ref<HTMLDivElement>`                                                                                      | none    | none                         | Reaches the root, the popup.                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `slotProps.trigger`    | `Tooltip.Trigger.Props`                                                                                    | none    | `Tooltip.Trigger`            | Props for the `trigger` part, such as `delay` or `closeOnClick`.                                                                                                                                                     |
| `slotProps.portal`     | `Tooltip.Portal.Props`                                                                                     | none    | `Tooltip.Portal`             | Props for the `portal` part, such as its `container`.                                                                                                                                                                |
| `slotProps.positioner` | `Tooltip.Positioner.Props`                                                                                 | none    | `Tooltip.Positioner`         | Props for the `positioner` part, such as `side`, `align` or `sideOffset`. Its `sideOffset` and `collisionPadding` replace Tooltip's defaults.                                                                        |

`TooltipProps` extends `Tooltip.Popup.Props` without its `children` and `ref`, so `render`, `className` and `style` are inherited with Base UI's JSDoc, and declares `children`, `trigger`, `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpen`, `onClose`, `ref` and `slotProps`. No `variant`, `size` or `color`: the popup has one look, the Tooltips family's, so its root carries no `data-variant`, `data-color` or `data-size`. No owned string, so no `*Label` prop. None of the names is one the contract's [Names from other libraries](README.md#names-from-other-libraries) table bans; `onOpenChange` stays inside the component.

## Tokens

One row per part, state and property. The popup has one design state, open: it renders only while open, and takes no hover, focus, press, selection or disabled look, since it holds no control. Rest below is the open popup. The trigger is the caller's element and keeps its own tokens in every state.

The popup takes the Tooltips family's treatment, as MapTooltip does: `color.surface.inverse` with `color.text.inverse`, no shadow, no border, `radius.md`, text in `typography.label-sm`, padded `space.150` on the block axis and `space.200` on the inline axis, its width following its content up to `--available-width`, Base UI's room between the trigger and the viewport's edge. The positioner takes `z-index.dialog`, as the contract's CSS section asks of everything that renders in a portal; the screen's `z-index.tooltip` is a pattern's token, outside a component's [families](README.md#token-families). In forced colours the popup draws a `border.width.025` outline in `CanvasText`, since the inverse fill becomes `Canvas`; an outline keeps its size. While Base UI marks the positioner `data-anchor-hidden`, the popup is hidden with `visibility: hidden`: it labels a control the reader can no longer see.

| Part         | State          | Property                 | Token                                                                          |
| ------------ | -------------- | ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `positioner` | rest           | `z-index`                | `z-index.dialog`                                                               |
| `positioner` | anchor hidden  | `visibility`             | `hidden`, on `[data-anchor-hidden]`                                            |
| `root`       | rest           | `background-color`       | `color.surface.inverse`                                                        |
| `root`       | rest           | `color`                  | `color.text.inverse`                                                           |
| `root`       | rest           | `font`, `letter-spacing` | `typography.label-sm`, with its tracking twin                                  |
| `root`       | rest           | `border-radius`          | `radius.md`                                                                    |
| `root`       | rest           | `padding-block`          | `space.150`                                                                    |
| `root`       | rest           | `padding-inline`         | `space.200`                                                                    |
| `root`       | rest           | `max-inline-size`        | `var(--available-width)`, Base UI's variable                                   |
| `root`       | rest           | `box-shadow`             | `none`                                                                         |
| `root`       | forced colours | `outline`                | `border.width.025` solid `CanvasText`, inside `@media (forced-colors: active)` |

The defaults Tooltip gives the positioner in script, read from the tokens' custom properties at run time:

| Part         | State | Property           | Token            |
| ------------ | ----- | ------------------ | ---------------- |
| `positioner` | rest  | `sideOffset`       | `space.200`      |
| `positioner` | rest  | `collisionPadding` | `size.panel-gap` |

Hover, highlighted, focus, pressed, disabled, selected and invalid don't apply to the popup: it is not a control. Base UI's `data-starting-style`, `data-ending-style` and `data-instant` take no look, as the popup has no transition (CR-10).

Base UI marks the trigger `data-popup-open` while its tooltip is open and `data-trigger-disabled` while it can't open. The trigger takes no look of Tooltip's own in either, keeping its own component's look: it is the caller's Button, IconButton or ToolbarButton, whose spec already gives its hover and focus; a tooltip labels it and changes nothing about it, and the Tooltips family's Hover and Selected columns are None.

## Keyboard and ARIA

From the Base UI reference for `Tooltip` and the installed `TooltipRoot`, `TooltipTrigger`, `TooltipPopup` and the focus, hover and dismiss hooks they build on. "From" says who does it.

| Key                         | Does                                                                                                                                                                         | From                                   |
| --------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| `Tab`, `Shift+Tab`          | Moving focus onto the trigger opens its tooltip at once, calling `onOpen` with `'trigger-focus'`; moving it off closes the tooltip, calling `onClose` with `'trigger-focus'` | The browser moves focus; Base UI opens |
| `Escape`                    | While the tooltip is open, from anywhere in the document: calls `onClose(event, 'escape-key', details)`, and focus stays on the trigger                                      | Base UI                                |
| `Enter`, `Space` on trigger | Run the trigger's own action, and close the tooltip with `'trigger-press'` while `closeOnClick` is on                                                                        | The browser, the trigger; Base UI      |

No other key: the popup is out of the tab order (`tabindex="-1"`) and holds no control, so Tab passes it by.

Tooltip adds no ARIA of its own, neither `role="tooltip"` on the popup nor `aria-describedby` or `aria-label` on the trigger, leaving the trigger named by its own words, as Base UI's guidelines ask. Perron's triggers already carry their names (an IconButton's required `label`, a Button's text), so a description that repeats the name would be read twice; `aria-describedby` would point at a popup that exists only while open, so the description would come and go with the hover; and the contract's first checklist line holds because the tooltip's words match the trigger's name, which the `Default` story checks. A word that says more than the name belongs in visible text or a popover, as the Do and don't table says.

| Element      | Role                                       | Accessible name from                                          | States announced                      |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| `trigger`    | The caller's element's own, such as button | Its own content or `aria-label`, such as IconButton's `label` | Its own, such as disabled; none added |
| `positioner` | `presentation`, from Base UI               | none                                                          | none                                  |
| `root`       | none: a `<div>` that reads as its text     | none: its `children` are read as text                         | none                                  |

What axe won't catch, from the contract, each with how this component meets it:

- [ ] Everything the eye is told, the ear is told, for every shape each prop accepts: the tooltip's words match the trigger's accessible name, which the trigger carries whether the tooltip is open or not; the popup draws no mark.
- [ ] Every landmark and named region has an accessible name: none here; the popup is not a landmark or a region.
- [ ] Every default label can be overridden: none here; Tooltip owns no strings.
- [ ] Every shape the type accepts renders, in every variant: `children` renders a string, an element and a list alike, as the `Content` story shows.
- [ ] A hidden copy kept for animation is `aria-hidden`, and a collapsed region is `inert`: none here; the popup leaves the document when it closes, and Base UI makes the positioner `inert` while it is closed.
- [ ] Native semantics first: the trigger is the caller's native `<button>` or Base UI button, and the popup a plain `<div>` for words, with no role.
- [ ] Focus moves in reading order and returns on close: the popup never takes focus, so opening and closing it leaves focus on the trigger.
- [ ] Every target is at least `size.target-min` square: the trigger, the caller's control, such as IconButton's `size.control` square; the popup takes no press.
- [ ] Loops stop when the system asks for less motion: none here; the popup has no loop and no transition.

## Owned strings

No owned strings: every word in the popup comes from the caller, as `children`, and the trigger's name from the trigger.

## Component rules

Rules for this component alone, numbered so the build and the review can cite them.

- **CR-1.** Tooltip renders `Tooltip.Root`, then `Tooltip.Trigger` and `Tooltip.Portal`, `Tooltip.Positioner` and `Tooltip.Popup`, and no `Tooltip.Provider`, `Tooltip.Arrow` or `Tooltip.Viewport`; the entry's `baseUiParts` name neither `Tooltip.Arrow` nor `Tooltip.Viewport`. `PerronProvider` renders one `Tooltip.Provider` with no props around its children, inside its locale context, so every tooltip under it shares Base UI's delay group.
- **CR-2.** Base UI already opens the tooltip on a resting mouse pointer and on `:focus-visible` focus, never on touch, keeps it open while the pointer is over the popup, closes it on leave, blur, Esc, a press outside and a press of the trigger, places, flips and shifts it inside the viewport, and marks the hidden trigger, so the component rebuilds none of it and adds no pointer or key handlers of its own.
- **CR-3.** The popup is the root: `{...rest}` comes before its own attributes, `ref` reaches it, and `className` is merged after `pn-Tooltip`. `children`, `trigger`, `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpen`, `onClose` and `slotProps` are taken out of `rest` first, so none reaches the `<div>`.
- **CR-4.** `onOpenChange(open, details)` is adapted once, inside the component: `onOpen(details.event, details)` when `open` is `true` and `onClose(details.event, details.reason, details)` when it is `false`. Tooltip exposes no `onOpenChange`.
- **CR-5.** Tooltip gives `Tooltip.Trigger` an id, the `trigger` element's own `id`, then `slotProps.trigger.id`, or one from React's `useId`, and passes it to `Tooltip.Root` as `defaultTriggerId`, or as `triggerId` when `open` is set, as the Base UI reference says for a tooltip open at first render or controlled, so such a tooltip sits against its trigger. The trigger renders through `Tooltip.Trigger`'s `render`, with `pn-Tooltip-trigger` beside the element's own class.
- **CR-6.** `slotProps.trigger`, `slotProps.portal` and `slotProps.positioner` are spread through `mergeProps` (`@base-ui/react/merge-props`), the component's own props last; each part's class is set after the merge by `withClass`, the part's class first, then the caller's `className`, a string or a function of the part's state. The positioner's `sideOffset` and `collisionPadding` are defaults: the component passes `space.200` and `size.panel-gap` only when `slotProps.positioner` gives none, reading their pixel lengths in script from `--perron-space-200` and `--perron-size-panel-gap` with `tokenValue`, never a literal, and with no document or before a token stylesheet gives both in pixels it passes neither, so Base UI's defaults apply. The reading is the shared helper `positionerOffsets`, in `packages/perron/src/internal/tokens.ts` beside `tokenValue` and in the contract's Shared helpers table, once MapTooltip's own; MapTooltip and Tooltip both import it, and neither declares it again.
- **CR-7.** The positioner takes `z-index.dialog`, and hides the popup with `visibility: hidden` while it carries `[data-anchor-hidden]`.
- **CR-8.** The popup's look is the Tooltips family's and MapTooltip's, and nothing more: `color.surface.inverse`, `color.text.inverse`, `radius.md`, `typography.label-sm` with its tracking twin, no shadow and no border, padded `space.150` on the block axis and `space.200` on the inline axis. Its text wraps (`overflow-wrap: break-word`, for a box that sizes to its content) inside `max-inline-size: var(--available-width)`, with `box-sizing: border-box` so the padding stays inside that cap.
- **CR-9.** The popup is a block: `children` flow as the caller writes them, and the component sets no flex or grid on them. Content takes the popup's colour through `currentColor`.
- **CR-10.** Opening and closing are immediate: no `duration.*` token fits a tooltip, so the CSS has no transition or animation, and `data-starting-style`, `data-ending-style` and `data-instant` take no look, as in MapTooltip.
- **CR-11.** In forced colours the popup draws a `border.width.025` solid `CanvasText` outline, inside `@media (forced-colors: active)`, so its geometry doesn't change.
- **CR-12.** The component adds no role or `aria-hidden` to the popup, and no `aria-describedby` or `aria-label` to the trigger, and gives the trigger no style of its own in any state, `[data-popup-open]` and `[data-trigger-disabled]` included.

## Stories

The deferred drawing has no variant property and no `State`: the popup has one look and one design state, open, so its one variant is `Default` (`penpot/README.md`, "Conventions"). The other stories are behaviour, which the `play` tests check.

The meta sets `parameters: { docs: { story: { inline: false, height: '480px' } } }`, since the popup portals to `<body>`, and each story renders in its own frame, with its trigger away from the frame's edges except in `NearTopEdge`. A trigger in a story is an [IconButton](icon-button.md) with the `plus`, `minus` or `locate` icon from `packages/perron/icons/`, its `label` the tooltip's words. Each `play` finds the popup through `screen`, outside `canvasElement`, and ends with it closed and focus back where it started.

| Story             | Shows                                                                                                                                                                      | `play` test                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Default`         | The subject story: the tooltip open (`defaultOpen`) above its trigger, an IconButton labelled "Zoom in", with the words "Zoom in"; its args pass every rule alone          | The popup has `pn-Tooltip`, no role, and the text "Zoom in", the same as the trigger's accessible name; the trigger has `pn-Tooltip-trigger` and no `aria-describedby`; the positioner has `data-side="top"` and the popup's bottom edge sits above the trigger's top; Esc with `details.cancel()` in `onClose` leaves it open; Esc again calls `onClose` with `'escape-key'` and the popup leaves the document |
| `Hover`           | The tooltip open (`defaultOpen`) at first, beside its trigger, which opens it again                                                                                        | A press outside closes the tooltip open at first; hovering the trigger then calls `onOpen` with `'trigger-hover'` and the popup appears; moving the pointer onto the popup keeps it open; moving it off both calls `onClose` with `'trigger-hover'` and the popup leaves the document                                                                                                                           |
| `Keyboard`        | The tooltip open (`defaultOpen`) at first, after a button "Before" that holds focus at the start                                                                           | A press outside closes the tooltip open at first; Tab focuses the trigger and calls `onOpen` with `'trigger-focus'`; Esc calls `onClose` with `'escape-key'` and focus stays on the trigger; Shift+Tab moves focus back to "Before" with the tooltip closed                                                                                                                                                     |
| `Controlled`      | The tooltip with `open` held in the story's state, set to `true` at first                                                                                                  | A click on the trigger calls `onClose` with `'trigger-press'` and the story clears `open`; hovering opens it again; a press outside calls `onClose` with `'outside-press'`; ends closed                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `Content`         | The tooltip open (`defaultOpen`) with a list of an element and a string as `children`, `[<strong>Zoom</strong>, ' in']`, on an IconButton labelled "Zoom in"               | The popup holds both in `color.text.inverse`, read as "Zoom in", the trigger's name, and stays inside the viewport                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `Group`           | Three triggers in a row, "Zoom in", "Zoom out" and "Centre the map", each in its own Tooltip, inside a `PerronProvider`, the first's tooltip open (`defaultOpen`) at first | A press outside closes the first's tooltip, open at first; hovering the first opens it again; moving the pointer straight to the second opens the second's at once, its popup marked `data-instant="delay"`, and closes the first's; leaving the row closes it                                                                                                                                                  |
| `NearTopEdge`     | The tooltip open (`defaultOpen`) on a trigger at the top of the frame, where there is no room above it                                                                     | The positioner flips to `data-side="bottom"`, and the popup's top edge sits below the trigger's bottom                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `DisabledTrigger` | The tooltip on a disabled IconButton labelled "Zoom in", with `focusableWhenDisabled`, open (`defaultOpen`) at first                                                       | A press outside closes the tooltip open at first; Tab focuses the disabled trigger and its tooltip opens; Esc closes it; the trigger keeps `data-disabled` and its own look                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |

## Do and don't

For a caller using the component, with the reason.

| Do                                                                                                                                         | Don't                                                                                                                                      |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Give an icon-only control a tooltip with the same words as its accessible name: an IconButton labelled "Zoom in" and the tooltip "Zoom in" | Write tooltip words that differ from the trigger's name: a screen reader hears only the name                                               |
| Keep the words to a short label, in sentence case                                                                                          | Put a sentence the reader needs in a tooltip: touch and screen reader users never see it, so put it in visible text or a popover           |
| Pass a control that takes a ref and spreads its props as `trigger`, such as a Button, an IconButton or a ToolbarButton                     | Pass a component that drops the props it is given: Base UI's hover and focus handlers never reach the element, and the tooltip never opens |
| Keep a disabled trigger focusable with `focusableWhenDisabled`, so its tooltip still opens from the keys                                   | Put the tooltip on a natively `disabled` button: it leaves the tab order, so the keyboard can't reach the tooltip                          |
| Put a button in a toolbar in a tooltip with `trigger={<ToolbarButton … />}`, the way round [Toolbar](toolbar.md) gives                     | Pass the tooltip's trigger to the button's `render`, as for popups                                                                         |
| Keep the app inside one `PerronProvider`, so a row of tooltips opens at once after the first                                               | Add a provider per tooltip: each waits the full delay again                                                                                |
| Use [MapTooltip](map-tooltip.md) for a card against a point on the map                                                                     | Wrap the map canvas in a Tooltip: it has one trigger, the whole canvas, not the vehicle under the pointer                                  |
| Put only words in the tooltip                                                                                                              | Put a link, a button or a field in it: the popup is out of the tab order, so the keys can't reach them                                     |
| Change the side through `slotProps.positioner`, such as `side: 'bottom'`                                                                   | Move the popup with a margin or a `transform`: Base UI's placement and flipping no longer match what is drawn                              |

title: Delay
markdown:
# Delay

How late or early a vehicle or departure runs, as a short figure in the delay's colour, such as "+3 min", with the same thing said in words to a screen reader.

## Anatomy

Penpot page `Components/Delay`. Family: none. Shared parts: VisuallyHidden.

The design is deferred (ADR 0010, `docs/adr/0010-unattended-runs-with-design-deferred.md`), so the layers below are the ones the drawing will name. Delay has no Base UI part: it is display text with no behaviour, so its root renders through Base UI's `useRender` hook (`@base-ui/react/use-render`), which gives it the `render` prop, and its inner parts are plain elements.

| Part (Penpot layer) | What it is                                                                                                                          | Base UI part                                   | Class                               | `slotProps` key |
| ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- | --------------- |
| `root`              | The whole delay, one inline run of text: a `<span>` in the delay's colour                                                           | none: a `<span>` rendered by `useRender`       | `pn-Delay`                          | none            |
| `value`             | The visible figure: the signed whole minutes ("+3", "−1"), "On time", or "—" when unknown                                           | none: a plain `<span>`, no behaviour to borrow | `pn-Delay-value`                    | none            |
| `unit`              | "min", after a space, shown only after a signed figure                                                                              | none: a plain `<span>`, no behaviour to borrow | `pn-Delay-unit`                     | none            |
| `label`             | The words a screen reader hears in place of the figure: "3 min late", "1 min early", "Delay unknown". Not drawn, so no Penpot layer | none: the VisuallyHidden shared part           | `pn-VisuallyHidden`, the part's own | none            |

Delay shows a signed figure with its unit, "+3 min" late and "−1 min" early (the true minus sign), "On time" in words when on time, and "—" with no unit when unknown, as content design writes numbers: a space before units, the true minus sign for early and "—" for unknown.

Delay's one Penpot variant property is `delay`, with the values `on-time`, `slight`, `late`, `early` and `unknown`. The code map maps it to the CSS state `[data-delay]` with the same value rather than to a prop, since the component works it out from `minutes`. The variants are `OnTime`, `Slight`, `Late`, `Early` and `Unknown`, and the stories carry those names.

## Base UI parts

Delay imports no Base UI component. It uses two Base UI utilities, at the version pinned in `package.json`: `useRender` (`@base-ui/react/use-render`) for the root and `mergeProps` (`@base-ui/react/merge-props`) to merge the caller's props over its own.

| Base UI part                     | Renders  | Perron sets                                                                                                          | Passed through                                        |
| -------------------------------- | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `useRender` (a hook, not a part) | `<span>` | `defaultTagName: 'span'`, `className` (`pn-Delay` first, then the caller's), `data-delay`, the children (CR-3, CR-4) | `render`, `ref`, `className`, `style`, the rest props |

Base UI already does: swapping the root element for the one `render` gives, keeping the class, data attribute and children; merging the caller's `ref` with the element's; and merging event handlers, `className` and `style` through `mergeProps`.

## Props

In MUI's layout. Every prop here gets this description as its JSDoc. Delay takes no `children`: it writes its own figure and words. It has no `slotProps`, because the contract keys `slotProps` by inner Base UI part and Delay has none; a caller restyles it through `className` on the root.

The delay is given as `minutes: number | null`, required, in minutes (positive late, negative early, `0` on time, `null` unknown) and rounded to the nearest whole minute, not as `value` or in seconds: the contract's `value` belongs to controls with `defaultValue` and `onChange`, and the tokens, the words and the visible figure all count whole minutes.

| Name                 | Type                   | Default      | Base UI prop         | Description                                                                                                                                                                               |
| -------------------- | ---------------------- | ------------ | -------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `minutes`            | `number \| null`       | (required)   | none                 | The delay in minutes: positive when late, negative when early, `0` on time, `null` when no real-time data says (timetable only, no signal). Rounded to the nearest whole minute.          |
| `render`             | Base UI's `render`     |              | inherited            | Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render. |
| `minutesUnitLabel`   | `string`               | The locale's | none                 | Overrides "min", the unit after the figure                                                                                                                                                |
| `minutesLateLabel`   | `string`               | The locale's | none                 | Overrides "min late", heard after the number when late                                                                                                                                    |
| `minutesEarlyLabel`  | `string`               | The locale's | none                 | Overrides "min early", heard after the number when early                                                                                                                                  |
| `onTimeLabel`        | `string`               | The locale's | none                 | Overrides "On time"                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `delayUnknownLabel`  | `string`               | The locale's | none                 | Overrides "Delay unknown", heard in place of "—"                                                                                                                                          |
| `className`, `style` | React's                |              | through `mergeProps` | Reaches the root; `className` is merged after `pn-Delay`                                                                                                                                  |
| `ref`                | `Ref<HTMLSpanElement>` |              | `useRender`'s `ref`  | Reaches the root element                                                                                                                                                                  |

## Tokens

Delay is not interactive, so its one design state is rest; each row's state names the `data-delay` value it applies to. Delay is not one of the contract's families, so it draws no fill, border or radius.

Delay comes in one size, set in `typography.data`, with no `size` prop; a caller who needs it larger (beside a `typography.data-lg` countdown) sets the font through `className`. `typography.data` is the role for "times, delays, counts and percentages in lists and tables", where Delay sits, and a second size can join later as a `size` prop without a break.

| Part    | State                          | Property               | Token                                                  |
| ------- | ------------------------------ | ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `root`  | rest, every `data-delay`       | `font`                 | `typography.data`                                      |
| `root`  | rest, every `data-delay`       | `letter-spacing`       | `typography.data-tracking`                             |
| `root`  | rest, every `data-delay`       | `font-variant-numeric` | none: the keyword `tabular-nums`, so figures line up   |
| `root`  | rest, every `data-delay`       | `white-space`          | none: the keyword `nowrap`, so "+3 min" never breaks   |
| `root`  | rest, `data-delay='on-time'`   | `color`                | `color.transit.delay.on-time`                          |
| `root`  | rest, `data-delay='slight'`    | `color`                | `color.transit.delay.slight`                           |
| `root`  | rest, `data-delay='late'`      | `color`                | `color.transit.delay.late`                             |
| `root`  | rest, `data-delay='early'`     | `color`                | `color.transit.delay.early`                            |
| `root`  | rest, `data-delay='unknown'`   | `color`                | `color.transit.delay.unknown`                          |
| `value` | rest, every `data-delay`       | `color`                | none: inherits the root's                              |
| `unit`  | rest, `data-delay` with a unit | `color`                | none: inherits the root's                              |
| `label` | rest                           | none                   | none: the VisuallyHidden part's own styles, never seen |

The space between `value` and `unit` is a text space, as content design writes "4 min", not a gap token, so a copied delay reads "+3 min".

## Keyboard and ARIA

Delay is text: it takes no focus, and no key does anything. A caller who makes it a link or button through `render` brings that element's own keys.

| Key  | Does                               | From   |
| ---- | ---------------------------------- | ------ |
| none | Delay is not focusable or operable | Perron |

| Element            | Role                         | Accessible name from                                                            | States announced |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------- |
| `root`             | none: a generic `<span>`     | Not named; its text is read in place, as part of the row or sentence it sits in | none             |
| `value` and `unit` | hidden, `aria-hidden="true"` | Not read, except "On time", which is read as shown (CR-3)                       | none             |
| `label`            | text                         | The owned strings: "3 min late", "1 min early", "Delay unknown"                 | none             |

The visible figure is `aria-hidden`, with a VisuallyHidden label saying the delay in words: the number without its sign and then "min late" or "min early" ("3 min late", "1 min early"), and "Delay unknown" in place of "—", while "On time" is read from the visible text. A screen reader reads "+3 min" as "plus 3 min" and skips or spells "—", so the ear would get less than the eye, and an `aria-label` on a role-less `<span>` is not allowed.

What axe won't catch, from the contract, each with how this component meets it:

- [ ] Everything the eye is told, the ear is told, for every shape each prop accepts: the colour and sign say late, slight, early or on time; the label says "N min late" or "N min early", "On time" is read as shown, and `null` says "Delay unknown". In forced colours the colour goes, and the sign and words still carry it.
- [ ] Every landmark and named region has an accessible name: none here; Delay is inline text.
- [ ] Every default label can be overridden: `minutesUnitLabel`, `minutesLateLabel`, `minutesEarlyLabel`, `onTimeLabel` and `delayUnknownLabel`.
- [ ] Every shape the type accepts renders, in every variant: `minutes` is a number or `null`; positive, negative, zero, fractional (rounded), `NaN` and infinite (both unknown, CR-1) all render, and a story's `play` test covers each kind.
- [ ] A hidden copy kept for animation is `aria-hidden`, and a collapsed region is `inert`: none here; Delay does not animate. The visible figure is `aria-hidden` because the label speaks for it, not for animation.
- [ ] Native semantics first: a `<span>`, with no role and no ARIA beyond `aria-hidden` on the figure the label replaces.
- [ ] Focus moves in reading order and returns on close: Delay takes no focus.
- [ ] Every target is at least `size.target-min` square: no target; Delay is not pressed.
- [ ] Loops stop when the system asks for less motion: none here; Delay has no motion.

## Owned strings

Every word Delay shows or announces is its own; the caller gives only `minutes`. The number is never part of a string: it renders as its own text run beside the word, so the dictionaries stay plain strings (CR-3).

| Key            | English         | Override            | Seen or heard where                                         |
| -------------- | --------------- | ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `minutesUnit`  | "min"           | `minutesUnitLabel`  | `unit`, seen after a signed figure, "+3 min"; `aria-hidden` |
| `minutesLate`  | "min late"      | `minutesLateLabel`  | `label`, heard after the number when late: "3 min late"     |
| `minutesEarly` | "min early"     | `minutesEarlyLabel` | `label`, heard after the number when early: "1 min early"   |
| `onTime`       | "On time"       | `onTimeLabel`       | `value`, seen and heard when `minutes` rounds to `0`        |
| `delayUnknown` | "Delay unknown" | `delayUnknownLabel` | `label`, heard in place of "—" when `minutes` is `null`     |

No key in `packages/perron/src/locale/en.ts` says any of these, so all five are new, each with a JSDoc line like its neighbours.

"On time" and "Delay unknown" join the data-state and delay words table in `docs/content-design.md`, with their Danish, Swedish and Norwegian, so every screen says a delay the same way; content design says delays always use the words in that table, and its test then holds the locale files to them. "min", "min late" and "min early" stay out of it, as parts of a number's phrase rather than words a screen shows on their own.

## Component rules

- **CR-1.** Delay works out its kind from `minutes` after rounding it with `Math.round`: `null`, `NaN` or an infinite number is `unknown`; `0` (and `-0`) is `on-time`; `1` or `2` is `slight`; `3` or more is `late`; `-1` or less is `early`. Early has no slight step. These are the bounds the `color.transit.delay.*` tokens describe.
- **CR-2.** The visible figure is "+N" when late and "−N" when early, with U+2212, never a hyphen-minus, then a text space and the `minutesUnit` word in `unit`. On time, `value` is the `onTime` word and there is no `unit`. Unknown, `value` is "—" (U+2014) and there is no `unit`.
- **CR-3.** When late, early or unknown, `value` and `unit` are `aria-hidden="true"` and the VisuallyHidden `label` holds the words: the number without its sign, a space and `minutesLate` or `minutesEarly`, or `delayUnknown` alone. The number and each word are separate text runs, so `expectOwnedStrings` reads the words as dictionary values. On time, `value` is read as shown and there is no `label`.
- **CR-4.** The root always carries `data-delay` with the kind from CR-1, `on-time`, `slight`, `late`, `early` or `unknown`, and the CSS reads the colour from it, as [Tokens](#tokens) gives.
- **CR-5.** Delay takes no data state. A caller showing a timetable-only or no-signal vehicle passes `minutes={null}`, as [Data states](../foundations/data-states.md#delays) says those always show an unknown delay.
- **CR-6.** Delay is not a live region. A screen that updates delays announces changes of state in its own polite live region, as [Accessibility](../foundations/accessibility.md) asks.
- **CR-7.** Delay composes the VisuallyHidden shared part from its folder in `packages/perron/src/`, and never draws its own hiding styles. If no earlier component has added the part yet, Delay's build adds it, as the contract's [Shared parts](README.md#shared-parts) table already describes it.
- **CR-8.** The root renders through `useRender` with `mergeProps`: Delay's own props (`className` starting with `pn-Delay`, `data-delay`, the children) win over the caller's rest props, and `minutes` and every `*Label` prop are taken out of the rest before the merge, so none reaches the DOM.

## Stories

One per variant the deferred design will draw, named as CR-1's kinds in PascalCase. Each `play` test reads the accessibility tree, not the pixels.

| Story     | Shows                                          | `play` test                                                                                                              |
| --------- | ---------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `OnTime`  | `minutes={0}`, "On time" in the on-time colour | `data-delay` is `on-time`; "On time" is visible and in the accessible text; no `label`; `minutes={0.4}` renders the same |
| `Slight`  | `minutes={2}`, "+2 min"                        | `data-delay` is `slight`; "+2 min" is visible and `aria-hidden`; the accessible text is "2 min late"                     |
| `Late`    | `minutes={7}`, "+7 min"                        | `data-delay` is `late`; the accessible text is "7 min late"; `minutes={2.6}` rounds to `late` and "+3 min"               |
| `Early`   | `minutes={-1}`, "−1 min" with U+2212           | `data-delay` is `early`; the figure starts with U+2212; the accessible text is "1 min early"                             |
| `Unknown` | `minutes={null}`, "—"                          | `data-delay` is `unknown`; "—" is `aria-hidden`; the accessible text is "Delay unknown"; `NaN` renders the same          |

## Do and don't

For a caller using the component, with the reason.

| Do                                                                                                                             | Don't                                                                                                                          |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Pass `minutes={null}` for a timetable-only or no-signal vehicle, because no real-time data says how late it is.                | Pass `0` when the delay is unknown: "On time" claims more certainty than the data has.                                         |
| Pass the delay in minutes, and let Delay round, sign and colour it.                                                            | Format the figure yourself and put it in a Text in a delay colour: the words for the ear and the `data-delay` kind go missing. |
| Set Delay beside stronger text, such as the departure time, because `color.transit.delay.unknown` is too faint to stand alone. | Use Delay alone as a row's only content when it may be unknown: "—" in that colour misses 4.5:1 by design.                     |
| Announce a changed delay in the screen's own polite live region, once, when its kind changes.                                  | Wrap Delay in a live region that reads every minute's change: it floods the screen reader.                                     |
| Use `color.transit.severity.delay` and its label for a delay disruption on a line.                                             | Use Delay for a line's disruption: it says how late one vehicle or departure runs.                                             |

title: LineBadge
markdown:
# LineBadge

A small filled label that names one Copenhagen line, a metro, S-tog, bus or regional train, in the operator's own line colour.

## Anatomy

Penpot page `Components/LineBadge`. Family: none. Shared parts: none.

The design is deferred (ADR 0010, `docs/adr/0010-unattended-runs-with-design-deferred.md`), so this spec sets the layers the drawing will have: a `root` board holding one text layer, `label`.

| Part (Penpot layer) | What it is                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | Base UI part                                  | Class          | `slotProps` key |
| ------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | -------------- | --------------- |
| `root`              | The badge: a fixed-height box in the line's colour, with the label centred in it                                                                                                                                                             | none: a `<span>` rendered through `useRender` | `pn-LineBadge` | none            |
| `label`             | The line's short name, such as "M1", "A" or "5C", from the caller's `children`. The `label` layer is the root's own text, with no element, class or `slotProps` key of its own: the root holds the text directly, so there is no inner part. | none: the root's text                         | none           | none            |

## Base UI parts

No Base UI component: `baseUiParts` is empty in `packages/perron/components.json`, and a badge has no behaviour to borrow. The root renders through Base UI's `useRender` hook, from `@base-ui/react/use-render` at the version pinned in `packages/perron/package.json`, so the contract's `render` prop works, and the component's props are merged with `mergeProps` from `@base-ui/react/merge-props`.

| Base UI part | Renders  | Perron sets                                                                                                              | Passed through                                                                       |
| ------------ | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `useRender`  | `<span>` | `defaultTagName: 'span'`; `className` `pn-LineBadge` then the caller's; `data-line` from `line`; `data-size` from `size` | `render`, `ref`, `children`, `className`, `style` and every other `<span>` attribute |

Base UI already does: swapping the root element for the `render` prop, merging the caller's `ref` with the element's under React 19, and merging `className`, `style` and event handlers in `mergeProps`.

## Props

In MUI's layout. Every prop here gets this description as its JSDoc. No slots: the badge has no inner part.

| Name        | Type                                                                                            | Default    | Base UI prop | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------- | ------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `line`      | `'m1' \| 'm2' \| 'm3' \| 'm4' \| 'a' \| 'b' \| 'c' \| 'e' \| 'f' \| 'h' \| 'bus' \| 'regional'` | none       | none         | The line whose colours the badge takes: a metro line (`m1` to `m4`), an S-tog line (`a` to `h`), any bus (`bus`), or any regional or Øresund train (`regional`). Required, with no default; set on the root as `data-line`. |
| `size`      | `'medium' \| 'large'`                                                                           | `'medium'` | none         | `medium` is the badge in rows and lists, `size.badge` tall; `large` is the badge in a panel's header, `size.badge-lg` tall. Both sizes set the label in `typography.badge`.                                                 |
| `children`  | `ReactNode`                                                                                     | none       | none         | The line's short name as riders know it: "M1", "A", "5C", "RE". Required: the badge never derives it from `line`, which holds no bus number.                                                                                |
| `render`    | Base UI's `render`                                                                              |            | inherited    | Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render.                                   |
| `className` | `string`                                                                                        |            | none         | Joined after `pn-LineBadge` on the root                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `style`     | `CSSProperties`                                                                                 |            | none         | Reaches the root                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `ref`       | `Ref<HTMLSpanElement>`                                                                          |            | none         | Reaches the root element                                                                                                                                                                                                    |

`className`, `style` and `ref` reach the root, as the contract's [Root](README.md#root) says.

## Tokens

One row per part, state and property. The badge has one design state, rest: it is never interactive (CR-2). Each `line` value sets the fill and its partner label colour, as [Semantic colours](../foundations/semantic-colours.md#line-colours) pairs them.

| Part   | State                 | Property         | Token                                                                                                                                                |
| ------ | --------------------- | ---------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `root` | rest, `line` m1       | `background`     | `color.transit.line.m1`                                                                                                                              |
| `root` | rest, `line` m1       | `color`          | `color.transit.line-on.m1`                                                                                                                           |
| `root` | rest, `line` m2       | `background`     | `color.transit.line.m2`                                                                                                                              |
| `root` | rest, `line` m2       | `color`          | `color.transit.line-on.m2`                                                                                                                           |
| `root` | rest, `line` m3       | `background`     | `color.transit.line.m3`                                                                                                                              |
| `root` | rest, `line` m3       | `color`          | `color.transit.line-on.m3`                                                                                                                           |
| `root` | rest, `line` m4       | `background`     | `color.transit.line.m4`                                                                                                                              |
| `root` | rest, `line` m4       | `color`          | `color.transit.line-on.m4`                                                                                                                           |
| `root` | rest, `line` a        | `background`     | `color.transit.line.a`                                                                                                                               |
| `root` | rest, `line` a        | `color`          | `color.transit.line-on.a`                                                                                                                            |

| `root` | rest, `line` regional | `background`     | `color.transit.mode.regional`                                                                                                                        |
| `root` | rest, `line` regional | `color`          | `color.transit.mode.on-regional`                                                                                                                     |
| `root` | rest                  | `font`           | `typography.badge`                                                                                                                                   |
| `root` | rest                  | `letter-spacing` | `typography.badge-tracking`, the role's twin                                                                                                         |
| `root` | rest                  | `border-radius`  | `radius.sm`                                                                                                                                          |
| `root` | rest, `size` medium   | `height`         | `size.badge`                                                                                                                                         |
| `root` | rest, `size` large    | `height`         | `size.badge-lg`                                                                                                                                      |
| `root` | rest, `size` medium   | `min-width`      | `size.badge`, so a one-letter line is square. The badge is at least as wide as it is tall, `size.badge` or `size.badge-lg`.                          |
| `root` | rest, `size` large    | `min-width`      | `size.badge-lg`                                                                                                                                      |
